subject: Chemistry
title: Energy of Photon
description: Energy of a quantum of light.
derivation:
From Planck's Quantum Theory.
Energy is proportional to frequency: $E \propto \nu$.
$E = h\nu$.
Since speed of light $c = \nu \lambda$, we have $\nu = c/\lambda$.
Substitute: $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda}$.

related_concepts.name: Planck's Constant
related_concepts.definition: $h \approx 6.626 \times 10^{-34} Js$. The fundamental quantum of action.

related_concepts.name: Photoelectric Effect
related_concepts.definition: Ejection of electrons from a metal surface when light of sufficient frequency strikes it.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bohr's Quantization
description: Angular momentum quantization condition.
derivation:
Bohr proposed that electron orbits are stable only if the circumference contains an integer number of de Broglie wavelengths.
$2\pi r = n\lambda$.
Substitute $\lambda = h/p = h/mv$:
$2\pi r = n(h/mv)$.
Rearrange: $mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$.

related_concepts.name: Stationary State
related_concepts.definition: An orbit where the electron does not radiate energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Radius of Bohr Orbit
description: Radius of nth orbit in hydrogen-like species.
derivation:
1. Force Balance: Electrostatic attraction = Centripetal force.
$\frac{kZe^2}{r^2} = \frac{mv^2}{r} \implies v^2 = \frac{kZe^2}{mr}$.
2. Quantization: $v = \frac{nh}{2\pi mr}$.
Square (2) and equate to (1):
$\frac{n^2 h^2}{4\pi^2 m^2 r^2} = \frac{kZe^2}{mr}$.
Solve for $r$: $r = \frac{n^2 h^2}{4\pi^2 m k Z e^2}$.

related_concepts.name: Bohr Radius (a0)
related_concepts.definition: The radius of the first orbit of Hydrogen ($n=1, Z=1$), approx $0.529 \mathring{A}$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Energy of Electron
description: Total energy of electron in nth orbit.
derivation:
Total Energy $E = K + U$.
$U = -\frac{kZe^2}{r}$ (Potential).
$K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{kZe^2}{2r}$ (from Force balance).
$E = \frac{kZe^2}{2r} - \frac{kZe^2}{r} = -\frac{kZe^2}{2r}$.
Substitute formula for $r \propto n^2/Z$:
$E \propto -\frac{Z^2}{n^2}$.

related_concepts.name: Ionization Energy
related_concepts.definition: Energy required to remove an electron from the ground state to infinity ($E_\infty = 0$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Rydberg Equation
description: Wavenumber of emitted photon during transition.
derivation:
Energy difference $\Delta E = E_{n2} - E_{n1}$.
$\Delta E = 13.6 Z^2 (\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2})$ eV.
Photon energy $E = hc/\lambda$.
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = \frac{13.6 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{hc} Z^2 (...)$.
The constant term corresponds to Rydberg Constant $R_H$.

related_concepts.name: Spectral Series
related_concepts.definition: Lyman (UV, $n_1=1$), Balmer (Visible, $n_1=2$), Paschen (IR, $n_1=3$).

subject: Chemistry
title: de Broglie Wavelength
description: Wave-particle duality relation.
derivation:
Analogy combining Mass-Energy and Planck Energy.
$E = mc^2$ and $E = h\nu = hc/\lambda$.
$mc^2 = hc/\lambda \implies \lambda = h/mc$.
Replacing $c$ with velocity $v$ for material particles:
$\lambda = h/mv$.

related_concepts.name: Matter Waves
related_concepts.definition: Waves associated with moving particles (electrons, protons, etc.).

subject: Chemistry
title: Wavelength (Charged Particle)
description: Wavelength of particle accelerated by potential V.
derivation:
Kinetic Energy gained by charge $Q$ falling through potential $V$ is $K = QV$.
Also $K = \frac{p^2}{2m} \implies p = \sqrt{2mK} = \sqrt{2mQV}$.
Substitute into de Broglie eq $\lambda = h/p$:
$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mQV}}$.

related_concepts.name: Electron Wavelength
related_concepts.definition: For an electron, $\lambda \approx \sqrt{150/V} \mathring{A}$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Heisenberg Uncertainty
description: Fundamental limit of precision. \(\Delta x\): uncertainty in position, \(\Delta p\): uncertainty in momentum.
derivation:
Derived from the wave nature of particles.
To localize a wave packet in space (small \(\Delta x\)), you need a superposition of many wavelengths (large \(\Delta \lambda\)), which implies large uncertainty in momentum (\(\Delta p\)).
Exact limit derived from operators: \(\sigma_x \sigma_p \ge \hbar/2\).

related_concepts.name: Complementary Variables
related_concepts.definition: Pairs of properties (like position/momentum) that cannot be simultaneously measured with arbitrary precision.

subject: Chemistry
title: Spin Magnetic Moment
description: Magnetic moment based on unpaired electrons ($n$).
derivation:
Derived from Quantum Mechanics for spin angular momentum.
Spin angular momentum $S = \sqrt{s(s+1)} (h/2\pi)$.
For $n$ unpaired electrons, total spin $s = n/2$.
Magnetic moment $\mu$ relates to $S$.
Simplified formula gives $\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ Bohr Magnetons.

related_concepts.name: Paramagnetism
related_concepts.definition: Attraction to magnetic fields due to presence of unpaired electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Orbital Nodes
description: Regions of zero probability density.
derivation:
Solutions to the radial part of the Schrödinger equation contain polynomials.
The number of roots (zeros) determines the number of radial nodes.
Radial Nodes = $n - l - 1$.
Angular Nodes = $l$ (planes passing through nucleus).
Total = $(n - l - 1) + l = n - 1$.

related_concepts.name: Nodal Plane
related_concepts.definition: A plane where the probability of finding an electron is zero.

subject: Chemistry
title: Photoelectric Effect
description: Conservation of energy for photon-electron interaction. $\Phi$: Work function.
derivation:
Einstein's Equation:
Energy of incident photon = Energy to remove electron + Kinetic Energy.
$E_{photon} = W + K_{max}$
$h\nu = h\nu_0 + \frac{1}{2}mv^2_{max}$
If $\nu < \nu_0$ (Threshold frequency), no emission occurs regardless of intensity.

related_concepts.name: Stopping Potential
related_concepts.definition: The negative potential ($V_0$) required to stop the most energetic photoelectrons: $eV_0 = KE_{max}$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Velocity in Bohr Orbit
description: Speed of electron in the n-th Bohr orbit. \(v_n\)=orbital velocity, \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n\)=principal quantum number. Equals \(\frac{Z}{n}\times\) (speed of light/137).
derivation:
Equate Coulomb force to centripetal force: \(\frac{kZe^2}{r^2} = \frac{mv^2}{r}\).
Use Bohr quantization \(mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}\) to eliminate \(r\).
Result: \(v_n = \frac{2\pi k Z e^2}{nh} = 2.18 \times 10^6 \frac{Z}{n}\) m/s.

related_concepts.name: Fine Structure Constant
related_concepts.definition: Ratio of electron speed in first Bohr orbit to speed of light, \(\approx 1/137\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Total Energy Relations
description: Virial theorem relations for an electron bound in a Bohr orbit. \(E\)=total energy, \(KE\)=kinetic energy, \(PE\)=potential energy. So \(PE = 2E\) and \(KE = -E\).

related_concepts.name: Virial Theorem
related_concepts.definition: For an inverse-square (Coulombic) force, \(PE = -2\,KE\), giving total energy equal to negative of kinetic energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Spectral Lines
description: Maximum spectral lines from electrons de-exciting between levels \(n_2\) and \(n_1\). \(N\)=number of lines. For de-excitation from level \(n\) to ground state, \(N = \frac{n(n-1)}{2}\).

related_concepts.name: Spectral Series
related_concepts.definition: Groups of lines (Lyman, Balmer, Paschen...) defined by the common lower level \(n_1\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Rydberg Constant Value
description: Standard value of the Rydberg constant for hydrogen. \(R_H\)=Rydberg constant. Equivalently \(R_H = 109678\) cm\(^{-1}\); \(R_H \cdot hc = 13.6\) eV.

related_concepts.name: Wavenumber
related_concepts.definition: Reciprocal of wavelength, \(\bar\nu = 1/\lambda\), expressed in cm\(^{-1}\) or m\(^{-1}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Series Limit Wavelength
description: Shortest-wavelength (highest energy) line of a spectral series, obtained as \(n_2 \to \infty\). \(\lambda_{limit}\)=series limit wavelength, \(n_1\)=lower level of the series.

related_concepts.name: Series Limit
related_concepts.definition: The convergence point of a spectral series where successive lines merge into a continuum.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ionization Energy (H-like)
description: Energy to remove the electron from the ground state of a hydrogen-like species. \(IE\)=ionization energy, \(Z\)=atomic number. From level \(n\): \(IE = 13.6\frac{Z^2}{n^2}\) eV.

related_concepts.name: Binding Energy
related_concepts.definition: Magnitude of the (negative) total energy of a bound electron; equals the energy needed to free it.

subject: Chemistry
title: Maximum Electrons in Shell
description: Maximum number of electrons that the n-th principal shell can hold. \(N_{max}\)=electron capacity, \(n\)=principal quantum number (shell).

related_concepts.name: Subshell Capacity
related_concepts.definition: An azimuthal subshell \(l\) holds at most \(2(2l+1)\) electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Orbitals in a Subshell
description: Count of orbitals and electron capacity of a subshell with azimuthal quantum number \(l\). Total orbitals in shell \(n\) is \(n^2\) (capacity \(2n^2\)).

related_concepts.name: Magnetic Quantum Number
related_concepts.definition: \(m_l\) ranges from \(-l\) to \(+l\), giving \(2l+1\) orientations (orbitals).

subject: Chemistry
title: Angular & Radial Nodes
description: Node count in an orbital. Angular (nodal planes) \(= l\); radial (spherical) nodes \(= n-l-1\); their sum equals total nodes \(n-1\).

related_concepts.name: Node
related_concepts.definition: A region where the probability of finding the electron (\(\psi^2\)) is zero.

subject: Chemistry
title: Orbital Angular Momentum
description: Magnitude of orbital angular momentum of an electron. \(L\)=angular momentum, \(l\)=azimuthal quantum number, \(h\)=Planck constant. Equals \(\sqrt{l(l+1)}\,\hbar\).

related_concepts.name: Azimuthal Quantum Number
related_concepts.definition: \(l\) defines orbital shape and subshell (\(s,p,d,f\) for \(l=0,1,2,3\)); ranges \(0\) to \(n-1\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Spin Angular Momentum
description: Magnitude of electron spin angular momentum. \(S\)=spin angular momentum, \(s=\tfrac{1}{2}\)=spin quantum number, \(m_s = \pm\tfrac{1}{2}\).

related_concepts.name: Spin Quantum Number
related_concepts.definition: \(m_s = \pm\tfrac{1}{2}\) gives the two spin orientations of an electron.

subject: Chemistry
title: de Broglie + Bohr Orbit
description: Bohr's stationary-orbit condition: orbit circumference holds a whole number of de Broglie wavelengths. \(r_n\)=orbit radius, \(n\)=quantum number, \(\lambda\)=de Broglie wavelength of electron.

related_concepts.name: Standing Wave
related_concepts.definition: A stable electron wave that closes on itself around the orbit without destructive interference.

subject: Chemistry
title: Time Period & Frequency
description: Revolution frequency of an electron in the n-th Bohr orbit. \(f\)=frequency, \(v_n\)=orbital speed, \(r_n\)=orbit radius; time period \(T = 1/f \propto \frac{n^3}{Z^2}\).

related_concepts.name: Orbital Current
related_concepts.definition: The revolving electron behaves as a current loop, \(I = ef\), producing a magnetic moment.

subject: Chemistry
title: Energy Difference (Transition)
description: Energy of photon emitted/absorbed in a transition between levels. \(\Delta E\)=energy gap, \(n_1\)=lower level, \(n_2\)=higher level, \(Z\)=atomic number.

related_concepts.name: Bohr Frequency Condition
related_concepts.definition: \(\Delta E = h\nu\): emitted/absorbed photon energy equals the gap between two stationary states.

subject: Chemistry
title: Threshold Frequency
description: Work function in terms of threshold frequency/wavelength for photoemission. \(\Phi\)=work function, \(\nu_0\)=threshold frequency, \(\lambda_0\)=threshold wavelength below which emission occurs.

related_concepts.name: Work Function
related_concepts.definition: Minimum energy needed to eject an electron from a metal surface.

subject: Chemistry
title: Stopping Potential
description: Stopping potential halts the fastest photoelectrons. \(V_0\)=stopping potential, \(e\)=electron charge, \(KE_{max}\)=max kinetic energy, \(\nu\)=light frequency, \(\Phi\)=work function.

related_concepts.name: Photoelectron
related_concepts.definition: An electron ejected from a surface when light of sufficient frequency strikes it.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Waves in Orbit
description: Number of de Broglie waves made by an electron in the n-th Bohr orbit equals the principal quantum number. \(n\)=principal quantum number.

related_concepts.name: Wave-Particle Duality
related_concepts.definition: Matter exhibits both particle and wave nature, quantified by \(\lambda = h/mv\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Charge to Mass (Cathode Ray)
description: Thomson's specific charge of the electron. \(e\)=electron charge, \(m\)=electron mass. Using \(e = 1.602\times10^{-19}\) C gives \(m = 9.11\times10^{-31}\) kg.

related_concepts.name: Millikan Oil Drop
related_concepts.definition: Experiment giving the electron charge \(e = 1.602\times10^{-19}\) C.

subject: Chemistry
title: Schrodinger Equation
description: Time-independent wave equation for an electron. \(\hat{H}\)=Hamiltonian operator, \(\psi\)=wave function (orbital), \(E\)=total energy of the electron.

related_concepts.name: Wave Function
related_concepts.definition: \(\psi\) has no physical meaning, but \(\psi^2\) gives the probability density of the electron.

subject: Chemistry
title: Electrons in a Subshell
description: Max electrons a subshell or single orbital can hold. \(l\)=azimuthal quantum number; each orbital holds 2 electrons (opposite spins).

subject: Chemistry
title: Allowed Quantum Numbers
description: Permitted values of the four quantum numbers. \(n\)=principal; \(l\)=azimuthal (0 to n-1); \(m_l\)=magnetic (2l+1 values); \(m_s\)=spin.

subject: Chemistry
title: Magnetic Quantum Number Count
description: Number of orientations (orbitals) for a given subshell. \(l\)=azimuthal quantum number; gives the count of \(m_l\) values from \(-l\) to \(+l\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Wavenumber (H-like ion)
description: Wavenumber/wavelength of photon emitted in transition for a hydrogen-like ion (He+, Li2+). \(R_H\)=Rydberg constant, \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n_1<n_2\)=energy levels.

subject: Chemistry
title: Energy nth Orbit (Numerical)
description: Standard plug-in form of Bohr energy for H-like species. \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n\)=orbit number; \(-13.6\) eV is the ground-state energy of hydrogen (per atom).

subject: Chemistry
title: Energy per Mole (H-like)
description: Bohr orbit energy expressed per mole of atoms. \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n\)=orbit number; \(1312\) kJ/mol is hydrogen ionization energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lyman / Balmer Series Range
description: Lower level for hydrogen spectral series. \(n_1\)=final level: Lyman (1, UV), Balmer (2, visible), Paschen (3), Brackett (4), Pfund (5), all IR.

subject: Chemistry
title: de Broglie (Thermal)
description: Wavelength from kinetic energy / temperature. \(h\)=Planck constant, \(m\)=mass, \(KE\)=kinetic energy, \(k\)=Boltzmann constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Subshells in Shell
description: The nth principal shell contains exactly \(n\) subshells. \(n\)=principal quantum number (e.g. n=3 has s, p, d).

subject: Chemistry
title: Wavelength of Spectral Line (H)
description: Direct wavelength of an emitted line. \(R_H\)=Rydberg constant, \(Z\)=atomic number, \(n_1<n_2\)=levels; rearrangement of the Rydberg equation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Rate of Reaction
description: Normalized rate for $aA \rightarrow bB$.
derivation:
Rate is change in concentration per unit time.
Since stoichiometry differs ($a$ moles of A disappear for $b$ moles of B to form), we divide by the coefficient to get a unique rate for the reaction.
Reactants decrease (-ve), Products increase (+ve).

related_concepts.name: Instantaneous Rate
related_concepts.definition: The rate at a specific moment in time ($slope$ of tangent to conc-time curve).

subject: Chemistry
title: Rate Law
description: Experimental relation between rate and concentration.
derivation:
This is an empirical law determined experimentally, not from stoichiometry.
$k$ is the specific rate constant.
$x$ and $y$ are reaction orders with respect to reactants A and B.
Overall order = $x + y$.

related_concepts.name: Order of Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Sum of powers of concentration terms in the rate law expression.

subject: Chemistry
title: Zero Order Integration
description: Concentration vs Time for Zero Order.
derivation:
Rate Law: $-d[A]/dt = k[A]^0 = k$.
$d[A] = -k dt$.
Integrate from $t=0$ ($[A]_0$) to $t$ ($[A]_t$):
$\int_{[A]_0}^{[A]_t} d[A] = -k \int_0^t dt$.
$[A]_t - [A]_0 = -kt$.

related_concepts.name: Linear Decay
related_concepts.definition: For zero order, the concentration decreases at a constant rate independent of concentration.

subject: Chemistry
title: First Order Integration
description: Exponential decay of concentration.
derivation:
Rate Law: $-d[A]/dt = k[A]^1$.
Separate variables: $d[A]/[A] = -k dt$.
Integrate:
$\int \frac{1}{[A]} d[A] = -k \int dt$.
$\ln [A]_t - \ln [A]_0 = -kt$.
$\ln([A]_t/[A]_0) = -kt \implies [A]_t = [A]_0 e^{-kt}$.

related_concepts.name: Natural Log Plot
related_concepts.definition: A plot of $\ln[A]$ vs $t$ gives a straight line with slope $-k$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Second Order Integration
description: Inverse concentration vs Time.
derivation:
Rate Law: $-d[A]/dt = k[A]^2$.
Separate variables: $-[A]^{-2} d[A] = k dt$.
Integrate ($ \int -x^{-2} dx = x^{-1} $):
$[ \frac{1}{[A]} ]_{[A]_0}^{[A]_t} = kt$.
$\frac{1}{[A]_t} - \frac{1}{[A]_0} = kt$.

related_concepts.name: Elementary Reaction
related_concepts.definition: A reaction that occurs in a single step ($2A \to P$ follows 2nd order kinetics).

subject: Chemistry
title: Half-Life (Zero Order)
description: Time for conc to drop to half.

related_concepts.name: Concentration Dependence
related_concepts.definition: Unlike 1st order, zero order half-life decreases as concentration decreases.

subject: Chemistry
title: Half-Life (First Order)
description: Constant half-life.

related_concepts.name: Radioactivity
related_concepts.definition: Nuclear decay follows first-order kinetics; half-life is a characteristic constant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Arrhenius (Two Temps)
description: Calculating Activation Energy.
derivation:
Take natural log of Arrhenius Eq: $\ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT}$.
Write for $T_1$: $\ln k_1 = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT_1}$.
Write for $T_2$: $\ln k_2 = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{RT_2}$.
Subtract (2) - (1):
$\ln k_2 - \ln k_1 = -\frac{E_a}{R} (\frac{1}{T_2} - \frac{1}{T_1}) = \frac{E_a}{R} (\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2})$.

related_concepts.name: Temperature Coefficient
related_concepts.definition: Ratio of rate constants at temperatures differing by 10°C (usually 2 to 3).

subject: Chemistry
title: Arrhenius Equation
description: Relationship between rate constant (k), activation energy (Ea), and temperature (T).
derivation:
1. Kinetic Energy: Fraction of molecules with energy \(\ge E_a\) is proportional to \(e^{-E_a/RT}\) (Boltzmann Factor).
2. Frequency Factor (A): Represents collision frequency and orientation probability.
3. Linear Form: \(\ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{R} \left(\frac{1}{T}\right)\).
   Slope of \(\ln k\) vs \(1/T\) graph is \(-E_a/R\).

related_concepts.name: Activation Energy
related_concepts.definition: Minimum energy required for reactants to form the activated complex.

subject: Chemistry
title: Pseudo First Order
description: Reaction appearing 1st order because reactant B is in large excess.
derivation:
True Rate Law: Rate = $k[A][B]$.
If $[B] \gg [A]$, concentration of B remains effectively constant ($[B] \approx [B]_0$).
Combine constants: $k' = k[B]_0$.
New Rate Law: Rate = $k'[A]$.
Example: Hydrolysis of ester in excess water.

related_concepts.name: Inversion of Cane Sugar
related_concepts.definition: A classic pseudo-first order reaction: Sucrose + Water -> Glucose + Fructose.

subject: Chemistry
title: Collision Frequency (Z)
description: Number of collisions per unit volume per second.
derivation:
From Kinetic Theory of Gases.
$Z$ depends on:
1. Collision Cross-section ($\sigma$): Size of molecules.
2. Average Velocity ($v_{avg} \propto \sqrt{T/\mu}$).
3. Number density ($N_A, N_B$).
Rate = $Z_{AB} \times e^{-E_a/RT} \times \rho$ (Steric Factor).

related_concepts.name: Steric Factor (P)
related_concepts.definition: Accounts for proper orientation requirement in collisions. Rate = $P Z e^{-Ea/RT}$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Parallel First Order Reaction
description: Reactant A forms B (k1) and C (k2) simultaneously.
derivation:
Rate Law:
$-\frac{d[A]}{dt} = k_1[A] + k_2[A] = (k_1 + k_2)[A]$
Integrated form: $[A] = [A]_0 e^{-(k_1+k_2)t}$
Product Ratio: $[B]/[C] = k_1/k_2$
Activation Energy: $E_{eff} = \frac{k_1 E_1 + k_2 E_2}{k_1 + k_2}$.

related_concepts.name: Selectivity
related_concepts.definition: The ratio of desired product rate constant to side reaction rate constants.

subject: Chemistry
title: Steady State Approximation
description: Assumption for reaction mechanisms involving unstable intermediates.
derivation:
Logic:
1. Intermediate (I) is very reactive.
2. Its concentration remains low and constant throughout the main reaction.
3. Rate of Formation of I = Rate of Consumption of I.
Used to derive Rate Laws for complex multi-step reactions.

related_concepts.name: Rate Determining Step (RDS)
related_concepts.definition: The slowest step in a reaction mechanism that governs the overall rate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Half-Life (Second Order)
description: Half-life of a second order reaction (inversely proportional to initial conc). \(k\)=rate constant, \([A]_0\)=initial concentration.

subject: Chemistry
title: Half-Life vs Order (General)
description: Dependence of half-life on initial conc for an n-th order reaction; used to find order from half-life data. \(n\)=order, \([A]_0\)=initial concentration.

subject: Chemistry
title: First Order (Log Form)
description: Working log form of the first order rate constant (most-used in numericals). \(k\)=rate constant, \(t\)=time, \([A]_0\)=initial conc, \([A]_t\)=conc at time \(t\).

subject: Chemistry
title: First Order (Gas, Pressure)
description: First order rate constant for a gas reaction \(A \rightarrow\) products via total pressure (where 1 mol gives n mol; here n=2 type). \(P_0\)=initial pressure, \(P_t\)=total pressure at time \(t\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Time for nth Half-Life (1st Order)
description: Fraction of reactant left after n half-lives for any first order reaction. \(n\)=number of half-lives, \([A]_0\)=initial conc, \(t_{1/2}\)=half-life.

subject: Chemistry
title: Average Rate vs Instantaneous
description: Average rate over an interval vs instantaneous rate at an instant. \(\Delta[A]\)=conc change, \(\Delta t\)=time interval, \(d[A]/dt\)=derivative at instant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Temperature Coefficient
description: Factor by which rate increases per 10 K rise (typically 2-3 near room temp). \(\mu\)=temperature coefficient, \(k_T\)=rate constant at \(T\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Arrhenius (Log Form)
description: Linear (log) form of Arrhenius equation; slope of \(\log k\) vs \(1/T\) gives \(E_a\). \(A\)=frequency factor, \(E_a\)=activation energy, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Arrhenius Slope
description: Slope of the \(\log k\) vs \(1/T\) straight-line plot, used to extract activation energy. \(E_a\)=activation energy, \(R\)=gas constant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Activation Energy & Enthalpy
description: Reaction enthalpy as difference of forward and backward activation energies. \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(E_{a,f}\)=forward \(E_a\), \(E_{a,b}\)=backward \(E_a\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Threshold Energy
description: Minimum energy colliding molecules must possess to react. \(E_a\)=activation energy, \(E_{reactants}\)=average energy of reactants.

subject: Chemistry
title: Collision Theory Rate Constant
description: Rate constant from collision theory including steric/probability factor. \(P\)=steric factor, \(Z\)=collision frequency, \(E_a\)=activation energy, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fraction of Effective Molecules
description: Fraction of molecules with energy \(\ge E_a\) (effective collisions). \(E_a\)=activation energy, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Zero Order Half-Life vs Completion
description: Time for a zero order reaction to go to completion (twice its half-life). \([A]_0\)=initial conc, \(k\)=rate constant, \(t_{1/2}\)=half-life.

subject: Chemistry
title: Units of Rate Constant
description: General units of the rate constant for an n-th order reaction. \(n\)=overall order of reaction.

subject: Chemistry
title: First Order (Fraction Reacted)
description: First order rate constant in terms of fraction \(x\) reacted. \(t\)=time, \(x\)=fraction of reactant converted.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acid Hydrolysis (Optical Rotation)
description: First order k for sucrose inversion / ester hydrolysis tracked by polarimeter. \(r_0\)=initial rotation, \(r_t\)=rotation at time \(t\), \(r_\infty\)=rotation at completion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Catalyst Effect (Lowered Ea)
description: Factor by which rate constant rises when a catalyst lowers activation energy at the same temperature. \(k_{cat}\)=catalysed rate constant, \(k_{uncat}\)=uncatalysed, \(E_a\)=uncatalysed activation energy, \(E_a'\)=catalysed (lower), \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.
derivation:
Arrhenius with same \(A\): \(k_{uncat} = A e^{-E_a/RT}\), \(k_{cat} = A e^{-E_a'/RT}\).
Dividing: \(\frac{k_{cat}}{k_{uncat}} = e^{(E_a - E_a')/RT}\).
Since \(E_a' < E_a\), exponent is positive \(\Rightarrow\) rate increases.

subject: Chemistry
title: Arrhenius Frequency Factor
description: Natural-log Arrhenius form used to extract \(A\) and \(E_a\) from a \(\ln k\) vs \(1/T\) plot. \(k\)=rate constant, \(A\)=frequency (pre-exponential) factor, \(E_a\)=activation energy, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature; intercept \(=\ln A\), slope \(=-E_a/R\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Activation Energy from Two Rate Constants
description: Activation energy from rate constants at two temperatures (rearranged Arrhenius). \(E_a\)=activation energy, \(k_1, k_2\)=rate constants at \(T_1, T_2\), \(R\)=gas constant.

subject: Chemistry
title: nth Order Integrated Rate Law
description: General integrated rate law for order \(n \neq 1\). \([A]_t\)=concentration at time \(t\), \([A]_0\)=initial concentration, \(n\)=order, \(k\)=rate constant, \(t\)=time.

subject: Chemistry
title: Half-Life Ratio Method (Order)
description: Order of reaction from two half-lives at two initial concentrations. \(n\)=order, \(t_{1/2,1}, t_{1/2,2}\)=half-lives, \([A]_{0,1}, [A]_{0,2}\)=corresponding initial concentrations.

subject: Chemistry
title: Initial Rate Method (Order)
description: Determines order with respect to A by comparing initial rates at two concentrations (others fixed). \(x\)=order in A, \(r_1, r_2\)=initial rates, \([A]_1, [A]_2\)=initial concentrations of A.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fraction Remaining (First Order)
description: Fraction of reactant left after time \(t\) for first-order kinetics. \([A]_t\)=concentration left, \([A]_0\)=initial, \(k\)=rate constant, \(t_{1/2}\)=half-life, \(t\)=elapsed time.

subject: Chemistry
title: Overall Order from Rate Law
description: Overall order is the sum of partial orders in the rate law \(\text{Rate} = k[A]^x[B]^y\). \(n\)=overall order, \(x\)=order in A, \(y\)=order in B (need not match stoichiometric coefficients).

subject: Chemistry
title: Time for 99.9% Completion (1st Order)
description: Time for a first-order reaction to reach 99.9% completion equals ten half-lives. \(k\)=rate constant, \(t_{1/2}\)=half-life.

subject: Chemistry
title: First Law (Chemistry)
description: Conservation of Energy (IUPAC Sign Convention).
derivation:
Internal Energy $U$ is a state function.
Change $\Delta U$ equals energy transferred TO the system.
$q$: Heat absorbed BY system (+).
$w$: Work done ON system (+).
Note: Physics often uses $w$ as work BY system (-).

related_concepts.name: State Function
related_concepts.definition: Property depending only on initial and final states, not the path (e.g., U, H, S).

subject: Chemistry
title: Work (Irreversible)
description: Work done against constant external pressure.
derivation:
Work = Force $\times$ Distance.
$F = P_{ext} A$.
$w = - F \Delta x$ (Negative because expansion $\Delta V > 0$ means system loses energy).
$w = - (P_{ext} A) \Delta x = -P_{ext} (A \Delta x)$.
$w = -P_{ext} \Delta V$.

related_concepts.name: Free Expansion
related_concepts.definition: Expansion into a vacuum ($P_{ext}=0$), so work done is zero ($w=0$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Work Done (Reversible Isothermal)
description: Maximum work done during the reversible expansion of an ideal gas. \(n\): moles, \(T\): temperature [K].
derivation:
Work is defined as the integral of external pressure over volume:
\(dw = -P_{ext} dV\)
For a reversible process, \(P_{ext} \approx P_{gas}\).
Using the Ideal Gas Law: \(P = nRT / V\).
Substituting into the integral:
\(w = -\int_{V_1}^{V_2} \frac{nRT}{V} dV\)
Since \(T\) is constant (Isothermal), we integrate \(1/V\):
\(w = -nRT [\ln V]_{V_1}^{V_2}\)
\(w = -nRT \ln(V_2/V_1)\)

related_concepts.name: Reversible Process
related_concepts.definition: A process carried out infinitely slowly so the system remains in equilibrium at every step.

related_concepts.name: Ideal Gas Law
related_concepts.definition: The equation of state \(PV=nRT\) for a hypothetical gas.

subject: Chemistry
title: Adiabatic Relation (Ideal Gas)
description: State variable relationship for reversible adiabatic processes. \(\gamma = C_p / C_v\) (Poisson's ratio).
derivation:
From the First Law of Thermodynamics, for adiabatic process (\(q=0\)):
\(dU = dw\)
Substitute definitions: \(nC_v dT = -P dV\)
Use Ideal Gas Law for P: \(P = nRT/V\)
\(nC_v dT = -\frac{nRT}{V} dV\)
Rearrange variables: \(\frac{dT}{T} = -\frac{R}{C_v} \frac{dV}{V}\)
Since \(R/C_v = \gamma - 1\), integrating both sides yields:
\(\ln T = -(\gamma-1) \ln V + C\)
\(TV^{\gamma-1} = \text{const}\)

related_concepts.name: Adiabatic Process
related_concepts.definition: A process where no heat is exchanged with the surroundings (\(q=0\)).

related_concepts.name: Heat Capacity Ratio
related_concepts.definition: The ratio \(\gamma = C_p/C_v\), always greater than 1.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy Definition
description: Total heat content of a system at constant pressure. \(\Delta H = q_p\).
derivation:
We define Enthalpy (H) to simplify constant-pressure energy calculations.
Definition: \(H = U + PV\)
Change in Enthalpy: \(\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta(PV)\)
At constant Pressure (\(P\)):
\(\Delta H = \Delta U + P\Delta V\)
From First Law (\(\Delta U = q + w\)) and expansion work (\(w = -P\Delta V\)):
\(\Delta H = (q_p - P\Delta V) + P\Delta V\)
\(\Delta H = q_p\)

related_concepts.name: Internal Energy (U)
related_concepts.definition: The total kinetic and potential energy of the particles within a system.

related_concepts.name: State Function
related_concepts.definition: A property whose value does not depend on the path taken to reach that specific value.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mayer's Relation
description: Relationship between molar heat capacities for 1 mole of an ideal gas. \(R\): universal gas constant.
derivation:
Start with Enthalpy definition for 1 mole:
\(H = U + PV\)
Since \(PV = RT\) for 1 mole:
\(H = U + RT\)
Differentiate with respect to Temperature (T):
\(\frac{dH}{dT} = \frac{dU}{dT} + \frac{d(RT)}{dT}\)
Substitute heat capacity definitions (\(C_p = dH/dT\) and \(C_v = dU/dT\)):
\(C_p = C_v + R\)
\(C_p - C_v = R\)

related_concepts.name: Molar Heat Capacity
related_concepts.definition: The amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of 1 mole of substance by 1 Kelvin.

subject: Chemistry
title: Entropy Change (Definition)
description: Thermodynamic definition of entropy change. Measure of molecular disorder.
derivation:
Clausius defined entropy change based on reversible heat transfer.
For an infinitesimal process:
\(dS = \frac{dq_{rev}}{T}\)
For a finite change from state 1 to 2:
\(\Delta S = \int_{1}^{2} \frac{dq_{rev}}{T}\)
This implies that for an adiabatic reversible process (\(dq=0\)), \(\Delta S = 0\).

related_concepts.name: Second Law of Thermodynamics
related_concepts.definition: Total entropy of an isolated system can never decrease over time.

subject: Chemistry
title: Entropy Change (Ideal Gas)
description: General formula for system entropy change during ideal gas expansion/compression.
derivation:
Start with First Law: \(dq_{rev} = dU - dw_{rev}\)
\(dq_{rev} = nC_v dT + P dV\)
Divide by T to find dS:
\(dS = \frac{dq_{rev}}{T} = nC_v \frac{dT}{T} + \frac{P}{T} dV\)
Substitute \(P/T = nR/V\) (Ideal Gas):
\(dS = nC_v \frac{dT}{T} + nR \frac{dV}{V}\)
Integrate from state 1 to 2:
\(\Delta S = nC_v \ln(T_2/T_1) + nR \ln(V_2/V_1)\)

related_concepts.name: Expansion Entropy
related_concepts.definition: Entropy increases as volume increases (disorder increases with more space).

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs Free Energy
description: Thermodynamic potential that predicts spontaneity at constant T and P. \(\Delta G < 0\) is spontaneous.
derivation:
To predict spontaneity for system conditions (const T, P), we introduce G.
Definition:
\(G = H - TS\)
Differentiating:
\(dG = dH - TdS - SdT\)
At constant temperature (\(dT=0\)):
\(dG = dH - TdS\)
This combines the energy factor (H) and entropy factor (S).

related_concepts.name: Spontaneity
related_concepts.definition: The inherent tendency of a process to occur without external work.

related_concepts.name: Exergonic Reaction
related_concepts.definition: A reaction where \(\Delta G\) is negative (releases free energy).

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs-Helmholtz Equation
description: Calculates free energy change from enthalpy and entropy changes at constant T.
derivation:
For a finite change at constant temperature:
Start with \(G = H - TS\)
\(\Delta G = \Delta(H - TS)\)
\(\Delta G = \Delta H - \Delta(TS)\)
Since T is constant:
\(\Delta G = \Delta H - T \Delta S\)
This equation determines if enthalpy or entropy dominates the spontaneity.

related_concepts.name: Entropy Driven
related_concepts.definition: A process where \(T\Delta S\) is the dominant term making \(\Delta G\) negative.

subject: Chemistry
title: Standard Free Energy & Equilibrium
description: Relates standard thermodynamics to the equilibrium constant \(K_{eq}\).
derivation:
The relationship between free energy and the reaction quotient Q is:
\(\Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln Q\)
At equilibrium, the system does no work, so \(\Delta G = 0\).
Also at equilibrium, \(Q\) becomes \(K_{eq}\).
Substituting:
\(0 = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln K_{eq}\)
\(\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K_{eq}\)

related_concepts.name: Equilibrium Constant
related_concepts.definition: The value of the reaction quotient when the reaction has reached equilibrium.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carnot Engine Efficiency
description: Maximum theoretical efficiency of a heat engine. Temperatures must be in Kelvin.
derivation:
Efficiency (\(\eta\)) is work output divided by heat input.
\(\eta = \frac{W}{Q_{hot}} = \frac{Q_{hot} - Q_{cold}}{Q_{hot}} = 1 - \frac{Q_{cold}}{Q_{hot}}\)
For a Carnot (reversible) cycle, heat is proportional to temperature (\(Q \propto T\)).
Therefore:
\(\eta = 1 - \frac{T_{cold}}{T_{hot}}\)

related_concepts.name: Carnot Cycle
related_concepts.definition: An ideal thermodynamic cycle consisting of two isothermal and two adiabatic processes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hess's Law
description: Enthalpy change is independent of the path taken.
derivation:
Since Enthalpy (H) is a State Function:
Path A: $Reactants \rightarrow Products$ ($\Delta H$)
Path B: $Reactants \rightarrow Intermediate \rightarrow Products$ ($\Delta H_1 + \Delta H_2$)
According to conservation of energy:
$\Delta H = \Delta H_1 + \Delta H_2$

related_concepts.name: State Function
related_concepts.definition: A property whose value does not depend on the path taken to reach that specific value.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bond Enthalpy Reaction
description: Calculating reaction enthalpy using bond energies.
derivation:
Chemical reaction involves breaking old bonds and forming new ones.
1. Energy absorbed to break reactant bonds: $+\sum BE_R$
2. Energy released to form product bonds: $-\sum BE_P$
Net Enthalpy: $\Delta H = \text{Energy absorbed} - \text{Energy released}$

related_concepts.name: Resonance Energy
related_concepts.definition: Difference between observed bond energy and theoretical bond energy calculated for a canonical structure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Clausius-Clapeyron Equation
description: Relates vapor pressure of a liquid to temperature.
derivation:
Starts from phase equilibrium condition $\Delta G = 0$.
Assume vapor behaves as Ideal Gas and molar volume of liquid is negligible.
$\frac{d \ln P}{dT} = \frac{\Delta H_{vap}}{RT^2}$.
Integrate between limits $(P_1, T_1)$ and $(P_2, T_2)$.

related_concepts.name: Boiling Point
related_concepts.definition: Temperature where vapor pressure equals external atmospheric pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kirchhoff's Law (Thermochemistry)
description: Variation of enthalpy of reaction with temperature.
derivation:
Heat capacity $C_p = (\partial H / \partial T)_P$.
For a reaction: $\Delta C_p = \sum (C_p)_{products} - \sum (C_p)_{reactants}$.
$\frac{d(\Delta H)}{dT} = \Delta C_p$.
Integrate: $\int_{\Delta H_1}^{\Delta H_2} d(\Delta H) = \int_{T_1}^{T_2} \Delta C_p dT$.
Assuming $\Delta C_p$ is constant over small T range: $\Delta H_2 = \Delta H_1 + \Delta C_p \Delta T$.

related_concepts.name: Heat Capacity
related_concepts.definition: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of a system by 1 degree.

subject: Chemistry
title: Born-Haber Cycle
description: Cycle to calculate Lattice Energy (U) of an ionic solid.
derivation:
Hess's Law application for formation of $MX(s)$:
1. Sublimation of Metal: $M(s) \to M(g)$ ($S$).
2. Ionization: $M(g) \to M^+(g)$ ($IE$).
3. Dissociation of Non-metal: $\frac{1}{2}X_2(g) \to X(g)$ ($\frac{1}{2}D$).
4. Electron Gain: $X(g) \to X^-(g)$ ($-EA$).
5. Lattice Formation: $M^+ + X^- \to MX(s)$ ($-U$).
Sum equals Enthalpy of Formation $\Delta H_f$.

related_concepts.name: Lattice Energy
related_concepts.definition: Energy released when one mole of ionic solid is formed from gaseous ions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy Change at Constant Pressure
description: Heat absorbed at constant pressure equals enthalpy change. \(q_p\)=heat at const. pressure, \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(P\)=pressure, \(\Delta V\)=volume change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Heat at Constant Volume
description: At constant volume work is zero, so heat absorbed equals internal energy change. \(q_v\)=heat at const. volume, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Relation between \(\Delta H\) and \(\Delta U\)
description: Links enthalpy and internal energy change for gaseous reactions. \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(\Delta n_g\)=moles of gaseous products minus reactants, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Heat Capacity Relation
description: Heat needed to change temperature. \(q\)=heat, \(n\)=moles, \(C\)=molar heat capacity, \(m\)=mass, \(c\)=specific heat, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molar Heat Capacities (Ideal Gas)
description: Heat capacities and adiabatic index from degrees of freedom. \(C_v\)=molar heat capacity at const. volume, \(C_p\)=at const. pressure, \(f\)=degrees of freedom (3 monatomic, 5 diatomic), \(R\)=gas constant, \(\gamma\)=heat capacity ratio.

subject: Chemistry
title: Internal Energy Change (Ideal Gas)
description: Internal energy change of an ideal gas depends only on temperature (valid for all processes). \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_v\)=molar heat capacity at const. volume, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy Change (Ideal Gas)
description: Enthalpy change of an ideal gas depends only on temperature (valid for all processes). \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_p\)=molar heat capacity at const. pressure, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Isothermal Process (Ideal Gas)
description: For an ideal gas at constant temperature, energy/enthalpy unchanged so all heat converts to work. \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(q\)=heat, \(w\)=work, \(n\)=moles, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature, \(V\)=volume.

subject: Chemistry
title: Adiabatic Process Work
visual_data: w = \Delta U = nC_v(T_2 - T_1) = \frac{P_2 V_2 - P_1 V_1}{\gamma - 1}
description: Work in an adiabatic process (q=0) equals internal energy change. \(w\)=work done on gas, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_v\)=molar heat capacity at const. volume, \(T\)=temperature, \(P\)=pressure, \(V\)=volume, \(\gamma\)=heat capacity ratio.

subject: Chemistry
title: Isochoric Process
description: At constant volume no work is done; all heat changes internal energy. \(w\)=work, \(q_v\)=heat at const. volume, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_v\)=molar heat capacity at const. volume, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Isobaric Process
visual_data: w = -P\Delta V = -nR\Delta T, \quad q_p = \Delta H = nC_p\Delta T
description: At constant pressure, work relates to volume change and heat equals enthalpy change. \(w\)=work, \(P\)=pressure, \(\Delta V\)=volume change, \(n\)=moles, \(R\)=gas constant, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change, \(q_p\)=heat at const. pressure, \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(C_p\)=molar heat capacity at const. pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Free Expansion (Ideal Gas)
description: Expansion into vacuum (\(P_{ext}=0\)) for an ideal gas: no work, no heat, no temperature change. \(q\)=heat, \(w\)=work, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(\Delta T\)=temperature change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Entropy Change (Phase Transition)
description: Entropy change for a reversible phase change at constant T (fusion, vaporization). \(\Delta S\)=entropy change, \(\Delta H_{trans}\)=enthalpy of transition, \(T\)=transition temperature (K).

subject: Chemistry
title: Entropy Change (Ideal Gas, T & P)
description: Entropy change of an ideal gas in terms of temperature and pressure. \(\Delta S\)=entropy change, \(n\)=moles, \(C_p\)=molar heat capacity at const. pressure, \(T\)=temperature, \(R\)=gas constant, \(P\)=pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Entropy Change of Surroundings
description: Entropy change of surroundings from heat exchanged at constant T and P. \(\Delta S_{surr}\)=entropy change of surroundings, \(\Delta H_{sys}\)=enthalpy change of system, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Second Law (Spontaneity Criterion)
description: Total entropy of universe increases for a spontaneous process; equals zero at equilibrium. \(\Delta S_{total}\)=total entropy change (universe), \(\Delta S_{sys}\)=system entropy change, \(\Delta S_{surr}\)=surroundings entropy change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs Energy & Spontaneity
description: Sign of Gibbs free energy change decides spontaneity at constant T, P. \(\Delta G\)=Gibbs free energy change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Maximum Non-Expansion Work
description: Gibbs energy change equals the maximum useful (non-PV) work obtainable at constant T and P. \(\Delta G\)=Gibbs free energy change, \(w_{non-exp,max}\)=maximum non-expansion (useful) work.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs Energy & Non-Standard Q
description: Gibbs energy change at any reaction state in terms of reaction quotient. \(\Delta G\)=Gibbs energy change, \(\Delta G^\circ\)=standard Gibbs energy change, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature, \(Q\)=reaction quotient.

subject: Chemistry
title: Temperature for Spontaneity
description: Crossover temperature at which \(\Delta G=0\); determines T-range of spontaneity for reactions with \(\Delta H,\Delta S\) of same sign. \(T\)=temperature, \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(\Delta S\)=entropy change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Standard Enthalpy of Reaction (Formation)
description: Reaction enthalpy from standard formation enthalpies. \(\Delta_r H^\circ\)=standard reaction enthalpy, \(\Delta_f H^\circ\)=standard enthalpy of formation, \(\nu_p,\nu_r\)=stoichiometric coefficients of products/reactants.

subject: Chemistry
title: Standard Entropy of Reaction
description: Reaction entropy from standard molar (absolute) entropies, via Third Law. \(\Delta_r S^\circ\)=standard reaction entropy, \(S^\circ\)=standard molar entropy, \(\nu_p,\nu_r\)=stoichiometric coefficients of products/reactants.

subject: Chemistry
title: van't Hoff Equation
description: Temperature dependence of the equilibrium constant. \(K\)=equilibrium constant, \(\Delta H^\circ\)=standard reaction enthalpy, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Trouton's Rule
description: Entropy of vaporization at normal boiling point is roughly constant for many liquids. \(\Delta S_{vap}\)=entropy of vaporization, \(\Delta H_{vap}\)=enthalpy of vaporization, \(T_b\)=normal boiling point (K).

subject: Chemistry
title: Integrated Enthalpy of Solution
description: Enthalpy of dissolution of an ionic solid splits into lattice and hydration terms. \(\Delta_{sol}H^\circ\)=enthalpy of solution, \(\Delta_{lattice}H^\circ\)=lattice enthalpy (for dissociation), \(\Delta_{hyd}H^\circ\)=hydration enthalpy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy of Neutralization
description: Heat released when 1 g-equivalent of acid is neutralized by base, forming 1 mol water. For strong acid + strong base it is constant \(\approx -57.1\) kJ/mol (just \(H^+ + OH^- \rightarrow H_2O\)); for weak acid/base it is less negative because ionization enthalpy is absorbed. \(\Delta_{neut}H^\circ\)=enthalpy of neutralization.

subject: Chemistry
title: van't Hoff Reaction Isotherm
description: Links standard free energy to the equilibrium constant; sign of \(\Delta G^\circ\) decides whether \(K>1\) or \(K<1\). \(\Delta G^\circ\)=standard Gibbs energy change, \(R\)=8.314 J/K/mol, \(T\)=temperature (K), \(K\)=equilibrium constant. \(\Delta G^\circ<0 \Rightarrow K>1\) (products favoured); \(\Delta G^\circ>0 \Rightarrow K<1\).
derivation:
At equilibrium \(Q=K\) and \(\Delta G=0\).
From \(\Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln Q\):
\(0 = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln K\)
\(\Rightarrow \Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy of Atomization
description: Enthalpy to break 1 mole of a substance completely into gaseous atoms (always endothermic). For a diatomic gas it equals the bond dissociation enthalpy. \(\Delta_a H^\circ\)=standard enthalpy of atomization.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy of Sublimation
description: Enthalpy to convert 1 mole of solid directly to vapour at constant T,P (a state function, so equals fusion plus vaporization). \(\Delta_{sub}H^\circ\)=sublimation, \(\Delta_{fus}H^\circ\)=fusion, \(\Delta_{vap}H^\circ\)=vaporization enthalpies.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ionization Enthalpy
description: Enthalpy to remove 1 mole of electrons from 1 mole of gaseous atoms/ions (always endothermic; successive values increase). \(\Delta_i H\)=ionization enthalpy, \(M(g)\)=gaseous atom.

subject: Chemistry
title: Electron Gain Enthalpy
description: Enthalpy change when 1 mole of gaseous atoms gains 1 mole of electrons; usually negative (energy released), but positive for noble gases/half-filled stable configs. \(\Delta_{eg}H\)=electron gain enthalpy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydration Enthalpy
description: Enthalpy released when 1 mole of gaseous ions is dissolved in a large amount of water (exothermic). \(\Delta_{hyd}H^\circ\)=hydration enthalpy; combines with lattice enthalpy to give enthalpy of solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bomb to Reaction Enthalpy
visual_data: \Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT, \quad \Delta n_g = n_{g,products} - n_{g,reactants}
description: Converts the constant-volume heat (\(\Delta U\)) measured in a bomb calorimeter to the constant-pressure enthalpy of reaction. \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(\Delta U\)=internal energy change, \(\Delta n_g\)=change in gaseous moles, \(R\)=8.314 J/K/mol, \(T\)=temperature (K).

subject: Chemistry
title: Kp and Kc Relation
description: Relationship between equilibrium constants. \(\Delta n_g\): moles gaseous products - reactants.
derivation:
Ideal Gas Law: \(P = (n/V)RT = CRT\).
For reaction \(aA \rightleftharpoons bB\):
\(K_p = \frac{(P_B)^b}{(P_A)^a} = \frac{([B]RT)^b}{([A]RT)^a}\)
Factor out concentrations and RT:
\(K_p = \frac{[B]^b}{[A]^a} (RT)^{b-a}\)
Since \(K_c = \frac{[B]^b}{[A]^a}\) and \(\Delta n_g = b-a\):
\(K_p = K_c (RT)^{\Delta n_g}\)

related_concepts.name: Partial Pressure
related_concepts.definition: The pressure hypothetically exerted if this gas alone occupied the entire volume.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reaction Quotient (Q)
description: Predicts reaction direction. \(Q < K\): forward, \(Q > K\): backward.
derivation:
The expression for Q is identical to the Equilibrium Constant K.
However, K uses concentrations *at equilibrium*.
Q uses concentrations at *any specific instant* in time.
Comparison:
If \(Q < K\), numerator (products) is too small \(\rightarrow\) Shift Right.
If \(Q > K\), numerator is too large \(\rightarrow\) Shift Left.

related_concepts.name: Le Chatelier's Principle
related_concepts.definition: If a constraint is applied to a system in equilibrium, the equilibrium shifts to counteract it.

subject: Chemistry
title: Law of Mass Action (Kc)
description: Equilibrium constant in terms of molar concentrations. \([X]\)=equilibrium molar concentration of \(X\); \(a,b,c,d\)=stoichiometric coefficients; \(K_c\)=concentration equilibrium constant.

related_concepts.name: Pure solids & liquids
related_concepts.definition: Activities of pure solids and pure liquids are taken as 1, so they are omitted from the $K_c$ expression.

related_concepts.name: Unit of Kc
related_concepts.definition: $(\text{mol L}^{-1})^{\Delta n}$ where $\Delta n = (c+d)-(a+b)$; dimensionless only if $\Delta n = 0$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Equilibrium Constant in Pressures (Kp)
description: Equilibrium constant for gaseous reactions using partial pressures. \(p_X\)=equilibrium partial pressure of gas \(X\); exponents are stoichiometric coefficients.

subject: Chemistry
title: Partial Pressure (Mole Fraction)
description: Relates partial pressure to mole fraction (Dalton's law), used to convert Kp problems. \(p_X\)=partial pressure, \(x_X\)=mole fraction, \(n_X\)=moles of \(X\), \(P_{total}\)=total pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kp vs Kx (Mole Fraction)
description: Links pressure constant to mole-fraction constant. \(K_x\)=equilibrium constant in mole fractions, \(P\)=total pressure, \(\Delta n_g\)=moles gaseous products − reactants.

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Dissociation
description: Fraction of reactant dissociated at equilibrium. \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation \((0 \le \alpha \le 1)\); often expressed as a percentage \(\times 100\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Dissociation: Kp vs α (A ⇌ 2B)
description: Kp for a 1→2 dissociation (e.g. \(N_2O_4 \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2\)). \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation, \(P\)=total pressure at equilibrium.
derivation:
Start: 1 mol A, dissociated \(\alpha\) gives \(2\alpha\) mol B; total \(= 1+\alpha\).
Mole fractions: \(x_A = \frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}\), \(x_B = \frac{2\alpha}{1+\alpha}\).
\(K_p = \frac{(x_B P)^2}{x_A P} = \frac{(2\alpha)^2 P}{(1-\alpha)(1+\alpha)}\).
\(K_p = \frac{4\alpha^2 P}{1-\alpha^2}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Small α Approximation
description: Quick estimate of dissociation for \(A \rightleftharpoons 2B\) when dissociation is small. \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation, \(K_p\)=pressure constant, \(P\)=total pressure. Shows \(\alpha \propto 1/\sqrt{P}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Vapour Density & Dissociation
description: Finds degree of dissociation from vapour density change. \(D\)=theoretical (initial) vapour density, \(d\)=observed vapour density at equilibrium, \(n\)=moles of gas produced per mole reactant.

related_concepts.name: Abnormal molar mass
related_concepts.definition: On dissociation observed molar mass $M_{obs} = 2d$ falls below theoretical $M = 2D$; $\frac{M}{M_{obs}} = 1 + (n-1)\alpha$.

subject: Chemistry
title: K of Reversed Reaction
description: Equilibrium constant of the reverse reaction. \(K\)=constant of forward reaction, \(K'\)=constant when the equation is reversed.

subject: Chemistry
title: K on Scaling Coefficients
description: Effect of multiplying a balanced equation by factor \(n\). \(K\)=original constant, \(n\)=multiplying factor (e.g. halving gives \(K^{1/2}\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: K of Added Reactions
description: When two reactions are added, their equilibrium constants multiply. \(K_1, K_2\)=constants of the individual steps, \(K_{net}\)=constant of the overall reaction.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs Energy & Reaction Quotient
description: Free energy change at any instant; predicts spontaneity and equilibrium. \(\Delta G\)=actual free energy change, \(\Delta G^\circ\)=standard value, \(Q\)=reaction quotient. At equilibrium \(\Delta G = 0\) and \(Q = K\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Van't Hoff Equation
description: Temperature dependence of the equilibrium constant. \(K_1, K_2\)=constants at \(T_1, T_2\); \(\Delta H^\circ\)=standard enthalpy of reaction; \(R\)=gas constant.

related_concepts.name: Sign of ΔH
related_concepts.definition: For endothermic ($\Delta H>0$) reactions $K$ rises with $T$; for exothermic ($\Delta H<0$) reactions $K$ falls with $T$ — consistent with Le Chatelier.

subject: Chemistry
title: Le Chatelier: Pressure Shift
description: Qualitative rule for pressure change at constant T (\(K\) unchanged). \(P\)=total pressure; increasing \(P\) favours the side with smaller \(\Delta n_g\). No shift if \(\Delta n_g = 0\).

related_concepts.name: Inert gas at constant V
related_concepts.definition: Adding inert gas at constant volume does not change partial pressures or concentrations, so equilibrium is unaffected.

related_concepts.name: Inert gas at constant P
related_concepts.definition: Adding inert gas at constant pressure increases volume, shifting equilibrium toward more gaseous moles.

subject: Chemistry
title: ΔG° and Equilibrium Constant
description: Links standard free energy change to equilibrium constant; used to compute K from \(\Delta G^\circ\) (and vice versa) and to judge spontaneity. \(\Delta G^\circ\)=standard Gibbs energy change, \(R\)=8.314 J/mol·K, \(T\)=temperature (K), \(K\)=equilibrium constant (\(K_p\) or \(K_c\)).
derivation:
At equilibrium \(\Delta G = 0\) and \(Q = K\).
Start from \(\Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln Q\).
Substitute: \(0 = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln K\).
Thus \(\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K\).

related_concepts.name: Spontaneity from K
related_concepts.definition: \(K>1 \Rightarrow \Delta G^\circ<0\) (forward favoured); \(K<1 \Rightarrow \Delta G^\circ>0\) (backward favoured); \(K=1 \Rightarrow \Delta G^\circ=0\).

related_concepts.name: ΔG° = ΔH° − TΔS°
related_concepts.definition: Combine with \(\Delta G^\circ=-RT\ln K\) to get \(\ln K = -\frac{\Delta H^\circ}{RT}+\frac{\Delta S^\circ}{R}\) (basis of van't Hoff).

subject: Chemistry
title: Kp vs α (A ⇌ B + C)
description: Dissociation giving two different products with equal stoichiometry (e.g. \(PCl_5 \rightleftharpoons PCl_3 + Cl_2\)), 1 mol start. \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation, \(P\)=total pressure.
derivation: Start 1 mol; at eqm: \(A=1-\alpha\), \(B=C=\alpha\), total \(=1+\alpha\).\nMole fractions \(\times P\) give partial pressures.\n\(K_p=\frac{(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}P)(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}P)}{\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}P}=\frac{\alpha^2 P}{1-\alpha^2}\).

related_concepts.name: Small α form
related_concepts.definition: For \(\alpha\ll 1\): \(\alpha\approx\sqrt{K_p/P}\); dissociation increases as \(P\) falls.

related_concepts.name: Effect of inert gas
related_concepts.definition: At constant pressure, adding inert gas raises total moles, lowers reactant partial pressure, and shifts dissociation forward (here \(\alpha\) increases).

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Dissociation (Kc form)
description: Concentration form for dissociation with initial concentration \(C\). \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation, \(C\)=initial molar concentration of \(A\); for \(\alpha\ll1\), \(\alpha\approx\sqrt{K_c/C}\) (Ostwald dilution analogue).

related_concepts.name: Dilution law trend
related_concepts.definition: As \(C\) decreases (dilution), \(\alpha\) increases — equilibrium shifts toward more dissociated species.

subject: Chemistry
title: Temperature Dependence of K (Integrated)
visual_data: \log K = -\frac{\Delta H^\circ}{2.303 \, R \, T} + \frac{\Delta S^\circ}{2.303 \, R}
description: Linear plot form of van't Hoff: \(\log K\) vs \(1/T\) gives slope \(-\Delta H^\circ/2.303R\). \(K\)=equilibrium constant, \(\Delta H^\circ\)=standard enthalpy, \(\Delta S^\circ\)=standard entropy, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature (K).
derivation: From \(\Delta G^\circ=-RT\ln K\) and \(\Delta G^\circ=\Delta H^\circ-T\Delta S^\circ\).\nEquate: \(-RT\ln K=\Delta H^\circ-T\Delta S^\circ\).\nDivide by \(-RT\): \(\ln K=-\frac{\Delta H^\circ}{RT}+\frac{\Delta S^\circ}{R}\).

related_concepts.name: Sign of slope
related_concepts.definition: Exothermic (\(\Delta H^\circ<0\)): \(K\) decreases with rising \(T\); endothermic (\(\Delta H^\circ>0\)): \(K\) increases with \(T\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Q vs K Predicting Direction
visual_data: Q < K \rightarrow \text{forward}, \quad Q = K \rightarrow \text{equilibrium}, \quad Q > K \rightarrow \text{backward}
description: Compares reaction quotient to constant to predict net reaction direction. \(Q\)=reaction quotient (same expression as \(K\) but with current values), \(K\)=equilibrium constant.

related_concepts.name: Link to ΔG
related_concepts.definition: \(\Delta G=RT\ln(Q/K)\); \(Q<K\Rightarrow\Delta G<0\) (spontaneous forward).

subject: Chemistry
title: Relation: Kc to Kp Units
visual_data: K_p = K_c (RT)^{\Delta n_g}, \quad K_c = K_p (RT)^{-\Delta n_g}
description: Inverse rearrangement to extract \(K_c\) from \(K_p\) when \(\Delta n_g\neq0\). \(\Delta n_g\)=change in gaseous moles, \(R\)=0.0821 L·atm/mol·K (match P units), \(T\)=temperature (K). For \(\Delta n_g=0\), \(K_p=K_c\) (dimensionless).

related_concepts.name: Units of K
related_concepts.definition: \(K_c\) has units \((mol/L)^{\Delta n_g}\); thermodynamic \(K\) is dimensionless (activities relative to standard state).

subject: Chemistry
title: Effect of Inert Gas Addition
visual_data: \text{const } V: \text{no shift}; \quad \text{const } P: \text{shift to higher } n_g
description: Predicts equilibrium response to inert (non-reacting) gas. At constant volume partial pressures unchanged so no shift; at constant pressure volume rises, partial pressures fall, shifting toward the side with more gaseous moles. \(n_g\)=total gaseous moles.

related_concepts.name: Why constant V is null
related_concepts.definition: Adding inert gas at fixed \(V\) does not change concentrations or partial pressures of reacting species, so \(Q\) stays equal to \(K\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Kp for A ⇌ 2B (Vapour Density)
description: Degree of dissociation from molar mass / vapour density drop on dissociation. \(M_t\)=theoretical (initial) molar mass, \(M_o\)=observed molar mass at equilibrium, \(D\)=theoretical vapour density, \(d\)=observed vapour density, \(n\)=moles of product per mole reactant.

related_concepts.name: Observed vs theoretical
related_concepts.definition: Dissociation increases total moles, so observed \(M_o<M_t\) and observed \(d<D\); the gap measures \(\alpha\).

subject: Chemistry
title: pH Definition
description: Logarithmic scale for acidity. For neutral water at 25C, pH = 7.
derivation:
Concentrations of \(H^+\) can vary over many orders of magnitude (e.g., \(10^{-1}\) to \(10^{-14}\)).
To make these numbers manageable, Sorensen introduced the negative log scale.
Definition:
\(pH = -\log_{10} a_{H^+} \approx -\log_{10} [H^+]\)
The negative sign ensures that as concentration drops, pH increases (becomes less acidic).

related_concepts.name: Auto-ionization of Water
related_concepts.definition: \(2H_2O \rightleftharpoons H_3O^+ + OH^-\). \(K_w = 10^{-14}\) at 25C.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ostwald's Dilution Law
description: Degree of dissociation for weak electrolytes. Valid when \(\alpha \ll 1\).
derivation:
Consider weak acid HA with conc C.
Equilibrium: \(HA \rightleftharpoons H^+ + A^-\)
Conc: \(C(1-\alpha)\) ... \(C\alpha\) ... \(C\alpha\)
\(K_a = \frac{[H^+][A^-]}{[HA]} = \frac{(C\alpha)(C\alpha)}{C(1-\alpha)} = \frac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}\)
For weak electrolytes, \(\alpha\) is very small, so \(1-\alpha \approx 1\).
\(K_a \approx C\alpha^2 \implies \alpha = \sqrt{K_a/C}\)

related_concepts.name: Degree of Dissociation
related_concepts.definition: The fraction of the total number of solute molecules that dissociate into ions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Henderson-Hasselbalch (Acidic)
description: Calculates pH of an acidic buffer solution.
derivation:
From the dissociation of weak acid HA:
\(K_a = \frac{[H^+][A^-]}{[HA]}\)
Take negative log of both sides:
\(-\log K_a = -\log [H^+] - \log \frac{[A^-]}{[HA]}\)
Substitute definitions (\(pK_a\) and \(pH\)):
\(pK_a = pH - \log \frac{[A^-]}{[HA]}\)
Rearrange (Note: \([A^-]\) comes from Salt):
\(pH = pK_a + \log \frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]}\)

related_concepts.name: Buffer Solution
related_concepts.definition: A solution that resists changes in pH upon the addition of small amounts of acid or base.

subject: Chemistry
title: Henderson-Hasselbalch (Basic)
description: Calculates pOH of a basic buffer solution. Use \(pH = 14 - pOH\).
derivation:
Similar to acidic buffers, start with weak base BOH:
\(K_b = \frac{[B^+][OH^-]}{[BOH]}\)
Take negative log:
\(-\log K_b = -\log [OH^-] - \log \frac{[B^+]}{[BOH]}\)
\(pK_b = pOH - \log \frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Base}]}\)
Rearrange:
\(pOH = pK_b + \log \frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Base}]}\)

related_concepts.name: pOH
related_concepts.definition: The negative logarithm of the hydroxide ion concentration.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility Product (Ksp)
description: Equilibrium constant for a solid dissolving into ions. Precipitation occurs if \(IP > K_{sp}\).
derivation:
For a sparingly soluble salt \(A_x B_y(s)\):
\(A_x B_y(s) \rightleftharpoons x A^{y+}(aq) + y B^{x-}(aq)\)
The equilibrium constant expression is:
\(K = \frac{[A^{y+}]^x [B^{x-}]^y}{[A_x B_y(s)]}\)
The concentration of a pure solid is constant (conventionally 1).
Therefore:
\(K_{sp} = [A^{y+}]^x [B^{x-}]^y\)

related_concepts.name: Common Ion Effect
related_concepts.definition: The suppression of the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte by adding a strong electrolyte containing a common ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis (Weak Acid-Strong Base)
description: pH of a salt solution like Sodium Acetate. Solution is basic (pH > 7).
derivation:
Anion \(A^-\)(from weak acid) reacts with water:
\(A^- + H_2O \rightleftharpoons HA + OH^-\)
This generates \(OH^-\), making the solution basic.
Using hydrolysis constant \(K_h = K_w/K_a\) and approx \([OH^-] = C\cdot h\):
\([OH^-] = \sqrt{K_h C} = \sqrt{\frac{K_w C}{K_a}}\)
Taking negative logs to find pOH, then pH:
\(pH = \frac{1}{2}pK_w + \frac{1}{2}pK_a + \frac{1}{2}\log C\)

related_concepts.name: Salt Hydrolysis
related_concepts.definition: Reaction of cation or anion of a salt with water to produce acidic or alkaline solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis (Strong Acid-Weak Base)
description: pH of a salt solution like Ammonium Chloride. Solution is acidic (pH < 7).
derivation:
Cation \(B^+\)(from weak base) reacts with water:
\(B^+ + H_2O \rightleftharpoons BOH + H^+\)
This generates \(H^+\), making the solution acidic.
\([H^+] = \sqrt{K_h C} = \sqrt{\frac{K_w C}{K_b}}\)
Taking -log:
\(pH = \frac{1}{2}pK_w - \frac{1}{2}pK_b - \frac{1}{2}\log C\)
Since \(pK_w = 14\) (at 25C), \(\frac{1}{2}pK_w = 7\).

related_concepts.name: Conjugate Acid
related_concepts.definition: A species formed by the reception of a proton (H+) by a base.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis (Weak Acid-Weak Base)
description: pH of salt like Ammonium Acetate. Independent of concentration.
derivation:
Both ions hydrolyze.
\([H^+] = K_a \sqrt{\frac{K_w}{K_a K_b}}\)
Taking negative logs:
\(pH = \frac{1}{2}pK_w + \frac{1}{2}pK_a - \frac{1}{2}pK_b\)
At 25C, \(pK_w = 14\), so:
\(pH = 7 + 0.5(pK_a - pK_b)\)
Note that the concentration term \(C\) cancels out.

related_concepts.name: Neutral Salt
related_concepts.definition: If \(K_a = K_b\), the solution is neutral (pH = 7).

subject: Chemistry
title: Indicator Theory (HIn)
description: Henderson equation applied to indicators. Determines color change range.
derivation:
Indicators are weak organic acids/bases.
$HIn (Color A) \rightleftharpoons H^+ + In^- (Color B)$.
$K_{In} = \frac{[H^+][In^-]}{[HIn]}$.
Take -log:
$pH = pK_{In} + \log([In^-]/[HIn])$.
Human eye detects color change when ratio shifts from 1:10 to 10:1 ($pH = pK_{In} \pm 1$).

related_concepts.name: Methyl Orange
related_concepts.definition: pH range 3.1-4.4. Red in acid, Yellow in base.

subject: Chemistry
title: Buffer Capacity
description: Moles of strong acid/base required to change pH of 1L buffer by 1 unit.
derivation:
Quantitative measure of buffer efficiency.
Maximum capacity occurs when $[Salt] = [Acid]$.
At this point, $pH = pK_a$.
The system can absorb maximum protons or hydroxide ions with minimal pH shift.

related_concepts.name: Buffer Action
related_concepts.definition: Mechanism by which added H+ or OH- ions are neutralized by buffer components.

subject: Chemistry
title: Double Indicator Titration
visual_data: V_{Ph} = \frac{1}{2} V_{CO_3} + V_{OH}; \quad V_{MeOH} = V_{CO_3} + V_{OH}
description: Titration of mixture (NaOH + Na2CO3) vs HCl using Phenolphthalein (Ph) and Methyl Orange (MeOH).
derivation:
1. Phenolphthalein ($pH$ 8-10): Detects completion of $NaOH \to NaCl$ and $Na_2CO_3 \to NaHCO_3$ (half neutralization).
2. Methyl Orange ($pH$ 3-4): Detects reaction of everything, including $NaHCO_3 \to H_2CO_3$.
Calculations:
$V_{Ph}$ corresponds to $OH^- + 1/2 CO_3^{2-}$.
$V_{Total}$ (MeOH) corresponds to $OH^- + CO_3^{2-}$.

related_concepts.name: Equivalence Point
related_concepts.definition: The point in a titration where the amount of titrant added is chemically equivalent to the amount of analyte.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ionic Product of Water
description: Self-ionization equilibrium constant of water. \(K_w\)=ionic product, \([H^+]\)=hydrogen ion conc, \([OH^-]\)=hydroxide ion conc (mol/L). \(K_w\) increases with temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: pH + pOH Relation
description: Links acidity and basicity scales at 25 deg C. \(pH=-\log[H^+]\), \(pOH=-\log[OH^-]\). Generally \(pH+pOH=pK_w\).

subject: Chemistry
title: pKw Relation
description: Definition of \(pK_w\) and its link to pH/pOH. \(pK_w=-\log K_w\). Used when temperature shifts \(K_w\) away from \(10^{-14}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: pH of Strong Acid
description: pH of a strong (fully dissociated) acid. \(C\)=acid concentration (mol/L), \(n\)=basicity (number of replaceable \(H^+\)). Valid when \(C \gg 10^{-7}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: pH of Strong Base
description: pH of a strong (fully dissociated) base. \(C\)=base concentration (mol/L), \(n\)=acidity (number of \(OH^-\) per formula unit).

subject: Chemistry
title: [H+] of Weak Acid
description: Hydrogen ion conc of a weak monoprotic acid. \(K_a\)=acid dissociation constant, \(C\)=initial conc, \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation. Valid for \(\alpha < 0.05\).

subject: Chemistry
title: pH of Weak Acid
description: pH of a weak monoprotic acid via Ostwald approximation. \(pK_a=-\log K_a\), \(C\)=initial acid conc (mol/L). Assumes \(\alpha\ll1\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Ka . Kb Relation
description: Links a conjugate acid-base pair. \(K_a\)=acid constant of the acid, \(K_b\)=base constant of its conjugate base, \(K_w\)=ionic product of water. Also \(pK_a+pK_b=pK_w=14\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Dissociation (Conductance)
description: Degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte from conductivity. \(\Lambda_m\)=molar conductivity at conc \(C\), \(\Lambda_m^\circ\)=molar conductivity at infinite dilution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis Constant (Salt of WA-SB)
description: Hydrolysis constant for a salt of weak acid and strong base. \(K_w\)=ionic product of water, \(K_a\)=dissociation constant of the weak acid. Solution is basic.

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Hydrolysis
description: Fraction of salt hydrolysed. \(K_h\)=hydrolysis constant, \(C\)=salt concentration (mol/L). For WA-SB and SA-WB salts; valid for \(h\ll1\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Hydrolysis (WA-WB)
description: Degree of hydrolysis for a salt of weak acid and weak base; independent of concentration. \(K_a\)=acid constant, \(K_b\)=base constant, \(K_w\)=ionic product.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility from Ksp (Binary AB)
description: Molar solubility of a 1:1 salt \(AB\) (e.g. AgCl). \(S\)=solubility (mol/L), \(K_{sp}\)=solubility product. From \(K_{sp}=S^2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility from Ksp (General)
visual_data: K_{sp} = x^x \, y^y \, S^{(x+y)} \implies S = \left( \frac{K_{sp}}{x^x y^y} \right)^{\frac{1}{x+y}}
description: Molar solubility for salt \(A_xB_y\). \(S\)=solubility (mol/L), \(K_{sp}\)=solubility product, \(x,y\)=stoichiometric coefficients of cation and anion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility of AB2 / A2B Type
description: Molar solubility for a 1:2 (or 2:1) salt e.g. \(CaF_2, Ag_2CrO_4\). \(S\)=solubility (mol/L), \(K_{sp}\)=solubility product.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ionic Product vs Ksp (Precipitation)
description: Criterion for precipitation. \(Q_{sp}\)=ionic product (current ion conc), \(K_{sp}\)=solubility product. \(Q_{sp}=K_{sp}\): saturated; \(Q_{sp}<K_{sp}\): unsaturated, no precipitate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Common Ion Effect on Solubility
description: Suppressed solubility of \(AB\) salt in presence of common ion conc \(C\). \(S\)=solubility in that solution, \(C\)=common ion concentration, \(K_{sp}\)=solubility product (\(C\gg S\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Relation [H+] and [OH-]
description: Couples the two ion concentrations in any aqueous solution. \(K_w=10^{-14}\) at 25 deg C. Used to convert between acidic and basic descriptions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Buffer Range
description: Effective working range of an acidic buffer. \(pK_a\)=of the weak acid; buffer is best when \([\text{salt}]=[\text{acid}]\) so \(pH=pK_a\). Basic analogue: \(pOH=pK_b\pm1\).

subject: Chemistry
title: pH at Half-Equivalence Point
description: At half-neutralization of a weak acid by strong base, salt equals remaining acid. \(pK_a\)=acid dissociation constant of the weak acid. Used to read \(pK_a\) off a titration curve.

subject: Chemistry
title: pH of Very Dilute Strong Acid
description: Exact \([H^+]\) when strong-acid conc \(C\) is comparable to \(10^{-7}\) (water's contribution counts). \(C\)=acid conc, \(K_w\)=ionic product. Then \(pH=-\log[H^+]\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Relative Strength of Two Weak Acids
description: Compares strengths of two weak acids at equal concentration (ratio of \([H^+]\) or degree of dissociation). \(K_{a_1}, K_{a_2}\)=dissociation constants, \(\alpha_1, \alpha_2\)=degrees of dissociation.

subject: Chemistry
title: pH of Mixture of Two Weak Acids
description: Net \([H^+]\) when two weak acids are mixed (or for the first step of a polyprotic acid). \(K_{a_1}, K_{a_2}\)=dissociation constants, \(C_1, C_2\)=molar concentrations.

subject: Chemistry
title: Overall Dissociation Constant (Polyprotic Acid)
visual_data: K_a = K_{a_1} \cdot K_{a_2} \cdot K_{a_3} \quad \implies \quad pK_a = pK_{a_1} + pK_{a_2} + pK_{a_3}
description: Overall \(K_a\) of a polyprotic acid (e.g. \(H_3PO_4\)) is the product of stepwise constants. \(K_{a_1}, K_{a_2}, K_{a_3}\)=successive (stepwise) dissociation constants.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sulfide Ion Concentration in H2S
description: Controls sulfide concentration via pH for selective sulfide precipitation (Group analysis). \(K_{a_1}, K_{a_2}\)=stepwise dissociation constants of \(H_2S\), \([H_2S]\)=undissociated acid concentration.

subject: Chemistry
title: Max pH for Hydroxide Precipitation
description: Threshold pH at which a metal hydroxide \(M(OH)_n\) just begins to precipitate. \(K_{sp}\)=solubility product, \([M^{n+}]\)=metal ion concentration, \(n\)=charge.
derivation: Onset of precipitation: \(Q_{sp} = K_{sp}\)\n\([M^{n+}][OH^-]^n = K_{sp}\)\n\([OH^-] = (K_{sp}/[M^{n+}])^{1/n}\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Selective Precipitation Ratio
description: Ratio of two ions with a common precipitant when the second salt just starts to precipitate (same stoichiometry). \(K_{sp_1}, K_{sp_2}\)=solubility products of the two salts.
derivation: At onset of 2nd salt: \([X^-]\) common\n\(K_{sp_1} = [A^{n+}][X^-]^n\), \(K_{sp_2} = [B^{n+}][X^-]^n\)\nDivide: \(\frac{[A^{n+}]}{[B^{n+}]} = \frac{K_{sp_1}}{K_{sp_2}}\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility in Pure Water vs Common Ion
description: Suppression of solubility of a sparingly soluble AB salt by a common ion. \(S\)=solubility in pure water, \(S'\)=solubility in presence of common ion, \(C\)=common ion concentration.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fraction Dissociated of Weak Acid
description: Exact degree of dissociation of a weak acid without the \(\alpha \ll 1\) approximation (used when \(\alpha\) is not small). \(K_a\)=dissociation constant, \(C\)=initial concentration.
derivation: \(K_a = \frac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}\)\n\(C\alpha^2 + K_a \alpha - K_a = 0\)\nSolve quadratic for \(\alpha\)

subject: Chemistry
title: pH at Equivalence Point (WA-SB Titration)
description: pH at the equivalence point of a weak acid titrated by a strong base (salt of WA-SB undergoes hydrolysis). \(pK_a\)=of weak acid, \(C_{salt}\)=salt concentration at equivalence.

subject: Chemistry
title: Amphiprotic (Amphoteric) Ion pH
description: pH of a solution of an amphiprotic species such as \(HCO_3^-\) or \(H_2PO_4^-\) (independent of concentration). \(pK_{a_1}, pK_{a_2}\)=consecutive dissociation constants of the parent acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nernst Equation
description: Calculates cell potential at non-standard conditions (at 298K).
derivation:
Thermodynamics relation: \(\Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln Q\)
Relate Free Energy to Potential: \(\Delta G = -nFE\)
Substitute:
\(-nFE = -nFE^\circ + RT \ln Q\)
Divide by \(-nF\):
\(E = E^\circ - \frac{RT}{nF} \ln Q\)
Convert natural log to log base 10 (\(\ln x = 2.303 \log x\)) and substitute constants (R, T=298K, F) to get 0.059.

related_concepts.name: Standard Electrode Potential
related_concepts.definition: The potential of a half-cell under standard conditions relative to the Standard Hydrogen Electrode.

related_concepts.name: Reaction Quotient (Q)
related_concepts.definition: Ratio of product concentrations to reactant concentrations at a specific moment.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs Energy & EMF
description: Relationship between standard thermodynamic potential and cell potential. \(F\): Faraday constant (96500 C/mol).
derivation:
Electrical work done by a galvanic cell is the product of charge and potential difference.
Charge flowed for \(n\) moles of electrons: \(Q = nF\)
Max Work done \(w_{max} = Q \times E^\circ_{cell} = nFE^\circ_{cell}\)
Thermodynamically, maximum useful work comes from the decrease in Gibbs Free Energy:
\(w_{max} = -\Delta G^\circ\)
Therefore:
\(\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{cell}\)

related_concepts.name: Spontaneous Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Requires \(\Delta G < 0\), which implies \(E_{cell} > 0\).

related_concepts.name: Faraday Constant
related_concepts.definition: The magnitude of electric charge per mole of electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Faraday's First Law
description: Mass of substance deposited at an electrode. \(E_{eq}\): equivalent weight, \(I\): current, \(t\): time.
derivation:
The mass (\(w\)) deposited is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity (\(Q\)) passed.
\(w \propto Q\)
Since \(Q = I \times t\) (Current \(\times\) Time):
\(w = Z \cdot I \cdot t\)
Where \(Z\) is the Electrochemical Equivalent.
\(Z = \frac{\text{Equivalent Weight}}{F} = \frac{E_{eq}}{96500}\)
Substituting \(Z\):
\(w = \frac{E_{eq} I t}{96500}\)

related_concepts.name: Equivalent Weight
related_concepts.definition: Molar Mass divided by the n-factor (valency factor).

subject: Chemistry
title: Molar Conductivity
description: Conducting power of all ions produced by 1 mole of electrolyte. \(\kappa\): specific conductance [S/cm].
derivation:
Conductivity (\(\kappa\)) is the conductance of a 1 cm\(^3\) solution.
Molar conductivity is the conductance of volume \(V\) containing 1 mole of electrolyte.
\(\Lambda_m = \kappa \times V\)
If Molarity is \(M\) (mol/L), then the volume containing 1 mole is:
\(V = \frac{1000 \text{ cm}^3/L}{M}\)
Substituting \(V\):
\(\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa \times 1000}{M}\)

related_concepts.name: Kohlrausch's Law
related_concepts.definition: Limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte is the sum of the limiting ionic conductivities of the cation and anion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kohlrausch's Law
description: Law of independent migration of ions at infinite dilution.
derivation:
At infinite dilution, the dissociation of electrolyte is complete and interionic effects disappear.
Each ion makes a definite contribution to the total molar conductivity, irrespective of the other ions present.
For \(A_x B_y\):
\(\Lambda_m^\circ = x \lambda^\circ_{A^+} + y \lambda^\circ_{B^-}\)
Used to calculate \(\Lambda_m^\circ\) for weak electrolytes (e.g., acetic acid) using strong electrolytes.

related_concepts.name: Infinite Dilution
related_concepts.definition: A theoretical state where concentration approaches zero and ions do not interact.

subject: Chemistry
title: Debye-Huckel-Onsager Equation
description: Describes conductivity variation for Strong Electrolytes.
derivation:
For strong electrolytes, ions are fully dissociated but interact.
As concentration (C) increases, conductivity decreases due to:
1. Relaxation Effect: Ionic atmosphere becomes asymmetric, retarding motion.
2. Electrophoretic Effect: Solvent molecules dragged by opposite ions retard motion.
Plot of \(\Lambda_m\) vs \(\sqrt{C}\) is linear with slope \(-A\).

related_concepts.name: Weak Electrolyte Graph
related_concepts.definition: Plot is a steep curve (rectangular hyperbola), not linear. Cannot find \(\Lambda_m^\circ\) by extrapolation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Efficiency of Galvanic Cell
description: Ratio of useful electrical work to the heat content (enthalpy) of the reaction.
derivation:
Thermodynamics of Cell:
Total energy change = Enthalpy change (\(\Delta H\)).
Useful work available (Electrical) = Gibbs Free Energy change (\(\Delta G\)).
Since \(\Delta G = -nFE_{cell}\):
Efficiency \(\eta = \frac{\text{Output}}{\text{Input}} = \frac{\Delta G}{\Delta H}\)
Typically \(\eta > 100\%\) is possible if cell absorbs heat from surroundings (endothermic).

related_concepts.name: Fuel Cell
related_concepts.definition: A cell converting chemical energy of fuel directly into electricity with high efficiency (~70%).

subject: Chemistry
