title: Lead Storage Battery (Discharge)
description: Secondary cell reaction used in automobiles. $H_2SO_4$ is consumed.
derivation:
Anode (Oxidation): $Pb + SO_4^{2-} \rightarrow PbSO_4 + 2e^-$
Cathode (Reduction): $PbO_2 + SO_4^{2-} + 4H^+ + 2e^- \rightarrow PbSO_4 + 2H_2O$
Overall: $H_2SO_4$ density decreases during discharge.
Recharging reverses the reaction (Electrolytic cell).

related_concepts.name: Secondary Battery
related_concepts.definition: A battery that can be recharged by passing current in the opposite direction.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fuel Cell (H2-O2)
description: Galvanic cell converting chemical energy directly to electricity.
derivation:
Electrolyte: Hot aqueous KOH.
Anode (Oxidation): $2H_2(g) + 4OH^-(aq) \rightarrow 4H_2O(l) + 4e^-$.
Cathode (Reduction): $O_2(g) + 2H_2O(l) + 4e^- \rightarrow 4OH^-(aq)$.
Net Reaction: $2H_2 + O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O$.
Pollution free, high efficiency ($\\eta \approx 70\\%$).

related_concepts.name: Apollo Space Program
related_concepts.definition: Used H2-O2 fuel cells for power and drinking water supply.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dry Cell (Leclanché)
description: Primary battery (non-rechargeable).
derivation:
Anode: Zinc container ($Zn \to Zn^{2+} + 2e^-$).
Cathode: Graphite rod surrounded by $MnO_2 + C$.
Reaction: $MnO_2$ is reduced to $MnO(OH)$ (Manganese goes from +4 to +3).
Electrolyte: Paste of $NH_4Cl + ZnCl_2$.
Ammonia produced complexes with $Zn^{2+}$ ($[Zn(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$), preventing pressure buildup.

related_concepts.name: Primary Cell
related_concepts.definition: Cell where reaction occurs only once and cannot be reversed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Conductance vs Dilution
description: Effect of adding water on Specific ($\kappa$) and Molar ($\Lambda_m$) conductance.
derivation:
1. Specific Conductance ($\kappa$): Conductivity of 1 cm$^3$ solution.
   On dilution, number of ions per cm$^3$ decreases $\rightarrow$ $\kappa$ Decreases.
2. Molar Conductance ($\Lambda_m = \kappa \times V$):
   Although $\kappa$ decreases, Volume ($V$) containing 1 mole increases much more.
   For weak electrolytes, degree of dissociation also increases.
   Net effect $\rightarrow$ $\Lambda_m$ Increases.

related_concepts.name: Debye-Huckel
related_concepts.definition: Interionic attractions decrease on dilution, aiding mobility in strong electrolytes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cell Constant
description: Geometric parameter of a conductivity cell.
derivation:
From resistance formula: $R = \rho \frac{l}{A}$.
Conductivity $\kappa = 1/\rho$.
$R = \frac{1}{\kappa} \left( \frac{l}{A} \right)$.
Rearrange: $\frac{l}{A} = \kappa \times R$.
The ratio $l/A$ is fixed for a given cell, called Cell Constant ($G^*$, unit $cm^{-1}$).

related_concepts.name: Wheatstone Bridge
related_concepts.definition: Circuit used to measure the resistance R of the electrolytic solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Corrosion (Rusting)
description: Electrochemical process occurring on iron surface.
derivation:
Anode (Iron surface): $Fe$ oxidizes to $Fe^{2+}$.
Electrons flow through metal to Cathode (Impurity/Stress point).
Cathode: Dissolved $O_2$ in water (with $H^+$ from $CO_2$) accepts electrons.
Product: $Fe^{2+}$ oxidizes further by air to $Fe_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O$ (Rust).

related_concepts.name: Sacrificial Protection
related_concepts.definition: Coating iron with a more active metal (Zn - Galvanization) to act as anode.

subject: Chemistry
title: Conductometric Titration (SA vs SB)
description: Conductance trend when NaOH is added to HCl.
derivation:
1. Initial: High conductance due to fast $H^+$.
2. Addition of NaOH: $H^+$ replaced by slower $Na^+$. Conductance decreases linearly.
3. Equivalence Point: Minimum conductance.
4. Excess NaOH: Conductance increases due to fast $OH^-$.
Result: V-shaped curve.

related_concepts.name: Ionic Mobility
related_concepts.definition: Velocity of ion per unit potential gradient. $H^+$ and $OH^-$ have exceptionally high mobility (Grotthuss mechanism).

subject: Chemistry
title: Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE)
description: Primary reference electrode. Potential defined as 0.00 V at all temperatures.
derivation:
Components: Platinum foil coated with Platinum black, immersed in 1M $H^+$ solution, bubbled with pure $H_2$ gas.
Half Reaction: $2H^+ + 2e^- \rightleftharpoons H_2(g)$.
It acts as Anode or Cathode depending on the other half-cell.
Limitations: Difficult to maintain 1M conc and 1 bar pressure continuously; susceptible to poisoning.

related_concepts.name: Calomel Electrode
related_concepts.definition: Secondary reference electrode ($Hg/Hg_2Cl_2/KCl$) often used in labs due to stability.

subject: Chemistry
title: EMF & Equilibrium Constant
description: Links standard cell potential to equilibrium constant of the cell reaction. \(K_c\)=equilibrium constant, \(n\)=moles of electrons, \(E^\circ_{cell}\)=standard cell emf (V).
derivation: At equilibrium \(\Delta G^\circ = -RT\ln K_c\) and \(\Delta G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{cell}\)\nSo \(nFE^\circ_{cell} = RT\ln K_c\)\nPutting \(2.303RT/F = 0.059\) at 298K: \(E^\circ_{cell} = \frac{0.059}{n}\log K_c\)

subject: Chemistry
title: ΔG° and Equilibrium Constant
description: Standard Gibbs energy from equilibrium constant of cell reaction. \(\Delta G^\circ\)=standard Gibbs energy (J), \(R\)=8.314 J/mol·K, \(T\)=temperature (K), \(K_c\)=equilibrium constant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nernst Equation (General, T)
description: Temperature-general form of the Nernst equation before substituting 0.059. \(R\)=8.314 J/mol·K, \(T\)=temp (K), \(n\)=electrons, \(F\)=96500 C, \(Q\)=reaction quotient.

subject: Chemistry
title: Single Electrode Potential
description: Nernst equation for a single metal electrode (reduction). \(E\)=electrode potential, \(n\)=electrons, \([M^{n+}]\)=ion concentration (M).

subject: Chemistry
title: Cell EMF from Electrodes
description: Standard cell emf from standard reduction potentials (both as reduction). \(E^\circ_{cathode}\)=right/reduction electrode, \(E^\circ_{anode}\)=left/oxidation electrode SRP.

subject: Chemistry
title: Concentration Cell EMF
description: EMF of a concentration cell (same electrodes, different ion conc.), \(E^\circ_{cell}=0\). \(C_2\)=higher (cathode) conc., \(C_1\)=lower (anode) conc., \(n\)=electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Faraday's Second Law
description: Same charge deposits masses in ratio of equivalent masses. \(w\)=mass deposited, \(E\)=equivalent mass of each substance.

subject: Chemistry
title: Charge & Moles of Electrons
description: Total charge passed and moles of electrons in electrolysis. \(Q\)=charge (C), \(I\)=current (A), \(t\)=time (s), \(n_e\)=moles of electrons, \(F\)=96500 C/mol.

subject: Chemistry
title: Specific Conductivity
description: Conductivity as reciprocal resistivity / from conductance & cell constant. \(\kappa\)=conductivity (S/cm), \(\rho\)=resistivity, \(G\)=conductance (S), \(l/A\)=cell constant (cm⁻¹).

subject: Chemistry
title: Equivalent Conductivity
description: Conductivity per gram-equivalent of electrolyte. \(\kappa\)=conductivity (S/cm), \(C_{eq}\)=normality (g-eq/L), \(\Lambda_{eq}\) in S·cm²/eq.

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Dissociation
description: Dissociation of a weak electrolyte from conductivity ratio. \(\Lambda_m\)=molar conductivity at conc. C, \(\Lambda_m^\circ\)=at infinite dilution, \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dissociation Constant (Ostwald)
description: Ostwald dilution law for weak electrolyte via conductivity. \(K_a\)=dissociation constant, \(C\)=concentration (M), \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation, \(\Lambda_m,\Lambda_m^\circ\)=molar conductivities.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility from Conductivity
description: Solubility of a sparingly soluble salt from conductivity (\(\Lambda_m \approx \Lambda_m^\circ\)). \(S\)=solubility (mol/L), \(\kappa\)=conductivity of saturated soln, \(\Lambda_m^\circ\)=limiting molar conductivity.

subject: Chemistry
title: Entropy from Temp Coefficient
description: Reaction entropy from temperature coefficient of cell emf. \(\Delta S\)=entropy change, \(n\)=electrons, \(F\)=Faraday, \((\partial E/\partial T)_P\)=temperature coefficient of emf.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enthalpy from Cell EMF
description: Reaction enthalpy via Gibbs-Helmholtz from emf and its temp coefficient. \(\Delta H\)=enthalpy change, \(E_{cell}\)=emf, \(T\)=temp (K), \((\partial E/\partial T)_P\)=temp coefficient.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mercury Cell
description: Overall reaction of the mercury button cell (constant ~1.35 V). Anode: \(Zn\) amalgam; Cathode: \(HgO\); electrolyte: KOH paste.

subject: Chemistry
title: Electrochemical Equivalent
description: Mass deposited per coulomb of charge. \(Z\)=electrochemical equivalent (g/C), \(E_{eq}\)=equivalent mass, \(M\)=molar mass, \(n\)=valency, \(F\)=96500 C.

subject: Chemistry
title: Galvanic Cell Notation
description: Standard IUPAC cell representation: anode (oxidation) left, cathode (reduction) right; \(||\)=salt bridge, \(|\)=phase boundary.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kohlrausch (Weak Electrolyte)
description: Limiting molar conductivity of a weak acid by combining strong-electrolyte values. Each \(\Lambda_m^\circ\)=limiting molar conductivity of that electrolyte.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass Deposited (Working Form)
description: Directly-applied electrolysis mass formula. \(m\)=mass deposited [g], \(E_{eq}\)=equivalent weight, \(M\)=molar mass, \(n\)=electrons transferred, \(I\)=current [A], \(t\)=time [s].
derivation:
Charge passed \(Q = It\)
Moles of electrons \(= \frac{It}{96500}\)
Moles of metal \(= \frac{It}{n \times 96500}\) (n electrons per ion)
Mass \(m = \text{moles} \times M = \frac{M\,It}{n \times 96500}\)

related_concepts.name: Equivalent Weight
related_concepts.definition: \(E_{eq} = \frac{M}{n}\), molar mass divided by the number of electrons exchanged (n-factor).

related_concepts.name: One Faraday
related_concepts.definition: 96500 C deposits one gram-equivalent of any substance.

subject: Chemistry
title: Time / Current from Faraday's Law
visual_data: t = \frac{m \times n \times F}{M \times I} \quad I = \frac{m \times n \times F}{M \times t}
description: Inverted Faraday's law to find time or current in electrolysis problems. \(m\)=mass deposited, \(M\)=molar mass, \(n\)=electrons, \(F\)=96500 C, \(I\)=current, \(t\)=time.

related_concepts.name: Series Electrolysis
related_concepts.definition: Same charge \(It\) passes through cells in series, so equivalents deposited are equal in each cell.

subject: Chemistry
title: E°cell from K_c (298 K)
description: Ready plug-in linking standard emf to equilibrium constant at 298 K. \(E^\circ_{cell}\)=standard cell emf, \(n\)=electrons, \(K_c\)=equilibrium constant.
derivation:
At equilibrium \(E_{cell} = 0\) and \(Q = K_c\)
Nernst (298 K): \(0 = E^\circ_{cell} - \frac{0.0591}{n}\log K_c\)
\(\Rightarrow E^\circ_{cell} = \frac{0.0591}{n}\log K_c\)

related_concepts.name: Equilibrium Spontaneity
related_concepts.definition: \(E^\circ_{cell} > 0 \Rightarrow K_c > 1\), reaction favours products.

subject: Chemistry
title: Volume of Gas at STP
description: Volume of gas (H\(_2\)/O\(_2\)/Cl\(_2\)) liberated at an electrode at STP. \(V\)=gas volume [mL], \(I\)=current, \(t\)=time, \(n\)=electrons per gas molecule, \(96500\)=1 F.
derivation:
Moles of gas \(= \frac{It}{n \times 96500}\) (n electrons per molecule)
At STP, 1 mole occupies 22400 mL
\(V = \frac{It}{n \times 96500} \times 22400\)

related_concepts.name: n-factor for Gases
related_concepts.definition: \(H_2\): n=2, \(O_2\): n=4, \(Cl_2\): n=2 (electrons exchanged per molecule).

related_concepts.name: Molar Gas Volume
related_concepts.definition: 22400 mL (22.4 L) per mole at STP (0°C, 1 atm).

subject: Chemistry
title: Raoult's Law (Volatile Liquids)
description: Total vapor pressure of a solution containing two volatile components. \(x\): mole fraction.
derivation:
According to Raoult's Law, the partial pressure of each component is proportional to its mole fraction.
\(P_A = P_A^\circ x_A\)
\(P_B = P_B^\circ x_B\)
According to Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures:
\(P_{total} = P_A + P_B\)
Substitute expressions:
\(P_{total} = P_A^\circ x_A + P_B^\circ x_B\)

related_concepts.name: Ideal Solution
related_concepts.definition: A solution that obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration.

subject: Chemistry
title: Relative Lowering of Vapor Pressure
description: Colligative property. The relative drop in VP depends only on the mole fraction of non-volatile solute.
derivation:
For a solution with non-volatile solute (B) and solvent (A):
\(P_{solution} = P_A = P_A^\circ x_A\)
We know \(x_A + x_B = 1 \implies x_A = 1 - x_B\).
Substitute \(x_A\):
\(P = P^\circ (1 - x_B)\)
\(P = P^\circ - P^\circ x_B\)
Rearrange:
\(P^\circ x_B = P^\circ - P\)
\(x_B = \frac{P^\circ - P}{P^\circ}\)

related_concepts.name: Colligative Properties
related_concepts.definition: Properties that depend on the number of solute particles, not their identity.

subject: Chemistry
title: Elevation in Boiling Point
description: Boiling point increases when a non-volatile solute is added. \(i\): Van't Hoff factor, \(K_b\): ebullioscopic constant.
derivation:
The addition of non-volatile solute lowers vapor pressure.
The solution must be heated to a higher temperature to match atmospheric pressure.
For dilute solutions, the elevation is proportional to molality (\(m\)):
\(\Delta T_b \propto m\)
\(\Delta T_b = K_b m\)
Incorporating dissociation/association factor \(i\):
\(\Delta T_b = i K_b m\)

related_concepts.name: Ebullioscopic Constant
related_concepts.definition: The elevation in boiling point for a 1 molal solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Depression in Freezing Point
description: Freezing point decreases upon solute addition. \(K_f\): cryoscopic constant.
derivation:
At freezing point, solid solvent and liquid solvent are in equilibrium (have same vapor pressure).
Solute lowers the liquid's VP, so the equilibrium curve intersects the solid VP curve at a lower T.
Similar to boiling point, for dilute solutions:
\(\Delta T_f \propto m\)
\(\Delta T_f = i K_f m\)

related_concepts.name: Cryoscopic Constant
related_concepts.definition: Depression in freezing point for a 1 molal solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Osmotic Pressure
description: Pressure required to stop osmosis. \(C\): molarity, \(R\): gas constant.
derivation:
Van't Hoff observed dilute solutions behave like ideal gases.
Ideal Gas Law: \(P V = n R T\)
Rearrange for Pressure (here \(\pi\)):
\(\pi = \frac{n}{V} R T\)
Since \(n/V = C\) (Molarity):
\(\pi = C R T\)
Including the Van't Hoff factor for particles:
\(\pi = i C R T\)

related_concepts.name: Isotonic Solutions
related_concepts.definition: Solutions having the same osmotic pressure at a given temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Van't Hoff Factor
description: Correction factor for dissociation. \(n\): particles per molecule, \(\alpha\): degree of dissociation.
derivation:
Consider electrolyte \(A_n \rightleftharpoons nA\).
Initial moles: 1
Equilibrium moles: \(1-\alpha\) (undissociated) + \(n\alpha\) (dissociated).
Total moles after dissociation = \(1 - \alpha + n\alpha\)
\(i = \frac{\text{Observed moles}}{\text{Theoretical moles}} = \frac{1 + (n-1)\alpha}{1}\)
\(i = 1 + (n-1)\alpha\)

related_concepts.name: Association
related_concepts.definition: When molecules join together (e.g., dimerization), \(i < 1\). Formula: \(i = 1 + (1/n - 1)\alpha\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Van't Hoff Factor (i)
description: Correction for Dissociation or Association of solute.
derivation:
1. Dissociation (e.g., NaCl \(\to\) 2 ions): Moles increase.
   \(i = 1 + (n-1)\alpha\) (where \(n\) is ions per molecule).
2. Association (e.g., Acetic acid in benzene \(\to\) Dimer): Moles decrease.
   \(i = 1 + (\frac{1}{n}-1)\beta\) (where \(n\) is number of molecules associating).
   For strong electrolytes (\(\alpha=1\)), \(i\) equals number of ions.

related_concepts.name: Abnormal Molar Mass
related_concepts.definition: Molar mass calculated from colligative properties differs from theoretical mass due to \(i \neq 1\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Azeotrope (Min Boiling)
description: Large positive deviation from Raoult's Law. Example: Ethanol + Water (95%).
derivation:
Interaction A-B is weaker than A-A or B-B.
Vapor pressure of mixture is higher than expected.
Boiling point is lower than either component.
At azeotropic composition, vapor phase composition = liquid phase composition ($y_A = x_A$), so separation by distillation is impossible.

related_concepts.name: Fractional Distillation
related_concepts.definition: Separation method that fails for azeotropes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Antifreeze (Ethylene Glycol)
description: Application of Depression in Freezing Point.
derivation:
Purpose: Prevent water in car radiators from freezing in winter.
Mechanism:
Ethylene Glycol (solute) is added to water (solvent).
The solute particles disrupt the formation of the ice crystal lattice.
This lowers the vapor pressure of the solid-liquid equilibrium.
Result: Freezing point drops below $0^\circ C$ (e.g., -30 to -40 C).

related_concepts.name: De-icing
related_concepts.definition: Sprinkling NaCl/CaCl2 on roads lowers FP of water, melting ice.

subject: Chemistry
title: Isotonic Solutions
description: Solutions having the same Osmotic Pressure at the same temperature.
derivation:
Formula: $\pi = iCRT$.
If $\pi_1 = \pi_2$ and $T$ is constant:
$i_1 C_1 = i_2 C_2$.
For non-electrolytes ($i=1$): Molar concentrations must be equal.
Significance: 0.9% (w/v) NaCl is isotonic with human blood (RBCs).

related_concepts.name: Hemolysis
related_concepts.definition: Bursting of RBCs when placed in a hypotonic solution (water enters cell).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mole Fraction
description: Fraction of moles of a component in a mixture; temperature independent. \(x_A\)=mole fraction of A, \(n_A,n_B\)=moles of A and B.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molarity (M)
description: Moles of solute per litre of solution; temperature dependent (volume changes). \(n\)=moles solute, \(V\)=volume of solution, \(w_B\)=mass solute, \(M_B\)=molar mass solute.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass Percentage (w/w)
description: Mass of component per 100 g of solution. \(w_A\)=mass of component A, \(w_B\)=mass of other component(s).

subject: Chemistry
title: Parts Per Million (ppm)
description: Concentration of very dilute solutions (trace impurities). Numerator and denominator in same units (mass or volume).

subject: Chemistry
title: Molarity-Molality Relation
description: Interconvert molarity and molality using solution density. \(M\)=molarity, \(m\)=molality, \(d\)=density (g/mL), \(M_B\)=molar mass of solute.

subject: Chemistry
title: Henry's Law
description: Solubility of a gas: partial pressure is proportional to its mole fraction in solution. \(p\)=partial pressure of gas, \(K_H\)=Henry's constant, \(x\)=mole fraction of gas in solution. Higher \(K_H\) means lower solubility.

subject: Chemistry
title: Raoult's Law (Single Volatile Solvent)
description: Partial vapour pressure of a solvent equals its pure vapour pressure times its mole fraction. \(p_A\)=partial pressure of solvent, \(p_A^\circ\)=vapour pressure of pure solvent, \(x_A\)=mole fraction of solvent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Vapour Phase Composition
description: Mole fraction of a component in the vapour above an ideal solution (Dalton's law). \(y_A\)=mole fraction of A in vapour, \(p_A\)=partial pressure of A, \(p_{total}\)=total vapour pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ideal Solution (Raoult Obeyed)
description: Conditions for an ideal solution obeying Raoult's law over the whole range (A-B interactions = A-A, B-B). E.g. benzene+toluene, n-hexane+n-heptane.

subject: Chemistry
title: Positive Deviation (Raoult)
description: Weaker A-B interactions than pure components; vapour pressure higher than predicted (minimum boiling azeotrope). E.g. ethanol+water, acetone+CS\(_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Molar Mass from RLVP
description: Determine molar mass of a non-volatile solute from relative lowering of vapour pressure (dilute solution). \(w_B,M_B\)=mass/molar mass solute, \(w_A,M_A\)=mass/molar mass solvent, \(p_A^\circ\)=pure VP, \(p_A\)=solution VP.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ebullioscopic Constant
description: Molal elevation constant linking \(\Delta T_b\) to molality. \(R\)=gas constant, \(M_A\)=molar mass solvent (kg/mol form), \(T_b\)=boiling point of pure solvent (K), \(\Delta H_{vap}\)=enthalpy of vaporization.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cryoscopic Constant
description: Molal depression constant linking \(\Delta T_f\) to molality. \(R\)=gas constant, \(M_A\)=molar mass solvent, \(T_f\)=freezing point of pure solvent (K), \(\Delta H_{fus}\)=enthalpy of fusion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molar Mass from Elevation
description: Molar mass of solute from boiling point elevation. \(K_b\)=ebullioscopic constant, \(w_B\)=mass solute, \(w_A\)=mass solvent (g), \(\Delta T_b\)=elevation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molar Mass from Osmotic Pressure
description: Molar mass of solute from osmotic pressure (best for macromolecules, measured at room T). \(w_B\)=mass solute, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature (K), \(\pi\)=osmotic pressure, \(V\)=volume of solution (L).

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Dissociation
description: Fraction of electrolyte dissociated, from van't Hoff factor. \(i\)=van't Hoff factor, \(n\)=number of ions per formula unit, \(\alpha\)=degree of dissociation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Abnormal Molar Mass
description: Van't Hoff factor as ratio of normal to observed molar mass; \(i>1\) for dissociation, \(i<1\) for association. \(M_{normal}\)=calculated molar mass, \(M_{observed}\)=experimental molar mass.

subject: Chemistry
title: Osmotic Pressure (Two Solutions Mixed)
description: Resultant osmotic pressure when two solutions of the same solute are mixed at constant T. \(\pi_1,\pi_2\)=osmotic pressures, \(V_1,V_2\)=volumes mixed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Konowaloff's Rule
description: The vapour is richer in the more volatile component than the liquid. \(y_A\)=mole fraction of A in vapour, \(x_A\)=mole fraction of A in liquid, \(p_A^\circ\)=pure VP of A.

subject: Chemistry
title: Effect of T on Gas Solubility (Henry)
description: Dissolution of a gas is exothermic, so solubility decreases with rising temperature (Le Chatelier). \(K_H\)=Henry's constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass % to Molarity
description: Converts a commercial solution's density + mass percentage into molarity (HCl, H_2SO_4 problems). \(M\)=molarity (mol/L), \(d\)=density of solution (g/mL), \(\%\,w/w\)=mass percentage of solute, \(M_B\)=molar mass of solute (g/mol).
derivation:
Take 100 g solution \(\Rightarrow\) solute mass \(=\%w/w\) g, moles \(=\frac{\%w/w}{M_B}\).
Volume \(=\frac{100}{d}\) mL \(=\frac{100}{1000\,d}\) L.
\(M=\frac{\%w/w / M_B}{100/(1000 d)}=\frac{10\,d\,(\%w/w)}{M_B}\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Volume Percentage (v/v)
description: Concentration of one liquid in another by volume (e.g. ethanol in water). \(V_{solute}\)=volume of solute, \(V_{solution}\)=total volume of solution (same units).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass by Volume % (w/v)
description: Mass of solute per 100 mL of solution, common in clinical/medicinal dosing. Mass of solute in grams, volume of solution in mL.

subject: Chemistry
title: Normality (N)
description: Equivalent-based concentration used in titrations/redox numericals. \(N\)=normality (eq/L), \(M\)=molarity, \(n\)-factor = basicity/acidity or electrons transferred. Gram-equivalents \(=\frac{w_B}{\text{equivalent mass}}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Dilution / Mixing (M1V1 = M2V2)
visual_data: M_1 V_1 = M_2 V_2 \quad ; \quad N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2
description: Conservation of moles (or equivalents) on dilution or mixing; for mixing two solutions of same solute \(M_{mix}=\frac{M_1V_1+M_2V_2}{V_1+V_2}\). \(M\)=molarity, \(N\)=normality, \(V\)=volume; subscripts 1=initial/conc., 2=final/dilute.

subject: Chemistry
title: i from Colligative Properties
visual_data: i = \frac{\Delta T_b^{obs}}{\Delta T_b^{calc}} = \frac{\Delta T_f^{obs}}{\Delta T_f^{calc}} = \frac{\pi_{obs}}{\pi_{calc}} = \frac{(\Delta p/p^\circ)_{obs}}{(\Delta p/p^\circ)_{calc}}
description: Operational form of van't Hoff factor: ratio of observed to normal (calculated) colligative property; equals \(\frac{M_{normal}}{M_{observed}}\). \(i\)=van't Hoff factor, obs=measured, calc=value assuming no dissociation/association.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mole Fraction from Molality
description: Interconverts molality to mole fraction of solute. \(x_B\)=mole fraction of solute, \(m\)=molality, \(M_A\)=molar mass of solvent (g/mol); based on 1 kg solvent = \(1000/M_A\) mol.

subject: Chemistry
title: Density of Unit Cell
description: Calculates density of crystal. \(Z\): atoms per cell, \(M\): molar mass, \(a\): edge length.
derivation:
Density is Mass per unit Volume.
Volume of cubic cell = \(a^3\).
Mass of cell = (No. of atoms) \(\times\) (Mass of 1 atom).
Mass of cell = \(Z \times m_{atom}\).
Since \(M = m_{atom} \times N_A\), then \(m_{atom} = M/N_A\).
Substitute:
\(\rho = \frac{Z \times (M/N_A)}{a^3} = \frac{ZM}{a^3 N_A}\)

related_concepts.name: Unit Cell
related_concepts.definition: The smallest repeating unit in a crystal lattice.

subject: Chemistry
title: Packing Efficiency (FCC/CCP)
description: Face Centered Cubic efficiency. Relation \(4r = a\sqrt{2}\).
derivation:
FCC has \(Z=4\) atoms.
Atoms touch along the face diagonal.
Face diagonal length = \(a\sqrt{2}\).
In terms of radius \(r\): \(4r = a\sqrt{2} \implies a = 2\sqrt{2}r\).
Volume of 4 spheres = \(4 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\).
Total Volume = \(a^3 = (2\sqrt{2}r)^3 = 16\sqrt{2}r^3\).
Ratio = \(\frac{16/3 \pi r^3}{16\sqrt{2}r^3} = \frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.74\)

related_concepts.name: Coordination Number (FCC)
related_concepts.definition: 12 (Each atom touches 12 nearest neighbors).

subject: Chemistry
title: Packing Efficiency (BCC)
description: Body Centered Cubic efficiency. Relation \(4r = a\sqrt{3}\).
derivation:
BCC has \(Z=2\) atoms.
Atoms touch along the body diagonal.
Body diagonal length = \(a\sqrt{3}\).
In terms of radius: \(4r = a\sqrt{3} \implies a = \frac{4r}{\sqrt{3}}\).
Volume of 2 spheres = \(2 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\).
Total Volume = \(a^3 = (4r/\sqrt{3})^3\).
Calculating ratio yields \(\approx 0.68\).

related_concepts.name: Coordination Number (BCC)
related_concepts.definition: 8 (Each atom touches 8 nearest neighbors).

subject: Chemistry
title: Bragg's Equation
description: Condition for constructive interference in X-ray diffraction. \(d\): interplanar spacing.
derivation:
Consider X-rays reflecting off two parallel crystal planes separated by distance \(d\).
The ray hitting the second plane travels an extra distance.
Geometry shows this extra path length is \(d \sin \theta\) for incidence and \(d \sin \theta\) for reflection.
Total path difference = \(2d \sin \theta\).
For constructive interference, this must equal an integer number of wavelengths:
\(n\lambda = 2d \sin \theta\)

related_concepts.name: Diffraction
related_concepts.definition: The bending of waves around obstacles and spreading out, used here to determine crystal structure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Radius Ratio (Octahedral)
description: Limiting ratio for Coordination Number 6 (e.g., NaCl).
derivation:
Consider a cation (r) in the void formed by 4 anions (R) in a square plane (cross-section of octahedron).
Diagonal of square = \(2R + 2r\).
Side of square = \(2R\).
Pythagoras: \((2R + 2r)^2 = (2R)^2 + (2R)^2\)
\(2(R+r) = 2\sqrt{2}R\)
\(R+r = \sqrt{2}R\)
\(r/R = \sqrt{2} - 1 = 1.414 - 1 = 0.414\)

related_concepts.name: Void
related_concepts.definition: Interstitial space between packed spheres in a lattice.

subject: Chemistry
title: Schottky Defect
description: Stoichiometric defect where equal numbers of cations and anions are missing.
derivation:
Thermodynamic Origin: Increases entropy of the crystal.
Characteristics:
1. Maintains electrical neutrality.
2. Volume remains constant (lattice structure holds).
3. Mass decreases (atoms missing).
4. Therefore, Density (\(\text{Mass}/\text{Volume}\)) decreases.
Occurs in high Coordination Number salts (NaCl, CsCl, KBr).

related_concepts.name: Point Defect
related_concepts.definition: Irregularities or deviations from ideal arrangement around a point or an atom.

subject: Chemistry
title: Frenkel Defect
description: Stoichiometric defect where an ion moves to an interstitial site.
derivation:
Also called 'Dislocation Defect'.
1. Smaller ion (usually cation, e.g., \(Ag^+\)) leaves its lattice site.
2. Occupies a void (interstitial site).
3. Mass remains constant (no ions lost).
4. Volume remains constant.
5. Therefore, Density remains unchanged.
Occurs when there is large difference in ion sizes (AgCl, ZnS).

related_concepts.name: AgBr
related_concepts.definition: Silver Bromide shows both Schottky and Frenkel defects.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of NaCl (Rock Salt)
description: Coordination Number 6:6. 4 formula units per unit cell.
derivation:
Arrangement:
1. Anions ($Cl^-$) form the Face Centered Cubic (FCC) lattice.
2. Cations ($Na^+$) occupy all Octahedral Voids (Body center + Edge centers).
Radius Ratio: $r^+/r^-$ is between 0.414 and 0.732.
Position of ions: Na+ at (1/2, 0, 0), Cl- at (0, 0, 0).

related_concepts.name: Formula Units (Z)
related_concepts.definition: Number of motifs per unit cell. For NaCl, $Z = 4$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of ZnS (Zinc Blende)
description: Coordination Number 4:4. 4 formula units per unit cell.
derivation:
Arrangement:
1. Sulfide ions ($S^{2-}$) form FCC lattice.
2. Zinc ions ($Zn^{2+}$) occupy 50% of Tetrahedral Voids (TVs).
   There are 8 TVs in FCC; Zn occupies 4.
Location: Body diagonals ($1/4$ distance from corner).
Note: Wurtzite is the HCP polymorph of ZnS.

related_concepts.name: Diamond Structure
related_concepts.definition: Same geometry as Zinc Blende but all atoms are Carbon.

subject: Chemistry
title: F-Centers (Farbe Centers)
description: Point defect causing color in ionic crystals (e.g., NaCl turns Yellow).
derivation:
Mechanism:
1. Crystal (NaCl) heated in metal vapor (Na).
2. Na atoms deposit on surface, $Cl^-$ diffuses out to form NaCl.
3. Electron lost by Na ($Na \to Na^+ + e^-$) diffuses *into* the crystal to occupy the vacant anion site.
4. Excitation of this trapped electron by visible light causes color.

related_concepts.name: Non-stoichiometric Defect
related_concepts.definition: Defects that change the ratio of cations to anions (Metal Excess Defect).

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Atoms per Unit Cell (Z)
description: Effective atoms per unit cell from shared positions. \(N_c\)=corner atoms (share \(1/8\)), \(N_f\)=face atoms (\(1/2\)), \(N_e\)=edge atoms (\(1/4\)), \(N_b\)=body-centre atoms (\(1\)).
derivation:
Corner shared by 8 cells \(\to 1/8\)
Face shared by 2 cells \(\to 1/2\)
Edge shared by 4 cells \(\to 1/4\)
Body centre fully inside \(\to 1\)

related_concepts.name: Z for SC
related_concepts.definition: Simple cubic: \(Z = 8 \times 1/8 = 1\)

related_concepts.name: Z for BCC
related_concepts.definition: Body-centred cubic: \(Z = 8 \times 1/8 + 1 = 2\)

related_concepts.name: Z for FCC
related_concepts.definition: Face-centred cubic: \(Z = 8 \times 1/8 + 6 \times 1/2 = 4\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Edge Length vs Radius (SC)
description: Relation for simple cubic where atoms touch along the edge. \(a\)=edge length, \(r\)=atomic radius.

subject: Chemistry
title: Packing Efficiency (SC)
description: Fraction of space filled in simple cubic. \(Z=1\), \(a=2r\). \(r\)=radius, \(a\)=edge.

subject: Chemistry
title: Coordination Numbers (Lattices)
description: Nearest-neighbour count for common metallic lattices. Higher CN \(\to\) higher packing efficiency.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Voids
description: For \(N\) close-packed (FCC/HCP) anions/atoms. Octahedral voids \(=N\); tetrahedral voids \(=2N\) (twice the atoms).

subject: Chemistry
title: Radius Ratio (Tetrahedral)
description: Cation occupies tetrahedral void (CN = 4) in this range. \(r^+\)=cation radius, \(r^-\)=anion radius.

subject: Chemistry
title: Radius Ratio (Cubic / 8-CN)
description: Cation occupies cubic body-centre void (CN = 8, e.g. CsCl) in this range. \(r^+\)=cation, \(r^-\)=anion radius.

subject: Chemistry
title: Radius Ratio (Trigonal / 3-CN)
description: Cation occupies trigonal planar void (CN = 3) in this range. \(r^+\)=cation, \(r^-\)=anion radius.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of CsCl
description: Cl\(^-\) at corners of simple cube, Cs\(^+\) at body centre (and vice-versa). \(Z=1\) formula unit, \(8{:}8\) coordination.

subject: Chemistry
title: CsCl Edge Length Relation
description: Cation and anion touch along the body diagonal in CsCl. \(a\)=edge length, \(r^+\)=cation radius, \(r^-\)=anion radius.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of CaF2 (Fluorite)
description: Ca\(^{2+}\) in FCC, F\(^-\) fill all 8 tetrahedral voids. \(Z=4\) formula units; coordination \(8{:}4\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Antifluorite Structure (Na2O)
description: Inverse of fluorite: O\(^{2-}\) form FCC, Na\(^+\) occupy all tetrahedral voids. Coordination \(4{:}8\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Tetrahedral Void Radius
description: Max sphere fitting a tetrahedral void of close-packed spheres of radius \(R\). \(r_{void}\)=void radius.

subject: Chemistry
title: Edge Length from Density
description: Edge length back-calculated from density. \(Z\)=atoms/cell, \(M\)=molar mass, \(\rho\)=density, \(N_A\)=Avogadro number.

subject: Chemistry
title: Distance Between Nearest Neighbours
description: Closest interatomic distance \(=2r\) for each cubic lattice. \(a\)=edge length.

subject: Chemistry
title: Conductor / Semiconductor Doping
visual_data: n\text{-type: group } 15 \text{ dopant};\quad p\text{-type: group } 13 \text{ dopant}
description: Doping Si/Ge (group 14): group-15 (e.g. P, As) gives extra \(e^-\) (n-type); group-13 (e.g. B, Ga) gives holes (p-type).

subject: Chemistry
title: Metal Excess / Metal Deficiency
description: Non-stoichiometric defects: metal excess (anion vacancy + trapped \(e^-\)) gives n-type semiconduction; metal deficiency (cation vacancy, e.g. FeO, FeS) gives p-type.

subject: Chemistry
title: Percentage Void Space per Lattice
description: Empty (unoccupied) space fraction in each lattice = 100% minus packing efficiency. Quick-recall complement of PE.

subject: Chemistry
title: Octahedral Void Size in FCC
description: Maximum radius of a sphere fitting an octahedral void in an FCC lattice along the edge. \(a\)=edge length, \(R\)=radius of lattice atom, \(r_{oct}\)=void radius.
derivation:
Along the FCC edge: \(2R + 2r_{oct} = a\).
Since \(a = 2\sqrt{2}R\):
\(2r_{oct} = 2\sqrt{2}R - 2R\)
\(r_{oct} = (\sqrt{2}-1)R = 0.414R = \frac{a}{2} - R\)

subject: Chemistry
title: n-type vs p-type Semiconductor
description: Carrier type produced by doping group-14 elements. Group-15 dopant donates an extra electron (n-type); group-13 dopant creates an electron hole (p-type).

subject: Chemistry
title: Magnetic Property Classification
visual_data: \begin{matrix} \text{Para: unpaired } e^-,\ \text{weakly attracted} \\ \text{Dia: paired } e^-,\ \text{weakly repelled} \\ \text{Ferro: } \uparrow\uparrow\uparrow\uparrow\ (\text{Fe, Co, Ni, CrO}_2) \\ \text{Antiferro: } \uparrow\downarrow\uparrow\downarrow\ (\text{MnO, net}=0) \\ \text{Ferri: } \uparrow\uparrow\downarrow\uparrow\uparrow\downarrow\ (\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4) \end{matrix}
description: Classification of solids by alignment of magnetic moments (domains). Ferro = parallel; Antiferro = equal antiparallel (cancel); Ferri = unequal antiparallel (net moment).

related_concepts.name: Paramagnetic
related_concepts.definition: Has unpaired electrons; weakly attracted by magnetic field; e.g. O2, Cu2+, TiO.

related_concepts.name: Diamagnetic
related_concepts.definition: All electrons paired; weakly repelled by magnetic field; e.g. NaCl, TiO2, C6H6.

related_concepts.name: Ferromagnetic
related_concepts.definition: Domains aligned parallel, strong permanent magnetism; e.g. Fe, Co, Ni, CrO2.

related_concepts.name: Antiferromagnetic
related_concepts.definition: Equal antiparallel alignment cancels net moment; e.g. MnO, Cr2O3, FeO.

related_concepts.name: Ferrimagnetic
related_concepts.definition: Unequal antiparallel alignment gives a small net moment; e.g. Fe3O4, ferrites MgFe2O4, ZnFe2O4.

subject: Chemistry
title: Stoichiometric Defects (Vacancy vs Interstitial)
visual_data: \text{Schottky: cation \& anion vacancies};\quad \text{Frenkel: ion shifted to interstitial}
description: Point defects keeping formula intact. Schottky lowers density (favoured by high CN, similar ion sizes); Frenkel keeps density same (favoured by low CN, large size difference).

related_concepts.name: Schottky example
related_concepts.definition: NaCl, KCl, CsCl, AgBr — high coordination number, comparable cation/anion sizes.

related_concepts.name: Frenkel example
related_concepts.definition: ZnS, AgCl, AgBr, AgI — low coordination number, large cation-anion size difference.

subject: Chemistry
title: Relation: Voids and Number of Atoms
visual_data: \frac{\text{No. of Tetrahedral voids}}{\text{No. of atoms}} = 2,\quad \frac{\text{No. of Octahedral voids}}{\text{No. of atoms}} = 1
description: Per close-packed sphere there are 2 tetrahedral and 1 octahedral void. Used to deduce formula from void occupancy. \(N\)=number of close-packed atoms.

subject: Chemistry
title: Spin Only Magnetic Moment
description: Calculates magnetic nature. \(n\): number of unpaired electrons. BM: Bohr Magneton.
derivation:
The magnetic moment arises from electron spin.
The formula is derived from quantum mechanics where angular momentum depends on total spin quantum number \(S\).
\(\mu = \sqrt{4S(S+1)}\)
Since each unpaired electron contributes spin \(1/2\), total spin \(S = n/2\).
Substitute \(S\):
\(\mu = \sqrt{4(n/2)(n/2 + 1)}\)
\(\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\)

related_concepts.name: Paramagnetic
related_concepts.definition: Substance with unpaired electrons, attracted by a magnetic field.

related_concepts.name: Diamagnetic
related_concepts.definition: Substance with all electrons paired, slightly repelled by a magnetic field.

subject: Chemistry
title: CFSE (Octahedral)
description: Crystal Field Stabilization Energy. \(P\): pairing energy.
derivation:
In an octahedral field, d-orbitals split into lower \(t_{2g}\) and higher \(e_g\).
The barycenter (average energy) is conserved.
\(t_{2g}\) orbitals stabilize by \(-0.4 \Delta_o\).
\(e_g\) orbitals destabilize by \(+0.6 \Delta_o\).
Total Energy = (Sum of electron contributions) + (Pairing energy if forced pairing occurs).
\(CFSE = (-0.4 t_{2g} + 0.6 e_g)\Delta_o\)

related_concepts.name: Spectrochemical Series
related_concepts.definition: A list of ligands ordered by the strength of the field splitting (\(\Delta\)) they produce.

subject: Chemistry
title: CFSE (Tetrahedral)
description: Relates splitting energy in tetrahedral field to octahedral field.
derivation:
In a tetrahedral field, only 4 ligands approach, compared to 6 in octahedral.
Also, ligands approach 'between' the axes, not directly along them.
The reduction in number of ligands reduces field by factor of \(2/3\).
The geometric angle approach reduces it by another \(2/3\).
Total factor: \(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{9}\).
Thus, \(\Delta_t \approx \frac{4}{9} \Delta_o\).

related_concepts.name: High Spin Complex
related_concepts.definition: Complexes where \(\Delta\) is small (weak field), favoring unpaired electrons over pairing.

subject: Chemistry
title: Crystal Field Splitting (Octahedral)
description: Splitting of d-orbitals in presence of 6 ligands. \(t_{2g}\) lowers, \(e_g\) raises.
derivation:
1. Isotropic Field: All 5 d-orbitals raised in energy equally by negative ligand charge.
2. Octahedral Field: Ligands approach along x, y, z axes.
   - \(d_{x^2-y^2}, d_{z^2}\) (e_g) point *at* ligands \(\rightarrow\) High Repulsion \(\rightarrow\) Energy rises (+0.6 \(\Delta_o\)).
   - \(d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{zx}\) (t_{2g}) point *between* ligands \(\rightarrow\) Less Repulsion \(\rightarrow\) Energy drops (-0.4 \(\Delta_o\)).

related_concepts.name: Spectrochemical Series
related_concepts.definition: Series ordering ligands by field strength (\(I^- < H_2O < NH_3 < CN^- < CO\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: CFT Splitting (Tetrahedral)
description: Splitting pattern is inverted relative to Octahedral. \(e_g\) is lower, \(t_{2g}\) is higher.
derivation:
1. Geometry: 4 ligands approach corners of a tetrahedron (alternating corners of a cube).
2. Interaction: The \(d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{zx}\) orbitals point *closer* to the ligands than the axial orbitals.
3. Result: \(t_{2g}\) set is repelled more (Higher Energy).
   \(e_g\) set is repelled less (Lower Energy).
4. Magnitude: \(\Delta_t < \Delta_o\) because there are fewer ligands (4 vs 6) and they don't point directly at orbitals.

related_concepts.name: High Spin Complex
related_concepts.definition: Tetrahedral complexes are almost always high spin because \(\Delta_t\) is usually smaller than Pairing Energy (P).

subject: Chemistry
title: Geometrical Isomerism (MA2B2)
description: Stereoisomerism based on ligand position. Common in Square Planar and Octahedral.
derivation:
Case: Square Planar \([MA_2B_2]\) (e.g., Cisplatin).
1. Cis-isomer: Identical ligands (A-A or B-B) are adjacent (90° angle).
2. Trans-isomer: Identical ligands are opposite (180° angle) across the metal center.
Note: Tetrahedral complexes do NOT show geometrical isomerism because all positions are equidistant and adjacent (109.5°).

related_concepts.name: Fac-Mer Isomerism
related_concepts.definition: Occurs in Octahedral \([MA_3B_3]\). Fac = Face (cis-like), Mer = Meridian (trans-like).

subject: Chemistry
title: Optical Isomerism
description: Chiral complexes that rotate plane-polarized light. Non-superimposable mirror images.
derivation:
Condition for Chirality: Absence of Plane of Symmetry (POS).
1. Example: \([Co(en)_3]^{3+}\) (Octahedral with 3 bidentate ligands).
   The chelate rings form a 'propeller' shape.
2. Mirror Image: The left-handed propeller cannot be superimposed on the right-handed one.
   Forms: Dextro (d) and Levo (l).
3. Trans-isomers with bidentate ligands often have a POS and are optically inactive (Meso).

related_concepts.name: Chelate Ring
related_concepts.definition: A ring structure formed when a polydentate ligand bonds to a central metal atom.

subject: Chemistry
title: 18 Electron Rule
description: Stability rule for organometallics. V: Valence e- of metal, L: e- from ligands.
derivation:
Based on filling s(2), p(6), and d(10) orbitals of the metal valence shell.
Example: $Fe(CO)_5$.
Fe ($d^6 s^2$) = 8e.
CO donates 2e $\times$ 5 = 10e.
Total = 18e (Stable).
Exceptions exist (e.g., Square planar $d^8$ complexes often stable at 16e).

related_concepts.name: Synergic Bonding
related_concepts.definition: Simultaneous donation from Ligand to Metal (sigma) and Metal to Ligand (pi back-bonding).

subject: Chemistry
title: Spectrochemical Series
visual_data: I^- < Br^- < Cl^- < F^- < OH^- < H_2O < NH_3 < CN^- < CO
description: Arrangement of ligands in increasing order of Crystal Field Splitting energy ($\Delta$).
derivation:
Empirical order determined by absorption spectra.
Trend Logic:
1. Halides (Weak): $\pi$-donors (filled p-orbitals) reduce $\Delta$.
2. Water/Ammonia (Intermediate): $\sigma$-donors only.
3. CN/CO (Strong): $\pi$-acceptors (vacant orbitals) allow Back Bonding, increasing $\Delta$ significantly.

related_concepts.name: Synergic Effect
related_concepts.definition: Self-strengthening bond mechanism in Metal Carbonyls due to sigma-donation and pi-backdonation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Color in Complexes
description: Color arises from d-d transitions or Charge Transfer.
derivation:
1. d-d Transition: Electron absorbs photon to jump from $t_{2g}$ to $e_g$ (in octahedral).
   Required energy corresponds to visible light.
   Example: $[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}$ is Purple.
2. Charge Transfer (CT): Electron moves between Ligand and Metal.
   Example: $KMnO_4$ (Deep Purple) has $d^0$ config, so color is due to $L \to M$ Charge Transfer, not d-d.

related_concepts.name: Complementary Color
related_concepts.definition: The color observed is complementary to the color absorbed (e.g., Absorb Yellow $\to$ See Violet).

subject: Chemistry
title: Jahn-Teller Distortion
description: Removal of degeneracy in unsymmetrically filled d-orbitals (e.g., $Cu^{2+}$ $d^9$).
derivation:
Thermodynamic Driver: System lowers its energy by distorting geometry.
Case: $d^9$ ($e_g^3$). The single hole could be in $dx^2-y^2$ or $dz^2$.
To resolve this, the ligands along the Z-axis move away (Z-out elongation).
Result: $dz^2$ energy lowers, $dx^2-y^2$ energy raises.
Stabilization Energy > Distortion Energy.

related_concepts.name: Z-out Distortion
related_concepts.definition: Most common J-T distortion where axial bonds are longer than equatorial bonds.

subject: Chemistry
title: Trans Effect
visual_data: CN^- > CO > NO > Ph^- > PR_3 > ... > H_2O
description: Kinetic effect in Square Planar complexes (Pt). Ligand directs incoming group to trans position.
derivation:
Mechanism depends on transition state stability.
Strong trans-directing ligands (like $\pi$-bonders $CN^-, CO$) weaken the bond trans to themselves by withdrawing electron density (Trans Influence) or stabilizing the 5-coordinate intermediate.
Result: Substitution happens opposite to the strong ligand.

related_concepts.name: Cisplatin Synthesis
related_concepts.definition: Uses trans effect sequence to ensure Chlorides end up cis to each other.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wilkinson's Catalyst
description: Homogeneous catalyst for hydrogenation of alkenes.
derivation:
Mechanism Cycle:
1. Dissociation: Loss of one $PPh_3$ to open a site.
2. Oxidative Addition: $H_2$ adds to Rh ($Rh^{+1} \to Rh^{+3}$).
3. Coordination: Alkene binds to metal.
4. Insertion: Hydride moves to alkene (forms Alkyl-Rh).
5. Reductive Elimination: Alkane leaves, regenerating catalyst.

related_concepts.name: Homogeneous Catalysis
related_concepts.definition: Catalyst and reactants are in the same phase (usually liquid solution).

subject: Chemistry
title: EAN Rule (Sidgwick)
description: Effective Atomic Number predicts stability (often = next noble gas). \(Z\)=atomic number of metal, \(O.S.\)=oxidation state of metal, \(C.N.\)=coordination number (no. of \(\sigma\)-bond pairs donated by ligands).
derivation:
Electrons left on metal \(= Z - O.S.\)
Each ligand donates 2 electrons \(\rightarrow 2 \times C.N.\)
\(EAN = (Z - O.S.) + 2(C.N.)\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Coordination Number
description: Total number of donor atoms (sigma bonds) bonded to the central metal. \(C.N.\)=coordination number; each polydentate ligand contributes its number of donor atoms (bidentate=2, tridentate=3, EDTA\(^{4-}\)=6).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation State of Metal
description: Finds the central metal oxidation state in a complex. \(x\)=oxidation state of metal; ligand charges summed (e.g. \(Cl^-=-1\), \(CN^-=-1\), \(NH_3=0\), \(H_2O=0\)); net charge = charge on the complex ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Pairing Energy vs Splitting
description: Decides spin state of octahedral d\(^4\)–d\(^7\) complexes. \(\Delta_o\)=octahedral crystal field splitting energy, \(P\)=electron pairing energy. Strong field (\(\Delta_o>P\)) gives low-spin; weak field (\(\Delta_o<P\)) gives high-spin.

subject: Chemistry
title: No Low-Spin Tetrahedral
description: Tetrahedral complexes are practically always high-spin. \(\Delta_t\)=tetrahedral splitting, \(\Delta_o\)=octahedral splitting, \(P\)=pairing energy. Since \(\Delta_t\) is small, it is always less than \(P\), so pairing is never favoured.

subject: Chemistry
title: CFSE in cm⁻¹ / kJ
description: Net stabilization after accounting for extra pairing in strong fields. \(CFSE\)=crystal field stabilization energy from d-orbital occupancy, \(n_p\)=number of extra electron pairs formed (vs free ion), \(P\)=pairing energy. Often quoted in \(\Delta_o\) units, cm\(^{-1}\) or kJ mol\(^{-1}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Werner Primary/Secondary Valency
description: Werner's theory of coordination. Primary valency = oxidation state, satisfied by negative ions, ionizable (gives ppt with AgNO\(_3\)); Secondary valency = coordination number, non-ionizable, directional (fixes geometry).

subject: Chemistry
title: Ions Precipitated by AgNO₃
description: Only counter (ionizable) ions outside the coordination sphere precipitate; ligands inside [ ] do not. \(n\)=number of free ionizable \(Cl^-\). E.g. \([Co(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2\) gives 2 AgCl; \([Co(NH_3)_3Cl_3]\) gives 0.

subject: Chemistry
title: Geometrical Isomers MA₄B₂ / MA₃B₃
description: Octahedral geometrical isomerism counts. \(MA_4B_2\) and \(MA_2B_4\) give cis/trans pairs; \(MA_3B_3\) gives facial (fac, three identical on one face) and meridional (mer, three around a meridian).

subject: Chemistry
title: Square Planar Geometrical Isomers
description: Square planar isomerism. \(Ma_2b_2\) (e.g. \([Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]\)) shows cis and trans; \(Mabcd\) shows 3 geometrical isomers. Tetrahedral \(Ma_2b_2\) shows NO geometrical isomerism.

subject: Chemistry
title: Types of Structural Isomerism
description: Four structural isomerism types for complexes. Ionisation (swap counter ion and ligand, e.g. \([Co(NH_3)_5SO_4]Br\) vs \([Co(NH_3)_5Br]SO_4\)); Hydrate/solvate; Linkage (ambidentate ligand, e.g. \(-NO_2\) vs \(-ONO\)); Coordination (ligand exchange between cation and anion complexes).

subject: Chemistry
title: Hybridisation vs Geometry
description: VBT hybridisation and resulting geometry. \(sp^3\)=tetrahedral, \(dsp^2\)=square planar (CN 4); \(sp^3d^2\)=outer-orbital octahedral (high spin), \(d^2sp^3\)=inner-orbital octahedral (low spin) (CN 6); \(sp\)=linear (CN 2).

subject: Chemistry
title: Inner vs Outer Orbital Complex
description: VBT classification of octahedral complexes. Inner-orbital (\(d^2sp^3\)) uses inner (n-1)d orbitals, strong field, low spin, less paramagnetic; outer-orbital (\(sp^3d^2\)) uses outer nd orbitals, weak field, high spin.

subject: Chemistry
title: Magnetic Moment to Unpaired e⁻
description: Back-calculate unpaired electrons from observed moment. \(\mu\)=spin-only magnetic moment (BM), \(n\)=number of unpaired electrons. Solve \(\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\): \(\mu\approx1.73\)(n=1), 2.83(n=2), 3.87(n=3), 4.90(n=4), 5.92(n=5).

subject: Chemistry
title: Chelate Effect / Stability
description: Polydentate (chelating) ligands form more stable complexes due to favourable entropy. \(\beta\)=overall (cumulative) stability/formation constant, \(\Delta G\)=Gibbs free energy, larger \(\beta\) means more stable complex; chelation increases \(\beta\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Overall vs Stepwise Constants
description: Relation between overall and stepwise formation constants. \(\beta_n\)=overall stability constant for \(ML_n\), \(K_1,K_2,\dots\)=stepwise stability constants. Generally \(K_1>K_2>\dots>K_n\) (statistical and steric factors).

subject: Chemistry
title: Total Optical + Geometrical Isomers
description: Optical activity in octahedral complexes. \(M(AA)_3\) (tris-bidentate, e.g. \([Co(en)_3]^{3+}\)) gives d and l (enantiomers); cis-\([M(AA)_2X_2]\) is chiral while trans is not.

subject: Chemistry
title: d-electron count dⁿ
description: Number of d-electrons on the metal ion in a complex. \(n\)=d-electron count, group no.= for transition metal (e.g. Fe=8), \(O.S.\)=oxidation state. E.g. \(Fe^{2+}=d^6\), \(Co^{3+}=d^6\), \(Ni^{2+}=d^8\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Crystal Field: Octa vs Tetra Order
description: Ordering of split d-orbital sets. Octahedral: lower \(t_{2g}\) (\(d_{xy},d_{yz},d_{zx}\)) below upper \(e_g\) (\(d_{z^2},d_{x^2-y^2}\)). Tetrahedral: order inverts, lower \(e\) below upper \(t_2\); no g subscript (no centre of symmetry).

subject: Chemistry
title: Barycentre Energy Levels
description: Energies of split orbitals relative to barycentre (hypothetical degenerate level). \(e_g\) raised by \(+0.6\Delta_o\) (\(+\tfrac{3}{5}\)), \(t_{2g}\) lowered by \(-0.4\Delta_o\) (\(-\tfrac{2}{5}\)). For tetrahedral: \(t_2=+0.4\Delta_t\), \(e=-0.6\Delta_t\).

subject: Chemistry
title: EAN Working Formula
description: Direct plug-in to compute Effective Atomic Number of a metal in a complex. \(Z\)=atomic number of metal, \(\text{O.S.}\)=oxidation state of metal, \(\text{C.N.}\)=coordination number (each \(\sigma\)-donor lone pair counts as 2). Stable complex when EAN equals the next noble gas number.
derivation:
Electrons left on metal ion \(= Z - \text{O.S.}\)
Each ligand donates a lone pair (2 e\(^-\)), total from ligands \(= 2 \times \text{C.N.}\)
Adding: \(EAN = (Z - \text{O.S.}) + 2(\text{C.N.})\)
e.g. \([Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}\): \(27 - 3 + 12 = 36\) (Kr)

subject: Chemistry
title: Ion Count vs Molar Conductance
description: Number of ions a complex furnishes fixes its molar conductivity and van't Hoff factor. More free ions \(\Rightarrow\) higher \(\Lambda_m\). Counts: \([Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3\to4\), \([Co(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2\to3\), \([Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]Cl\to2\), \([Co(NH_3)_3Cl_3]\to0\). \(\Lambda_m\)=molar conductivity, \(i\)=van't Hoff factor = total ions per formula unit.

subject: Chemistry
title: van't Hoff Factor of Complex
visual_data: i = (\text{no. of complex ions}) + (\text{no. of free counter ions})
description: van't Hoff factor for a coordination salt = total particles on complete dissociation; governs colligative properties. \(i\)=van't Hoff factor. e.g. \([Pt(NH_3)_4Cl_2]Cl_2 \rightarrow [Pt(NH_3)_4Cl_2]^{2+} + 2Cl^-\), \(i=3\); neutral \([Pt(NH_3)_2Cl_2]\) gives \(i=1\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Tris-Chelate M(AA)3 Isomers
description: Symmetrical bidentate tris-chelate is chiral with no geometrical isomerism. \((AA)\)=symmetrical bidentate ligand (en, ox, gly-N,N). e.g. \([Co(en)_3]^{3+}\), \([Cr(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}\) exist only as a non-superimposable \(d/l\) (\(\Delta/\Lambda\)) enantiomeric pair.

subject: Chemistry
title: Unsymmetrical Tris-Chelate M(AB)3
description: Unsymmetrical bidentate tris-chelate gives both geometrical (facial/meridional) and optical isomers. \((AB)\)=unsymmetrical bidentate (e.g. gly = glycinate, NH\(_2\)CH\(_2\)COO\(^-\)). Total \(= 2\) (fac, mer) \(\times\,2\) (\(d,l\)) \(= 4\). e.g. \([Co(gly)_3]\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Cis/Trans M(AA)2X2 Optical Activity
description: In bis-chelate dihalides only the cis form is chiral; trans has a plane of symmetry. \((AA)\)=bidentate, \(X\)=monodentate. e.g. cis-\([Co(en)_2Cl_2]^+\) shows \(d,l\) pair (3 isomers total: cis-d, cis-l, trans).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation State of Central Metal
description: Quick computation of metal oxidation number inside the coordination sphere. \(x\)=O.S. of metal; net charge = charge on the whole complex ion; neutral ligands contribute 0. e.g. \([Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}\): \(x + 6(-1) = -4 \Rightarrow x = +2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Van der Waals Equation
description: Equation of state for real gases correcting for intermolecular forces and molecular volume.
derivation:
Ideal Gas Law \(PV=nRT\) ignores molecular size and attraction.
1. Volume Correction: Molecules occupy space.
   Available volume = \(V_{container} - V_{molecules}\)
   \(V_{real} = V - nb\) (where \(b\) is excluded volume).
2. Pressure Correction: Attractive forces reduce impact on walls.
   \(P_{ideal} = P_{real} + p'\)
   Attraction depends on density squared (\(n/V\)).
   \(p' = a(n/V)^2\)
Combining both:
\((P + an^2/V^2)(V-nb) = nRT\)

related_concepts.name: Compressibility Factor (Z)
related_concepts.definition: The ratio \(PV/nRT\), indicating deviation from ideal behavior.

related_concepts.name: Critical Constants
related_concepts.definition: Temperature, pressure, and volume at the critical point where gas and liquid phases are indistinguishable.

subject: Chemistry
title: Root Mean Square Speed
description: Statistical measure of the magnitude of gas molecule velocity. \(M\): molar mass in kg/mol.
derivation:
From the Kinetic Molecular Theory of Gases:
Pressure equation: \(PV = \frac{1}{3} N m u_{rms}^2\)
Since \(N \times m = \text{Total Mass} = n \times M\):
\(PV = \frac{1}{3} n M u_{rms}^2\)
From Ideal Gas Law, substitute \(PV = nRT\):
\(nRT = \frac{1}{3} n M u_{rms}^2\)
Cancel \(n\) and rearrange:
\(u_{rms}^2 = \frac{3RT}{M} \implies u_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}\)

related_concepts.name: Maxwell-Boltzmann Distribution
related_concepts.definition: A probability distribution used for describing particle speeds in ideal gases.

subject: Chemistry
title: Graham's Law of Effusion
description: Rate of effusion (r) is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass.
derivation:
At a constant temperature, the average Kinetic Energy of two gases is equal.
\(KE_1 = KE_2\)
\(\frac{1}{2} m_1 v_1^2 = \frac{1}{2} m_2 v_2^2\)
Rearranging the velocities:
\(\frac{v_1^2}{v_2^2} = \frac{m_2}{m_1}\)
Since rate of effusion \(r\) is proportional to velocity \(v\):
\(\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}}\)

related_concepts.name: Effusion
related_concepts.definition: The process of gas molecules escaping through a tiny hole into a vacuum.

subject: Chemistry
title: Compressibility Factor
description: Factor indicating deviation from ideal behavior. \(Z=1\) for ideal gas.
derivation:
Defined to measure deviation from Ideal Gas Law.
For Ideal Gas: \(PV = nRT \implies Z = 1\).
For Real Gas:
If \(Z < 1\): Attractive forces dominate (gas is more compressible, easier to liquefy).
If \(Z > 1\): Repulsive forces dominate (gas is less compressible, difficult to liquefy).

related_concepts.name: Boyle Temperature
related_concepts.definition: The temperature at which a real gas behaves like an ideal gas over a range of pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dalton's Law
description: Total pressure of a non-reacting gas mixture is the sum of partial pressures.
derivation:
Assume gases behave ideally and independently.
\(P_1 = n_1 RT/V\)
\(P_2 = n_2 RT/V\)
\(P_{total} = (n_1 + n_2 + ...) \frac{RT}{V}\)
\(P_{total} = P_1 + P_2 + ...\)
Partial Pressure \(P_i\) is related to mole fraction \(x_i = n_i/n_{total}\):
\(P_i = x_i P_{total}\)

related_concepts.name: Partial Pressure
related_concepts.definition: The pressure that a gas would exert if it were present alone in the container.

subject: Chemistry
title: Critical Temperature (Tc)
description: Temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied, no matter the pressure.
derivation:
Derived from Van der Waals equation at the Critical Point (inflection point).
Conditions: $(\frac{\partial P}{\partial V})_T = 0$ and $(\frac{\partial^2 P}{\partial V^2})_T = 0$.
Solving these for $T$ yields $T_c$ in terms of constants $a$ and $b$.
At $T_c$, gas behaves ideally only at low pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Inversion Temperature
description: Temp at which Joule-Thomson coefficient is zero (no heating/cooling on expansion).
derivation:
For a real gas, expansion usually causes cooling (work done against attractive forces).
However, if $T > T_i$, repulsive forces dominate, and expansion causes heating.
Relation: $T_i = 2 T_{Boyle} = \frac{2a}{Rb}$.
For Hydrogen/Helium, $T_i$ is very low (requires precooling for liquefaction).

related_concepts.name: Joule-Thomson Effect
related_concepts.definition: Temperature change of a real gas or liquid when it is forced through a valve or porous plug while kept insulated.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ideal Gas Equation
description: Equation of state relating P, V, T for n moles of an ideal gas. \(P\)=pressure, \(V\)=volume, \(n\)=moles, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=absolute temperature.
derivation:
Combine the gas laws.
Boyle: \(V \propto 1/P\)
Charles: \(V \propto T\)
Avogadro: \(V \propto n\)
Combining: \(V \propto \frac{nT}{P} \implies PV = nRT\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Boyle's Law
visual_data: P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2 \quad (T, n \text{ const})
description: At constant T and n, volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to pressure. \(P\)=pressure, \(V\)=volume.

related_concepts.name: Isothermal process
related_concepts.definition: A process occurring at constant temperature; on a P-V plot it gives a hyperbola (isotherm).

subject: Chemistry
title: Charles's Law
description: At constant P and n, volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to absolute temperature. \(V\)=volume, \(T\)=temperature in K.

related_concepts.name: Absolute zero
related_concepts.definition: Extrapolated temperature \(-273.15^\circ C\) at which an ideal gas would have zero volume.

subject: Chemistry
title: Combined Gas Law
description: Relates the two states of a fixed amount of gas. \(P\)=pressure, \(V\)=volume, \(T\)=temperature in K.

related_concepts.name: State variables
related_concepts.definition: P, V, T together fix the macroscopic state of a fixed amount of gas.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ideal Gas (Density Form)
description: Links gas density to molar mass. \(M\)=molar mass, \(\rho\)=density, \(P\)=pressure, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.
derivation:
Start with \(PV = nRT\) and \(n = \frac{w}{M}\).
\(PV = \frac{w}{M}RT\)
\(P = \frac{w}{V}\cdot\frac{RT}{M} = \frac{\rho RT}{M}\)
\(\implies PM = \rho RT\)

related_concepts.name: Vapour density
related_concepts.definition: \(VD = M/2\) for a gas relative to \(H_2\); molar mass \(= 2 \times VD\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Average (Mean) Speed
description: Arithmetic mean of molecular speeds from Maxwell distribution. \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature, \(M\)=molar mass in kg/mol.

subject: Chemistry
title: Speeds Ratio
description: Fixed numerical ratio of the three characteristic molecular speeds \(\approx 1 : 1.128 : 1.224\). All measured at the same T for the same gas.

subject: Chemistry
title: Average Kinetic Energy (per mole)
description: Average translational kinetic energy of one mole of an ideal gas; depends only on T. \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=absolute temperature.

related_concepts.name: Per molecule KE
related_concepts.definition: \(\overline{KE} = \frac{3}{2} k_B T\), where \(k_B = R/N_A\) is the Boltzmann constant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Boltzmann Constant
description: Gas constant per molecule. \(R\)=universal gas constant, \(N_A\)=Avogadro number.

related_concepts.name: Energy per degree of freedom
related_concepts.definition: Each degree of freedom contributes \(\frac{1}{2}k_B T\) per molecule (equipartition theorem).

subject: Chemistry
title: Kinetic Gas Equation
description: Pressure from kinetic theory of gases. \(m\)=mass of one molecule, \(N\)=number of molecules, \(u_{rms}\)=root mean square speed.

related_concepts.name: Pressure form
related_concepts.definition: \(P = \frac{1}{3}\rho u_{rms}^2\), where \(\rho\) is gas density.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mole Fraction & Partial Pressure
description: Partial pressure of a component equals its mole fraction times total pressure. \(P_i\)=partial pressure, \(x_i\)=mole fraction, \(n_i\)=moles of component i.

related_concepts.name: Sum of mole fractions
related_concepts.definition: \(\sum x_i = 1\) for any mixture.

subject: Chemistry
title: Pressure of Moist Gas
description: Pressure of a gas collected over water after subtracting aqueous tension. \(P_{total}\)=measured pressure, \(P_{water}\)=vapour pressure (aqueous tension) of water at that T.

related_concepts.name: Aqueous tension
related_concepts.definition: The partial vapour pressure exerted by water vapour over liquid water at a given temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Van der Waals Constants (Units)
description: Meaning and units of vdW constants. \(a\)=intermolecular attraction (higher \(a\) means easier liquefaction); \(b\)=effective molecular volume (excluded volume).

related_concepts.name: Excluded volume
related_concepts.definition: \(b = 4 \times\) actual volume of the molecules per mole \(= 4 N_A v_{molecule}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Critical Constants (vdW)
description: Critical pressure, volume and temperature in terms of van der Waals constants. \(a, b\)=vdW constants, \(R\)=gas constant.

related_concepts.name: Critical point
related_concepts.definition: The point on the isotherm where liquid and gas phases become indistinguishable; an inflection point with zero slope.

subject: Chemistry
title: Critical Compressibility Factor
description: Universal value of compressibility factor at the critical point predicted by the vdW equation. \(P_c, V_c, T_c\)=critical constants.
derivation:
Substitute vdW critical constants.
\(Z_c = \frac{P_c V_c}{R T_c} = \frac{(a/27b^2)(3b)}{R(8a/27Rb)}\)
\(= \frac{a/9b}{8a/27b} = \frac{27b}{9b \cdot 8} = \frac{3}{8}\)

related_concepts.name: Real gas deviation
related_concepts.definition: Most real gases have \(Z_c \approx 0.27\text{-}0.30\), lower than vdW's 0.375.

subject: Chemistry
title: Compressibility (Low Pressure)
description: Approximate Z for a vdW gas at low pressure where attractive forces dominate, giving \(Z<1\). \(a\)=attraction constant, \(V\)=molar volume, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.

related_concepts.name: Attractive regime
related_concepts.definition: At low P the \(a/V^2\) correction dominates, so \(Z<1\) and the gas is more compressible than ideal.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mean Free Path
description: Average distance a molecule travels between successive collisions. \(d\)=molecular diameter, \(n\)=number density (molecules per volume).

related_concepts.name: Dependence
related_concepts.definition: \(\lambda \propto T/P\); rises with temperature and falls with pressure (denser gas).

subject: Chemistry
title: Collision Frequency
description: Number of collisions made by one molecule per unit time. \(d\)=molecular diameter, \(u_{avg}\)=mean speed, \(n\)=number density.

related_concepts.name: Mean free path link
related_concepts.definition: \(Z_1 = u_{avg}/\lambda\); free path is mean speed divided by collision frequency.

subject: Chemistry
title: Graham's Law (Volume/Time)
description: Rate of effusion compared via equal-volume times and densities. \(V/t\)=effusion rate, \(M\)=molar mass, \(\rho\)=density at same T, P.

related_concepts.name: Same volume
related_concepts.definition: For equal volumes effused, \(\frac{t_2}{t_1} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}}\); the heavier gas takes longer.

subject: Chemistry
title: KE per Molecule
description: Average translational kinetic energy of a SINGLE gas molecule. \(\overline{KE}\)=mean KE per molecule, \(k_B\)=Boltzmann constant \(=1.38\times10^{-23}\) J/K, \(T\)=absolute temperature. Independent of molar mass — depends only on \(T\).
derivation:
Per mole: \(KE = \frac{3}{2}RT\)
Divide by \(N_A\) molecules: \(\overline{KE} = \frac{3}{2}\frac{R}{N_A}T\)
Since \(k_B = R/N_A\): \(\overline{KE} = \frac{3}{2}k_B T\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Total KE of n Moles
description: Total translational kinetic energy (internal energy of ideal monatomic gas) of \(n\) moles. \(E\)=total KE, \(n\)=moles, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature. Equals \(\frac{3}{2}PV\) using \(PV=nRT\); used as \(U\) in thermodynamics.

subject: Chemistry
title: Equipartition of Energy
visual_data: E_{molecule} = \frac{f}{2} k_B T, \quad E_{mole} = \frac{f}{2} R T
description: Energy associated with each degree of freedom is \(\frac{1}{2}k_BT\) per molecule. \(f\)=degrees of freedom, \(k_B\)=Boltzmann constant, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature. \(f=3\) monatomic, \(5\) diatomic (linear), \(6\) nonlinear polyatomic.

related_concepts.name: Degrees of Freedom (f)
related_concepts.definition: Independent modes of motion. Monatomic: f=3 (translation only). Diatomic at room T: f=5 (3 trans + 2 rot). Nonlinear polyatomic: f=6 (3 trans + 3 rot).

related_concepts.name: Cv, Cp and gamma link
related_concepts.definition: From equipartition: \(C_v=\frac{f}{2}R\), \(C_p=(\frac{f}{2}+1)R\), \(\gamma=C_p/C_v=1+\frac{2}{f}\). Monatomic \(\gamma=5/3\), diatomic \(\gamma=7/5\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Maxwell-Boltzmann Distribution
description: Fraction of molecules with speed between \(u\) and \(u+du\). \(N\)=total molecules, \(M\)=molar mass, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature, \(u\)=molecular speed. Total area under curve = 1 (all molecules); peak = most probable speed.

related_concepts.name: Effect of Temperature
related_concepts.definition: On raising \(T\), the peak (most probable speed) shifts to higher speed (right) and the curve flattens & broadens; total area stays constant.

related_concepts.name: Effect of Molar Mass
related_concepts.definition: Lighter gas (smaller \(M\)) at same \(T\) has peak shifted right with a broader, flatter curve; heavier gas peaks at lower speed and is taller/narrower.

subject: Chemistry
title: Freundlich Isotherm
description: Empirical relationship for adsorption extent at moderate pressures. \(n > 1\).
derivation:
Based on experimental observation of physical adsorption.
Plotting \(\log(x/m)\) vs \(\log P\) gives a straight line.
\(\log \frac{x}{m} = \log k + \frac{1}{n} \log P\)
Slope = \(1/n\) and Intercept = \(\log k\).
At low pressure, graph is linear (\(1/n = 1\)).
At high pressure, graph flattens (\(1/n = 0\)).

related_concepts.name: Physisorption
related_concepts.definition: Adsorption involving weak van der Waals forces.

subject: Chemistry
title: Langmuir Isotherm
description: Model for monolayer adsorption. \(\theta\): fractional coverage.
derivation:
Assumes dynamic equilibrium between adsorption and desorption.
Rate of Adsorption \(\propto P(1-\theta)\) (Pressure \(\times\) vacant sites).
Rate of Desorption \(\propto \theta\) (Occupied sites).
At equilibrium: \(k_a P(1-\theta) = k_d \theta\)
\(k_a P - k_a P \theta = k_d \theta\)
\(k_a P = \theta (k_d + k_a P)\)
\(\theta = \frac{k_a P}{k_d + k_a P} = \frac{(k_a/k_d)P}{1 + (k_a/k_d)P}\)

related_concepts.name: Chemisorption
related_concepts.definition: Adsorption involving strong chemical bonds.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hardy-Schulze Rule
description: Coagulating power increases with the valency \(Z\) of the oppositely charged ion.
derivation:
Coagulation occurs when charge on colloid is neutralized.
Higher valency ions (e.g., \(Al^{3+}\) vs \(Na^+\)) compress the electric double layer more effectively.
The critical coagulation concentration (CCC) decreases roughly as the inverse sixth power of valency.
\(CCC \propto 1/Z^6\)
Power is inverse of CCC.

related_concepts.name: Flocculation
related_concepts.definition: The process where colloids come out of suspension in the form of floc or flake.

subject: Chemistry
title: Tyndall Effect Conditions
description: Criteria for light scattering by colloidal particles (why true solutions don't show it).
derivation:
1. Size Condition: The diameter of the dispersed particles (d) must be comparable to the wavelength (\(\lambda\)) of light used.
2. Refractive Index Condition: There must be a large magnitude difference between the refractive indices of the dispersed phase (\(n_1\)) and dispersion medium (\(n_2\)).
   This ensures significant scattering at the interface.

related_concepts.name: Lyophobic Colloids
related_concepts.definition: Show strong Tyndall effect due to large difference in refractive indices.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gold Number
description: Measure of protective power of lyophilic colloids. Lower Gold Number = Better Protection.
derivation:
Definition Standard:
- Volume of Gold Sol: 10 ml.
- Electrolyte added: 1 ml of 10% NaCl.
- Result to prevent: Color change from Red to Blue (Coagulation).
The Gold Number is the milligrams of protective colloid needed to just prevent this change.
Example: Gelatin (0.005) is a better protector than Starch (25).

related_concepts.name: Lyophilic Colloid
related_concepts.definition: Solvent-loving colloids (e.g., Gelatin, Gum) that protect unstable lyophobic colloids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Critical Micelle Concentration (CMC)
description: Concentration above which surfactants aggregate to form micelles.
derivation:
Mechanism:
1. Low Conc: Surfactants exist as individual ions/molecules on surface.
2. At CMC: Surface is saturated. Bulk concentration increases.
3. Hydrophobic tails cluster away from water to minimize energy.
4. Hydrophilic heads face outward, forming a sphere (Micelle).
For soaps, CMC $\approx 10^{-4}$ to $10^{-3}$ mol/L.

related_concepts.name: Kraft Temperature
related_concepts.definition: The minimum temperature required for micelle formation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Freundlich Log Form
description: Linearized Freundlich isotherm; plot \(\log(x/m)\) vs \(\log P\) gives slope \(1/n\), intercept \(\log k\). \(x/m\)=amount adsorbed per unit mass adsorbent, \(P\)=pressure (or concentration for solution), \(k,n\)=constants \((n>1)\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Freundlich Pressure Limits
description: Limiting behaviour of Freundlich isotherm with pressure. At low \(P\): \(1/n \to 1\) (linear); at high \(P\): \(1/n \to 0\) (saturation, independent of \(P\)); intermediate \(P\): fractional power \(0<1/n<1\). \(x/m\)=extent of adsorption, \(P\)=pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Adsorption Thermodynamics
description: Spontaneity criterion for adsorption. \(\Delta H<0\) (exothermic, released as adsorption enthalpy) and \(\Delta S<0\) (gas molecules lose freedom on surface); for \(\Delta G<0\) we need \(|\Delta H|>|T\Delta S|\). As adsorption proceeds \(\Delta H\) becomes less negative until \(\Delta G=0\) (equilibrium). \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Catalysis & Activation Energy
visual_data: k = A e^{-E_a / RT}, \quad E_{a,\text{cat}} < E_a
description: Catalyst speeds reaction by lowering activation energy via an alternative path (does not change \(\Delta H\) or equilibrium). \(k\)=rate constant, \(A\)=frequency factor, \(E_a\)=activation energy (uncatalysed), \(E_{a,\text{cat}}\)=catalysed activation energy, \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Langmuir Linear Form
description: Linearized Langmuir isotherm; plot \(P/(x/m)\) vs \(P\) gives slope \(1/x_m\) and intercept \(1/(Kx_m)\). \(x/m\)=amount adsorbed per unit mass, \(x_m\)=monolayer (max) adsorption capacity, \(K\)=adsorption equilibrium constant, \(P\)=pressure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Coagulation / Flocculation Value
description: Minimum millimoles of electrolyte per litre of sol needed to coagulate it in 2 hours; coagulating power \(\propto 1/\text{C.V.}\) Lower coagulation value means greater coagulating power (consistent with Hardy-Schulze, higher counter-ion charge). \(\text{C.V.}\)=coagulation (flocculation) value in millimol/L.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hardy-Schulze (CCC)
description: Quantitative form of Hardy-Schulze rule: critical coagulation concentration falls steeply with counter-ion valency. \(\text{CCC}\)=critical coagulation conc. (min. electrolyte needed to coagulate), \(Z\)=valency of the active (oppositely charged) ion.
derivation:
Coagulating power \(\propto Z^6\) (from electric double layer theory).
Coagulating power \(\propto \frac{1}{\text{CCC}}\).
\(\Rightarrow \text{CCC} \propto \frac{1}{Z^6}\)
Ratio for \(Na^+ : Ba^{2+} : Al^{3+}\) coagulating an As\(_2\)S\(_3\) (negative) sol \(\approx 1 : 2^6 : 3^6 = 1 : 64 : 729\) in power.

related_concepts.name: Coagulation value
related_concepts.definition: Millimoles of electrolyte per litre of sol needed to just cause coagulation; equals the CCC.

related_concepts.name: Counter-ion
related_concepts.definition: Ion of charge opposite to that of the colloidal particle; it is the one effective in coagulation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Finkelstein Reaction
description: Halogen exchange to prepare Alkyl Iodides. Driven by precipitation of NaX.
derivation:
General Reaction: \(R-Cl + NaI \rightleftharpoons R-I + NaCl\)
Key Principle: Le Chatelier's Principle.
Solubility: NaI is soluble in acetone, but NaCl and NaBr are NOT.
Since NaCl precipitates out, the concentration of product decreases.
This shifts the equilibrium forward to replace it.

related_concepts.name: SN2 Mechanism
related_concepts.definition: This reaction typically proceeds via SN2, so \(1^\circ\) halides react fastest.

subject: Chemistry
title: Swarts Reaction
description: Synthesis of Alkyl Fluorides using metallic fluorides (AgF, Hg2F2, SbF3).
derivation:
Direct fluorination with \(F_2\) is explosive/uncontrollable.
Swarts reaction uses heavy metal fluorides for a milder exchange.
The driving force is the formation of stable metal bromide/chloride precipitates (like AgBr).
It is a substitution reaction where F replaces Cl or Br.

related_concepts.name: Transition Metal Catalysis
related_concepts.definition: Using d-block metals to facilitate reactions that are otherwise difficult.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sandmeyer Reaction
description: Substitution of diazonium group with Halogen using Copper(I) salts.
derivation:
1. Diazotization: Aniline + \(NaNO_2/HCl\) at 0-5°C forms Benzene Diazonium Chloride (\(Ph-N_2^+Cl^-\)).
2. Radical Transfer: The Cuprous ion (\(Cu^+\)) acts as a catalyst.
   Electron transfer from CuCl generates an aryl radical (\(Ph^\bullet\)).
   Radical captures Cl from CuCl2.
   Product \(Ph-Cl\) forms and \(N_2\) gas is released.

related_concepts.name: Diazonium Salt
related_concepts.definition: A group of organic compounds sharing a common functional group \(R-N_2^+ X^-\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Wurtz Reaction
description: Coupling of two alkyl halides to form a symmetrical alkane.
derivation:
Two proposed mechanisms:
1. Ionic: \(R-X + 2Na \rightarrow R^- Na^+ + NaX\).
   Then \(R^- (nucleophile)\) attacks \(R-X\) (SN2) to form \(R-R\).
2. Free Radical: \(R-X + Na \rightarrow R^\bullet + NaX\).
   Then \(R^\bullet + R^\bullet \rightarrow R-R\).
Requires Dry Ether to prevent Na reacting with moisture.

related_concepts.name: Wurtz-Fittig Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Coupling between an alkyl halide and an aryl halide to form alkylbenzene.

subject: Chemistry
title: Friedel-Crafts Alkylation
description: Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution to attach alkyl group to benzene ring.
derivation:
1. Generation of Electrophile:
   \(R-Cl + AlCl_3 \rightarrow R^+ + AlCl_4^-\)
   (Lewis Acid \(AlCl_3\) pulls Cl away).
2. Attack:
   Benzene pi electrons attack the carbocation \(R^+\).
3. Deprotonation:
   \(AlCl_4^-\)
 removes H from the ring to restore aromaticity, releasing HCl and regenerating \(AlCl_3\).

related_concepts.name: Carbocation Rearrangement
related_concepts.definition: Primary carbocations may rearrange to more stable secondary/tertiary forms before attacking benzene.

subject: Chemistry
title: Grignard Reagent
description: Formation of organomagnesium halide. Reverses polarity of Carbon (Umpolung).
derivation:
Mechanism involves Single Electron Transfer (SET) on the Mg surface.
\(R-X + \cdot Mg \cdot \rightarrow R^\bullet + \cdot MgX\)
\(R^\bullet + \cdot MgX \rightarrow R-Mg-X\)
Carbon becomes Nucleophilic (carbanion-like) because Mg is electropositive.
Must be kept anhydrous as \(R-Mg-X\) acts as a strong base with water: \(R-H + Mg(OH)X\).

related_concepts.name: Nucleophilic Addition
related_concepts.definition: Grignard reagents add to carbonyl carbons (aldehydes/ketones) to form alcohols.

subject: Chemistry
title: SN1 Mechanism
description: Unimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution. Favored by \(3^\circ\) halides and polar protic solvents.
derivation:
Step 1 (Slow/RDS): Leaving group departs, forming planar carbocation.
   \(R-X \rightarrow R^+ + X^-\)
Step 2 (Fast): Nucleophile attacks carbocation.
   \(R^+ + Nu^- \rightarrow R-Nu\)
Since \(R^+\) is planar, attack can happen from front or back, leading to Racemization.

related_concepts.name: Racemization
related_concepts.definition: Formation of a 50:50 mixture of enantiomers, resulting in zero optical rotation.

subject: Chemistry
title: SN2 Mechanism
