description: Bimolecular Nucleophilic Substitution. Favored by \(1^\circ\) halides and polar aprotic solvents.
derivation:
Concerted one-step process.
1. Nucleophile attacks Carbon from the side opposite to the Leaving Group (Backside Attack).
2. Transition State: Carbon is temporarily pentavalent (bonded to both Nu and X).
3. Leaving group departs as bond to Nu forms fully.
Result: Walden Inversion (umbrella flip) of configuration.

related_concepts.name: Steric Hindrance
related_concepts.definition: Bulky groups block the nucleophile's path, slowing down SN2 reactions (Reason \(3^\circ\) don't do SN2).

subject: Chemistry
title: N-Bromosuccinimide (NBS)
description: Allylic and Benzylic Bromination (Substitution, not Addition).
derivation:
Mechanism: Free Radical Substitution.
1. NBS provides a constant, low concentration of \(Br_2\) (prevents addition to double bond).
2. Propagation: Bromine radical abstracts an Allylic Hydrogen.
   Reason: Allylic radical is Resonance Stabilized.
3. The radical reacts with \(Br_2\) to form Allyl Bromide.

related_concepts.name: Wohl-Ziegler Reaction
related_concepts.definition: The formal name for allylic bromination using NBS.

subject: Chemistry
title: E1 Mechanism (Elimination)
description: Unimolecular elimination. Competing reaction with SN1.
derivation:
Step 1 (Slow): Loss of Leaving Group forms Carbocation.
   $R-CH_2-C^+R_2$.
Step 2 (Fast): Weak base (solvent) removes $\beta$-hydrogen.
   $H^+$ leaves, C-C double bond forms.
Favored by: $3^\circ$ substrates, weak bases, high temperature (Entropy favored).

related_concepts.name: Saytzeff Product
related_concepts.definition: The more substituted, more stable alkene is the major product in E1.

subject: Chemistry
title: E2 Mechanism (Elimination)
description: Bimolecular elimination. Single step concerted process.
derivation:
Concerted Reaction:
1. Base abstracts $\beta$-proton.
2. C-H bond breaks, C=C bond starts forming.
3. Leaving Group departs simultaneously.
Stereochemistry: Requires Anti-Periplanar geometry (H and LG must be $180^\circ$ apart).

related_concepts.name: Hofmann Product
related_concepts.definition: Less substituted alkene formed when using bulky bases (e.g., t-BuOK).

subject: Chemistry
title: SNi Mechanism
description: Internal Nucleophilic Substitution. Occurs with Thionyl Chloride. Retention of Config.
derivation:
1. Formation of Chlorosulfite ester: $R-O-SO-Cl$.
2. Intramolecular Attack: The Chlorine atom attacks the alkyl group from the *same side* as the leaving oxygen.
   Reaction proceeds via a cyclic transition state.
   Result: Retention of Stereochemistry.
Note: If Pyridine is added, mechanism changes to SN2 (Inversion) because Pyridine removes HCl and frees $Cl^-$ for backside attack.

related_concepts.name: Darzen's Process
related_concepts.definition: Preparation of alkyl chlorides using $SOCl_2$ (preferred as byproducts are gases).

subject: Chemistry
title: E1cB Mechanism
description: Elimination Unimolecular conjugate Base. Occurs when leaving group is poor (F, OH) and acidic H is present.
derivation:
Step 1 (Fast): Base removes acidic $\beta$-proton.
   Forms a Carbanion intermediate (stabilized by EWG like -CO, -NO2).
Step 2 (Slow/RDS): Poor leaving group departs.
   $C^- - C - LG \rightarrow C=C + LG^-$.
Order is Second Order, but mechanism is stepwise (unlike E2).

related_concepts.name: Aldol Elimination
related_concepts.definition: Dehydration of aldol product follows E1cB due to acidic alpha-hydrogen and OH leaving group.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hunsdiecker Reaction
description: Decarboxylative bromination of silver salt of carboxylic acids.
derivation:
Mechanism: Free Radical.
1. Formation of Acyl Hypobromite: $RCOOAg + Br_2 \rightarrow RCOOBr + AgBr$.
2. Homolysis: $RCOO-Br \xrightarrow{\Delta} RCOO^\bullet + Br^\bullet$.
3. Decarboxylation: Unstable radical loses $CO_2$. $RCOO^\bullet \rightarrow R^\bullet + CO_2$.
4. Propagation: $R^\bullet + RCOOBr \rightarrow R-Br + RCOO^\bullet$.
Yield: Primary > Secondary > Tertiary.

related_concepts.name: Simonini Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Reaction of silver salt with Iodine to form Ester ($2RCOOAg + I_2 \to RCOOR$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Balz-Schiemann Reaction
description: Preparation of Fluorobenzene. Direct fluorination is too violent.
derivation:
1. Salt Formation: Diazonium chloride reacts with Fluoroboric acid ($HBF_4$).
   Precipitates stable Diazonium Fluoroborate ($PhN_2^+ BF_4^-$).
2. Thermal Decomposition: Dry heating decomposes the salt.
   $PhN_2^+ BF_4^- \rightarrow Ph-F + N_2 \uparrow + BF_3 \uparrow$.

related_concepts.name: Diazonium Stability
related_concepts.definition: Fluoroborate is one of the few stable diazonium salts that can be isolated.

subject: Chemistry
title: Benzyne Mechanism
description: Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution via Elimination-Addition.
derivation:
1. Elimination: Strong base ($NH_2^-$) removes proton ortho to Chlorine.
   Loss of $Cl^-$ generates **Benzyne** intermediate (Triple bond in ring).
2. Addition: Nucleophile ($NH_2^-$) attacks the Benzyne triple bond.
   Since the triple bond is symmetric, attack can occur at either carbon (ipso or ortho).
   Protonation yields Aniline.

related_concepts.name: Cine Substitution
related_concepts.definition: When the incoming nucleophile occupies a position adjacent to the leaving group.

subject: Chemistry
title: SNAr Mechanism
description: Nucleophilic Aromatic Substitution (Addition-Elimination). Requires EWG at o/p positions.
derivation:
Example: p-Nitrochlorobenzene + $OH^-$.
1. Addition (Slow/RDS): Nucleophile attacks carbon bonded to halogen.
   Resonance stabilized Carbanion intermediate (Meisenheimer Complex).
   The negative charge is delocalized onto the Nitro group.
2. Elimination (Fast): Loss of Halide ion restores aromaticity.
   Reactivity: $F \gg Cl > Br > I$ (Stronger C-F dipole favors step 1).

related_concepts.name: Meisenheimer Complex
related_concepts.definition: Stable anionic intermediate formed during SNAr reactions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ullmann Reaction
description: Coupling of Aryl Halides (especially Iodides) to form Biaryls.
derivation:
Reagent: Copper Powder at high temperature.
Mechanism: Radical anion intermediate.
Application: Synthesis of Biphenyls.
Note: Specific for Aryl halides, unlike Wurtz (Alkyl) or Fittig (Aryl+Alkyl).

related_concepts.name: Fittig Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Coupling of two aryl halides using Sodium metal.

subject: Chemistry
title: Saytzeff Rule
description: Predicts major alkene in dehydrohalogenation (\(\beta\)-elimination): the more substituted (more stable) alkene predominates. \(X\)=halogen; alc. KOH=alcoholic potassium hydroxide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Markovnikov Addition (HX to Alkene)
description: Acid addition to alkenes: H adds to the carbon with more H's, halogen to the more substituted carbon (via more stable carbocation). \(X\)=Cl, Br, I.

subject: Chemistry
title: Anti-Markovnikov (Peroxide Effect)
description: Kharasch effect: HBr (only) adds anti-Markovnikov via free-radical mechanism in presence of peroxide; Br goes to less substituted carbon. Works for HBr, not HCl/HI.

subject: Chemistry
title: Free Radical Halogenation
description: Photochemical chlorination of alkanes via chain mechanism (initiation, propagation, termination); gives mixture of mono- & poly-halides. \(h\nu\)=UV light.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reactivity Order of Halogenation
description: Order of halogen reactivity in free-radical halogenation of alkanes; \(F_2\) too violent, \(I_2\) too unreactive (reaction reversible). Selectivity is opposite: \(Br_2 > Cl_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Reactivity Order: SN1
description: SN1 rate order for alkyl halides — governed by carbocation stability (more substituted = more stable intermediate). Allylic & benzylic halides react very fast (resonance-stabilised cation).

subject: Chemistry
title: C-X Bond Reactivity Order
description: Order of reactivity of alkyl halides in nucleophilic substitution — weakest C-X bond (C-I, lowest bond enthalpy) is most reactive; C-F strongest, least reactive.

subject: Chemistry
title: Walden Inversion (SN2)
visual_data: Nu^- + R-X \rightarrow [Nu \cdots R \cdots X]^{\neq} \rightarrow Nu-R + X^-
description: SN2 proceeds with inversion of configuration (umbrella flip) at the stereocentre via a pentacoordinate transition state; \(Nu^-\)=nucleophile, \([\;]^{\neq}\)=TS.

subject: Chemistry
title: SN1 Stereochemistry (Racemisation)
description: SN1 via planar carbocation; nucleophile attacks both faces giving racemic mixture (partial racemisation with slight inversion). Optically active substrate gives optically inactive product.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reduction of Haloalkanes
description: Reductive dehalogenation of alkyl halides to alkanes using a metal/acid couple (Zn/HCl, Zn-Cu, or \(LiAlH_4\)). \([H]\)=nascent hydrogen.

subject: Chemistry
title: Williamson Ether Synthesis
description: Sodium alkoxide + alkyl halide gives ether (SN2). Best with primary R-X; \(3^\circ\) R-X gives elimination instead. \(R'O^-\)=alkoxide nucleophile.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cyanide vs Isocyanide (Ambident)
description: Ambident nucleophile: \(KCN\) (ionic) gives nitrile (R-CN, C-attack); \(AgCN\) (covalent) gives isocyanide (R-NC, N-attack). \(R-CN\)=alkyl cyanide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitrite vs Nitro (Ambident)
description: Ambident nitrite ion: \(AgNO_2\) gives nitroalkane (R-NO\(_2\), N-attack); \(KNO_2\) gives alkyl nitrite (R-O-N=O, O-attack).

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis to Alcohol
description: Aqueous KOH converts alkyl halide to alcohol (substitution). Aqueous = substitution to alcohol; alcoholic = elimination to alkene. \(R-OH\)=alcohol.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fittig Reaction
description: Aryl halide + Na in dry ether gives biaryl (diphenyl). \(C_6H_5\)=phenyl; analogous to Wurtz but for aryl halides.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wurtz-Fittig Reaction
description: Aryl halide + alkyl halide + Na gives alkylbenzene. Used to attach an alkyl chain to an aromatic ring. \(X\)=halogen, \(R\)=alkyl.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dehalogenation of vic-Dihalides
description: Vicinal dihalides lose both halogens with Zn dust to form alkene (anti-elimination). \(vic\)=halogens on adjacent carbons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ring Halogenation of Haloarene
description: Halogen on arene is o/p-directing but deactivating; further electrophilic substitution gives ortho & para products. \(FeCl_3\)=Lewis acid catalyst.

subject: Chemistry
title: Activation of SNAr by -NO2
description: Electron-withdrawing groups (\(-NO_2\)) at o/p positions hugely accelerate nucleophilic aromatic substitution by stabilising the Meisenheimer intermediate. More \(NO_2\) = milder conditions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chloroform Oxidation (Phosgene)
description: Chloroform is slowly air-oxidised in light to poisonous phosgene (\(COCl_2\)); hence stored in dark bottles with ~1% ethanol. \(COCl_2\)=carbonyl chloride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
description: Phenol + chloroform + NaOH gives salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde) via electrophilic dichlorocarbene (\(:CCl_2\)). Introduces -CHO ortho to -OH.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dichlorocarbene Generation
description: \(\alpha\)-elimination from chloroform by base gives electron-deficient dichlorocarbene (\(:CCl_2\)), the reactive electrophile in carbylamine & Reimer-Tiemann reactions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Optical Rotation (Specific Rotation)
description: Defines specific rotation of a chiral (optically active) halide. \([\alpha]_D^t\)=specific rotation, \(\alpha\)=observed rotation (\(^\circ\)), \(l\)=path length (dm), \(c\)=concentration (g/mL).

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Optical Isomers
description: Maximum number of optical isomers (stereoisomers) for a molecule with \(n\) dissimilar (non-equivalent) chiral centres. \(N\)=max stereoisomers; halved if internal symmetry (meso) exists.

subject: Chemistry
title: Allylic/Benzylic SN1 Stability
description: Allyl & benzyl halides undergo very fast SN1 because the carbocation is resonance-stabilised (delocalised). Vinyl & aryl halides are unreactive (no SN1/SN2) due to partial double-bond character.

subject: Chemistry
title: Alcohol to Halide: SOCl2
description: Best prep of R-Cl from alcohol; gaseous by-products escape so product is pure (Darzens). \(R\)=alkyl, \(SOCl_2\)=thionyl chloride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Alcohol to Halide: PCl3 / PBr3 / PI3
description: Prep of haloalkane from alcohol via phosphorus trihalide (\(PBr_3\), \(PI_3\) often made in situ from red P + X2). \(X\)=Cl/Br/I, \(H_3PO_3\)=phosphorous acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Alcohol to Halide: Lucas Test
description: Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + anhyd. ZnCl2) distinguishes 1°/2°/3° alcohols by turbidity time: 3° instant, 2° in 5 min, 1° no reaction at RT. \(ZnCl_2\)=Lewis acid catalyst.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wurtz Symmetry Rule (No. of Products)
description: Wurtz gives clean alkane only with one halide; two different halides give a mixture of 3 alkanes (separation hard). Use only for symmetrical alkanes. \(R \neq R'\).

subject: Chemistry
title: SN Reactivity Order (Leaving Group)
description: Rate of nucleophilic substitution vs halogen: I leaves fastest (weakest C-X bond, best leaving group); F slowest. Parallels decreasing C-X bond strength F>Cl>Br>I.

subject: Chemistry
title: Haloalkane to Amine (Ammonolysis)
description: Excess NH3 gives 1° amine; excess R-X over-alkylates to 2°, 3° amine and quaternary salt (a mixture). \(R\)=alkyl, \(R_4N^+X^-\)=quaternary ammonium salt.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitrile to Acid (via KCN)
description: Chain-lengthening: halide to nitrile (1 extra C) then hydrolysis to carboxylic acid (or reduction to amine). \(R\)=alkyl, \(CN\)=cyano.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dipole Moment: Haloalkane vs Haloarene
description: Chlorobenzene has smaller dipole moment than chloromethane: sp2 carbon is more electronegative and resonance shifts e- density toward ring reducing net polarity. \(\mu\)=dipole moment.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hofmann (Anti-Saytzeff) Elimination
description: With bulky bases (t-BuOK) or quaternary ammonium hydroxides, elimination gives the least substituted (Hofmann) alkene as major, opposite to Saytzeff. \(R\)=alkyl substrate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dipole Moment
description: Vector quantity measuring bond polarity. \(q\): magnitude of charge, \(d\): distance.
derivation:
A dipole arises when electron density is unequal between two atoms.
Calculated as the product of partial charge (\(\delta\)) and bond length.
For polyatomic molecules, \(\mu_{net}\) is the vector sum of individual bond dipoles.
\(\mu_{net} = \sqrt{\mu_1^2 + \mu_2^2 + 2\mu_1\mu_2 \cos \theta}\)
Symmetrical molecules (e.g., \(CO_2, BF_3\)) have \(\mu = 0\).

related_concepts.name: Polar Molecule
related_concepts.definition: A molecule with a non-zero net dipole moment.

subject: Chemistry
title: Formal Charge
description: Theoretical charge on an atom in a molecule. \(V\): valence e-, \(L\): lone pair e-, \(S\): shared e-.
derivation:
Method to determine the most stable Lewis structure (lowest FC is best).
Formula logic:
1. Start with atom's group number (Valence, \(V\)).
2. Subtract all non-bonding electrons owned entirely by the atom (\(L\)).
3. Subtract half of the bonding electrons (\(S/2\)), assuming equal sharing.
\(FC = V - (L + S/2)\)

related_concepts.name: Lewis Structure
related_concepts.definition: Diagram showing bonding between atoms and lone pairs of electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bond Order
description: Stability index from Molecular Orbital Theory. Higher BO = stronger bond.
derivation:
Bond Order represents the effective number of bonds.
\(N_b\): Number of electrons in Bonding Molecular Orbitals (Lower energy, stabilizing).
\(N_a\): Number of electrons in Antibonding Molecular Orbitals (Higher energy, destabilizing).
Net bonding interaction is excess of bonding over antibonding electrons, shared by 2 atoms.

related_concepts.name: Bond Length
related_concepts.definition: Inversely proportional to Bond Order (Higher BO = Shorter Bond).

subject: Chemistry
title: Hybridization (Steric Number)
description: Formula to predict hybridization. \(V\): Valence e-, \(M\): Monovalent atoms.
derivation:
Steric Number (SN) counts the number of electron domains around the central atom.
\(V\): Valence electrons of central atom.
\(M\): Add 1 for each monovalent atom (H, Cl, F) forming a sigma bond.
\(C\): Subtract charge if cation (lost electrons).
\(A\): Add charge if anion (gained electrons).
Result:
2=sp, 3=sp2, 4=sp3, 5=sp3d, 6=sp3d2.

related_concepts.name: VSEPR Theory
related_concepts.definition: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory, used to predict geometry based on steric number.

subject: Chemistry
title: Percentage Ionic Character
description: Hannay-Smith equation. Estimates ionic character based on electronegativity diff (\(\Delta \chi\)).
derivation:
Empirical relation.
If \(\Delta \chi = 0\) (e.g., H-H), ionic character is 0%.
If \(\Delta \chi = 1.7\), ionic character is approx 50%.
Term 1 (\(16\Delta\chi\)) accounts for linear dependence.
Term 2 (\(3.5\Delta\chi^2\)) corrects for larger differences.

related_concepts.name: Electronegativity
related_concepts.definition: Tendency of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fajan's Rule
description: Rules determining covalent character in ionic bonds due to polarization.
derivation:
No bond is 100% ionic. Cation distorts anion's electron cloud (Polarization).
Favorable conditions for Covalent Character:
1. Small Cation (High charge density).
2. Large Anion (Electrons loosely held, easy to distort).
3. High Charge on either ion.
4. Pseudo-noble gas config (\(ns^2 np^6 nd^{10}\)) of cation (e.g., Cu+, Ag+).

related_concepts.name: Polarizability
related_concepts.definition: The ease with which an anion's electron cloud can be distorted.

subject: Chemistry
title: MOT Energy Order (Z > 7)
description: Orbital filling order for $O_2$ and $F_2$.
derivation:
Due to large energy gap between 2s and 2p orbitals (high Zeff), there is no s-p mixing.
The $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital (head-on overlap) forms a strong bond and lowers in energy significantly, dropping below the $\pi$ orbitals.
Order: $\sigma_{1s} < \sigma^*_{1s} < \sigma_{2s} < \sigma^*_{2s} < \sigma_{2p_z} < \pi_{2p} < \pi^*_{2p} < \sigma^*_{2p_z}$.

related_concepts.name: s-p Mixing
related_concepts.definition: Interaction that raises the energy of $\sigma_{2p}$ above $\pi_{2p}$ for lighter elements ($B_2, C_2, N_2$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrogen Bonding Conditions
description: Requires H attached to electronegative X (F, O, N) and a lone pair on Y.
derivation:
Electrostatic attraction.
1. High electronegativity of X creates a strong partial positive charge ($\delta+$) on Hydrogen.
2. Small size of Hydrogen allows it to approach the lone pair of atom Y closely.
Strength: $F-H...F > O-H...N > N-H...N$.

related_concepts.name: Chelation
related_concepts.definition: Intramolecular Hydrogen bonding (e.g., o-nitrophenol) forms a ring-like structure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Back Bonding (p-pi - p-pi)
description: Donation of lone pair from substituent to empty orbital of central atom.
derivation:
Case $BF_3$: Boron has empty 2p orbital. Fluorine has filled 2p lone pair.
Overlap: $2p(B) - 2p(F)$ is effective due to similar size.
Electron density moves from F to B, satisfying B's electron deficiency.
This reduces Lewis Acid character.
In $BCl_3$, overlap is $2p(B) - 3p(Cl)$ (mismatched sizes), so back bonding is weak, acidity is higher.

related_concepts.name: Lewis Acid Strength
related_concepts.definition: $BF_3 < BCl_3 < BBr_3 < BI_3$.

subject: Chemistry
title: VSEPR Lone Pair Count
description: Lone pairs on central atom to predict shape. \(LP\)=lone pairs, \(V\)=valence electrons of central atom, \(B\)=electrons used in sigma bonds (one per bonded atom for single bonds).

subject: Chemistry
title: VSEPR Repulsion Order
description: Decreasing order of electron-pair repulsion strength governing bond-angle distortion. \(lp\)=lone pair, \(bp\)=bond pair.

subject: Chemistry
title: Unpaired Electrons (Magnetic)
description: Spin-only magnetic moment from MOT/unpaired electrons; \(\mu \neq 0 \Rightarrow\) paramagnetic. \(\mu\)=magnetic moment, \(n\)=number of unpaired electrons, BM=Bohr Magneton.

subject: Chemistry
title: s-Character vs Bond Angle
description: More s-character means greater bond angle and shorter, stronger bonds. \(\theta\)=bond angle; %s-character = 50, 33.3, 25 for \(sp, sp^2, sp^3\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Drago's Rule
description: For heavier p-block hydrides (central atom EN < 2.5, principal quantum number \(\ge 3\)), no hybridisation occurs; pure p-orbitals give ~90 degree bond angles (\(PH_3, H_2S, AsH_3\)). \(\chi\)=electronegativity.

subject: Chemistry
title: Born-Lande Lattice Energy
visual_data: U = -\frac{N_A M z^+ z^- e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r_0}\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)
description: Lattice energy of an ionic crystal. \(N_A\)=Avogadro number, \(M\)=Madelung constant, \(z^+ z^-\)=ionic charges, \(e\)=electron charge, \(r_0\)=interionic distance, \(n\)=Born exponent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lattice Energy Proportionality
description: Quick comparison of lattice energies: rises with ionic charges, falls with larger ion size. \(z\)=charge magnitude, \(r^+ + r^-\)=sum of ionic radii (interionic distance).

subject: Chemistry
title: Net Dipole of Symmetric Molecules
description: Vector sum of bond dipoles; cancels for symmetric geometry (\(CO_2, BF_3, CCl_4, SF_6\)) making them nonpolar. \(\vec{\mu}_i\)=individual bond dipole vectors.

subject: Chemistry
title: Resultant of Two Bond Dipoles
description: Magnitude of net dipole moment from two bond dipoles at angle \(\theta\). \(\mu_1, \mu_2\)=bond dipole moments, \(\theta\)=angle between them.

subject: Chemistry
title: Pauling Electronegativity Difference
description: Electronegativity gap from bond energies (\(\Delta\) in kcal/mol). \(\chi\)=Pauling electronegativity, \(\Delta = E_{A-B} - \sqrt{E_{A-A}\,E_{B-B}}\) (resonance/extra ionic energy).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mulliken Electronegativity
description: Electronegativity as average of ionisation energy and electron affinity. \(IE\)=ionisation energy, \(EA\)=electron affinity (both in same units, e.g. eV).

subject: Chemistry
title: Bond Length vs Bond Order
description: Higher bond order shortens and strengthens the bond. Order: \(C \equiv C < C = C < C - C\) in length; reverse in bond enthalpy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Covalent Bond Length
description: Schomaker-Stevenson estimate of covalent bond length. \(r_A, r_B\)=covalent radii (\(\mathring{A}\)), \(\chi_A, \chi_B\)=electronegativities; correction term shortens polar bonds.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bond Energy vs Order & Length
description: Relative bond strength: higher bond order (multiplicity) and shorter length mean stronger bond. Single < double < triple. \(\text{Bond energy}\)=enthalpy to break 1 mol of bonds (kJ/mol); \(\text{Bond order}\)=number of shared electron pairs.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reaction Enthalpy from Bond Energies
description: Heat of reaction from mean bond enthalpies (gaseous species). \(\Delta H_{rxn}\)=reaction enthalpy; \(E_{bonds\,broken}\)=energy of reactant bonds (endothermic, +); \(E_{bonds\,formed}\)=energy of product bonds (exothermic, -).

subject: Chemistry
title: s-Character in Hybrid Orbitals
description: Fractional s-character of a hybrid orbital; higher %s gives larger bond angle, more acidity and shorter/stronger bonds. \(x\)=number of p orbitals mixed (\(sp \to x=1\), \(sp^2 \to x=2\), \(sp^3 \to x=3\)). Values: \(sp\)=50%, \(sp^2\)=33.3%, \(sp^3\)=25%, \(sp^3d\)=20%, \(sp^3d^2\)=16.7%.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lucas Test
description: Distinguishes \(1^\circ, 2^\circ, 3^\circ\) alcohols based on turbidity rate.
derivation:
Reaction proceeds via SN1 mechanism involving Carbocation intermediate.
Rate depends on Carbocation Stability: \(3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ\).
1. \(3^\circ\): Stable carbocation, reacts instantly \(\rightarrow\) Immediate turbidity (insoluble alkyl halide).
2. \(2^\circ\): Less stable, takes ~5 mins.
3. \(1^\circ\): Unstable, no reaction at room temp (requires heat).

related_concepts.name: Carbocation Stability
related_concepts.definition: Stability order: Tertiary > Secondary > Primary > Methyl.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reimer-Tiemann Reaction
description: Formylation of phenol at ortho position.
derivation:
1. Electrophile Generation: \(OH^-\) removes H from \(CHCl_3\), Cl leaves \(\rightarrow :CCl_2\) (Dichlorocarbene).
2. Attack: Phenoxide ion attacks electron-deficient \(:CCl_2\) at ortho position.
3. Hydrolysis: The \(-CHCl_2\) group is hydrolyzed by alkali to \(-CHO\).
4. Acidification gives o-hydroxybenzaldehyde.

related_concepts.name: Carbene
related_concepts.definition: A neutral reactive intermediate containing a divalent carbon with six valence electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kolbe's Reaction
description: Carboxylation of phenol. Industrial method for Aspirin precursor.
derivation:
1. Phenol is treated with NaOH to form Phenoxide (stronger nucleophile).
2. Phenoxide attacks weak electrophile \(CO_2\) (O=C=O) at ortho position.
3. Tautomerization restores aromaticity.
4. Acidification yields Salicylic Acid (o-hydroxybenzoic acid).

related_concepts.name: Electrophilic Substitution
related_concepts.definition: A reaction where an electrophile replaces an atom (usually H) on an aromatic ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Williamson Ether Synthesis
description: Preparation of symmetrical and asymmetrical ethers via SN2.
derivation:
Mechanism: SN2 attack.
Alkoxide ion (\(RO^-\)) acts as Nucleophile.
Alkyl Halide (\(RX\)) acts as Substrate.
Constraint: The Alkyl Halide must be Primary (\(1^\circ\)).
If RX is \(3^\circ\), Elimination dominates over Substitution (forming alkene instead of ether) because alkoxides are also strong bases.

related_concepts.name: Elimination Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Removal of atoms to form a double bond, competing with substitution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dehydration of Alcohols
description: Elimination of water to form alkene. Mechanism involves carbocation.
derivation:
Mechanism:
1. Protonation: Alcohol accepts H+ \(\rightarrow R-OH_2^+\) (Good leaving group).
2. Formation of Carbocation (Slow): Water leaves \(\rightarrow R^+\).
3. Elimination: H+ is removed from adjacent carbon to form double bond.
Note: At lower temp (413K), substitution competes to form Ether.

related_concepts.name: Saytzeff Rule
related_concepts.definition: In elimination, the more substituted alkene (more stable) is the major product.

subject: Chemistry
title: Victor Meyer Test
description: Colorimetric test to distinguish primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols.
derivation:
Reaction Sequence:
1. Alcohol \(\xrightarrow{P/I_2}\) Alkyl Iodide.
2. Alkyl Iodide \(\xrightarrow{AgNO_2}\) Nitroalkane.
3. Nitroalkane treated with \(HNO_2\) (Nitrous Acid) then NaOH.

Results:
- \(1^\circ\) (Primary): Forms Nitrolic Acid \(\rightarrow\) Dissolves in NaOH \(\rightarrow\) **Red** color.
- \(2^\circ\) (Secondary): Forms Pseudonitrole \(\rightarrow\) Insoluble \(\rightarrow\) **Blue** color.
- \(3^\circ\) (Tertiary): No H on \(\alpha\)-carbon \(\rightarrow\) No reaction with \(HNO_2\) \(\rightarrow\) **Colorless**.

related_concepts.name: Alpha Hydrogen
related_concepts.definition: A hydrogen atom attached to the carbon atom adjacent to a functional group.

subject: Chemistry
title: PCC (Pyridinium Chlorochromate)
description: Selective oxidation of primary alcohols to Aldehydes (stops here).
derivation:
Reagent: \(CrO_3 + HCl + Pyridine\).
Key Feature: Anhydrous conditions (usually in \(CH_2Cl_2\)).
Logic:
Since water is absent, the intermediate Aldehyde cannot form the Gem-diol hydrate.
Without the hydrate, the second oxidation step to Carboxylic acid is impossible.
Thus, reaction stops at Aldehyde.

related_concepts.name: Collins Reagent
related_concepts.definition: CrO3 with 2 Pyridine molecules, also used for stopping oxidation at aldehyde.

subject: Chemistry
title: Claisen Rearrangement
description: [3,3]-Sigmatropic rearrangement. Intramolecular migration.
derivation:
Thermal Concerted Mechanism:
1. The $\pi$-bond of the allyl group attacks the benzene ring at the ortho position.
2. Simultaneously, the C-O bond breaks and the C-C bond forms (cyclic transition state).
3. Tautomerization: The intermediate ketone enolizes to restore aromaticity, yielding the Phenol.
Note: If ortho positions are blocked, migration occurs to para position.

related_concepts.name: Sigmatropic Shift
related_concepts.definition: Pericyclic reaction where a sigma bond migrates across a pi system.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fries Rearrangement
description: Conversion of Phenolic Esters to Acyl Phenols.
derivation:
Mechanism involves Lewis Acid ($AlCl_3$).
1. Complexation: $AlCl_3$ coordinates with ester oxygen.
2. Cleavage: Acylium ion ($RCO^+$) is generated.
3. Electrophilic Attack: $RCO^+$ attacks the ring at Ortho/Para positions.
Temperature Effect: Low temp favors Para; High temp favors Ortho (Thermodynamic product, chelation stabilized).

related_concepts.name: Acylium Ion
related_concepts.definition: Resonance stabilized cation ($R-C^+=O \leftrightarrow R-C\equiv O^+$).

subject: Chemistry
title: MnO2 Oxidation
description: Selective oxidation of Allylic and Benzylic alcohols to Aldehydes/Ketones.
derivation:
Manganese Dioxide ($MnO_2$) acts as a mild oxidant.
Selectivity:
It oxidizes -OH groups activated by a double bond or benzene ring (Allylic/Benzylic).
It leaves ordinary primary/secondary alcohols and double bonds untouched at room temperature.

related_concepts.name: Chemo-selectivity
related_concepts.definition: Preferential reaction of a reagent with one functional group over another.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ester Hydrolysis (Saponification)
description: Base-catalyzed hydrolysis. Irreversible. $B_{AC}2$ mechanism.
derivation:
Mechanism: $B_{AC}2$ (Base catalyzed, Acyl cleavage, Bimolecular).
1. Attack: $OH^-$ attacks Carbonyl carbon (Tetrahedral intermediate).
2. Elimination: Alkoxide ($R'O^-$) leaves, forming Carboxylic Acid ($RCOOH$).
3. Acid-Base (Irreversible): Strong base $R'O^-$ deprotonates the acid instantly.
   Forms stable Carboxylate ion ($RCOO^-$) and Alcohol ($R'OH$).

related_concepts.name: Saponification Value
related_concepts.definition: Mg of KOH required to saponify 1g of fat/oil.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acid-Catalysed Hydration
description: Markovnikov addition of water to alkene giving alcohol. \(H^+\)=acid catalyst (dil. \(H_2SO_4\)).
derivation:
1. Protonation of alkene \(\rightarrow\) more stable carbocation (Markovnikov).
2. Nucleophilic attack of \(H_2O\) on \(C^+\).
3. Deprotonation gives alcohol.
Note: Rearrangement possible; \(-OH\) adds to more substituted carbon.

related_concepts.name: Markovnikov Rule
related_concepts.definition: In addition to unsymmetrical alkenes, the negative part (OH) adds to the carbon bearing fewer hydrogens.

subject: Chemistry
title: Esterification (Fischer)
description: Acid-catalysed reversible formation of ester from acid and alcohol. \(H^+\) (conc. \(H_2SO_4\)) catalyst.
derivation:
Acyl-oxygen cleavage (\(AAc2\)): the \(-OH\) of acid is lost as water (proved by isotopic \(^{18}O\) labelling of alcohol appearing in ester).
Reversible; driven forward by excess reactant or removing \(H_2O\).

related_concepts.name: Reactivity Order
related_concepts.definition: Esterification rate of alcohols: 1° > 2° > 3° (steric).

subject: Chemistry
title: Reaction with HX (1° vs 3°)
description: Alcohol to alkyl halide. Reactivity \(3^\circ>2^\circ>1^\circ\); \(HX\): \(HI>HBr>HCl\).
derivation:
1° alcohols: SN2 (no carbocation, no rearrangement).
3° alcohols: SN1 via carbocation (fast, gives turbidity in Lucas test).
HCl needs \(ZnCl_2\) (Lucas reagent) for 1°/2°.

related_concepts.name: Leaving Group
related_concepts.definition: Protonation converts poor -OH into good leaving group -OH2+ (water).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation of Alcohols
description: Strong oxidant fully oxidises \(1^\circ\) alcohol to acid; \(2^\circ\) to ketone; \(3^\circ\) resists.
derivation:
1° alcohol \(\rightarrow\) aldehyde \(\rightarrow\) carboxylic acid (strong oxidant, full).
2° alcohol \(\rightarrow\) ketone (no further easy oxidation).
3° alcohol: no \(\alpha\)-H \(\rightarrow\) resistant; oxidises only under drastic conditions with C-C cleavage.

related_concepts.name: Cu / 573K Dehydrogenation
related_concepts.definition: 1° → aldehyde, 2° → ketone, 3° → alkene (dehydration), on heated copper.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dehydration Ease & Order
description: Relative ease of acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols to alkenes via carbocation stability.

related_concepts.name: Saytzeff Product
related_concepts.definition: More substituted (more stable) alkene predominates.

subject: Chemistry
title: Phenol from Diazonium
description: Hydrolysis of benzenediazonium salt to phenol on warming with dilute acid.

related_concepts.name: Diazonium Salt
related_concepts.definition: ArN2+ from aniline + NaNO2/HCl at 273-278K; versatile aryl precursor.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bromination of Phenol
description: Phenol with bromine water gives white ppt of 2,4,6-tribromophenol (no catalyst needed).
derivation:
In water, phenol ionises slightly to highly activating phenoxide \(\rightarrow\) very fast multi-substitution.
In \(CS_2\) (non-polar, low temp) only mono-bromination \(\rightarrow\) mainly p-bromophenol.

related_concepts.name: -OH Activation
related_concepts.definition: OH is strongly activating and o/p-directing via +M effect, increasing ring electron density.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitration of Phenol
description: Dilute \(HNO_3\) gives o-/p-nitrophenol; conc. \(HNO_3\) gives picric acid.

related_concepts.name: o/p Separation
related_concepts.definition: o-nitrophenol is steam-volatile (intramolecular H-bond); p-isomer is not (intermolecular H-bond).

subject: Chemistry
title: Acidity Order (Phenols)
description: EWG (\(-NO_2\)) at o/p increases phenol acidity; EDG (\(-CH_3\)) decreases it.
derivation:
Acidity \(\propto\) stability of conjugate base (phenoxide / alkoxide).
Phenoxide is resonance-stabilised \(\rightarrow\) phenol (pKa~10) >> alcohol (pKa~16).
o-/p-\(NO_2\) delocalises negative charge \(\rightarrow\) more acidic; m-\(NO_2\) only -I, less effect.

related_concepts.name: pKa Values
related_concepts.definition: Phenol ≈ 10, picric acid ≈ 0.4, ethanol ≈ 16, water ≈ 15.7.

subject: Chemistry
title: Azo Coupling of Phenol
description: Phenol couples with diazonium salt at para position giving orange azo dye.

related_concepts.name: Coupling Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Electrophilic substitution of activated arene (phenol/aniline) by weak diazonium electrophile; mildly alkaline medium for phenol.

subject: Chemistry
title: Phenol to Salicylaldehyde vs Salicylic Acid
description: Reimer-Tiemann variant: \(CHCl_3\) gives salicylaldehyde; \(CCl_4\) gives salicylic acid.

related_concepts.name: Trichloromethyl Carbanion
related_concepts.definition: CCl4 gives :CCl3-derived electrophile leading to -CCl3 then -COOH on hydrolysis.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reduction of Phenol
description: Phenol distilled with zinc dust gives benzene (removes -OH as ZnO).

related_concepts.name: Hydrogenation
related_concepts.definition: Phenol + H2 / Ni → cyclohexanol (ring reduction, different product).

subject: Chemistry
title: Ether Cleavage by HI
description: Hot conc. HI cleaves ether; smaller alkyl gives iodide (\(1^\circ\) by SN2).
derivation:
1. Protonation of ether oxygen \(\rightarrow\) good leaving group.
2. I- attacks SN2 at less hindered carbon \(\rightarrow\) smaller R-I + larger R'-OH.
3. With excess HI / 3° or aryl ether, the alkyl part forms iodide and aryl part stays as phenol.

related_concepts.name: Anisole Cleavage
related_concepts.definition: C6H5-O-CH3 + HI → C6H5OH + CH3I (aryl-O bond not cleaved; phenol forms).

subject: Chemistry
title: Ether from Dehydration (Bimolecular)
description: Low-temp acid dehydration of \(1^\circ\) alcohol gives symmetrical ether (SN2).

related_concepts.name: Temperature Control
related_concepts.definition: 413K → ether (substitution); 443K → alkene (elimination). Only good for 1° alcohols.

subject: Chemistry
title: Friedel-Crafts on Anisole
description: \(-OCH_3\) is activating, o/p-directing; alkylation/acylation gives mainly para product.

related_concepts.name: -OR Directing
related_concepts.definition: Alkoxy group donates electrons by +M, activating ortho/para positions; para favoured by sterics.

subject: Chemistry
title: Boiling Point Trend
description: Alcohols boil higher than ethers/alkanes of similar mass due to intermolecular H-bonding.
derivation:
Alcohols: strong O-H...O hydrogen bonds \(\rightarrow\) high b.p.
Ethers: no O-H, only dipole-dipole \(\rightarrow\) b.p. close to alkanes.
Branching lowers b.p. (less surface area).

related_concepts.name: Hydrogen Bonding
related_concepts.definition: O-H...O attraction raises b.p. and water-solubility of lower alcohols.

subject: Chemistry
title: Liebermann Nitroso Test
description: Confirmatory test for phenols (with free o/p position) via nitroso/indophenol colour.

related_concepts.name: Indophenol
related_concepts.definition: Coloured condensation product responsible for the characteristic colour change.

subject: Chemistry
title: NaBH4 / LiAlH4 Reduction to Alcohol
description: Hydride reduction of carbonyls to alcohols: aldehyde -> 1\(^\circ\), ketone -> 2\(^\circ\) alcohol. \(NaBH_4\)=mild, reduces only aldehyde/ketone; \(LiAlH_4\)=strong, also reduces acid/ester/acid-chloride to alcohol.

related_concepts.name: Selectivity
related_concepts.definition: NaBH4 leaves -COOH, -COOR, -C=C and -NO2 untouched; LiAlH4 reduces -COOH/-COOR/-CONH2 to alcohol/amine.

related_concepts.name: Catalytic H2
related_concepts.definition: H2/Ni (or Pt, Pd) also reduces >C=O to alcohol but simultaneously reduces C=C double bonds.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydroboration-Oxidation
description: Anti-Markovnikov, syn hydration of alkenes; -OH adds to the less-substituted carbon with no rearrangement. \(BH_3\)=borane (B goes to less hindered C), \(H_2O_2/OH^-\)=oxidative work-up retaining position with retention of configuration.

related_concepts.name: Regiochemistry
related_concepts.definition: Net anti-Markovnikov: OH on terminal (less substituted) carbon; opposite of acid-catalysed hydration.

related_concepts.name: Stereochemistry
related_concepts.definition: Syn addition of H and OH across the same face; oxidation proceeds with retention of configuration at C.

related_concepts.name: No rearrangement
related_concepts.definition: No carbocation intermediate, so no hydride/alkyl shifts (unlike acid hydration).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxymercuration-Demercuration
description: Markovnikov hydration of alkene WITHOUT rearrangement; OH goes to more substituted carbon. \(Hg(OAc)_2\)=mercuric acetate (forms bridged mercurinium ion, no free carbocation), \(NaBH_4\)=removes Hg (demercuration).

related_concepts.name: vs Acid hydration
related_concepts.definition: Same Markovnikov product but oxymercuration avoids carbocation rearrangements that plague H+/H2O hydration.

related_concepts.name: vs Hydroboration
related_concepts.definition: Opposite regiochemistry to hydroboration-oxidation (Markovnikov vs anti-Markovnikov).

related_concepts.name: Mercurinium ion
related_concepts.definition: Cyclic bridged intermediate; water attacks more substituted carbon -> Markovnikov, anti addition.

subject: Chemistry
title: Williamson Synthesis: 3deg Halide Failure
description: Why unsymmetrical ethers must use 1\(^\circ\) halide + alkoxide: bulky alkoxide on a 3\(^\circ\) halide gives elimination (alkene), not ether. SN2 needs the less hindered carbon, so pick CH\(_3\)/1\(^\circ\) R-X.

related_concepts.name: SN2 vs E2 trap
related_concepts.definition: Alkoxide is a strong base; with 3deg/hindered R-X, E2 elimination dominates over SN2 substitution.

related_concepts.name: Correct disconnection
related_concepts.definition: For t-Bu methyl ether use CH3-X + (CH3)3C-O- Na+, NOT (CH3)3C-X + CH3O-.

related_concepts.name: Aryl ethers
related_concepts.definition: Aryl/vinyl halides cannot be used as the R-X (no SN2 on sp2 C); use aryl alkoxide (ArO-) + alkyl halide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kucherov Reaction (Alkyne Hydration)
description: Markovnikov hydration of alkynes via enol that tautomerizes to carbonyl. Acetylene gives acetaldehyde; any other terminal/internal alkyne gives a ketone. \(HgSO_4/H_2SO_4\)=catalyst.

related_concepts.name: Tautomerism
related_concepts.definition: Unstable enol (vinyl alcohol) rapidly rearranges to the more stable keto form.

related_concepts.name: Product rule
related_concepts.definition: Acetylene -> acetaldehyde (only aldehyde); all higher alkynes -> ketones.

subject: Chemistry
title: Rosenmund Reduction
description: Selective hydrogenation of acid chlorides to aldehydes using Lindlar's catalyst.
derivation:
Catalytic hydrogenation usually reduces carbonyls all the way to alcohols.
To stop at the Aldehyde stage, the catalyst activity is lowered ('poisoned').
Catalyst: Palladium (Pd) deposited on Barium Sulfate (\(BaSO_4\)).
Poison: Sulfur or Quinoline.
This prevents further reduction: \(RCHO \nrightarrow RCH_2OH\).

related_concepts.name: Lindlar's Catalyst
related_concepts.definition: A heterogeneous catalyst used for selective hydrogenation of alkynes to cis-alkenes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Stephen Reaction
description: Preparation of aldehydes from nitriles via an imine intermediate.
derivation:
1. Reduction: Stannous chloride (\(SnCl_2\)) and HCl generate nascent hydrogen.
   \(SnCl_2 + 2HCl \rightarrow SnCl_4 + 2[H]\)
2. Imine Formation: Nitrile (\(R-C\equiv N\)) is reduced to Imine hydrochloride (\(R-CH=NH\cdot HCl\)).
3. Hydrolysis: Boiling with water converts the imine to aldehyde.
   \(R-CH=NH + H_2O \rightarrow RCHO + NH_3\)

related_concepts.name: Partial Reduction
related_concepts.definition: Stopping a reduction reaction at an intermediate oxidation state.

subject: Chemistry
title: Etard Reaction
description: Oxidation of Toluene to Benzaldehyde using Chromyl Chloride.
derivation:
1. Chromyl chloride (\(CrO_2Cl_2\)) attacks the methyl group of toluene.
2. Formation of brown Chromium Complex (precipitate):
   \(Ph-CH(OCrOHCl_2)_2\)
3. Hydrolysis: The complex is decomposed by water to give Benzaldehyde.
Solvent \(CS_2\) or \(CCl_4\) is used as it is non-polar.

related_concepts.name: Mild Oxidation
related_concepts.definition: Oxidation that stops at the aldehyde/ketone stage without proceeding to carboxylic acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gatterman-Koch Reaction
description: Formylation of benzene ring (Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution).
derivation:
1. Generation of Electrophile:
   Carbon monoxide (CO) and HCl react in situ to form Formyl Chloride (unstable).
   \(CO + HCl \rightleftharpoons HCOCl\)
   Lewis acid \(AlCl_3\) helps generate the electrophile \([HCO]^+ \leftrightarrow [C^+=O]\).
2. Attack: Benzene attacks the formyl cation.
3. Restoration: Loss of proton restores aromaticity, yielding Benzaldehyde.

related_concepts.name: Friedel-Crafts Acylation
related_concepts.definition: Similar mechanism using RCOCl to add an acyl group.

subject: Chemistry
title: Clemmensen Reduction
description: Deoxygenation of carbonyl group to methylene. Uses Acidic medium.
derivation:
Mechanism involves electron transfer from Zinc metal surface.
1. Carbonyl oxygen is protonated by acid.
2. Zn donates electrons to Carbon, C-O bond breaks.
3. Sequential protonation and electron transfer reduce \(C=O\) to \(CH_2\).
Constraint: Cannot be used if the molecule contains acid-sensitive groups (like -OH, -C=C-).

related_concepts.name: Amalgam
related_concepts.definition: An alloy of mercury with another metal (Zn-Hg), used to moderate the reactivity of the metal.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
description: Deoxygenation of carbonyl group to methylene. Uses Basic medium.
derivation:
1. Hydrazone Formation: Ketone reacts with Hydrazine (\(NH_2NH_2\)).
   \(C=O + H_2NNH_2 \rightarrow C=N-NH_2\)
2. Base Catalysis: KOH removes protons from the -NH2 group.
3. Nitrogen Elimination: \(N_2\) gas leaves (entropy driver).
4. Protonation: The carbon picks up protons from solvent (Ethylene Glycol) to become \(CH_2\).

related_concepts.name: Nucleophilic Addition-Elimination
related_concepts.definition: Mechanism where nucleophile adds to C=O, followed by loss of water (e.g., imine formation).

subject: Chemistry
title: Aldol Condensation
description: Reaction of aldehydes/ketones with \(\alpha\)-hydrogen. Forms \(\beta\)-hydroxy aldehyde.
derivation:
1. Enolate Formation: Base (OH-) removes acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogen.
   \(CH_3CHO \rightarrow [\cdot CH_2CHO]^-\)
2. Nucleophilic Attack: Enolate attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule.
3. Protonation: Forms 'Aldol' (Aldehyde + Alcohol).
4. Condensation (Heating): Water is eliminated (E1cB mechanism) to form an \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated aldehyde (stable due to conjugation).

related_concepts.name: Cross Aldol
related_concepts.definition: Condensation between two different aldehydes/ketones. Gives 4 products if both have alpha-H.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cannizzaro Reaction
description: Disproportionation (Self-Redox) of aldehydes with NO \(\alpha\)-hydrogen.
derivation:
1. Nucleophilic Attack: OH- attacks Carbonyl C (High conc NaOH drives this).
   Forms a dianion intermediate.
2. Hydride Transfer (RDS): A hydride ion (\(H^-\)) shifts from the intermediate to the carbonyl carbon of the second molecule.
3. Result: One molecule is Oxidized (Acid salt) and one is Reduced (Alcohol).
   \(HCHO \rightarrow HCOO^-\)
   \(HCHO \rightarrow CH_3OH\)

related_concepts.name: Disproportionation
related_concepts.definition: A redox reaction where the same element is simultaneously oxidized and reduced.

subject: Chemistry
title: HVZ Reaction
description: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky. Halogenation at the \(\alpha\)-carbon of carboxylic acids.
derivation:
Mechanism relies on the formation of Acyl Halide.
1. P + \(X_2\) forms \(PX_3\), which converts Acid to Acid Halide (\(RCH_2COX\)).
2. Enolization: Acid halides enolize more easily than acids.
3. Halogenation: \(X_2\) attacks the enol to substitute alpha-H.
4. Hydrolysis: The acid halide hydrolyzes back to Carboxylic Acid upon workup.

related_concepts.name: Alpha Substitution
related_concepts.definition: Substitution reaction occurring at the carbon atom adjacent to the functional group.

subject: Chemistry
title: Soda-Lime Decarboxylation
description: Removal of \(CO_2\) to form an alkane with one less carbon atom.
derivation:
Mechanism involves Carbanion intermediate.
1. Heat causes loss of \(CO_2\) from the carboxylate ion.
2. Formation of unstable Carbanion (\(R^-\)).
3. Rapid protonation from moisture or solvent to form Alkane (\(R-H\)).
Role of CaO: Keeps NaOH dry (hygroscopic) and keeps the fusion mix porous.

related_concepts.name: Step Down Reaction
related_concepts.definition: A reaction series that reduces the length of the carbon chain.

subject: Chemistry
title: Jones Reagent
description: Strong oxidizing agent. Converts \(1^\circ\) alcohols to carboxylic acids.
derivation:
Composition: \(CrO_3 + H_2SO_4\) in Acetone.
Mechanism:
1. Formation of Chromate Ester between Alcohol and Chromic Acid.
2. Elimination (E2-like): Water removes alpha-hydrogen.
3. Forms Aldehyde.
4. In presence of water (acidic medium), Aldehyde hydrates to Gem-diol.
5. Gem-diol oxidizes further to Carboxylic Acid.

related_concepts.name: Oxidation State
related_concepts.definition: Chromium reduces from +6 (Orange) to +3 (Green).

subject: Chemistry
title: Lithium Aluminium Hydride
description: Strong reducing agent. Reduces acids, esters, amides, nitriles.
derivation:
Source of Nucleophilic Hydride (\(H^-\)).
Al-H bond is polar (Al is +ve, H is -ve).
1. \(H^-\) attacks the carbonyl carbon (Nucleophilic Addition).
2. Leaving group leaves (if acid/ester).
3. Second \(H^-\) attack reduces it to alkoxide.
4. Workup with water gives alcohol.
Caution: Reacts violently with water/alcohol (must use dry ether).

related_concepts.name: Sodium Borohydride
related_concepts.definition: Weaker reducer. Only reduces Aldehydes/Ketones. Safe in protic solvents.

subject: Chemistry
title: DIBAL-H
description: Selective reduction of Esters and Nitriles to Aldehydes.
derivation:
Full Name: Di-isobutyl Aluminium Hydride.
Mechanism:
1. Steric Bulk: Two large isobutyl groups prevent the reagent from attacking twice.
2. Complexation: Forms a stable Aluminium-Nitrogen intermediate at low temp (-78°C).
3. Hydrolysis: The intermediate breaks down upon adding water to yield Aldehyde.
If warmed, it may reduce fully to amine/alcohol.

related_concepts.name: Partial Reduction
related_concepts.definition: Stopping a reduction reaction at a specific intermediate stage.

subject: Chemistry
title: Pinacol-Pinacolone Rearrangement
description: Acid catalyzed conversion of Vicinal Diols to Ketones involving Methyl shift.
derivation:
1. Protonation: One -OH group accepts $H^+$ and leaves as water ($H_2O$).
2. Carbocation Formation: A stable tertiary carbocation forms.
3. 1,2-Methyl Shift: Alkyl group migrates to the cation to form a more stable cation (Octet complete on Oxygen via Resonance).
   $C^+(OH)-C(Me) \rightarrow C(=O^+H)-C(Me)$.
4. Deprotonation: Yields Pinacolone (t-butyl methyl ketone).

related_concepts.name: Migratory Aptitude
related_concepts.definition: Order of group migration: Aryl > Alkyl (Tertiary > Secondary > Primary) > Methyl.

subject: Chemistry
title: Tischenko Reaction
description: Modified Cannizzaro reaction. All aldehydes (with or w/o alpha-H) form Esters.
derivation:
Reagent: Aluminium Ethoxide.
Mechanism:
1. Similar to Cannizzaro (hydride transfer).
2. Instead of forming separate Alcohol and Acid, the intermediate coordinates with Aluminium.
3. Hydride transfer occurs intermolecularly or intramolecularly to form an Ester directly.
Example: Acetaldehyde $\to$ Ethyl Acetate.

related_concepts.name: Disproportionation
related_concepts.definition: One molecule oxidized to acid part, one reduced to alcohol part, combined as ester.

subject: Chemistry
title: Benzoin Condensation
description: Self-condensation of aromatic aldehydes to alpha-hydroxy ketone (Benzoin).
derivation:
Catalyst: Cyanide ion ($CN^-$).
1. Nucleophilic attack: $CN^-$ attacks Carbonyl.
2. Umpolung: The intermediate carbanion is stabilized by resonance with -CN.
3. Attack 2: Carbanion attacks second aldehyde molecule.
4. Proton Transfer & Elimination of $CN^-$.
Result: Formation of new C-C bond.

related_concepts.name: Umpolung
related_concepts.definition: Reversal of polarity of a functional group (Carbonyl carbon acts as nucleophile).

subject: Chemistry
title: Perkin Reaction
description: Condensation of aromatic aldehyde with acid anhydride to form Cinnamic Acid.
derivation:
Base: Acetate ion (from salt).
1. Base creates carbanion from anhydride ($\alpha$-hydrogen).
2. Carbanion attacks aldehyde carbonyl.
3. Intramolecular acylation and subsequent hydrolysis/dehydration.
Product: $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carboxylic acid.

related_concepts.name: Cinnamic Acid
related_concepts.definition: 3-Phenylprop-2-enoic acid, common product of Perkin reaction.

subject: Chemistry
title: Beckmann Rearrangement
description: Conversion of Ketoxime to N-substituted Amide.
derivation:
1. Protonation of -OH group of oxime -> leaves as water.
2. Migration: The alkyl group *anti* (trans) to the leaving -OH group migrates to Nitrogen.
   Simultaneous C-N bond formation and C-C bond breaking.
3. Hydrolysis of the resulting nitrilium ion gives the amide.
Stereospecific reaction.

related_concepts.name: Caprolactam
related_concepts.definition: Monomer for Nylon-6, produced via Beckmann rearrangement of cyclohexanone oxime.

subject: Chemistry
title: Heating Effect (Dicarboxylic Acids)
description: Blanc's Rule regarding ring size stability.
derivation:
Behavior depends on $n$ (carbon chain length):
- $n=0, 1$ (Oxalic, Malonic): Loss of $CO_2$ (Decarboxylation).
  Example: Oxalic $\to CO + CO_2 + H_2O$.
- $n=2, 3$ (Succinic, Glutaric): Loss of $H_2O$ to form Cyclic Anhydride (5, 6 membered rings).
- $n=4, 5$ (Adipic, Pimelic): Loss of $CO_2 + H_2O$ to form Cyclic Ketone (5, 6 membered rings).

related_concepts.name: Blanc's Rule
related_concepts.definition: Formation of 5- and 6-membered rings is favored upon heating dicarboxylic acids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Periodic Acid Oxidation (HIO4)
description: Oxidative cleavage of Vicinal Diols (Glycols). Malaprade Reaction.
derivation:
Mechanism:
1. Formation of cyclic periodate ester intermediate.
2. C-C bond cleavage occurs.
3. The -OH groups are oxidized to Carbonyls.
Requirement: -OH or =O groups must be on adjacent carbons.
Note: $HCOOH$ is formed if terminal $CH_2OH$ is present.

related_concepts.name: Lead Tetraacetate (LTA)
related_concepts.definition: Pb(OAc)4 performs similar cleavage of 1,2-diols.

subject: Chemistry
title: Claisen Condensation
description: Reaction of esters with $\alpha$-hydrogen to form $\beta$-keto esters.
derivation:
1. Enolate Formation: Strong base ($EtO^-$) removes $\alpha$-H from ester.
2. Nucleophilic Attack: Enolate attacks carbonyl of second ester molecule.
3. Elimination: Ethoxide ion ($EtO^-$) leaves, restoring double bond (C=O).
4. Acidification: Final workup gives $\beta$-keto ester.
Constraint: Requires at least 2 $\alpha$-hydrogens to prevent base hydrolysis consuming the product.

related_concepts.name: Dieckmann Condensation
related_concepts.definition: Intramolecular Claisen condensation producing a cyclic $\beta$-keto ester.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reformatsky Reaction
description: Organozinc reaction. Less reactive than Grignard, tolerates ester groups.
derivation:
1. Organozinc Formation: $\alpha$-bromoester reacts with Zinc dust.
   $Br-CH_2-COOEt + Zn \rightarrow Br-Zn-CH_2-COOEt$ (Zinc Enolate).
2. Nucleophilic Attack: C-Zn bond acts as nucleophile attacking Aldehyde/Ketone carbonyl.
3. Hydrolysis: Acid workup yields $\beta$-hydroxy ester.
Note: Magnesium (Grignard) would attack the ester group itself; Zn does not.

related_concepts.name: Organometallic
related_concepts.definition: Compounds containing a direct Metal-Carbon bond.

subject: Chemistry
title: Knoevenagel Condensation
description: Condensation of aldehyde with active methylene compound (e.g., Malonic Acid).
derivation:
Reagents: Weak base (Pyridine/Piperidine).
Active Methylene: $Z-CH_2-Z'$ where Z is Electron Withdrawing ($COOH, CN, COOR$).
1. Base removes proton from active methylene $\rightarrow$ Carbanion.
2. Attack on Aldehyde Carbonyl.
3. Dehydration leads to $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated product.
If Malonic acid is used, heating causes decarboxylation $\rightarrow$ Cinnamic acid derivative.

related_concepts.name: Active Methylene
related_concepts.definition: A CH2 group flanked by two electron-withdrawing groups, making hydrogens acidic.

subject: Chemistry
title: Baeyer-Villiger Oxidation
description: Oxidation of Ketones to Esters using Peroxyacids (e.g., m-CPBA).
derivation:
Mechanism: Nucleophilic attack of peracid on carbonyl.
1. Criegee Intermediate forms.
2. Rearrangement: Alkyl group migrates from Carbon to Oxygen.
   Migratory Aptitude: $3^\circ Alkyl > 2^\circ > Phenyl > 1^\circ > Methyl$.
   The group best able to stabilize positive charge migrates.
3. Result: Insertion of Oxygen to form Ester.

related_concepts.name: Peroxyacid
related_concepts.definition: Acid containing an acidic -OOH group (e.g., Peracetic acid, Trifluoroperacetic acid).

subject: Chemistry
title: Michael Addition
description: Thermodynamic 1,4-addition of a nucleophile (Michael Donor) to an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carbonyl (Michael Acceptor).
derivation:
1. Donor Formation: Base removes proton from active methylene (e.g., Malonic ester) $\rightarrow$ Enolate.
2. Attack: Enolate attacks the $\beta$-carbon of the $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated system.
   Reason: Soft nucleophiles prefer Soft electrophilic centers ($\beta$-carbon) over Hard centers (Carbonyl C).
3. Protonation: Enol tautomerizes to stable Ketone.

related_concepts.name: Robinson Annulation
related_concepts.definition: Michael addition followed by Intramolecular Aldol condensation to form a 6-membered ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: MPV Reduction
description: Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction. Selective reduction of Ketones to Secondary Alcohols.
derivation:
Mechanism: Hydride Transfer via Cyclic Transition State.
1. Coordination: Carbonyl oxygen binds to Aluminum of Aluminum Isopropoxide.
2. Hydride Shift: A hydride ion ($H^-$) transfers from the Isopropoxide group to the Ketone carbonyl carbon via a 6-membered cyclic transition state.
3. Result: Ketone becomes Alcohol (after hydrolysis); Isopropoxide becomes Acetone (oxidized).

related_concepts.name: Oppenauer Oxidation
related_concepts.definition: The reverse reaction. Uses Aluminum t-butoxide to oxidize alcohols to ketones.

subject: Chemistry
title: Benzilic Acid Rearrangement
description: Conversion of 1,2-Diketone (Benzil) to $\alpha$-Hydroxy Acid salt (Benzilate).
derivation:
1. Nucleophilic Attack: $OH^-$ attacks one carbonyl carbon.
2. 1,2-Phenyl Shift: The Phenyl group migrates to the adjacent carbonyl carbon (which is electron deficient).
   Driving Force: Formation of stable Carboxylate anion.
3. Proton Transfer: Rapid intramolecular proton transfer from -OH to alkoxide oxygen.

related_concepts.name: Intramolecular Redox
related_concepts.definition: One carbon is oxidized (to acid), the other reduced (to alcohol).

subject: Chemistry
title: Arndt-Eistert Synthesis
description: Homologation of carboxylic acid (adding one CH2 unit).
derivation:
1. Acid Chloride formation.
2. Diazomethane ($CH_2N_2$) addition forms Diazoketone.
3. Wolff Rearrangement ($Ag_2O, \Delta$): Loss of $N_2$ generates Ketene ($R-CH=C=O$).
4. Hydration: Ketene reacts with water to form higher Homologue Acid.

related_concepts.name: Wolff Rearrangement
related_concepts.definition: Key step converting alpha-diazoketones into ketenes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Tollens' Test (Silver Mirror)
description: Distinguishes aldehydes (positive, silver mirror) from ketones (negative). \(R\)=alkyl/aryl; \([Ag(NH_3)_2]^+\)=Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal \(AgNO_3\)); \(Ag\)=metallic silver mirror.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fehling's Test
description: Detects aliphatic aldehydes (red-brown \(Cu_2O\) ppt); aromatic aldehydes & ketones do not respond. \(Cu^{2+}\)=cupric tartrate complex (Fehling's A+B); \(Cu_2O\)=cuprous oxide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Iodoform Test (Haloform Reaction)
description: Confirms methyl ketones / \(CH_3CH(OH)-\) groups; gives yellow \(CHI_3\). \(R\)=H, alkyl or aryl (not \(OH\)/\(OR\)); \(CHI_3\)=iodoform (yellow ppt). Acetaldehyde, ethanol also give positive test.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nucleophilic Addition of HCN
description: Forms cyanohydrins; reactivity \(HCHO > CH_3CHO > \) ketones. \(\rangle C=O\)=carbonyl; product=cyanohydrin (\(\alpha\)-hydroxynitrile), useful for one-carbon ascent to \(\alpha\)-hydroxy acids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bisulphite Addition
description: Forms crystalline bisulphite adduct; used to purify/separate aldehydes & methyl ketones (regenerated by dil. acid/base). \(NaHSO_3\)=sodium bisulphite; adduct=white crystalline solid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acetal / Ketal Formation
description: Protects carbonyl as acetal (from aldehyde) / ketal (from ketone); stable to base, hydrolysed by aqueous acid. \(R'OH\)=alcohol; \(\rangle C(OR')_2\)=gem-diether (protecting group).

subject: Chemistry
title: Imine / Schiff's Base (1° Amine)
description: Condensation with primary amine gives an imine (Schiff's base). \(H_2N-R\)=primary amine; \(\rangle C=N-R\)=imine. Fastest near mildly acidic pH.

subject: Chemistry
title: Addition of Ammonia Derivatives (2,4-DNP)
description: 2,4-DNP (Brady's reagent) gives orange/red ppt confirming \(\rangle C=O\) in aldehydes & ketones. Related derivatives: oxime (\(NH_2OH\)), hydrazone (\(NH_2NH_2\)), semicarbazone (\(NH_2NHCONH_2\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Cross Aldol Condensation
description: Between one non-enolisable (\(PhCHO\)) and one enolisable carbonyl gives a single major \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated product (cinnamaldehyde). Avoids the 4-product mixture of two different enolisable aldehydes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbonyl Reduction to Alcohol (NaBH4 / LiAlH4)
description: Reduces aldehydes to 1° alcohols, ketones to 2° alcohols. \(NaBH_4\)=mild (selective for \(\rangle C=O\), not \(-COOH\)/ester); \(LiAlH_4\)=strong (reduces acids, esters too).

subject: Chemistry
title: Catalytic Hydrogenation of C=O
description: Metal-catalysed addition of \(H_2\) reduces carbonyl to alcohol; any \(C=C\) present is also reduced. \(\rangle C=O\)=aldehyde/ketone; product=1°/2° alcohol.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aldehyde Oxidation (Mild)
description: Aldehydes are readily oxidised to carboxylic acids by mild oxidants; ketones resist mild oxidation. Oxidants: Tollens', Fehling's, \(KMnO_4\), \(K_2Cr_2O_7\). \([O]\)=oxidising agent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carboxylic Acid from Grignard + CO2
description: Grignard reagent adds to \(CO_2\) (dry ice) giving acid with one more carbon. \(R-MgX\)=Grignard; product acid has one extra \(C\) than the halide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitrile Hydrolysis to Acid
description: Acid/base hydrolysis of nitriles (via amide) gives carboxylic acids; net one-carbon ascent from alkyl halide (\(RX \to RCN \to RCOOH\)). \(R-C\equiv N\)=nitrile.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ester Formation (Fischer Esterification)
description: Acid-catalysed, reversible esterification of acid with alcohol. \(R-COOH\)=acid, \(R'OH\)=alcohol, \(R-COOR'\)=ester. Drive forward by excess alcohol or removing water (Le Chatelier).

subject: Chemistry
title: Acid to Acid Chloride
description: Converts \(-COOH\) to acyl chloride; \(SOCl_2\) preferred as by-products are gases (easy purification). Other reagents: \(PCl_3\), \(PCl_5\). \(R-COCl\)=acyl chloride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Anhydride Formation (Dehydration)
description: Two acid molecules lose water to give acid anhydride. \(P_2O_5\)=dehydrating agent; \((RCO)_2O\)=anhydride. Cyclic anhydrides form intramolecularly from suitable diacids (succinic, glutaric, phthalic).

subject: Chemistry
title: Kolbe Electrolysis
description: Electrolysis of sodium carboxylate gives symmetrical alkane (\(R-R\)) at anode via decarboxylation. \(R-R\)=dimer alkane; \(CO_2\) at anode, \(H_2\) at cathode.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acidity: Effect of Substituent (Ka / pKa)
description: Quantifies carboxylic acid strength. \(K_a\)=acid dissociation constant; lower \(pK_a\) = stronger acid. Electron-withdrawing groups (\(-Cl\), \(-NO_2\)) raise \(K_a\); \(-CH_3\) lowers it. e.g. \(HCOOH > CH_3COOH\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Electrophilic Substitution (Ring Deactivation)
description: \(-CHO\), \(-COR\), \(-COOH\) are deactivating, meta-directing groups (Friedel-Crafts fails on them). Aromatic ring undergoes nitration/halogenation/sulphonation at the meta position.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ring Chlorination of Acid (vs HVZ)
description: On benzoic acid, halogen (with Lewis acid) substitutes the ring at meta (\(-COOH\) deactivates, meta-directs). Contrast \(\alpha\)-halogenation (HVZ) which targets the alkyl \(\alpha\)-carbon of aliphatic acids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reactivity Order: Nucleophilic Addition
description: Decreasing ease of nucleophilic addition to carbonyl C=O. Aldehydes react faster than ketones; aromatic carbonyls are slowest. Governs HCN, NaHSO_3, acetal, imine additions. \(R\)=alkyl, \(Ar\)=aryl.
derivation:
Two effects make the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic and less hindered.
Electronic: alkyl/aryl groups are electron-donating (+I, +R), reducing the partial positive charge \(\delta^+\) on the carbonyl C; more such groups means a less electrophilic carbon.
Ketones have two such groups, aldehydes only one, so aldehydes are more reactive.
Steric: two bulky groups in ketones hinder nucleophile approach to the sp\(^2\) carbon.
Aromatic carbonyls (e.g. \(C_6H_5CHO\), \(C_6H_5COCH_3\)) are least reactive because the ring lone pair conjugates into C=O (\(+R\)), stabilising it and lowering electrophilicity.

related_concepts.name: Steric Hindrance
related_concepts.definition: Bulky alkyl/aryl groups around the sp\(^2\) carbonyl carbon block the nucleophile's line of attack; two such groups in ketones slow addition more than the single group in aldehydes.

related_concepts.name: Electronic (+I / +R) Effect
related_concepts.definition: Electron-donating alkyl groups (\(+I\)) and conjugating aryl groups (\(+R\)) reduce the carbonyl carbon's \(\delta^+\), lowering its electrophilicity and hence reactivity.

related_concepts.name: Why HCHO is Most Reactive
related_concepts.definition: Formaldehyde has only H atoms on the carbonyl carbon: no \(+I\) donation and minimal steric bulk, so its carbon carries the largest \(\delta^+\) and is most open to attack.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acidity Order of Carboxylic Acids
visual_data: HCOOH > CH_3COOH; \quad Cl_3C\text{-}COOH > Cl_2CH\text{-}COOH > ClCH_2COOH > CH_3COOH
description: Comparative acid strength of carboxylic acids. Electron-withdrawing groups (\(-I\)) stabilise \(RCOO^-\) and increase acidity; \(-I\) effect falls with distance from \(-COOH\). \(K_a\uparrow \Rightarrow\) stronger acid.
derivation:
Acidity is set by the stability of the conjugate base \(RCOO^-\).
Electron-withdrawing groups (Cl, NO\(_2\), F) pull electron density away by \(-I\), dispersing the negative charge and stabilising the carboxylate, so acidity rises with the number of EWGs (\(Cl_3C\text{-} > Cl_2CH\text{-} > ClCH_2\text{-}\)).
Electron-donating alkyl groups (\(+I\)) destabilise the anion, so \(CH_3COOH\) is weaker than \(HCOOH\).
The \(-I\) effect weakens with distance: a substituent farther from \(-COOH\) raises acidity less.

related_concepts.name: Inductive Effect (\(-I\))
related_concepts.definition: Electron-withdrawing atoms/groups stabilise the carboxylate anion by dispersing its negative charge; effect is additive and decreases with distance from \(-COOH\).

related_concepts.name: Aromatic vs Aliphatic
related_concepts.definition: Benzoic acid (\(pK_a\approx 4.2\)) is stronger than acetic acid; electron-withdrawing ring substituents (e.g. \(-NO_2\)) raise acidity, electron-donating ones (e.g. \(-OCH_3\)) lower it.

related_concepts.name: Why Carboxylic Acids > Phenols > Alcohols
related_concepts.definition: \(RCOO^-\) is resonance-stabilised over two equivalent oxygens, far more than phenoxide; hence \(RCOOH\) (\(pK_a\approx 4-5\)) is more acidic than phenol (\(\approx 10\)) and alcohols (\(\approx 16\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Glucose Structure
description: Aldohexose. D-Glucose is the most abundant monosaccharide.
derivation:
Evidence for structure:
1. Straight Chain: HI reduction gives n-hexane.
2. Carbonyl Group: Reacts with hydroxylamine (\(NH_2OH\)).
3. Aldehyde Group: Oxidized by Bromine water to Gluconic Acid.
4. Five -OH groups: Acetylation gives pentaacetate.
5. Primary -OH: Nitric acid oxidation gives Saccharic acid (dicarboxylic).

related_concepts.name: Anomers
related_concepts.definition: Isomers (alpha/beta) differing only in configuration at the hemiacetal carbon (C1).

subject: Chemistry
title: Peptide Bond Formation
description: Amide linkage joining amino acids in proteins.
derivation:
Condensation reaction between Carboxyl group of one amino acid and Amino group of another.
1. Nucleophilic attack of Nitrogen lone pair on Carbonyl carbon.
2. Elimination of a water molecule.
3. The C-N bond has partial double bond character due to resonance, making the peptide backbone planar.

related_concepts.name: Polypeptide
related_concepts.definition: A chain of many amino acids linked by peptide bonds (Protein primary structure).

subject: Chemistry
title: Zwitter Ion
description: Internal salt form of amino acids. Net charge is zero at Isoelectric Point (pI).
derivation:
Amino acids contain both acidic (-COOH) and basic (-NH2) groups.
1. In solution, the proton (H+) transfers from Acid to Base.
2. -COOH becomes -COO- (Carboxylate).
3. -NH2 becomes -NH3+ (Ammonium).
This makes amino acids amphoteric (react with both acids and bases).

related_concepts.name: Isoelectric Point (pI)
related_concepts.definition: The pH at which a molecule carries no net electrical charge.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mutarotation
description: Spontaneous change in specific rotation of an optically active compound.
derivation:
Glucose crystallizes in two forms:
- $\alpha$-form ($+112^\circ$)
- $\beta$-form ($+19^\circ$)
In aqueous solution, the hemiacetal ring opens and re-closes dynamically.
Equilibrium mixture attains a constant rotation of $+52.7^\circ$ (approx 36% $\alpha$, 64% $\beta$).
Driven by the stability of the chair conformations.

related_concepts.name: Anomers
related_concepts.definition: Isomers differing in configuration at C1 (Hemiacetal carbon).

subject: Chemistry
title: Isoelectric Point (Amino Acids)
description: pH at which amino acid exists as Zwitterion (net charge 0) and does not migrate in electric field.
derivation:
For neutral amino acid (e.g., Glycine):
$Cation (+1) \xrightarrow{K_{a1}} Zwitterion (0) \xrightarrow{K_{a2}} Anion (-1)$.
We need max concentration of Zwitterion.
$pH = pK_{a1} + \log([Z]/[Cat])$ and $pH = pK_{a2} + \log([An]/[Z])$.
At pI, $[Cat] = [An]$. Adding equations gives $2pH = pK_{a1} + pK_{a2}$.

related_concepts.name: Electrophoresis
related_concepts.definition: Technique to separate amino acids based on migration in electric field at a specific pH.

subject: Chemistry
title: Biuret Test
description: Test for presence of Peptide bonds (-CONH-). Proteins give violet color.
derivation:
Reagent: Alkaline $CuSO_4$ (1%).
Principle:
$Cu^{2+}$ ions form a square planar coordination complex with the lone pairs of 4 Nitrogen atoms from peptide bonds.
Requirement: Minimum two peptide linkages (tripeptide or larger) are needed for positive test.
Amino acids (monomers) do NOT give this test.

related_concepts.name: Xanthoproteic Test
related_concepts.definition: Test for aromatic amino acids (Tyrosine, Tryptophan) using Conc HNO3 (Yellow color).

subject: Chemistry
title: Barfoed's Test
description: Distinguishes Monosaccharides from Disaccharides.
derivation:
Reagent: Copper Acetate in Acetic Acid (Weakly acidic).
Principle:
Monosaccharides are stronger reducing agents than disaccharides.
In weakly acidic medium, only Monosaccharides reduce $Cu^{2+}$ to $Cu_2O$ within 2-3 minutes.
Disaccharides take much longer (>10 mins) or require hydrolysis first.

related_concepts.name: Benedict's Test
related_concepts.definition: Similar to Fehling's but uses Citrate. Used for general reducing sugars.

subject: Chemistry
title: Seliwanoff's Test
description: Distinguishes Ketoses (Fructose) from Aldoses (Glucose).
derivation:
Reagent: Resorcinol in Conc HCl.
Principle:
Ketoses dehydrate rapidly in conc acid to yield Furfural derivatives (e.g., Hydroxymethylfurfural).
Furfural condenses with Resorcinol to form a Cherry Red complex.
Aldoses dehydrate slowly, giving faint pink or no color in the same time.

related_concepts.name: Furfural
related_concepts.definition: Heterocyclic aldehyde derivative formed from dehydration of sugars.

subject: Chemistry
title: DNA Double Helix
description: Watson-Crick Model. Two antiparallel strands held by H-bonds.
derivation:
Base Pairing Rules:
1. Adenine (Purine) pairs with Thymine (Pyrimidine) via **2 Hydrogen Bonds**.
2. Guanine (Purine) pairs with Cytosine (Pyrimidine) via **3 Hydrogen Bonds**.
Backbone: Sugar-Phosphate-Sugar chain on the outside (Hydrophilic).
Base Stacking: Hydrophobic interactions between stacked bases stabilize the helix.

related_concepts.name: Chargaff's Rule
related_concepts.definition: In DNA, moles of Purines = moles of Pyrimidines ($A+G = T+C$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Reducing Sugars
description: Sugars capable of reducing Tollens'/Fehling's reagents.
derivation:
Structural Requirement:
Must have a Hemiacetal group (Carbon bonded to -OH, -OR, -H, -R).
This allows the ring to open in solution, regenerating the free Aldehyde group.
Examples: Glucose, Fructose (tautomerizes to aldose), Maltose, Lactose.
Exception: Sucrose (non-reducing) because linkage involves both anomeric carbons ($C1-C2$).

related_concepts.name: Mutarotation
related_concepts.definition: Change in optical rotation because of interconversion between alpha and beta anomers via open chain.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molisch's Test
description: General test for Carbohydrates.
derivation:
Reagent: $\alpha$-Naphthol in alcohol + Conc $H_2SO_4$.
Mechanism:
1. Acid dehydrates the sugar to form Furfural (from pentose) or Hydroxymethylfurfural (from hexose).
2. Furfural condenses with two molecules of $\alpha$-Naphthol.
3. Product: Violet/Purple ring at the junction of two liquids.

related_concepts.name: Dehydration
related_concepts.definition: Removal of water molecules by conc. sulfuric acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ninhydrin Test
description: General test for Amino Acids (Free -NH2 group).
derivation:
Reaction:
Amino acid + Ninhydrin $\rightarrow$ Aldehyde + $CO_2$ + Reduced Ninhydrin + $NH_3$.
Then, Reduced Ninhydrin + $NH_3$ + Ninhydrin $\rightarrow$ Purple Complex.
Note: Proline (secondary amine) gives a Yellow color.

related_concepts.name: Chromatography
related_concepts.definition: Ninhydrin is used as a locating agent to visualize amino acid spots.

subject: Chemistry
title: Glucose + HI (Reduction)
description: Prolonged reduction of glucose with HI gives n-hexane, proving a straight chain of 6 carbons. \(HI\)=hydroiodic acid (strong reducing/deoxygenating agent).

subject: Chemistry
title: Glucose + Br2 Water
description: Mild oxidation of -CHO of glucose to -COOH, giving gluconic acid; confirms presence of an aldehyde group. \(Br_2/H_2O\)=mild oxidising agent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Glucose + HNO3 (Oxidation)
description: Strong oxidation by nitric acid converts both terminal -CHO and -CH2OH to -COOH, giving a dicarboxylic acid; confirms a primary -OH at the other end. \(HNO_3\)=conc. nitric acid (strong oxidant).

subject: Chemistry
title: Glucose Acetylation
description: Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to form a pentaacetate, proving the presence of five -OH groups. \((CH_3CO)_2O\)=acetic anhydride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Glucose + Hydroxylamine
description: Formation of an oxime with hydroxylamine confirms the presence of a carbonyl (aldehyde) group in glucose. \(NH_2OH\)=hydroxylamine.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sucrose Inversion
description: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives equimolar glucose and fructose; specific rotation changes from \(+66.5^\circ\) to \(-39.9^\circ\), so it is called invert sugar. Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

subject: Chemistry
title: Maltose & Lactose Linkage
visual_data: \text{Maltose: } C_1 - O - C_4 \quad (\alpha) \qquad \text{Lactose: } C_1 - O - C_4 \quad (\beta)
description: Maltose = two \(\alpha\)-glucose units (C1-C4); Lactose = \(\beta\)-galactose + glucose (C1-C4). Both have a free anomeric -OH, so both are reducing disaccharides.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cellulose Linkage
description: Structural polysaccharide of plant cell walls; a straight-chain polymer of \(\beta\)-D-glucose joined by \(\beta\)-1,4-glycosidic bonds. Not digestible by humans.

subject: Chemistry
title: Protein Hydrolysis
description: Complete acid hydrolysis of a protein cleaves all peptide bonds to give its constituent \(\alpha\)-amino acids. Reverse of peptide bond formation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Levels of Protein Structure
description: 1° = sequence of amino acids; 2° = \(\alpha\)-helix / \(\beta\)-pleated sheet (H-bonds); 3° = overall 3D folding; 4° = assembly of multiple polypeptide subunits.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nucleotide vs Nucleoside
description: Nucleoside = base + sugar (\(N\)-glycosidic bond at C1'). Nucleotide = base + sugar + phosphate (ester bond at C5'). Nucleotides link via phosphodiester bonds to form nucleic acids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chargaff's Rule
description: In double-stranded DNA, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine, so molar amounts of purines equal pyrimidines. Basis of complementary base pairing.

subject: Chemistry
title: Vitamin Solubility Classes
visual_data: \text{Fat-soluble: } A, D, E, K \quad | \quad \text{Water-soluble: } B, C
description: Vitamins A, D, E, K dissolve in fat and are stored in liver/adipose tissue; B-complex and C are water-soluble and must be supplied regularly as they are excreted. \(B_{12}\) is stored.

subject: Chemistry
title: Starch: Amylose vs Amylopectin
description: Composition of starch, the storage polysaccharide of plants. Amylose = water-soluble linear glucose polymer with \(\alpha\text{-}1,4\) glycosidic links; amylopectin = water-insoluble branched polymer with \(\alpha\text{-}1,4\) backbone and \(\alpha\text{-}1,6\) links at branch points. Both made of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose.

subject: Chemistry
title: Protein Denaturation
visual_data: \text{Native Protein} \xrightarrow{\text{heat, acid, } pH} \text{Denatured Protein}\\ 2^\circ, 3^\circ \text{ structure lost} \quad 1^\circ \text{ intact}
description: Loss of biological activity when 2° and 3° structure unfold by breaking H-bonds and disulfide linkages; peptide bonds (1° structure) stay intact. Examples: coagulation of egg white on boiling, curdling of milk. \(1^\circ\)=primary, \(2^\circ\)=secondary, \(3^\circ\)=tertiary structure.

subject: Chemistry
title: DNA vs RNA
visual_data: \text{DNA: deoxyribose, bases } A,G,C,T, \text{ double strand}\\ \text{RNA: ribose, bases } A,G,C,U, \text{ single strand}
description: Standard comparison of the two nucleic acids. DNA has 2-deoxyribose sugar, thymine (T), is double-stranded (helix). RNA has ribose sugar, uracil (U) in place of T, is usually single-stranded. Common purines \(A,G\); pyrimidines \(C,T\) (DNA) / \(C,U\) (RNA).

subject: Chemistry
title: Fehling's & Tollens' Tests
visual_data: \text{Reducing sugar} + 2Cu^{2+} \rightarrow Cu_2O \downarrow \text{ (brick-red)}\\ \text{Reducing sugar} + Ag^+ \rightarrow Ag \downarrow \text{ (silver mirror)}
description: Positive tests confirming a reducing sugar (free \(-CHO\) or \(\alpha\)-hydroxy ketone). Fehling's gives brick-red \(Cu_2O\); Tollens' gives a silver mirror (\(Ag\)). Glucose, fructose, maltose, lactose are reducing (positive); sucrose is non-reducing (negative, no free anomeric -OH).

subject: Chemistry
title: Glycogen Structure
description: Storage polysaccharide of animals ("animal starch"), found in liver and muscles. Structure resembles amylopectin but is more highly branched: \(\alpha\text{-}1,4\) glycosidic backbone with frequent \(\alpha\text{-}1,6\) branch points. \(n\)=degree of polymerization.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sucrose Composition
description: Disaccharide formed by glucose and fructose joined through both their anomeric carbons (\(C_1\) of glucose, \(C_2\) of fructose). Since no free anomeric -OH remains, sucrose is non-reducing. Molecular formula \(C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Nylon 6,6
description: Polyamide condensation polymer. '6,6' refers to carbons in each monomer.
derivation:
Reaction: Step-Growth Polymerization.
Monomers:
