1. Adipic Acid: \(HOOC-(CH_2)_4-COOH\)
2. Hexamethylenediamine: \(H_2N-(CH_2)_6-NH_2\)
Process: Condensation with removal of water molecules.
Forms strong hydrogen bonds between chains (high tensile strength).

related_concepts.name: Condensation Polymer
related_concepts.definition: Polymer formed with the loss of a small molecule like water or HCl.

subject: Chemistry
title: Vulcanization of Rubber
description: Heating natural rubber with Sulfur to improve properties.
derivation:
Natural Rubber (cis-1,4-polyisoprene) is soft and sticky.
Mechanism:
1. Sulfur forms cross-links between the polymer chains at the allylic positions (reactive C=C sites).
2. Result: Formation of a 3D network.
   - Increases elasticity.
   - Increases tensile strength.
   - Reduces solubility in organic solvents.

related_concepts.name: Elastomer
related_concepts.definition: Polymer with viscoelasticity and weak intermolecular forces, allowing stretching.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nylon-6 (Preparation)
description: Polyamide formed by Ring Opening Polymerization of Caprolactam.
derivation:
Monomer: $\epsilon$-Caprolactam (7-membered ring containing Amide).
Process:
1. Hydrolysis: Water opens the ring to form $\epsilon$-Aminocaproic acid ($H_2N-(CH_2)_5-COOH$).
2. Polymerization: Self-condensation of the amino acid at high temp (533K).
   Forms peptide bonds between units.
Uses: Tire cords, fabrics, ropes.

related_concepts.name: Beckmann Rearrangement
related_concepts.definition: Industrial route to Caprolactam starting from Cyclohexanone Oxime.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bakelite (Network)
description: Thermosetting polymer (Phenol-Formaldehyde resin).
derivation:
Steps:
1. Electrophilic Sub: $HCHO$ adds to Phenol (o/p positions) forming Methylol phenols ($Ph-CH_2OH$).
2. Linear Polymer: Condensation gives **Novolac** (Linear chains used in paints).
3. Cross-linking: Heating with excess HCHO connects the linear chains via $-CH_2-$ bridges at all ortho/para positions.
Result: Infusible, hard 3D solid.

related_concepts.name: Thermosetting Plastic
related_concepts.definition: Polymer that becomes irreversibly hard upon heating and cannot be remolded.

subject: Chemistry
title: PHBV (Biodegradable)
description: Poly-beta-hydroxybutyrate-co-beta-hydroxyvalerate.
derivation:
Copolymerization:
Monomer 1: $CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-COOH$
Monomer 2: $CH_3-CH_2-CH(OH)-CH_2-COOH$
Reaction: Esterification (Condensation) between -OH of one and -COOH of another.
Significance: Bacterial degradation breaks ester linkages.

related_concepts.name: Nylon-2-nylon-6
related_concepts.definition: Another biodegradable copolymer of Glycine and Aminocaproic acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dacron (Terylene)
description: Polyester. Used in crease-resistant fabrics.
derivation:
Condensation Polymerization:
Monomers: 1,4-Benzene dicarboxylic acid + Ethane-1,2-diol.
Process: Loss of water molecules at high temp ($420-460K$) with Zinc Acetate-Antimony Trioxide catalyst.
Linkage: Ester ($ -CO-O- $).

related_concepts.name: Step-Growth Polymerization
related_concepts.definition: Polymerization mechanism involving stepwise reaction between functional groups.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ziegler-Natta Catalyst
description: Used for coordination polymerization of ethene/propene.
derivation:
Action:
Produces **High Density Polyethylene (HDPE)**.
The catalyst provides a template for the monomer to add in a regular, stereospecific manner.
Result: Linear chains with no branching, allowing close packing and high density/strength.

related_concepts.name: Stereoregularity
related_concepts.definition: Isotactic or Syndiotactic polymers formed via stereospecific catalysis.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number-Average Molar Mass
description: Average molar mass by number of polymer molecules. \(N_i\)=number of molecules of molar mass \(M_i\). Measured by colligative properties (osmotic pressure).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass-Average Molar Mass
description: Average molar mass weighted by mass of each fraction. \(N_i\)=number of molecules of molar mass \(M_i\). Measured by light scattering / ultracentrifugation. Always \(\overline{M}_w \ge \overline{M}_n\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Polydispersity Index (PDI)
description: Measures spread of molar masses in a polymer. \(\overline{M}_w\)=mass-average, \(\overline{M}_n\)=number-average. PDI=1 for natural polymers (monodisperse); PDI>1 for synthetic polymers.

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Polymerization
description: Number of repeating monomer units in a polymer chain. \(\overline{M}_{polymer}\)=average molar mass of polymer, \(M_0\)=molar mass of one repeating (monomer) unit.

subject: Chemistry
title: Polythene (Addition)
description: Addition polymer of ethene. High-pressure free-radical route gives branched LDPE; Ziegler-Natta gives linear HDPE.

subject: Chemistry
title: PVC
description: Poly(vinyl chloride), addition polymer of vinyl chloride. Used for raincoats, pipes, vinyl flooring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Teflon (PTFE)
description: Polytetrafluoroethene, addition polymer of tetrafluoroethene. Chemically inert, heat-resistant non-stick coating.

subject: Chemistry
title: Polyacrylonitrile (PAN)
description: Orlon/Acrilan, addition polymer of acrylonitrile. Substitute for wool; used in sweaters and blankets.

subject: Chemistry
title: Polystyrene
description: Addition polymer of styrene. Used in insulation, packaging and disposable cups.

subject: Chemistry
title: Polypropene
description: Addition polymer of propene (Ziegler-Natta). Used for ropes, manufacture of toys and pipes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Buna-S (SBR)
description: Styrene-butadiene rubber, copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and styrene. 'S'=styrene. Used in tyres, soles.

subject: Chemistry
title: Buna-N (NBR)
description: Nitrile rubber, copolymer of 1,3-butadiene and acrylonitrile. 'N'=acrylonitrile. Oil/solvent resistant; used in hoses, gaskets.

subject: Chemistry
title: Neoprene
description: Polychloroprene, addition polymer of chloroprene (2-chloro-1,3-butadiene). Resistant to oils; used for conveyor belts, gaskets.

subject: Chemistry
title: Natural Rubber
description: cis-1,4-polyisoprene; monomer is isoprene (2-methyl-1,3-butadiene). All cis double bonds give the coiled elastic structure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nylon-2-Nylon-6
description: Biodegradable polyamide copolymer of glycine (amino acid, 2C) and aminocaproic acid (6C).

subject: Chemistry
title: Melamine-Formaldehyde
description: Thermosetting condensation polymer of melamine and formaldehyde. Used for unbreakable crockery (Melmac).

subject: Chemistry
title: Urea-Formaldehyde
description: Thermosetting condensation polymer of urea and formaldehyde. Used in adhesives and moulding.

subject: Chemistry
title: Glyptal (Alkyd Resin)
description: Polyester of ethylene glycol and phthalic acid (ortho). Used in paints and lacquers.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nylon-6,10
description: Polyamide of sebacic acid (10C diacid) and hexamethylenediamine (6C diamine).

subject: Chemistry
title: Carothers Equation
description: Average degree of polymerization vs extent of reaction in step-growth (condensation) polymers. \(\overline{DP}\)=avg degree of polymerization, \(p\)=fraction of functional groups reacted (extent of reaction, \(0 \le p < 1\)).
derivation:
Start with \(N_0\) monomer molecules; after reaction \(N\) molecules remain.
Number of bonds formed \(= N_0 - N\), and \(p = \frac{N_0 - N}{N_0}\).
So \(N = N_0(1 - p)\).
\(\overline{DP} = \frac{N_0}{N} = \frac{1}{1 - p}\).

related_concepts.name: Step-Growth Polymerization
related_concepts.definition: Polymerization where bifunctional monomers react stepwise; high molar mass needs p very close to 1.

related_concepts.name: Extent of Reaction (p)
related_concepts.definition: Fraction of original functional groups that have reacted; e.g. p=0.99 gives DP=100.

subject: Chemistry
title: PMMA (Plexiglas)
description: Addition polymer of methyl methacrylate; transparent acrylic glass (Lucite/Plexiglas, lenses). \(n\)=number of monomer units.
derivation:
Monomer: Methyl methacrylate \(CH_2{=}C(CH_3)COOCH_3\).
Mechanism: Free-radical chain (addition) polymerization across the \(C{=}C\).
Properties: Hard, transparent, shatter-resistant.
Uses: Lenses, signboards, aircraft windows, dentures.

related_concepts.name: Addition Polymer
related_concepts.definition: Polymer formed by repeated addition of unsaturated monomers with no loss of small molecules.

related_concepts.name: Acrylic Polymer
related_concepts.definition: Polymer of acrylic/methacrylic acid esters; PMMA is the methyl methacrylate ester.

subject: Chemistry
title: Free-Radical Addition (Mechanism)
description: Chain mechanism for addition (vinyl) polymers like polythene using a peroxide initiator. \(R{-}R\)=initiator (e.g. benzoyl peroxide), \(R^{\bullet}\)=free radical.
derivation:
1. Initiation: Initiator homolysis gives radicals \(R^{\bullet}\) that add to monomer.
2. Propagation: Growing radical adds successive \(CH_2{=}CH_2\) units, chain grows.
3. Termination: Two radical chains combine (or disproportionate) to end growth.

related_concepts.name: Chain-Growth Polymerization
related_concepts.definition: Polymerization proceeding via reactive radical/ionic chain ends adding monomer one at a time.

related_concepts.name: Initiator
related_concepts.definition: Species (benzoyl peroxide, AIBN, persulphate) that generates the starting free radicals.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation
description: Conversion of primary amide to primary amine with one less carbon.
derivation:
1. Bromination: Amide + \(Br_2/OH^-\) forms N-bromoamide.
2. Formation of Nitrene: Loss of HBr gives unstable Acyl Nitrene intermediate.
3. Rearrangement (RDS): Alkyl group (R) migrates from Carbon to Nitrogen.
   Forms Isocyanate (\(R-N=C=O\)).
4. Hydrolysis: Isocyanate reacts with KOH to release \(CO_2\) and form Amine \(R-NH_2\).

related_concepts.name: Intramolecular Rearrangement
related_concepts.definition: Reaction where a group moves from one atom to another within the same molecule.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbylamine Reaction
description: Test for Primary Amines (Isocyanide Test). Produces foul smell.
derivation:
1. Electrophile Formation: Alpha-elimination of HCl from Chloroform gives Dichlorocarbene (\(:CCl_2\)).
2. Attack: Amine nitrogen attacks electron-deficient carbene.
3. Elimination: Loss of protons and Cl- ions results in Isocyanide (\(R-N^+\equiv C^-\)).
Only primary amines have 2 hydrogens available to be removed for this triple bond formation.

related_concepts.name: Alpha Elimination
related_concepts.definition: Removal of two atoms/groups from the same carbon atom.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hinsberg Test
description: Distinguishes Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Amines.
derivation:
Reaction with Amine:
1. \(1^\circ\) Amine: Forms Sulfonamide (\(PhSO_2NHR\)). Has acidic H on Nitrogen. Soluble in NaOH.
2. \(2^\circ\) Amine: Forms Sulfonamide (\(PhSO_2NR_2\)). No acidic H. Insoluble in NaOH.
3. \(3^\circ\) Amine: No H on Nitrogen. No reaction. Remains insoluble (or dissolves in acid).

related_concepts.name: Sulfonamides
related_concepts.definition: Class of compounds including 'Sulfa drugs' (antibiotics).

subject: Chemistry
title: Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis
description: Preparation of pure primary aliphatic amines.
derivation:
1. Acid-Base: Phthalimide (acidic NH) + KOH $\to$ Potassium Phthalimide ($N^-K^+$).
2. SN2 Attack: $N^-$ attacks Alkyl Halide ($RX$). Forms N-Alkyl Phthalimide.
   Constraint: $RX$ must be suitable for SN2 (Primary/Secondary). Aryl halides do not react.
3. Hydrolysis: NaOH cleaves the imide bond releasing $R-NH_2$.

related_concepts.name: Nucleophilic Substitution
related_concepts.definition: The phthalimide anion acts as a bulky nucleophile.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diazonium Coupling
description: Electrophilic aromatic substitution to form Azo Dyes.
derivation:
Electrophile: Weak Diazonium cation ($Ph-N_2^+$).
Substrate: Activated benzene ring ($G = -OH, -NH_2$).
Mechanism:
1. Electrophile attacks Para position (sterically favored).
2. Loss of proton restores aromaticity.
Conditions:
- Phenols: pH 9-10 (Basic, forms Phenoxide).
- Amines: pH 4-5 (Acidic, but not too acidic to protonate amine).

related_concepts.name: Azo Dye
related_concepts.definition: Colored compounds containing $-N=N-$ linkage (e.g., Methyl Orange).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mustard Oil Reaction
description: Test for Primary Amines. Formation of Alkyl Isothiocyanate.
derivation:
1. Addition: Primary amine reacts with Carbon Disulfide ($CS_2$) to form Dithiocarbamic acid salt.
   $RNH_2 + S=C=S \rightarrow R-NH-CS-S^- H^+$.
2. Decomposition: On heating with $HgCl_2$, it eliminates $H_2S$ (as $HgS$ ppt) and HCl.
   Product $R-N=C=S$ smells like mustard oil.

related_concepts.name: Hoffmann Isocyanide
related_concepts.definition: Another test for primary amines giving a foul smell (Carbylamine).

subject: Chemistry
title: Liebermann Nitroso Test
description: Test for Phenols and Secondary Amines.
derivation:
1. Electrophile: $HNO_2$ generates Nitrosonium ion ($NO^+$).
2. Reaction with Phenol: Electrophilic substitution at para position $\rightarrow$ p-Nitrosophenol.
3. Tautomerism: Rearranges to Quinone Monoxime.
4. Condensation: Reacts with excess phenol/acid to form Indophenol (Red).
5. Alkali: In NaOH, the Indophenol anion is Blue.

related_concepts.name: N-Nitrosamine
related_concepts.definition: Yellow oily liquid formed when secondary amines react with nitrous acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Curtius Rearrangement
description: Thermal decomposition of Acyl Azide to Isocyanate, then Amine.
derivation:
1. Precursor: Acyl Azide ($RCON_3$) formed from Acid Chloride + $NaN_3$.
2. Rearrangement: Loss of $N_2$ gas drives migration of Alkyl group ($R$) from Carbon to Nitrogen.
   Forms Isocyanate ($R-N=C=O$).
3. Hydrolysis: Isocyanate reacts with water to form Carbamic Acid ($RNHCOOH$), which spontaneously decarboxylates to Amine.

related_concepts.name: Schmidt Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Similar rearrangement using Hydrazoic Acid ($HN_3$) directly with Carboxylic Acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis
description: Synthesis of pure primary aliphatic amines.
derivation:
1. Acid-Base: Phthalimide (pKa ~8.3) + KOH $\rightarrow$ Potassium Phthalimide (Nucleophile).
2. SN2: Nucleophile attacks $1^\circ$ Alkyl Halide ($RX$).
   *Note: Aryl halides cannot be used (No SN2).*
3. Hydrolysis: Hydrazine ($NH_2NH_2$) or Acid cleaves the amide bonds, releasing pure $1^\circ$ Amine.

related_concepts.name: Nucleophilicity
related_concepts.definition: The phthalimide anion is a strong, bulky nucleophile.

subject: Chemistry
title: Schotten-Baumann Reaction
description: Benzoylation of phenols or amines using Benzoyl Chloride in alkaline medium.
derivation:
1. Nucleophilic Attack: Amine/Phenol attacks carbonyl of Benzoyl Chloride.
2. Elimination: Chloride ion ($Cl^-$) leaves.
3. Role of Base ($NaOH$): Neutralizes the HCl produced.
   This shifts the equilibrium forward and prevents protonation of the amine reactant.

related_concepts.name: Benzoylation
related_concepts.definition: Introduction of a Benzoyl group ($Ph-CO-$) to protect -OH or -NH2 groups.

subject: Chemistry
title: Schmidt Reaction
description: One-step conversion of Carboxylic Acid to Primary Amine.
derivation:
Reagent: Hydrazoic Acid ($HN_3$) in Conc $H_2SO_4$.
Mechanism:
1. Protonation of acid -> Loss of water -> Acylium ion.
2. Addition of $HN_3$ -> Rearrangement similar to Curtius.
3. Loss of $N_2$ leads to migration of R group.
4. Hydrolysis gives Amine.

related_concepts.name: Lossen Rearrangement
related_concepts.definition: Similar rearrangement starting from Hydroxamic Acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Basicity Order (Aqueous)
description: Order of basic strength of ethyl amines in aqueous solution (net effect of +I, steric & H-bonded solvation). \(2^\circ > 3^\circ > 1^\circ > NH_3\) for ethyl series; for methyl series \(2^\circ > 1^\circ > 3^\circ > NH_3\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Aniline vs Aliphatic Basicity
description: Aryl amines are weaker bases than ammonia/alkyl amines because the lone pair on N is delocalised into the ring. \(K_b\) decreases as more aryl groups attach to N.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ammonolysis of Alkyl Halide
description: Nucleophilic substitution of alkyl halide by ammonia gives a mixture of 1°, 2°, 3° amines and quaternary salt. Excess \(NH_3\) favours the 1° amine; reactivity \(RI > RBr > RCl\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Reduction of Nitro Compounds
visual_data: R-NO_2 \xrightarrow{H_2 / \text{Ni, Pd or Pt}} R-NH_2 \quad ; \quad R-NO_2 \xrightarrow{Sn/HCl} R-NH_2
description: Nitro compounds reduce to 1° amines. Catalytic \(H_2\) or \(Sn/HCl\) (also \(Fe/HCl\)) gives the amine; this is the main route to aniline from nitrobenzene.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reduction of Nitriles & Amides
visual_data: R-C\equiv N \xrightarrow{H_2/Ni \text{ or } LiAlH_4} R-CH_2-NH_2 \quad ; \quad R-CONH_2 \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} R-CH_2-NH_2
description: Nitriles and amides reduce to 1° amines with one extra C than the parent acid/halide. Note \(\equiv\) shown as triple bond on N; \(LiAlH_4\) reduces amide C=O fully to \(CH_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Diazotization Reaction
description: 1° aromatic amine + nitrous acid (\(NaNO_2 + HCl\)) at \(0-5^\circ C\) gives benzene diazonium chloride. Low temp needed as the salt decomposes above \(278\,K\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Sandmeyer Reaction
description: Diazonium group replaced by \(Cl, Br\) or \(CN\) using the corresponding cuprous halide/cyanide. \(N_2\) gas is evolved in each case.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gattermann Reaction
description: Halogen (\(Cl/Br\)) introduced using copper powder + halogen acid (alternative to Sandmeyer using Cu metal instead of Cu(I) salt). Lower yields than Sandmeyer.

subject: Chemistry
title: Balz-Schiemann Reaction
description: Aryl fluoride from diazonium via the fluoroborate salt, which is then heated. Only practical route to introduce \(F\) directly on the ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diazonium to Phenol
visual_data: C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{warm } / 283 K} C_6H_5OH + N_2 + HCl
description: Hydrolysis of diazonium salt in warm water gives phenol with evolution of \(N_2\). \(-N_2^+\) replaced by \(-OH\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Diazonium to Arene (H replacement)
visual_data: C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^- + H_3PO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_6 + N_2 + H_3PO_3 + HCl
description: Replacement of \(-N_2^+\) by \(-H\) using hypophosphorous acid (\(H_3PO_2\)) or ethanol. Used to remove an \(-NH_2\) directing group after synthesis.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diazonium to Iodide
description: Iodobenzene formed simply by warming diazonium salt with KI (no cuprous salt needed, unlike Cl/Br). \(N_2\) evolved.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diazonium to Nitroarene
description: \(-N_2^+\) replaced by \(-NO_2\) using sodium nitrite with copper catalyst. Completes the suite of diazonium replacement reactions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Azo Dye Coupling (Aniline)
description: Diazonium couples with aniline at para position giving yellow azo dye (aminoazobenzene). Coupling is electrophilic substitution at the activated ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Azo Coupling with Phenol
description: Diazonium couples with phenol in mildly alkaline medium to give orange p-hydroxyazobenzene. Couples at para (or ortho if para blocked).

subject: Chemistry
title: Amine + HNO2 (1°,2°,3°)
visual_data: 1^\circ: R-NH_2 \xrightarrow{HNO_2} R-OH + N_2\uparrow \quad ; \quad 2^\circ: R_2NH \xrightarrow{HNO_2} R_2N-N=O \quad ; \quad 3^\circ: R_3N \xrightarrow{HNO_2} \text{salt}
description: Action of nitrous acid distinguishes amines: 1° aliphatic gives alcohol + brisk \(N_2\); 2° gives yellow N-nitrosamine; 3° forms a soluble salt. Diagnostic test.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acetylation of Amines
description: 1°/2° amines react with acid anhydride/chloride to give substituted amides (acylation). Used to protect \(-NH_2\) and reduce its activating power before substitution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bromination of Aniline
description: Aniline is so strongly activated that bromine water gives the 2,4,6-tribromo product (white ppt) directly, no catalyst. Monobromination needs acetylation first.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitration of Aniline
description: Direct nitration oxidises aniline & gives much meta; so the \(-NH_2\) is acetylated first to get mainly para-nitroaniline, then hydrolysed back. Key directing-group strategy.

subject: Chemistry
title: No Friedel-Crafts on Aniline
visual_data: C_6H_5NH_2 + AlCl_3 \rightarrow C_6H_5\overset{+}{N}H_2 \cdots AlCl_3^- \quad (\text{no F.C. reaction})
description: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts because the basic \(-NH_2\)/N lone pair forms a salt with Lewis acid \(AlCl_3\), deactivating the ring. Standard exception result.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reductive Amination
description: Preparation of amines by condensation of a carbonyl with ammonia/amine, then reduction. \(R\)=alkyl/aryl; reductant = \(H_2/Ni\), \(NaBH_3CN\) or \(NaBH(OAc)_3\).
derivation:
1. Carbonyl + ammonia/amine condense to form an imine (Schiff base): \(R-CHO + NH_3 \rightarrow R-CH=NH + H_2O\).
2. The C=N is reduced to C-N: \(R-CH=NH \xrightarrow{H_2/Ni} R-CH_2-NH_2\).
3. Aldehyde gives \(1^\circ\); ketone or use of a \(1^\circ\) amine gives \(2^\circ\); use of a \(2^\circ\) amine gives \(3^\circ\) amine.
\(NaBH_3CN\) selectively reduces the iminium ion, not the carbonyl, so it works at mildly acidic pH.

related_concepts.name: Schiff Base (Imine)
related_concepts.definition: Intermediate \(>C=N-\) formed by condensation of a carbonyl with a primary amine/ammonia, reduced in situ.

related_concepts.name: NaBH3CN selectivity
related_concepts.definition: Sodium cyanoborohydride reduces protonated imines (iminium) but not aldehydes/ketones at pH 6-8, making it ideal for reductive amination.

subject: Chemistry
title: Azo Coupling pH & Orientation
description: Diagnostic conditions for diazonium coupling. Phenols couple in mildly alkaline medium, amines in mildly acidic medium; substitution is at the para position (ortho if para blocked).
derivation:
Coupling is electrophilic substitution by the weak electrophile \(Ar-N_2^+\).
Phenol: alkali converts it to the far more reactive phenoxide \(ArO^-\), but too high pH destroys the diazonium (\(\rightarrow\) diazotate); optimum pH 9-10.
Amine: mild acid keeps the ring activated yet most amine free (not fully protonated to deactivated \(-NH_3^+\)); optimum pH 4-5.
Coupling occurs para to \(-OH\)/\(-NH_2\) due to least steric strain and stable azo product.

related_concepts.name: Weak electrophile
related_concepts.definition: Diazonium ion couples only with strongly activated rings (phenols, anilines); it cannot attack plain benzene.

related_concepts.name: Azo dye -N=N-
related_concepts.definition: The chromophoric azo linkage formed; basis of indicators like methyl orange and many fabric dyes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hinsberg Separation Scheme
description: Identification/separation of 1deg, 2deg, 3deg amines using benzenesulfonyl chloride (Hinsberg reagent). \(1^\circ\) sulfonamide is alkali-soluble, \(2^\circ\) is alkali-insoluble, \(3^\circ\) does not react.
derivation:
Reagent: \(C_6H_5SO_2Cl\) (Hinsberg's reagent).
1^\circ amine: forms \(R-NH-SO_2C_6H_5\); the N-H is acidic (\(-SO_2-\) electron-withdrawing) so it dissolves in NaOH as the sodium salt.
2^\circ amine: forms \(R_2N-SO_2C_6H_5\) with no N-H, so it is insoluble in NaOH (remains as precipitate).
3^\circ amine: has no N-H to react, so no sulfonamide forms (amine stays unreacted, separable by being basic/soluble in HCl).
This solubility difference separates the three classes.

related_concepts.name: Hinsberg reagent
related_concepts.definition: Benzenesulfonyl chloride \(C_6H_5SO_2Cl\), used to distinguish and separate primary, secondary and tertiary amines.

related_concepts.name: Acidic sulfonamide N-H
related_concepts.definition: In the 1deg-amine product the strongly electron-withdrawing sulfonyl group makes the N-H acidic, allowing dissolution in alkali.

subject: Chemistry
title: Gabriel Synthesis Limitation
description: Standard exam fact: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis cannot prepare aromatic primary amines (e.g. aniline) because aryl halides do not undergo the required nucleophilic substitution with potassium phthalimide.

related_concepts.name: Aryl halide unreactivity
related_concepts.definition: C-X in aryl halides has partial double-bond character and the ring resists SN2/SN1, so phthalimide anion cannot displace it.

related_concepts.name: Only 1deg amines
related_concepts.definition: Gabriel synthesis yields exclusively primary amines (no 2deg/3deg), but only aliphatic ones.

subject: Chemistry
title: Effective Nuclear Charge
description: Net positive charge experienced by an electron. \(\sigma\): shielding constant.
derivation:
Outer electrons are pushed away by inner electrons (Shielding Effect).
Slater's Rules estimate \(\sigma\).
Trend:
- Across Period: Z increases by 1, \(\sigma\) increases by <1 (electrons added to same shell). So \(Z_{eff}\) Increases.
- Down Group: Z increases, but shells increase. \(Z_{eff}\) remains roughly constant.

related_concepts.name: Atomic Radius
related_concepts.definition: Inversely proportional to Z effective. Decreases across a period.

subject: Chemistry
title: Electron Gain Enthalpy (Cl vs F)
description: Energy released when adding an electron. Cl releases more energy than F.
derivation:
Expected Trend: F should be higher due to high Zeff.
Exception Reality:
1. Fluorine is extremely small (2p orbital).
2. Existing 7 valence electrons are crowded.
3. Inter-electronic repulsion resists the incoming electron.
4. Chlorine (3p) is larger, has less repulsion, and accepts electron more easily.

related_concepts.name: Electron Affinity
related_concepts.definition: The energy change when a neutral atom attracts an electron to become a negative ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Pauling Electronegativity Difference
description: Pauling's electronegativity difference from bond energies. \(\chi_A,\chi_B\)=electronegativities, \(\Delta = E_{A-B} - \sqrt{E_{A-A}\cdot E_{B-B}}\) extra ionic resonance energy in kcal/mol (0.208 becomes 0.1017 if \(\Delta\) in kJ/mol).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mulliken Electronegativity
description: Electronegativity as average of ionization energy and electron affinity (same energy units). \(IE\)=ionization energy, \(EA\)=electron affinity. Pauling value \(\chi_P \approx \chi_M(eV)/2.8\); i.e. \(\chi_M \approx 2.8\,\chi_P\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Successive Ionization Energies
description: Each successive electron is removed from an increasingly positive ion, so energy rises. A large jump in \(IE\) marks completion of a noble-gas (stable) configuration, revealing the number of valence electrons. \(IE_n\)=nth ionization energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Periodic Trends: IE and Atomic Radius
description: Ionization energy rises with effective nuclear charge and falls with atomic size. \(IE_1\)=first ionization enthalpy, \(Z_{eff}\)=effective nuclear charge, \(r\)=atomic radius. Across a period \(Z_{eff}\uparrow, r\downarrow \Rightarrow IE\uparrow\); down a group \(r\uparrow \Rightarrow IE\downarrow\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Anomalous IE Order (Group 13/14, 15/16)
description: Half-filled and fully-filled subshells have extra stability, breaking the smooth across-period rise. \(Be(2s^2)\) > \(B\); \(N(2p^3)\) half-filled > \(O\). Same pattern: \(Mg>Al\), \(P>S\). \(IE_1\)=first ionization energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ionic Radius vs Atomic Radius
description: Cation is smaller (electrons lost, \(Z_{eff}/e\) rises); anion is larger (electron added, repulsion rises). \(r\)=radius. For isoelectronic species, larger nuclear charge \(Z\) gives smaller radius.

subject: Chemistry
title: Isoelectronic Series Radius Trend
description: Among isoelectronic species (equal electrons), radius decreases as nuclear charge increases. \(r\)=ionic radius, \(Z\)=nuclear charge. e.g. \(N^{3-} > O^{2-} > F^- > Na^+ > Mg^{2+} > Al^{3+}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Covalent & van der Waals Radius
description: Covalent radius is half the internuclear distance in a homonuclear single bond; van der Waals radius is half the distance between non-bonded atoms of adjacent molecules (\(r_{vdW} > r_{cov}\)). \(d_{A-A}\)=bond length.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diagonal Relationship
visual_data: Li \sim Mg, \quad Be \sim Al, \quad B \sim Si
description: Element resembles the element diagonally to its lower-right (period 2 vs 3) due to similar charge/radius ratio (ionic potential). Holds across Li-Mg, Be-Al, B-Si pairs. \(\sim\)=similar properties.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ionic Potential (Polarizing Power)
description: Charge density of a cation, governing covalent character and acidity of oxides. \(\phi\)=ionic potential, \(Z\)=cation charge, \(r\)=cation radius. Higher \(\phi\Rightarrow\) more covalent/more acidic (Fajans' polarizing power).

subject: Chemistry
title: Metallic vs Non-metallic Character Trend
description: Metallic (electropositive) character decreases left-to-right and increases down a group; non-metallic character is the reverse. Tracks ionization energy and electronegativity inversely. Most metallic = bottom-left (Cs/Fr).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxide Nature vs Periodic Position
description: Oxide character changes left-to-right across a period from basic (metals, e.g. \(Na_2O\)) through amphoteric (\(Al_2O_3\)) to acidic (non-metals, e.g. \(SO_3, Cl_2O_7\)). Down a group acidity decreases / basicity increases.

subject: Chemistry
title: Highest Oxidation State vs Group
description: Maximum positive oxidation state of a main-group element equals its group's valence-electron count; in oxides \(E_2O_n\) the value of \(n\) tracks the group. \(OS_{max}\)=highest oxidation state. e.g. Cl in \(Cl_2O_7\) is +7.

subject: Chemistry
title: Slater's Rules (Screening Constant)
description: Quantitative method to compute screening constant \(\sigma\) and hence \(Z_{eff}\) for a chosen electron. \(Z\)=atomic number, \(\sigma\)=total shielding, \(n_i\)=number of other electrons in a group, \(s_i\)=per-electron contribution.
derivation:
Write config in Slater groups: \((1s)(2s,2p)(3s,3p)(3d)(4s,4p)\dots\)
For an electron in \(ns,np\):
- Same group (each other \(e^-\)): \(0.35\) (but \(1s\) same-group = \(0.30\)).
- \(n-1\) shell: \(0.85\) each.
- \(n-2\) or lower: \(1.00\) each.
For an electron in \(nd\) or \(nf\):
- Same group: \(0.35\) each.
- All electrons to its left (lower groups): \(1.00\) each.

related_concepts.name: Worked example (valence e of Na, Z=11)
Worked example (3p e of S, Z=16)

subject: Chemistry
title: Pauling Electronegativity from Bond Energies
description: Computes electronegativity difference from bond dissociation energies. \(\Delta\)=extra ionic resonance energy (kcal/mol), \(E_{A-B}\)=heteronuclear bond energy, \(E_{A-A},E_{B-B}\)=homonuclear bond energies; \(0.208\) is for \(\Delta\) in kcal/mol (use \(0.1017\) if \(\Delta\) in kJ/mol).
derivation:
A pure covalent A-B bond energy = geometric mean \(\sqrt{E_{A-A}E_{B-B}}\).
Real A-B bond is stronger by \(\Delta\) (ionic resonance), since \(\chi_A \neq \chi_B\).
Pauling related this extra energy to EN gap: \(\Delta \propto (\chi_A-\chi_B)^2\).
Fitting in kcal/mol gives \(|\chi_A-\chi_B| = 0.208\sqrt{\Delta}\).

related_concepts.name: Arithmetic-mean variant
related_concepts.definition: Some texts use \(\Delta = E_{A-B} - \frac{1}{2}(E_{A-A}+E_{B-B})\) (arithmetic mean) instead of the geometric mean; both appear in problems.

related_concepts.name: kJ conversion constant
related_concepts.definition: \(0.208 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{4.184}} \approx 0.1017\), so \(|\Delta\chi| = 0.1017\sqrt{\Delta_{kJ}}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Pauling % Ionic Character (Exponential)
description: Pauling's exponential estimate of ionic character of a bond from EN difference. \(\Delta\chi\)=electronegativity difference of bonded atoms; distinct from the linear Hannay-Smyth form.

related_concepts.name: 50% ionic rule of thumb
related_concepts.definition: A bond is taken as ~50% ionic when \(\Delta\chi \approx 1.7\); above this it is treated as predominantly ionic.

related_concepts.name: Compare: Hannay-Smyth
related_concepts.definition: Linear-quadratic form \(\%IC = 16|\Delta\chi| + 3.5|\Delta\chi|^2\) usually gives a higher value than the Pauling exponential at the same \(\Delta\chi\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Allred-Rochow Electronegativity
description: Electronegativity as the electrostatic force on a valence electron. \(Z_{eff}\)=effective nuclear charge (Slater), \(r\)=covalent radius in \(\mathring{A}\); constants chosen to match the Pauling scale.
derivation:
Force on a valence electron \(F = \frac{Z_{eff}\,e^2}{r^2}\).
Electronegativity assumed \(\propto F\), i.e. \(\propto \frac{Z_{eff}}{r^2}\).
Scaling to the Pauling scale gives \(\chi_{AR} = 0.359\frac{Z_{eff}}{r^2} + 0.744\) (with \(r\) in \(\mathring{A}\)).

related_concepts.name: Why three scales agree
related_concepts.definition: Pauling (bond energies), Mulliken (\(\frac{IE+EA}{2}\)), and Allred-Rochow (\(\propto Z_{eff}/r^2\)) give closely matching values and the same periodic trend.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mulliken-Jaffe Scale Conversion
description: Converts Mulliken electronegativity (in eV) to the Pauling scale. \(\chi_P\)=Pauling value, \(\chi_M=\frac{IE+EA}{2}\) in eV; the simple \(\div 2.8\) form is the common exam shortcut.

related_concepts.name: Units caution
related_concepts.definition: Mulliken's \(\frac{IE+EA}{2}\) must use the SAME unit (eV) for both terms before dividing by 2.8 to reach the Pauling scale.

subject: Chemistry
title: Born-Lande Lattice Energy
visual_data: U = -\frac{N_A M z_+ z_- e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r_0}\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right)
description: Lattice energy of an ionic crystal. \(N_A\)=Avogadro number, \(M\)=Madelung constant, \(z_+,z_-\)=ion charges, \(r_0\)=cation-anion distance, \(n\)=Born exponent, \(\varepsilon_0\)=permittivity.

related_concepts.name: Charge & size dependence
related_concepts.definition: \(U \propto \frac{z_+ z_-}{r_0}\): lattice energy rises sharply with higher ionic charges and smaller ions (governs melting point, hardness, solubility).

related_concepts.name: Kapustinskii approximation
related_concepts.definition: When \(M\) is unknown, \(U \approx \frac{1.21\times10^5 \, \nu \, z_+ z_-}{r_+ + r_-}\) kJ/mol, with \(\nu\)=number of ions per formula unit.

subject: Chemistry
title: Born-Haber Cycle (Lattice Energy)
description: Hess-law cycle linking formation enthalpy of an ionic solid (e.g. NaCl) to its lattice energy \(U\). \(\Delta_{sub}H\)=sublimation, \(\Delta_{diss}H\)=bond dissociation, \(IE\)=ionization energy, \(\Delta_{eg}H\)=electron gain enthalpy.

related_concepts.name: Sign convention
related_concepts.definition: \(\Delta_{eg}H\) and \(U\) are negative (energy released); \(\Delta_{sub}H\), \(\Delta_{diss}H\) and \(IE\) are positive (energy absorbed).

related_concepts.name: Use
related_concepts.definition: Most JEE problems give all terms except one (usually \(U\) or \(\Delta_{eg}H\)) and ask to solve the cycle for the missing quantity.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hall-Heroult Process
description: Electrolytic reduction of Alumina to Aluminium.
derivation:
Pure Alumina (\(Al_2O_3\)) has high MP (2050°C) and low conductivity.
Solution:
1. Add Cryolite (\(Na_3AlF_6\)) and Fluorspar (\(CaF_2\)).
   - Lowers MP to ~900°C.
   - Increases conductivity.
2. Electrolysis:
   Cathode (Steel vessel + Graphite): \(Al^{3+} + 3e^- \rightarrow Al(l)\)
   Anode (Graphite rods): \(C(s) + O^{2-} \rightarrow CO/CO_2 + e^-\)

related_concepts.name: Electrometallurgy
related_concepts.definition: Process of reduction of metals using electricity, used for reactive metals (Na, Mg, Al).

subject: Chemistry
title: Van Arkel Method
description: Vapor phase refining for Zirconium and Titanium. Based on thermal decomposition.
derivation:
Principle: Impurity does not react with Iodine, or the iodide is non-volatile.
1. Formation (T1 ~ 870K): Impure metal is heated with Iodine.
   \(Zr(s) + 2I_2(g) \rightarrow ZrI_4(g)\) (Volatile Iodide).
2. Decomposition (T2 ~ 2075K): The gas is passed over a hot Tungsten filament.
   \(ZrI_4(g) \rightarrow Zr(s) + 2I_2(g)\)
   Pure metal deposits on the filament.

related_concepts.name: Vapor Phase Refining
related_concepts.definition: Purification method where metal is converted to a volatile compound and then decomposed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mond Process
description: Purification of Nickel. Relies on formation of volatile Nickel Tetracarbonyl.
derivation:
1. Complexation: Impure Nickel reacts with Carbon Monoxide at moderate temp.
   \(Ni + 4CO \rightarrow Ni(CO)_4\)
   Impurities remain solid.
2. Decomposition: The volatile carbonyl is heated to higher temp.
   \(Ni(CO)_4 \rightarrow Ni \downarrow + 4CO \uparrow\)
   The CO gas is recycled.

related_concepts.name: Metal Carbonyls
related_concepts.definition: Coordination complexes of transition metals with carbon monoxide ligands.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ellingham Diagram
description: Graph of \(\Delta G^\circ\) of oxide formation vs Temperature. Predicts reducing agents.
derivation:
Thermodynamics of Reduction:
For reduction \(MO + C \rightarrow M + CO\) to be spontaneous, total \(\Delta G\) must be negative.
Graph Logic:
1. Plots formation of oxides (e.g., \(2M + O_2 \rightarrow 2MO\)).
2. Any metal whose line is *below* another metal's line can reduce the upper metal oxide.
3. The intersection point defines the temperature above which reduction becomes feasible.

related_concepts.name: Pyrometallurgy
related_concepts.definition: Extraction of metals using heat (smelting, roasting).

subject: Chemistry
title: MacArthur-Forrest Process
description: Cyanide process for extraction of Silver (Ag) and Gold (Au).
derivation:
1. Leaching: Impure metal treated with dilute NaCN in presence of Air ($O_2$).
   Oxygen acts as oxidizing agent ($Au^0 \to Au^+$).
   Forms soluble complex: Sodium Dicyanoaurate(I).
2. Displacement: Zinc dust is added.
   $2[Au(CN)_2]^- + Zn \rightarrow [Zn(CN)_4]^{2-} + 2Au \downarrow$.
   Zinc acts as reducing agent.

related_concepts.name: Hydrometallurgy
related_concepts.definition: Separation of a metal from other material by aqueous processes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cupellation
description: Refining of Silver containing Lead impurity.
derivation:
Principle: Lead is easily oxidized, Silver is not.
Process: Molten alloy is heated in a cupel (boat made of bone ash) with air blast.
Lead oxidizes to PbO (Litharge).
PbO either volatilizes or is absorbed by the porous cupel.
Pure silver remains behind.

related_concepts.name: Parting
related_concepts.definition: Separation of Gold from Silver using nitric acid (Silver dissolves, Gold does not).

subject: Chemistry
title: Poling
description: Refining of Blister Copper containing its own oxide ($Cu_2O$).
derivation:
Process: Molten metal is stirred with logs of green wood.
Mechanism:
Heat decomposes the green wood, releasing Hydrocarbon gases (Methane).
These gases act as reducing agents.
$3Cu_2O + CH_4 \rightarrow 6Cu + 2H_2O + CO$.
Reduces the oxide impurity back to metal.

related_concepts.name: Pyrometallurgy
related_concepts.definition: Branch of metallurgy involving high temperatures.

subject: Chemistry
title: Self-Reduction (Auto-reduction)
description: Extraction of less electropositive metals (Cu, Pb, Hg) from sulfide ores.
derivation:
Process: Partial Roasting.
1. Roasting: Sulfide ore is partially oxidized to Oxide.
   $2Cu_2S + 3O_2 \rightarrow 2Cu_2O + 2SO_2$.
2. Self-Reduction: Air supply is cut off. Remaining Sulfide reacts with formed Oxide.
   $Cu_2S + 2Cu_2O \rightarrow 6Cu + SO_2$.
No external reducing agent (C/CO) is needed.

related_concepts.name: Bessemerization
related_concepts.definition: The process carried out in a Bessemer converter for Copper extraction.

subject: Chemistry
title: Liquation
description: Refining method for low melting metals (Sn, Pb, Bi).
derivation:
Principle: Difference in Melting Points.
Process:
Impure metal is placed on the sloping hearth of a reverberatory furnace.
Temperature is kept just above the MP of the metal but below MP of impurity.
Pure metal melts and flows down, leaving solid dross (impurities) behind.

related_concepts.name: Zone Refining
related_concepts.definition: Purification based on solubility difference in molten vs solid state (for Si, Ge).

subject: Chemistry
title: Blast Furnace Zones
description: Temperature zones in Iron extraction (Top to Bottom: Low to High T).
derivation:
1. Reduction (Top, 500-900K): $Fe_2O_3 + CO \rightarrow Fe$.
2. Slag Formation (Middle, 1000K): $CaCO_3 \to CaO + CO_2$; $CaO + SiO_2 \to CaSiO_3$.
3. Fusion (Lower, 1500K): Iron melts, dissolves Carbon.
4. Combustion (Base, 2200K): $C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2$ (Exothermic heat source).

related_concepts.name: Pig Iron
related_concepts.definition: Iron obtained from blast furnace containing ~4% Carbon and impurities.

subject: Chemistry
title: Concentration of Cu in Roasting
description: Roasting of sulphide ore to oxide (partial), a key step in copper extraction (Matte formation precursor). Sulphide ore heated below MP in excess air.

subject: Chemistry
title: Calcination
description: Heating carbonate/hydroxide ore in limited/absence of air to expel volatile matter (\(CO_2\), \(H_2O\)) giving oxide. Also \(Fe_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O \rightarrow Fe_2O_3 + H_2O\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Roasting of Zinc Blende
description: Sulphide ore (ZnS) converted fully to oxide before reduction. Standard pre-reduction roasting step in Zn metallurgy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Smelting (Slag Formation)
description: Acidic flux \(SiO_2\) removes basic impurity \(FeO\) as fusible slag (iron silicate) during copper smelting. Flux + gangue \(\rightarrow\) slag.

subject: Chemistry
title: Blast Furnace Reduction (Iron)
description: Indirect reduction of haematite by CO at the upper (lower-temperature) zones of the blast furnace. CO is the main reducing agent here.

subject: Chemistry
title: Coke Combustion & CO Generation
description: Combustion zone reactions generating heat and reducing gas CO (Boudouard reaction \(CO_2 + C \rightleftharpoons 2CO\)) which reduces the ore upstream.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bessemerisation (Copper)
description: Blast of air through molten matte in Bessemer converter: FeS oxidised & slagged off, then self-reduction yields blister copper. \(SiO_2\) added as flux.

subject: Chemistry
title: Thermite (Aluminothermy) Reaction
description: Goldschmidt thermite process: Al reduces oxides of Cr/Mn/Fe (less reactive metals); highly exothermic giving molten metal. \(3Mn_3O_4 + 8Al \rightarrow 9Mn + 4Al_2O_3\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Electrolytic Refining
visual_data: \text{Anode: } M \rightarrow M^{n+} + ne^-; \quad \text{Cathode: } M^{n+} + ne^- \rightarrow M
description: Impure metal anode dissolves, pure metal deposits at cathode; insoluble impurities form anode mud. \(M\)=metal (Cu, Ag, Au, Al), \(n\)=valency.

subject: Chemistry
title: Faraday's Law (Metal Deposited)
visual_data: w = \frac{E \cdot I \cdot t}{F} = \frac{M \cdot I \cdot t}{n \cdot F}
description: Mass of metal refined/deposited at cathode. \(w\)=mass, \(E\)=equivalent weight \(=M/n\), \(M\)=molar mass, \(I\)=current, \(t\)=time, \(n\)=electrons, \(F=96500\,C\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Feasibility of Reduction (Ellingham)
description: A reductant reduces a metal oxide only if net \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\), i.e. its oxidation line lies BELOW the metal-oxide line in the Ellingham diagram. More negative \(\Delta G^\circ\) line reduces the upper one.

subject: Chemistry
title: C/CO Crossover Temperature
visual_data: C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2 \;(\Delta S^\circ \approx 0); \quad 2C + O_2 \rightarrow 2CO \;(\Delta S^\circ > 0)
description: Why C is a cheap universal reductant: the \(C \to CO\) line slopes DOWNWARD (\(\Delta S^\circ>0\)), so above a crossover T it falls below every metal-oxide line, making reduction spontaneous.

subject: Chemistry
title: Leaching of Bauxite (Baeyer)
description: Concentration of bauxite: amphoteric \(Al_2O_3\) dissolves in hot conc. NaOH leaving \(Fe_2O_3\)/\(SiO_2\) impurities; sodium aluminate (or sodium tetrahydroxoaluminate) formed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Baeyer Precipitation of Alumina
description: Aluminate solution seeded/treated with \(CO_2\) to precipitate \(Al(OH)_3\), then calcined to pure alumina feed for the Hall-Heroult cell.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cryolite Role (Hall-Heroult)
description: Cryolite \(Na_3AlF_6\) + fluorspar \(CaF_2\) lower the fusion temperature of alumina (\(2323\,K \rightarrow \sim1173\,K\)) and increase melt conductivity for electrolysis.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hall-Heroult Electrode Reactions
description: Half-reactions of molten alumina electrolysis. Carbon anode is consumed (forming CO/\(CO_2\)), so it is periodically replaced. \(O^{2-}\) from dissolved alumina.

subject: Chemistry
title: Froth Flotation
description: Concentration of sulphide ores: ore particles wetted by oil rise with froth, gangue wetted by water settles. Depressant NaCN can selectively suppress one sulphide (e.g. ZnS).

subject: Chemistry
title: MacArthur-Forrest Displacement
description: Recovery step of cyanide leaching: more electropositive Zn displaces Au (or Ag) from its dicyanido complex. Same for \(2[Ag(CN)_2]^- + Zn \rightarrow [Zn(CN)_4]^{2-} + 2Ag\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Reduction by Active Metals
description: Kroll process: highly electropositive Mg (or Na) reduces volatile metal halide to free metal under inert atmosphere. \(TiCl_4 + 4Na \rightarrow Ti + 4NaCl\) (IMI process).

subject: Chemistry
title: Zone Refining Principle
description: Ultra-purification (Si, Ge, Ga): impurities are more soluble in the molten zone than the solid, so a moving heater sweeps them to one end. \(k\)=distribution coeff; \(k<1\) means impurity concentrates in melt.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chromatographic Separation
description: Refining based on differential adsorption of components on a stationary phase (column chromatography); used to purify elements available in minute amounts / with close properties.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrogen Reduction
description: Reduction of oxide by \(H_2\) for metals whose carbides are undesirable (e.g. tungsten). Gives high-purity metal; also used for \(MoO_3\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Roasting of Galena (Self-Reduction)
description: Partial roasting of galena to PbO then auto-reduction (carbon-free) of remaining sulphide gives lead. Classic self-reduction example alongside Cu.

subject: Chemistry
title: Copper Refining Electrolyte
description: Electrolytic refining of blister copper in acidified \(CuSO_4\); noble metals (Ag, Au, Pt) collect as valuable anode mud while Cu purifies at cathode (>99.95%).

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs-Helmholtz (Ellingham Slope)
description: Thermodynamic basis of every Ellingham line; reduction feasible when \(\Delta G^\circ < 0\). \(\Delta G^\circ\)=standard free energy change, \(\Delta H^\circ\)=enthalpy, \(\Delta S^\circ\)=entropy, \(T\)=temperature (K). Plot of \(\Delta G^\circ\) vs \(T\) has slope \(-\Delta S^\circ\).
derivation:
For metal oxidation \(2M + O_2 \rightarrow 2MO\), gaseous \(O_2\) is consumed so \(\Delta S^\circ < 0\).
Thus \(-\Delta S^\circ > 0\): line slopes UPWARD with \(T\).
For \(2C + O_2 \rightarrow 2CO\), gas moles increase (\(1 \rightarrow 2\)), \(\Delta S^\circ > 0\), so slope is negative: line slopes DOWNWARD.
For \(C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2\), \(\Delta n_{gas}=0\), \(\Delta S^\circ \approx 0\): line is nearly horizontal.

subject: Chemistry
title: Coupling of Ellingham Reactions
description: Net free energy when an oxide is reduced by coupling with an oxidant line; reduction occurs only when the reductant line lies BELOW the metal-oxide line. \(\Delta G^\circ_{net}\)=free energy of overall reduction \(MO+C \rightarrow M+CO\). Subtract the oxide-formation \(\Delta G^\circ\) from the oxidant-oxidation \(\Delta G^\circ\).
derivation:
Formation: \(2M + O_2 \rightarrow 2MO,\; \Delta G^\circ_1\)
Oxidant: \(2C + O_2 \rightarrow 2CO,\; \Delta G^\circ_2\)
Reverse first and add second:
\(2MO + 2C \rightarrow 2M + 2CO,\; \Delta G^\circ_{net} = \Delta G^\circ_2 - \Delta G^\circ_1\)
Feasible when \(\Delta G^\circ_2 < \Delta G^\circ_1\), i.e. carbon line below metal-oxide line at that \(T\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Electrochemical Free Energy
description: Links Ellingham/electrolytic reduction to electrochemistry; gives minimum decomposition voltage to reduce an oxide electrolytically (e.g. alumina). \(\Delta G^\circ\)=free energy change, \(n\)=electrons transferred, \(F\)=96500 C/mol, \(E^\circ\)=standard cell potential, \(E^\circ_{decomp}\)=minimum decomposition EMF.

subject: Chemistry
title: Vapour-Phase Refining Condition
visual_data: T_{\text{(compound formation)}} < T_{\text{(decomposition)}}; \quad M + xL \xrightarrow{T_1} ML_x \xrightarrow{T_2} M + xL
description: General criterion for vapour-phase refining (Mond, Van Arkel); metal forms a volatile compound at low \(T_1\), which decomposes back to pure metal at high \(T_2\). \(M\)=impure metal, \(L\)=ligand/halogen, \(ML_x\)=volatile intermediate. Ni(CO)\(_4\): form ~330-350 K, decompose ~450-470 K; TiI\(_4\)/ZrI\(_4\): form ~523 K, decompose on ~1700 K filament.

subject: Chemistry
title: Haber Process
description: Industrial synthesis of Ammonia. Catalyst: Iron with Molybdenum promoter.
derivation:
According to Le Chatelier's Principle:
1. Concentration: High conc of reactants pushes equilibrium forward.
2. Pressure: Reaction reduces moles (4 mol \(\to\) 2 mol). High Pressure (200 atm) favors product.
3. Temperature: Reaction is Exothermic. Low Temperature favors product, but slows rate.
   Optimization: Moderate Temp (~700K) with Catalyst.

related_concepts.name: Le Chatelier's Principle
related_concepts.definition: If a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts to counteract the disturbance.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ostwald Process
description: Industrial preparation of Nitric Acid via catalytic oxidation of ammonia.
derivation:
Step 1: Catalytic Oxidation (Exothermic)
   \(NH_3\) oxidized to NO over Pt/Rh gauge at 500K, 9 bar.
Step 2: Oxidation to \(NO_2\)
   \(2NO + O_2 \rightleftharpoons 2NO_2\)
Step 3: Absorption in Water
   \(3NO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow 2HNO_3 + NO\)
   The NO produced is recycled.

related_concepts.name: Azeotrope
related_concepts.definition: Constant boiling mixture. Conc. HNO3 forms azeotrope at 68% by mass.

subject: Chemistry
title: Contact Process
description: Manufacture of Sulfuric Acid. Absorption of SO3 in acid prevents fog formation.
derivation:
1. Production of \(SO_2\) (burning sulfur).
2. Conversion to \(SO_3\) (Key Step):
   Reversible and Exothermic. Needs \(V_2O_5\) catalyst, 2 bar pressure, 720K.
3. Absorption:
   Direct reaction \(SO_3 + H_2O\) is too violent.
   Instead, \(SO_3\) is absorbed in 98% \(H_2SO_4\) to form Oleum (\(H_2S_2O_7\)).
   \(H_2S_2O_7 + H_2O \rightarrow 2H_2SO_4\)

related_concepts.name: Oleum
related_concepts.definition: Fuming sulfuric acid (Pyrosulfuric acid), mixture of H2SO4 and SO3.

subject: Chemistry
title: Interhalogen Compounds
description: Compounds formed between two different halogens. X is larger than X'.
derivation:
Formation: Direct combination or reaction of halogen with lower interhalogen.
Structure (VSEPR):
- \(XX'_3\) (e.g., \(ClF_3\)): sp3d, T-shaped (2 lone pairs).
- \(XX'_5\) (e.g., \(BrF_5\)): sp3d2, Square Pyramidal (1 lone pair).
- \(XX'_7\) (e.g., \(IF_7\)): sp3d3, Pentagonal Bipyramidal.
Reactivity: Bond \(X-X'\) is weaker than \(X-X\) (except F-F), making them highly reactive.

related_concepts.name: Pseudo-halide
related_concepts.definition: Polyatomic anions (like CN-, SCN-) that resemble halide ions in chemistry.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis of XeF6
description: Complete hydrolysis of Xenon Hexafluoride yields explosive Xenon Trioxide.
derivation:
Mechanism involves stepwise replacement of F atoms with O.
1. Partial: \(XeF_6 + H_2O \rightarrow XeOF_4 + 2HF\)
2. Partial: \(XeOF_4 + H_2O \rightarrow XeO_2F_2 + 2HF\)
3. Complete: \(XeO_2F_2 + H_2O \rightarrow XeO_3 + 2HF\)
\(XeO_3\) has Pyramidal structure (sp3, 1 lone pair).

related_concepts.name: Noble Gas Chemistry
related_concepts.definition: Study of compounds involving Group 18 elements, primarily Xenon due to its lower ionization energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Holme's Signal
description: Signal used in ships. Uses spontaneous combustion of Phosphine.
derivation:
A container with Calcium Carbide (\(CaC_2\)) and Calcium Phosphide (\(Ca_3P_2\)) is thrown into the sea.
1. Water enters, reacting to release Acetylene (\(C_2H_2\)) and Phosphine (\(PH_3\)).
2. Impure \(PH_3\) (containing \(P_2H_4\)) catches fire spontaneously.
3. This ignites the Acetylene, producing a bright luminous flame.

related_concepts.name: Phosphine
related_concepts.definition: Toxic gas (PH3) with rotten fish smell. Weak base compared to Ammonia.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of White Phosphorus
description: Discrete tetrahedral P4 molecules. Highly reactive and glows in dark (chemiluminescence).
derivation:
Structure:
4 Phosphorus atoms at corners of a regular tetrahedron.
Each P is bonded to 3 other P atoms.
Bond Angle (PPP) = 60°.
Strain:
Ideal angle for p-orbitals is 90° (or sp3 109.5°).
The deviation to 60° creates immense Angular Strain.
Result: P-P bonds are weak and easily broken, making White P highly reactive.

related_concepts.name: Red Phosphorus
related_concepts.definition: Polymeric structure formed by opening P4 rings. Less strained, less reactive, non-toxic.

subject: Chemistry
title: Basicity of Oxoacids (P)
description: Basicity depends on the number of ionizable -OH groups.
derivation:
Structure Logic:
Phosphorus forms sp3 hybrid orbitals (Tetrahedral).
One bond is always \(P=O\).
Rest are \(P-OH\) or \(P-H\).
- \(H_3PO_4\) (Orthophosphoric): 1 \(P=O\), 3 \(P-OH\). 3 H+ can release. Basicity = 3.
- \(H_3PO_3\) (Phosphorous): 1 \(P=O\), 2 \(P-OH\), 1 \(P-H\). Basicity = 2.
- \(H_3PO_2\) (Hypophosphorous): 1 \(P=O\), 1 \(P-OH\), 2 \(P-H\). Basicity = 1.

related_concepts.name: Reducing Property
related_concepts.definition: P-H bonds are responsible for reducing character. H3PO2 is a strong reducing agent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of XeF4
description: Xenon Tetrafluoride geometry via VSEPR theory.
derivation:
Electron Count:
Xe (Valence) = 8.
F (Monovalent) = 4.
Total Pairs = (8+4)/2 = 6.
Hybridization: \(sp^3d^2\) (Octahedral geometry).
Bond Pairs = 4 (Xe-F).
Lone Pairs = 6 - 4 = 2.
Arrangement: To minimize repulsion, the 2 Lone Pairs occupy axial positions (180° apart).
Shape: Square Planar.

related_concepts.name: VSEPR Theory
related_concepts.definition: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory predicts geometry based on minimizing e- pair repulsion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis of NCl3
description: Nitrogen Trichloride hydrolyzes explosively. NF3 does NOT hydrolyze.
derivation:
Reason for Hydrolysis:
Chlorine has vacant d-orbitals.
Water oxygen (Nucleophile) attacks the Cl atom.
Intermediate forms, N-Cl bond breaks.
\(H\) goes to \(N\), \(OH\) goes to \(Cl\).
Repeat 3 times \(\rightarrow NH_3 + 3HOCl\).
Contrast \(NF_3\): Fluorine has NO d-orbitals, and C-F bond is strong, so no hydrolysis.

related_concepts.name: Orbital Availability
related_concepts.definition: Absence of d-orbitals in Period 2 elements limits their covalency and reactivity patterns.

subject: Chemistry
title: Borazine Structure
description: Inorganic Benzene. Isoelectronic with benzene.
derivation:
Synthesis: $3B_2H_6 + 6NH_3 \rightarrow 2B_3N_3H_6 + 12H_2$.
Structure:
Planar hexagonal ring with alternating B and N atoms.
Backbonding: N donates lone pair to empty p-orbital of B.
Reactivity: Unlike benzene, it undergoes addition reactions because the B-N bond is polar.

related_concepts.name: Back Bonding
related_concepts.definition: Transfer of electrons from a filled orbital of one atom to an empty orbital of an adjacent atom.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diborane Structure
description: Electron deficient bonding in $B_2H_6$.
derivation:
Boron ($s^2 p^1$) has only 3 valence electrons but forms 4 bonds in dimer.
Terminal H: 4 normal $2c-2e$ bonds.
Bridging H: 2 bonds where one H atom bridges two Boron atoms.
Configuration: $B-H-B$.
Electrons involved: 2 (one from B, one from H). Atoms involved: 3.
Result: Three-center two-electron bond.

related_concepts.name: Electron Deficient
related_concepts.definition: Molecules that do not have enough electrons to form normal 2-electron bonds between all atoms.

subject: Chemistry
title: Silicates (Basic Unit)
description: Tetrahedral structural unit of all silicates.
derivation:
Silicon is $sp^3$ hybridized.
Si is at the center, bonded to 4 Oxygen atoms at the corners of a tetrahedron.
Sharing of corners (Oxygen atoms) leads to chains, sheets, and 3D networks.
- 0 shared: Orthosilicate.
- 1 shared: Pyrosilicate.
- 2 shared: Chain silicate.

related_concepts.name: Zeolites
related_concepts.definition: Aluminosilicates with microporous structures used as catalysts (e.g., ZSM-5).

subject: Chemistry
title: Deacon's Process
description: Industrial recovery of Chlorine from HCl byproduct.
derivation:
Catalytic Oxidation.
Catalyst: Cupric Chloride ($CuCl_2$).
Mechanism: Cu acts as oxygen carrier.
1. $2CuCl_2 \to Cu_2Cl_2 + Cl_2$
2. $Cu_2Cl_2 + O_2 \to 2CuO + Cl_2$
3. $CuO + 2HCl \to CuCl_2 + H_2O$
Net: Oxidation of HCl by air.

related_concepts.name: Weldon's Process
related_concepts.definition: Older method using $MnO_2$ to oxidize HCl: $MnO_2 + 4HCl \to MnCl_2 + Cl_2$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Marshall's Acid (Structure)
description: Contains Peroxide linkage ($O-O$). Oxidation state of S is +6.
derivation:
Calculating O.S. using formula gives $2x + 2(1) + 8(-2) = 0 \implies x = +7$ (Wrong, max is +6).
Structure Logic:
Two $HSO_4$ units joined by peroxide bridge.
$HO-SO_2-O-O-SO_2-OH$.
The two peroxide oxygens have O.S. -1.
Calc: $2x + 2(+1) + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \implies x = +6$.

related_concepts.name: Caro's Acid
related_concepts.definition: Peroxomonosulfuric acid ($H_2SO_5$). Contains one peroxide group ($S-O-O-H$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Boric Acid Structure
description: Planar $BO_3$ units linked by Hydrogen Bonds. Slippery solid.
derivation:
Hybridization: Boron is $sp^2$ (Trigonal Planar).
Network:
Each $B(OH)_3$ unit is H-bonded to 6 others.
This creates a sheet-like structure similar to graphite.
Weak Van der Waals forces between layers make it soft/slippery.
Acidity: Acts as Lewis acid accepting $OH^-$ from water, not proton donor.

related_concepts.name: Lewis Acid
related_concepts.definition: An electron pair acceptor ($B(OH)_3 + H_2O \rightleftharpoons [B(OH)_4]^- + H^+$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Silicones (Polymers)
description: Organosilicon polymers. Water repellent, heat resistant.
derivation:
Synthesis:
1. $RCl + Si \xrightarrow{Cu} R_2SiCl_2$ (Rochow Process).
2. Hydrolysis: $R_2SiCl_2 + H_2O \rightarrow R_2Si(OH)_2$.
3. Polymerization: Condensation of silanols with loss of water.
   Forms $Si-O-Si$ backbone with organic $R$ side groups.
Chain length controlled by adding $R_3SiCl$ (Chain terminator).

related_concepts.name: Hydrophobic
related_concepts.definition: Water-repelling nature due to non-polar alkyl groups on the surface.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of PCl5 (Solid)
description: In solid state, PCl5 exists as an ionic solid to improve packing efficiency.
derivation:
1. Gas Phase: Trigonal Bipyramidal ($sp^3d$).
2. Solid Phase: Auto-ionization occurs.
   $2PCl_5 \rightarrow [PCl_4]^+ + [PCl_6]^-$.
   - Cation $[PCl_4]^+$: Tetrahedral ($sp^3$).
   - Anion $[PCl_6]^-$: Octahedral ($sp^3d^2$).
   This arrangement maximizes electrostatic lattice energy.

related_concepts.name: PBr5 Solid
related_concepts.definition: Exists as $[PBr_4]^+ Br^-$ because huge $[PBr_6]^-$ is sterically unstable.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of H2O2
description: Non-planar structure. Dihedral angle depends on phase.
derivation:
O-O bond allows rotation, but lone pair repulsion creates a twisted shape.
1. Gas Phase: Dihedral angle $\approx 111.5^\circ$. Minimized repulsion.
2. Solid Phase: Dihedral angle $\approx 90.2^\circ$.
   Reason: Strong intermolecular Hydrogen Bonding in the crystal lattice pulls the structure closer.

related_concepts.name: Peroxide Linkage
related_concepts.definition: O-O single bond, characteristic of peroxides, oxidation state -1.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of P4O10
description: Dimer of P2O5. Dehydrating agent.
derivation:
Geometry: Based on $P_4$ tetrahedron.
1. Insert an Oxygen atom into each of the 6 P-P edges (Bridging Oxygens).
2. Add a terminal Oxygen atom to each of the 4 Phosphorus atoms ($P=O$).
Total P-O-P bonds = 6.
Each P is surrounded by 4 Oxygens (Tetrahedral environment).

related_concepts.name: Anhydride
related_concepts.definition: P4O10 is the anhydride of Phosphoric Acid ($P_4O_{10} + 6H_2O \rightarrow 4H_3PO_4$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of N2O5
description: Dinitrogen Pentoxide. Structure changes with phase.
derivation:
1. Gas Phase: Covalent molecule. Planar. $N-O-N$ bond angle is non-linear.
   Resonance makes terminal N-O bonds identical.
2. Solid Phase: Nitronium Nitrate.
   Ionizes to $[NO_2]^+$ (Linear, sp) and $[NO_3]^-$ (Trigonal Planar, sp2).
   This ionic character makes it a solid at room temp.

related_concepts.name: Anhydride
related_concepts.definition: N2O5 is the anhydride of Nitric Acid ($N_2O_5 + H_2O \rightarrow 2HNO_3$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of ClO2
description: Chlorine Dioxide. Paramagnetic yellow gas.
derivation:
Valence Electrons: $7 (Cl) + 2 \times 6 (O) = 19 e^-$.
Structure: Bent shape ($sp^2$ hybridized Cl).
Unpaired electron is delocalized, but ClO2 does not dimerize easily (unlike $NO_2$).
Bond Angle: $117^\circ$ (Repulsion between double bonds > single electron).

related_concepts.name: Bleaching Agent
related_concepts.definition: Used in paper industry; acts by oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of I3-
description: Triiodide ion. Formed when $I_2$ dissolves in KI.
derivation:
Central Atom: Iodine.
Valence e-: 7 + 2 (bonding) + 1 (charge) = 10.
Electron Pairs: 5.
Hybridization: $sp^3d$.
Geometry: Trigonal Bipyramidal.
Lone Pairs: 3 (Equatorial positions to minimize repulsion).
Bond Pairs: 2 (Axial positions).
Shape: Linear ($180^\circ$).

related_concepts.name: Polyhalides
related_concepts.definition: Ions like $I_3^-$, $Br_3^-$, $ICl_2^-$ formed by halogens combining with halide ions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bleaching Powder
description: Commercial formula. Active ingredient is Calcium Hypochlorite.
derivation:
Preparation: Action of Chlorine gas on Dry Slaked Lime.
$Ca(OH)_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CaOCl_2 + H_2O$.
Mechanism of Bleaching:
$CaOCl_2 + H_2SO_4 \text{ (dil)} \rightarrow CaSO_4 + CaCl_2 + 2HOCl$.
$HOCl \rightarrow HCl + [O]$ (Nascent Oxygen).
Nascent oxygen oxidizes colored matter to colorless.

related_concepts.name: Available Chlorine
related_concepts.definition: Measure of bleaching powder quality, determined by iodine liberation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of S8
description: Most stable allotrope of Sulfur (Rhombic/Monoclinic).
derivation:
Atomic Arrangement:
8 Sulfur atoms form a cyclic ring.
To minimize repulsion between lone pairs on adjacent Sulfurs, the ring adopts a non-planar 'Crown' conformation.
Bond Angle: $107^\circ$.
Dihedral Angle: $98^\circ$.
Note: $S_6$ (Chair form) is another allotrope.

related_concepts.name: Catenation
related_concepts.definition: Self-linking property. Sulfur shows strong catenation (second only to Carbon).

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of Borax Anion
description: The structural unit in Borax ($Na_2[B_4O_5(OH)_4] \cdot 8H_2O$).
derivation:
Network of Boron and Oxygen:
1. Two Boron atoms are $sp^2$ (Triangular).
2. Two Boron atoms are $sp^3$ (Tetrahedral).
3. Five $B-O-B$ linkages form two 6-membered rings fused together.
4. Four $-OH$ groups are attached, one to each Boron.
Correct formula emphasizes it contains 8 water molecules of crystallization.

related_concepts.name: Buffer Action
related_concepts.definition: Borax solution acts as a buffer (pH ~9) due to formation of weak acid $H_3BO_3$ and $OH^-$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Silanes (General Formula)
description: Silicon hydrides. Homologous series similar to Alkanes but much more reactive.
derivation:
Stability:
Si-Si and Si-H bonds are weaker than C-C and C-H bonds.
Reactivity:
Spontaneously flammable in air: $SiH_4 + 2O_2 \rightarrow SiO_2 + 2H_2O$.
Hydrolysis: Reacts with water/alkali to release Hydrogen.
$SiH_4 + 2H_2O \rightarrow SiO_2 + 4H_2 \uparrow$.

related_concepts.name: Reducing Agent
related_concepts.definition: Silanes are strong reducing agents used in organic synthesis.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cyclotrimetaphosphoric Acid
description: Cyclic trimer of metaphosphoric acid.
derivation:
Structure:
Six-membered ring with alternating P and O atoms.
Each Phosphorus is bonded to:
- Two ring oxygens.
- One terminal oxygen ($P=O$).
- One hydroxyl group ($-OH$).
It is tribasic (3 ionizable protons).

related_concepts.name: Polyphosphates
related_concepts.definition: Linear or cyclic polymers containing P-O-P linkages.

subject: Chemistry
title: Inert Pair Effect
description: Reluctance of s-electrons to participate in bonding in heavy post-transition elements.
derivation:
Cause: Poor shielding by d and f orbitals.
Effect: The valence s-electrons ($ns^2$) are held tightly by the nucleus.
Trend: Stability of lower oxidation state ($Group No. - 2$) increases down the group.
Example: $Pb^{+2}$ is more stable than $Pb^{+4}$ (Lead storage battery works on this stability).

related_concepts.name: Oxidizing Agent
related_concepts.definition: $PbO_2$ and $Bi(V)$ are strong oxidizers because they want to revert to +2 and +3 states respectively.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bridge Bonding (Al2Cl6)
description: Dimer structure of Aluminum Chloride.
derivation:
Aluminum in $AlCl_3$ is electron deficient (6e).
To complete octet, it accepts a lone pair from Chlorine of another $AlCl_3$ molecule.
Geometry: Each Al is Tetrahedral.
Two types of Al-Cl bonds: Terminal (shorter) and Bridging (longer).
Unlike $B_2H_6$ (3c-2e), this bridge involves a full lone pair (3c-4e).

related_concepts.name: Dimerization
related_concepts.definition: Process where two identical molecules join. $Al_2Cl_6$ dissociates to monomer at high temp.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis Mechanism (SiCl4 vs CCl4)
description: Role of d-orbitals in hydrolysis.
derivation:
1. $SiCl_4$: Silicon has vacant 3d orbitals.
   Water oxygen attacks Si, expanding its coordination number.
   $Cl^-$ leaves, OH replaces it.
2. $CCl_4$: Carbon has no d-orbitals (Period 2).
   Steric crowding prevents backside attack on Carbon.
   Result: $CCl_4$ is inert to hydrolysis.

related_concepts.name: Expansion of Octet
related_concepts.definition: Ability of elements from Period 3 onwards to accommodate more than 8 valence electrons.

subject: Chemistry
title: Silicate Types
description: Classification based on number of shared oxygen corners per tetrahedron.
derivation:
Basic Unit: $SiO_4^{4-}$.
- Ortho: 0 shared ($SiO_4^{4-}$).
- Pyro: 1 shared ($Si_2O_7^{6-}$).
- Cyclic/Chain: 2 shared ($(SiO_3)_n^{2n-}$).
- Sheet: 3 shared ($Si_2O_5^{2-}$).
- 3D Network: 4 shared ($SiO_2$).

related_concepts.name: Tectosilicates
related_concepts.definition: 3D network silicates like Quartz and Feldspars.

subject: Chemistry
title: Xenon Fluoride Hydrolysis
description: Redox hydrolysis for XeF2; Non-redox for XeF6.
derivation:
1. $XeF_2$: Unstable in water. Oxidizes water to $O_2$ and reduces itself to $Xe$ gas.
2. $XeF_4$: Disproportionation. Gives $Xe$, $XeO_3$, $HF$, $O_2$.
3. $XeF_6$: Complete hydrolysis yields explosive $XeO_3$ (Xenon Trioxide) + $HF$. No change in O.S. (+6).

related_concepts.name: Partial Hydrolysis
related_concepts.definition: $XeF_6 + H_2O \to XeOF_4 + 2HF$.

subject: Chemistry
title: Interhalogen Shapes
description: VSEPR structures of $XX'_n$.
derivation:
1. $ClF_3$: 7+21=28e. 3 Bond Pairs, 2 Lone Pairs. T-shape to put LPs equatorial.
2. $BrF_5$: 7+35=42e. 5 BPs, 1 LP. Square Pyramidal.
3. $IF_7$: 7+49=56e. 7 BPs, 0 LPs. Pentagonal Bipyramidal.

related_concepts.name: Berry Pseudorotation
related_concepts.definition: Mechanism allowing axial and equatorial ligands to swap in trigonal bipyramidal molecules.

subject: Chemistry
title: Brown Ring Test
description: Classic test for nitrate ion \(NO_3^-\); brown ring at the interface. \(Fe^{2+}\) is oxidised by \(NO_3^-\) (in conc. \(H_2SO_4\)) to \(Fe^{3+}\), and the liberated \(NO\) coordinates to \(Fe^{2+}\) giving the brown nitrosyl-iron complex.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ring Test Redox
description: Reduction of nitrate that supplies \(NO\) for the brown ring test. \(Fe^{2+}\)=reductant, \(NO_3^-\)=oxidant in acidic medium.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aqua Regia
description: 1:3 conc. \(HNO_3\):\(HCl\) mixture that dissolves noble metals (Au, Pt) by supplying nascent chlorine. \(NOCl\)=nitrosyl chloride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Conc. HNO3 with Cu
description: Reaction of copper with concentrated nitric acid liberating brown \(NO_2\). Dilute \(HNO_3\) gives \(NO\) instead.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dilute HNO3 with Cu
description: Reaction of copper with dilute nitric acid liberating colourless \(NO\) (browns in air). Contrast with conc. \(HNO_3\) which gives \(NO_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Lab Prep of NH3
description: Laboratory preparation of ammonia by heating an ammonium salt with slaked lime; \(NH_3\) dried over CaO (not \(H_2SO_4\)/\(CaCl_2\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Thermal Decomp. of NH4NO3
description: Controlled heating of ammonium nitrate is the lab route to nitrous oxide (laughing gas) \(N_2O\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Disproportionation of P4 (alkali)
description: Ionic form showing P disproportionating from \(0\) to \(-3\) (in \(PH_3\)) and \(+1\) (in hypophosphite).

subject: Chemistry
title: PCl3 from White P
description: Direct chlorination of white phosphorus (limited \(Cl_2\)) gives phosphorus trichloride; excess \(Cl_2\) gives \(PCl_5\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrolysis of PCl3
description: PCl3 fumes in moist air; hydrolysis gives phosphorous acid \(H_3PO_3\). Also reacts with -OH compounds.

subject: Chemistry
title: PCl5 Geometry (Gas)
description: Gaseous/molten \(PCl_5\) is TBP with unequal P-Cl bonds (axial \(>\) equatorial); solid is ionic \([PCl_4]^+[PCl_6]^-\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation States of P Oxoacids
description: Oxidation number of P in common oxoacids; higher O.S. is less reducing. \(H_3PO_2\)=hypophosphorous, \(H_3PO_3\)=phosphorous, \(H_3PO_4\)=orthophosphoric.

subject: Chemistry
title: P-H Bonds and Basicity
description: P-OH protons are ionisable (acidic); P-H bonds are not and give reducing power. \(H_3PO_4\):3 P-OH (tribasic), \(H_3PO_3\):2 P-OH + 1 P-H (dibasic), \(H_3PO_2\):1 P-OH + 2 P-H (monobasic).

subject: Chemistry
title: Pyrophosphoric Acid
description: Condensed (di)phosphoric acid formed on dehydrating two \(H_3PO_4\); tetrabasic with a P-O-P bridge.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lab Prep of SO2
description: Laboratory preparation of sulphur dioxide by acidifying a sulphite; \(SO_2\) is angular (\(sp^2\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Lab Prep of H2S
description: Kipp's apparatus preparation of hydrogen sulphide from iron(II) sulphide and dilute acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dehydrating Action of H2SO4
description: Concentrated sulphuric acid chars sugar by removing water (strong dehydrating agent).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidising Action of Hot Conc. H2SO4
description: Hot concentrated \(H_2SO_4\) acts as an oxidiser, itself reduced to \(SO_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Caro's Acid
description: Peroxo-oxoacid of sulphur with one \(-O-O-H\) (peroxide) linkage; S in \(+6\). Contrast Marshall's acid \(H_2S_2O_8\).

subject: Chemistry
title: S-O-O Peroxo Linkages
description: Number of peroxide \(-O-O-\) bonds: both Caro's and Marshall's acid have exactly one; ordinary \(H_2SO_4\) has none.

subject: Chemistry
title: S in Oxoacids (Oxidation State)
description: Oxidation number of S in key oxoacids; thiosulphuric \(H_2S_2O_3\) is conventionally taken as average \(+2\). \(H_2SO_3\)=sulphurous, \(H_2SO_4\)=sulphuric.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lab Prep of Cl2 (MnO2)
description: Laboratory preparation of chlorine by oxidising conc. HCl with manganese dioxide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lab Prep of HCl
description: Preparation of hydrogen chloride from rock salt and conc. \(H_2SO_4\); at higher T gives \(Na_2SO_4 + 2HCl\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Chlorine + Cold Dilute NaOH
description: Disproportionation of \(Cl_2\) (0 \(\to\) -1, +1) in cold dilute alkali giving chloride + hypochlorite (bleach).

subject: Chemistry
title: Chlorine + Hot Conc. NaOH
description: Disproportionation of \(Cl_2\) (0 \(\to\) -1, +5) in hot concentrated alkali giving chloride + chlorate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Halogen Oxoacid Acid Strength
description: Acid strength rises with oxidation state / number of terminal O atoms (greater anion stabilisation). \(HClO_4\) is the strongest oxoacid of Cl.

subject: Chemistry
title: Borax to Boric Acid
description: Acidification of borax yields orthoboric acid; basis of borax titration with acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Borax Bead Test
description: On heating, borax loses water and gives a glassy bead of sodium metaborate + boric anhydride \(B_2O_3\), which forms coloured metaborates with transition metal ions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Boric Acid as Lewis Acid
description: Boric acid is a weak monobasic Lewis acid: it accepts \(OH^-\) from water rather than donating \(H^+\). \(pK_a \approx 9.25\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Diborane + Water
description: Diborane is readily hydrolysed by water to boric acid with liberation of hydrogen.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diborane Combustion
description: Combustion of diborane is highly exothermic (high heat of combustion -> rocket fuel interest).

subject: Chemistry
title: Amphoterism of Al2O3 / Al(OH)3
description: Aluminium oxide/hydroxide dissolves in both acid (salt) and base (aluminate) -> amphoteric. \(NaAlO_2\)=sodium meta-aluminate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Thermite Reaction
description: Highly exothermic aluminothermic reduction; Al is a strong reducing agent used to weld rails and extract less-reactive metals.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbon Monoxide as Reductant
description: CO is a powerful reducing agent (lone pair on C); reduces metal oxides in the blast furnace.

subject: Chemistry
title: CO2 with Lime Water
visual_data: Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3 + H_2O; \quad CaCO_3 + CO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(HCO_3)_2
description: Lime-water turns milky with \(CO_2\) (\(CaCO_3\)) and clears with excess \(CO_2\) (soluble bicarbonate). Standard test for \(CO_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: CO2 Geometry
description: Carbon dioxide is linear, \(sp\)-hybridised, nonpolar; contrast bent \(SO_2\) and \(SiO_2\) (giant covalent).

subject: Chemistry
title: Drago's Rule (No Hybridisation)
description: For heavier p-block hydrides (3rd period onward) with low electronegativity central atom, bonds use nearly pure p-orbitals, so angles approach \(90^\circ\) and hybridisation is not assumed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bond Angle Trend in Hydrides (15)
description: Group-15 hydride bond angle decreases down the group (lower electronegativity -> more p-character, less bp-bp repulsion).

subject: Chemistry
title: Thermal Stability of Hydrides (15)
description: Stability of group-15 hydrides decreases down the group as E-H bond strength falls; \(BiH_3\) least stable.

subject: Chemistry
title: Reducing Power of Hydrides (16)
description: Reducing character of group-16 hydrides increases down the group (weaker E-H bond); thermal stability shows the reverse order.

subject: Chemistry
title: HX Acid Strength (17)
description: Acidic strength of hydrogen halides increases down the group; \(HF\) is weakest due to strong H-F bond and H-bonding.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bond Enthalpy Anomaly (Halogens)
description: X-X bond dissociation enthalpy order; \(F_2\) is anomalously low due to interelectronic repulsion of lone pairs in the small F atom.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidising Power of Halogens
description: Standard reduction potential / oxidising ability decreases down group 17; \(F_2\) is the strongest oxidiser among them.

subject: Chemistry
title: Electron Gain Enthalpy Anomaly
description: Chlorine has more negative electron gain enthalpy than fluorine (small F atom -> high e-e repulsion in 2p). Same anomaly: O<S, N<P.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fluorine + Water
description: Fluorine oxidises water to oxygen (and some \(O_3\)); unlike \(Cl_2/Br_2\) which disproportionate in water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lattice/Hydration & Anomalous Sln.
description: Iodine dissolves in KI by forming the triiodide ion \(I_3^-\); accounts for the brown solution and \(I_3^-\) linear structure.

subject: Chemistry
title: Catenation Tendency (14)
description: Self-linking (E-E bond) ability in group 14 falls sharply down the group as bond enthalpy decreases; C is exceptional.

subject: Chemistry
title: Allotrope Conductivity (C)
description: Graphite conducts via delocalised \(\pi\) electrons (layered \(sp^2\)); diamond is a hard insulator (3D \(sp^3\) network).

subject: Chemistry
title: Fullerene Composition
description: Buckminsterfullerene is a soccer-ball cage; only allotrope of carbon that is molecular and soluble. Each C is \(sp^2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation of NO
description: Colourless \(NO\) instantly browns in air forming \(NO_2\); explains the brown fumes in nitric acid reactions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dimerisation of NO2
description: Brown paramagnetic \(NO_2\) (odd electron) dimerises to colourless diamagnetic \(N_2O_4\); favoured by cooling.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ozone Preparation & Decomp.
description: Ozone forms endothermically from \(O_2\); it is thermodynamically unstable and a powerful oxidiser. Bent molecule (\(sp^2\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Ozone Estimation (Iodometry)
description: Ozone oxidises iodide to iodine (estimated by titrating \(I_2\) with thiosulphate); distinguishes \(O_3\) from \(O_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Aluminium Passivation by HNO3
description: Conc. \(HNO_3\) renders Al, Fe, Cr passive by forming a protective oxide film; hence conc. \(HNO_3\) is transported in Al containers.

subject: Chemistry
title: Inertness of N2 (Bond Order)
description: Triple bond with very high bond enthalpy makes \(N_2\) inert at room temperature; explains why nitrogen fixation is difficult.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oleum Formation
description: Oleum (fuming/pyrosulphuric acid) from Contact Process. \(H_2S_2O_7\)=oleum; absorbing \(SO_3\) in conc. \(H_2SO_4\) avoids fog. Diluting oleum gives \(H_2SO_4\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Thiosulphate + Iodine (Iodometry)
description: Iodometric titration end-step; hypo reduces \(I_2\). \(S_2O_3^{2-}\)(+2)\(\to S_4O_6^{2-}\)(+2.5, tetrathionate). Starch=indicator (blue\(\to\)colourless).

subject: Chemistry
title: Thiosulphate + Dilute Acid
description: Hypo with dilute acid disproportionates to S + \(SO_2\) (milky turbidity). Confirms \(S_2O_3^{2-}\); basis of clock reaction.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hypo in Photography
