description: 'Hypo' fixes photographic film by dissolving unexposed \(AgBr\) as soluble dithiosulphato complex. \(Na_3[Ag(S_2O_3)_2]\)=soluble fixing complex.

subject: Chemistry
title: Allotropes of Phosphorus
description: Order of stability/reactivity. White=discrete \(P_4\), strained 60° angle, reactive, toxic; Red=polymeric chains of \(P_4\), stable; Black=most stable, layered.

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of P4O6
description: Phosphorus trioxide (P in +3). 4 P at tetrahedron corners, 6 bridging O on edges, NO terminal \(P{=}O\). Contrast \(P_4O_{10}\) (adds 4 terminal \(P{=}O\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: P4O6 / P4O10 with Water
description: Anhydrides of P oxoacids. \(P_4O_6\)(+3)\(\to\) phosphorous acid; \(P_4O_{10}\)(+5)\(\to\) phosphoric acid. \(P_4O_{10}\)=powerful dehydrating agent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Geometry of SF6
description: Group 16 fluoride. \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation, 6 bond pairs, no lone pair. Kinetically inert (steric crowding shields S), hence non-hydrolysed.

subject: Chemistry
title: SF6 Inertness vs SeF6/TeF6
description: Steric, not thermodynamic, inertness. S too small/shielded for \(H_2O\) attack; larger Se, Te allow \(H_2O\) approach so \(SeF_6\)/\(TeF_6\) hydrolyse.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bleaching by Cl2 (Nascent O)
description: Permanent bleaching by Cl\(_2\)/HOCl via oxidation (nascent oxygen \([O]\)). Acts only in moist conditions; oxidative bleaching is irreversible (vs \(SO_2\) reductive).

subject: Chemistry
title: Interhalogen Hybridisation Table
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} ClF_3: sp^3d,\ \text{T-shape} \\ BrF_5: sp^3d^2,\ \text{sq. pyramidal} \\ IF_7: sp^3d^3,\ \text{pentagonal bipyramidal} \end{array}
description: Specific hybridisation+shape of interhalogens. \(ClF_3\)(2 lp), \(BrF_5\)(1 lp), \(IF_7\)(0 lp, \(sp^3d^3\)) — \(IF_7\) is the classic trick (rare \(sp^3d^3\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Xenon Compound Shapes
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} XeF_2: sp^3d,\ \text{linear (3 lp)} \\ XeF_4: sp^3d^2,\ \text{square planar (2 lp)} \\ XeF_6: sp^3d^3,\ \text{distorted octahedral (1 lp)} \end{array}
description: VSEPR of Xe fluorides. \(XeF_2\)=2 bp+3 lp linear; \(XeF_4\)=4 bp+2 lp sq. planar; \(XeF_6\)=6 bp+1 lp distorted octahedral.

subject: Chemistry
title: Xenon Oxide / Oxofluoride Shapes
visual_data: XeO_3: sp^3,\ \text{pyramidal (1 lp)}; \quad XeOF_4: sp^3d^2,\ \text{square pyramidal (1 lp)}
description: Xe oxygen-species shapes. \(XeO_3\)=3 bp+1 lp pyramidal (explosive); \(XeOF_4\)=5 bp+1 lp square pyramidal.

subject: Chemistry
title: Partial Hydrolysis of XeF6
description: Stepwise (partial) hydrolysis of \(XeF_6\); complete hydrolysis gives \(XeO_3\). Products: oxofluorides \(XeOF_4\), \(XeO_2F_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Diagonal Relationship B-Si
visual_data: B \sim Si: \text{covalent hydrides, acidic oxides, similar } \frac{\text{charge}}{\text{radius}}
description: B (Gp 13) resembles Si (Gp 14) diagonally. Both: form covalent volatile hydrides, weakly acidic oxides (\(B_2O_3\), \(SiO_2\)), halides hydrolyse, semiconducting/network solids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Anomalous Behaviour of First Member
visual_data: \text{N,O,F: small size, no } d\text{-orbital, high E.N.} \Rightarrow \text{max covalency}=4
description: First member of each p-block group differs (small size, high E.N., no \(d\)-orbitals). E.g. N max covalency 4 (no \(NCl_5\)); F only \(-1\); B no simple \(B^{3+}\); O no \(d\pi\)-\(d\pi\).

subject: Chemistry
title: CO2 with NaOH (mono vs di)
visual_data: CO_2 + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 + H_2O; \quad CO_2(\text{excess}) + NaOH \rightarrow NaHCO_3
description: Product depends on \(CO_2\):NaOH ratio. Excess NaOH \(\to\) carbonate; excess \(CO_2\) \(\to\) bicarbonate. Basis of stoichiometry numericals.

subject: Chemistry
title: Producer Gas vs Water Gas
visual_data: \begin{array}{l} \text{Producer gas: } CO + N_2 \\ C + air \xrightarrow{\Delta} CO + N_2 \\ \text{Water gas (syngas): } CO + H_2 \\ C + H_2O \xrightarrow{1273K} CO + H_2 \end{array}
description: Group 14 industrial fuel gases. Producer gas=\(CO+N_2\) (air over hot coke); water gas/syngas=\(CO+H_2\) (steam over hot coke, endothermic).

subject: Chemistry
title: SO2 as Reducing/Bleaching Agent
description: \(SO_2\) reduces (decolourises acidified \(KMnO_4\)/\(Cl_2\)) and bleaches by reduction (\([H]\)) — temporary, colour returns on air exposure (vs Cl\(_2\) permanent).

subject: Chemistry
title: Phosphine Lab Purity (Spontaneous Combustion)
description: Pure \(PH_3\) is not spontaneously flammable; trace \(P_2H_4\) (diphosphine) impurity causes it to catch fire in air. \(PH_3\) burns to \(P_2O_5\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Markownikoff's Rule
description: Addition to unsymmetrical alkene. Negative part of addendum goes to carbon with fewer hydrogens.
derivation:
Based on Carbocation Stability.
1. Electrophile (\(H^+\)) attacks alkene.
2. Possibility A: Forms \(1^\circ\) carbocation (\(CH_3-CH_2-CH_2^+\)). Unstable.
3. Possibility B: Forms \(2^\circ\) carbocation (\(CH_3-CH^+-CH_3\)). Stable.
4. Nucleophile (\(Br^-\)) attacks the stable carbocation.
Result: 2-Bromopropane (Major).

related_concepts.name: Hyperconjugation
related_concepts.definition: Stabilization interaction that delocalizes electrons, explaining carbocation stability order (3 > 2 > 1).

subject: Chemistry
title: Anti-Markownikoff (Kharasch Effect)
description: Free radical addition. Valid ONLY for HBr with Organic Peroxide.
derivation:
Mechanism: Free Radical Chain Reaction.
1. Initiation: Peroxide homolysis gives Alkoxy radical (\(RO^\bullet\)).
   \(RO^\bullet + HBr \rightarrow ROH + Br^\bullet\)
2. Propagation: \(Br^\bullet\) attacks alkene to form the MORE stable carbon radical.
   \(R-CH=CH_2 + Br^\bullet \rightarrow R-C^\bullet H-CH_2Br\) (Secondary Radical).
3. H-abstraction: Radical takes H from HBr.
   \(R-CH_2-CH_2Br\) + \(Br^\bullet\).

related_concepts.name: Homolysis
related_concepts.definition: Bond cleavage where each atom retains one electron, forming radicals.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ozonolysis (Reductive)
description: Cleavage of double bond to form Carbonyls. Zn prevents oxidation to acid.
derivation:
1. Addition: Ozone adds across double bond to form Molozonide (unstable), which rearranges to Ozonide.
2. Cleavage: Zn dust with water acts as a reducing agent.
   It reacts with the oxygen atom of the ozonide linkage: \(Zn + [O] \rightarrow ZnO\).
   The C-C bond breaks, forming two C=O bonds.
Without Zn, \(H_2O_2\) forms and oxidizes aldehydes.

related_concepts.name: Locating Double Bonds
related_concepts.definition: Ozonolysis is historically used to determine the position of unsaturation in unknown alkenes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kolbe's Electrolysis
description: Electrochemical decarboxylation to form symmetric alkanes.
derivation:
Mechanism: Free Radical.
At Anode (Oxidation):
1. Acetate ion loses electron: \(2CH_3COO^- \rightarrow 2CH_3COO^\bullet + 2e^-\)
2. Decarboxylation: Unstable radical breaks down.
   \(2CH_3COO^\bullet \rightarrow 2CH_3^\bullet + 2CO_2\)
3. Dimerization: Methyl radicals combine.
   \(CH_3^\bullet + CH_3^\bullet \rightarrow C_2H_6\)
pH of solution increases as NaOH is formed at cathode.

related_concepts.name: Soda-Lime Process
related_concepts.definition: Alternative thermal decarboxylation method yielding alkane with one less carbon (R-H).

subject: Chemistry
title: Birch Reduction
description: Stereoselective reduction of internal alkynes to trans-alkenes.
derivation:
Mechanism: Dissolving Metal Reduction.
1. Na donates electron to alkyne \(\rightarrow\) Radical Anion.
2. Protonation by \(NH_3\) \(\rightarrow\) Vinyl Radical.
3. Second electron donation \(\rightarrow\) Vinyl Anion.
4. Second protonation \(\rightarrow\) Alkene.
Stereochemistry: The intermediate Vinyl Anion adopts a Trans geometry to minimize repulsion between the lone pair and the alkyl group.

related_concepts.name: Solvated Electron
related_concepts.definition: Free electron in solution (ammoniated electron), responsible for deep blue color and reducing nature.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lindlar's Catalyst
description: Stereoselective hydrogenation. Catalyst poisoned with Quinoline or Sulfur.
derivation:
Mechanism: Surface Catalysis.
1. Hydrogen adsorbs onto the Palladium surface.
2. Alkyne approaches the surface.
3. Two hydrogen atoms transfer to the alkyne from the *same side* (Syn-addition).
4. Poisoning (Quinoline) lowers catalyst activity, preventing further reduction to alkane.

related_concepts.name: Syn-Addition
related_concepts.definition: Addition of two substituents to the same side (face) of a double or triple bond.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aromatization
description: Conversion of alkanes (6+ carbons) into aromatic hydrocarbons at high T.
derivation:
Process involves Dehydrogenation and Cyclization.
n-Hexane passed over oxide catalyst (Cr, V, or Mo supported on Alumina).
1. Removal of Hydrogen allows ring closure.
2. Formation of conjugated double bonds achieves aromatic stability.
n-Heptane gives Toluene under same conditions.

related_concepts.name: Reforming
related_concepts.definition: Processing of hydrocarbons to improve fuel quality (octane number) often via aromatization.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxymercuration-Demercuration
description: Hydration of alkene. Markovnikov addition. NO Rearrangement.
derivation:
Step 1 (Oxymercuration): Electrophilic attack by $Hg(OAc)^+$.
   Forms cyclic Mercurinium Ion (Bridged).
   Water attacks the *more substituted* carbon (backside).
Step 2 (Demercuration): $NaBH_4$ replaces the $HgOAc$ group with Hydrogen.
Key Advantage: Avoids carbocation rearrangements common in acid-catalyzed hydration.

related_concepts.name: Markovnikov's Rule
related_concepts.definition: Negative part of the addendum attaches to the carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydroboration-Oxidation
visual_data: R-CH=CH_2 \xrightarrow{1. BH_3 \cdot THF}{2. H_2O_2, OH^-} R-CH_2-CH_2-OH
description: Hydration of alkene. Anti-Markovnikov product. Syn-Addition.
derivation:
Step 1: Syn-addition of $H-BH_2$ across the double bond.
   Boron adds to the *less hindered* carbon (Anti-Markovnikov regioselectivity).
   Forms Trialkylborane $R_3B$.
Step 2: Oxidation with alkaline $H_2O_2$.
   Boron is replaced by -OH group with retention of configuration.

related_concepts.name: Syn-Addition
related_concepts.definition: Both H and OH add to the same face of the double bond.

subject: Chemistry
title: Osmium Tetroxide (OsO4)
description: Syn-hydroxylation of alkenes (Addition of two OH groups to same side).
derivation:
Mechanism: Concerted Cycloaddition.
1. $OsO_4$ adds to the double bond forming a cyclic Osmate Ester.
   Geometry requires oxygen atoms to add from the same face (Syn).
2. Hydrolysis: $NaHSO_3$ cleaves the O-Os bonds, releasing the cis-1,2-diol.
Stereochemistry: Cis-alkene $\rightarrow$ Meso diol; Trans-alkene $\rightarrow$ Racemic diol.

related_concepts.name: Cold Alkaline KMnO4
related_concepts.definition: Baeyer's Reagent. Also performs syn-hydroxylation but can over-oxidize.

subject: Chemistry
title: Diels-Alder Reaction
description: [4+2] Cycloaddition reaction. Forms 6-membered rings.
derivation:
Concerted Pericyclic Mechanism:
1. Interaction between HOMO of Diene (electron rich, 4$\pi$) and LUMO of Dienophile (electron poor, 2$\pi$).
2. Three $\pi$-bonds break, two $\sigma$-bonds and one new $\pi$-bond form simultaneously.
3. Stereochemistry: Syn-addition. Retains stereochemistry of reactants.

related_concepts.name: Woodward-Hoffmann Rules
related_concepts.definition: Rules predicting stereochemistry of pericyclic reactions based on orbital symmetry.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cope Elimination
description: Thermal elimination of Amine Oxides to form Alkenes.
derivation:
Mechanism: Cyclic Syn-Elimination (Ei).
1. The Oxygen of the amine oxide acts as an internal base.
2. It abstracts a $\beta$-proton from the alkyl chain.
3. Simultaneous C-H bond breaking and C-N bond cleavage via a 5-membered transition state.
Result: Stereoselective formation of alkene (Syn product).

related_concepts.name: Pyrolysis of Esters
related_concepts.definition: Another syn-elimination reaction yielding alkenes/acids upon heating esters.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wittig Reaction
description: Synthesis of Alkenes from Carbonyls using Phosphorus Ylide.
derivation:
Reagent: Phosphonium Ylide ($Ph_3P^+-C^-R_2$).
1. Nucleophilic Attack: Ylide carbon attacks Carbonyl carbon.
   Forms a Betaine intermediate (zwitterion).
2. Ring Closure: Oxygen bonds to Phosphorus forming a 4-membered Oxaphosphetane ring.
3. Elimination: Strong P=O bond formation drives the ring opening to yield Alkene and Triphenylphosphine Oxide.

related_concepts.name: Ylide
related_concepts.definition: A neutral molecule with positive and negative charges on adjacent atoms.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hofmann Elimination (Amine)
description: Elimination of Quaternary Ammonium Hydroxides. Gives Less Substituted Alkene (Hofmann Product).
derivation:
Mechanism: E2 (Concerted).
Leaving Group: Bulky Trialkylamine ($-NR_3$).
Base: Hydroxide ($OH^-$).
Logic:
Due to the steric bulk of the leaving group, the base abstracts the *least hindered* (acidic) $\beta$-proton (terminal methyl).
This leads to the less stable (less substituted) alkene as the major product.

related_concepts.name: Saytzeff Rule
related_concepts.definition: Opposite rule favoring the more substituted alkene (Thermodynamic product).

subject: Chemistry
title: Corey-House Synthesis
description: Preparation of unsymmetrical alkanes using Gilman Reagent.
derivation:
1. Formation of Gilman Reagent: $2RLi + CuI \rightarrow R_2CuLi + LiI$.
2. Coupling: Reaction with Alkyl Halide $R'X$.
   Mechanism: Nucleophilic attack of $R$ from cuprate on $R'$.
   Constraint: $R'$ must be Methyl, Primary, or Secondary halide (SN2 type). $R$ can be any group.

related_concepts.name: Wurtz Limitation
related_concepts.definition: Wurtz reaction gives mixture of products for unsymmetrical alkanes ($R-R, R'-R', R-R'$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Frankland Reaction
description: Preparation of symmetrical alkanes using Zinc.
derivation:
Similar to Wurtz reaction but uses Zinc instead of Sodium.
Mechanism: Formation of Organozinc intermediate ($RZnX$).
Better control than Wurtz for laboratory synthesis.

related_concepts.name: Organozinc Compounds
related_concepts.definition: Less reactive than Grignard reagents, used in Reformatsky reaction.

subject: Chemistry
title: 1,2 vs 1,4 Addition (Dienes)
description: Kinetic vs Thermodynamic Control.
derivation:
Reaction: $CH_2=CH-CH=CH_2 + HBr$.
1. Low Temp (-80C): 1,2-addition product ($CH_3-CHBr-CH=CH_2$) dominates. **Kinetic Control** (Lower activation energy).
2. High Temp (40C): 1,4-addition product ($CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2Br$) dominates. **Thermodynamic Control** (More stable alkene due to hyperconjugation).

related_concepts.name: Resonance Stabilization
related_concepts.definition: The intermediate allyl carbocation has charge delocalized over C2 and C4.

subject: Chemistry
title: Free Radical Halogenation Selectivity
visual_data: Br^\bullet \text{ is selective, } Cl^\bullet \text{ is reactive}
description: Hammond's Postulate application.
derivation:
1. Chlorination: Exothermic. Transition state resembles reactants (early). Low activation energy difference between $1^\circ, 2^\circ, 3^\circ$ H abstraction. Low selectivity.
2. Bromination: Endothermic. Transition state resembles products (late). Radical character is developed in TS. Stability of radical ($3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$) strongly influences rate. High selectivity.

related_concepts.name: Hammond Postulate
related_concepts.definition: The transition state structure resembles the species (reactant or product) to which it is closer in energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wurtz Reaction
description: Alkane synthesis by coupling two alkyl halides (gives symmetrical alkane). \(R\)=alkyl, \(X\)=halogen (Cl, Br, I).
derivation:
1. Forms organosodium: \(R-X + 2Na \rightarrow R-Na + NaX\)
2. \(R-Na\) attacks second \(R-X\): \(R-Na + R-X \rightarrow R-R + NaX\)
Note: Mixed halides give mixture of products; methane cannot be prepared.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wurtz-Fittig Reaction
description: Couples aryl halide with alkyl halide to give alkylbenzene. \(Ar\)=aryl, \(R\)=alkyl, \(X\)=halogen.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sabatier-Senderens Hydrogenation
description: Catalytic hydrogenation of alkene/alkyne to alkane (syn addition). Catalysts: Ni, Pt, Pd. \(H_2\)=dihydrogen.

subject: Chemistry
title: Decarboxylation (Soda-Lime)
description: Sodium salt of carboxylic acid loses \(CO_2\) to give alkane with one less carbon. NaOH+CaO = soda lime.

subject: Chemistry
title: Saytzeff (Zaitsev) Rule
description: In elimination, the more substituted (more stable) alkene is the major product. \(X\)=halogen.
derivation: More alkyl groups on the double bond \(\Rightarrow\) more hyperconjugative structures \(\Rightarrow\) greater stability \(\Rightarrow\) major product.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dehydrohalogenation
description: Alkene from alkyl halide by removal of HX (\(\beta\)-elimination). Reagent: alcoholic KOH. \(X\)=halogen.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dehydration of Alcohol
description: Alkene by acid-catalysed loss of water from alcohol. Ease: \(3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ\). Follows Saytzeff.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dehalogenation of Vic-Dihalide
description: Alkene by removing adjacent halogens from a vicinal dihalide using Zn dust. \(R\)=alkyl.

subject: Chemistry
title: Addition of Halogen (Anti)
description: Halogen adds across C=C (anti addition via halonium ion). Decolourises bromine water = unsaturation test.
derivation:
1. \(Br_2\) forms cyclic bromonium ion on one face.
2. \(Br^-\) attacks from opposite face.
Result: anti (trans) addition.

subject: Chemistry
title: Halohydrin Formation
description: Alkene + halogen in water gives halohydrin; OH and X add anti, OH at more substituted C (Markownikoff). \(X\)=halogen.

subject: Chemistry
title: Baeyer's Test (Cold KMnO4)
description: Cold dilute alkaline \(KMnO_4\) gives syn vicinal diol; purple decolourises = test for unsaturation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hot KMnO4 Cleavage
description: Acidic hot \(KMnO_4\) cleaves C=C oxidatively. \(=CH-\) gives acid, \(=CR_2\) gives ketone, \(=CH_2\) gives \(CO_2+H_2O\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Combustion of Hydrocarbon
description: Complete combustion of an alkane. \(n\)=number of carbons; products are \(CO_2\) and water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Terminal Alkyne Acidity
description: Acidic terminal H of alkyne (\(sp\) carbon) replaced by Na/NaNH2 giving acetylide. Acidity: \(sp > sp^2 > sp^3\).
derivation: More s-character (\(sp\)=50%) \(\Rightarrow\) C holds electrons closer \(\Rightarrow\) C-H more acidic \(\Rightarrow\) stable carbanion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kucherov Reaction (Alkyne Hydration)
description: Markownikoff hydration of alkyne via enol that tautomerises. Acetylene gives acetaldehyde; others give ketones.
derivation:
1. \(H_2O\) adds (Markownikoff) to give enol \(CH_2=CH-OH\).
2. Tautomerisation: enol \(\rightleftharpoons\) keto form \(CH_3-CHO\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Benzene from Acetylene
description: Cyclic polymerisation (trimerisation) of ethyne (acetylene) gives benzene. \(C_2H_2\)=ethyne.

subject: Chemistry
title: Friedel-Crafts Alkylation
description: Electrophilic substitution attaching alkyl group to benzene. Catalyst: anhyd. \(AlCl_3\). Electrophile = \(R^+\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitration of Benzene
description: Electrophilic substitution giving nitrobenzene. Electrophile = nitronium ion \(NO_2^+\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Sulphonation of Benzene
description: Reversible electrophilic substitution giving benzenesulphonic acid. Electrophile = \(SO_3\) (or \(SO_3H^+\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Halogenation of Benzene
description: Electrophilic substitution with halogen and Lewis-acid carrier (\(FeCl_3\)/\(FeBr_3\)). Electrophile = \(X^+\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Directive Influence (EAS)
description: Activating + halogen groups direct ortho/para; deactivating (electron-withdrawing) groups direct meta in benzene substitution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Allylic Bromination (NBS)
description: NBS (N-bromosuccinimide) substitutes the allylic/benzylic C-H via free radicals at low \(Br_2\) conc.

subject: Chemistry
title: Clemmensen Reduction
description: Reduces carbonyl (C=O) of aldehyde/ketone to \(CH_2\) under acidic conditions. Used after F-C acylation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Wolff-Kishner Reduction
description: Reduces C=O to \(CH_2\) via hydrazone under basic conditions (alkali/ethylene glycol). Base-stable substrates.

subject: Chemistry
title: Isomerisation of Alkane
description: Straight-chain alkane converted to branched-chain isomers (raises octane number). Catalyst: \(AlCl_3\)+HCl.

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Unsaturation
description: Counts rings + \(\pi\)-bonds in a formula. \(C\)=carbons, \(H\)=H, \(N\)=N, \(X\)=halogen; O ignored.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acid-Catalysed Hydration
description: Direct hydration of alkene gives Markovnikov alcohol via carbocation (rearrangement possible). \(H^+\)=catalyst, \(-OH\) adds to more substituted C. Contrast: oxymercuration (Markovnikov, no rearrangement) and hydroboration (anti-Markovnikov).

subject: Chemistry
title: Halogenation Reactivity Order
description: Reactivity of halogens and ease of H-abstraction in free-radical halogenation. \(F_2\) most reactive/least selective; \(I_2\) does not react. Tertiary H abstracted fastest (lowest BDE).

subject: Chemistry
title: Huckel's (4n+2) Rule
description: Criterion for aromaticity. Ring must be planar, cyclic, fully conjugated and have \((4n+2)\) delocalised \(\pi\) electrons. \(4n\) electrons = antiaromatic. e.g. benzene \(6\pi\) (\(n=1\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Polymerisation of Alkene
description: Addition polymerisation of ethene to polythene. \(n\)=number of monomer units; product is polyethylene (polythene).

subject: Chemistry
title: Terminal Alkyne Metal Acetylides
visual_data: H-C\equiv CH \xrightarrow{AgNO_3 / NH_4OH} AgC\equiv CAg \downarrow \;;\; \xrightarrow{CuCl / NH_4OH} CuC\equiv CCu \downarrow
description: Test for terminal alkynes: acidic terminal H gives white silver acetylide and red copper acetylide precipitates. Distinguishes terminal from internal/non-acidic alkynes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aromatic Reactivity & Directing
description: EAS reactivity: activating groups speed reaction and direct ortho/para; deactivating slow it and direct meta. Halogens are exceptions: deactivating yet o/p-directing.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of C=C/Pi Bonds (DoU)
description: General formulae linking degree of unsaturation to molecular type. \(C_nH_{2n+2}\)=alkane (0 DoU), \(C_nH_{2n}\)=alkene/cycloalkane, \(C_nH_{2n-2}\)=alkyne/diene.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ozonolysis (Oxidative)
description: Oxidative work-up of ozonide gives carboxylic acids (terminal =CH2 gives \(CO_2 + H_2O\)). Contrast reductive (Zn/H2O) which gives aldehydes/ketones.

subject: Chemistry
title: Magnetic Moment
description: Spin-only magnetic moment. \(n\): unpaired electrons.
derivation:
Magnetic moment arises from electron spin and orbital motion.
For 3d series, orbital contribution is quenched by crystal field.
Only spin contributes.
Spin Angular Momentum \(S = n/2\).
Formula: \(\mu = \sqrt{4S(S+1)} = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\).
Example: \(Fe^{3+} ([Ar]3d^5)\) has n=5. \(\mu = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\) BM.

related_concepts.name: Diamagnetism
related_concepts.definition: Condition where all electrons are paired (n=0, \(\mu=0\)), leading to repulsion by magnetic field.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chromyl Chloride Test
description: Confirmatory test for Chloride ions. Uses K2Cr2O7 and Conc H2SO4.
derivation:
1. Formation of Chromic Acid in situ: \(K_2Cr_2O_7 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CrO_3\).
2. Reaction with Chloride: \(CrO_3 + 2HCl \rightarrow CrO_2Cl_2 + H_2O\).
   \(CrO_2Cl_2\) is Chromyl Chloride (Deep Red Vapors).
3. Confirmation: Vapors passed into NaOH give yellow solution (\(Na_2CrO_4\)).
   \(CrO_2Cl_2 + 4OH^- \rightarrow CrO_4^{2-} + 2Cl^- + 2H_2O\).

related_concepts.name: Qualitative Analysis
related_concepts.definition: Branch of chemistry dealing with identification of ions/compounds.

subject: Chemistry
title: KMnO4 Titration (Acidic)
description: Permanganate as oxidizing agent in acidic medium. n-factor = 5.
derivation:
Oxidation State Change:
Reactant: \(MnO_4^-\), Mn is +7.
Product: \(Mn^{2+}\), Mn is +2.
Change = \(7 - 2 = 5\) electrons gained.
Equivalent Weight = Molar Mass / 5.
Indicator: KMnO4 acts as a self-indicator (Purple to Colorless).

related_concepts.name: Redox Titration
related_concepts.definition: Titration based on a redox reaction between analyte and titrant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lanthanoid Contraction
description: Steady decrease in atomic size along Lanthanoids causes 4d and 5d elements to have similar radii.
derivation:
Cause: Poor Shielding of 4f electrons.
1. As we move from La to Lu, electrons enter 4f subshell.
2. f-orbitals are diffuse and shield the nucleus poorly.
3. Nuclear charge (Z) increases by 1 each step.
4. Result: Effective Nuclear Charge (Zeff) increases significantly, pulling shells closer.
Consequence: The normal size increase down a group (4d to 5d) is cancelled by this contraction.

related_concepts.name: Chemical Twins
related_concepts.definition: Elements like Zr/Hf or Nb/Ta having identical size and properties, making separation difficult.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chromate-Dichromate Equilibrium
description: pH dependent equilibrium. Acid favors Dichromate; Alkali favors Chromate.
derivation:
Le Chatelier's Principle:
1. Add Acid ($H^+$): Equilibrium shifts Right (Consumes H+). Solution turns Orange.
2. Add Base ($OH^-$): Removes H+, shifts Left. Solution turns Yellow.
Note: Oxidation state of Cr remains +6 in both; it is not a redox reaction.

related_concepts.name: Condensation Reaction
related_concepts.definition: Two tetrahedral chromate units join through an oxygen bridge to form dichromate.

subject: Chemistry
title: d-Block General Config
description: General valence electronic configuration of transition (d-block) elements. \((n-1)d\)=penultimate d-subshell, \(ns\)=outermost s-subshell, \(n\)=period number.

subject: Chemistry
title: Unpaired Electrons from Moment
description: Back-calculate number of unpaired electrons from spin-only magnetic moment (rearranged \(\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\)). \(n\)=unpaired electrons, \(\mu\)=magnetic moment in BM.
derivation:
Start: \(\mu^2 = n(n+2) = n^2+2n\)
\(n^2+2n-\mu^2=0\)
Solve quadratic: \(n=\frac{-2+\sqrt{4+4\mu^2}}{2}=\sqrt{1+\mu^2}-1\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Dichromate Oxidation (Acidic)
description: Reduction half-reaction of dichromate ion in acidic medium (basis of K2Cr2O7 titrations). \(n\)=6 electrons transferred; \(E^\circ = +1.33\) V. Cr goes +6 to +3.

subject: Chemistry
title: K2Cr2O7 + Fe2+ Titration
description: Standard redox titration of ferrous iron by dichromate in acid. 1 mol dichromate oxidises 6 mol \(Fe^{2+}\); n-factor of \(Cr_2O_7^{2-}\)=6.

subject: Chemistry
title: K2Cr2O7 + I- (Iodometry)
description: Dichromate oxidises iodide to iodine in acid (iodometric estimation). Liberated \(I_2\) titrated with thiosulphate. n-factor of \(Cr_2O_7^{2-}\)=6.

subject: Chemistry
title: KMnO4 (Neutral/Faintly Basic)
description: Permanganate reduction in neutral or weakly alkaline medium (Mn +7 to +4). n-factor=3; product is brown \(MnO_2\). Used for oxidising iodide/thiosulphate to iodate/sulphate.

subject: Chemistry
title: KMnO4 (Strongly Basic)
description: Permanganate reduction in strongly alkaline medium (Mn +7 to +6, green manganate). n-factor=1. Occurs with excess OH-.

subject: Chemistry
title: KMnO4 + Oxalate
description: Standardisation of \(KMnO_4\) against oxalic acid/oxalate in hot acid. 2 mol permanganate oxidise 5 mol oxalate; warm to ~60 C to start.

subject: Chemistry
title: KMnO4 + Fe2+
description: Permanganate titration of ferrous ion in acidic medium. 1 mol \(MnO_4^-\) oxidises 5 mol \(Fe^{2+}\); self-indicating (pink endpoint).

subject: Chemistry
title: Manganate Disproportionation
description: Green manganate (+6) disproportionates in acid/neutral medium to permanganate (+7) and \(MnO_2\) (+4). Basis of converting \(K_2MnO_4 \to KMnO_4\).

subject: Chemistry
title: KMnO4 Preparation (Pyrolusite)
description: First step in industrial \(KMnO_4\) manufacture: pyrolusite fused with KOH and an oxidant (\(O_2\)/\(KNO_3\)) gives green manganate; later oxidised electrolytically.

subject: Chemistry
title: K2Cr2O7 Preparation
description: Roasting of chromite ore with \(Na_2CO_3\) in air to sodium chromate (first stage of \(K_2Cr_2O_7\) manufacture). Chromate later acidified to dichromate, then KCl gives \(K_2Cr_2O_7\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Spin-Only Moment (Detailed)
description: Spin-only magnetic moment in terms of total spin quantum number. \(S\)=total spin (\(=n/2\)), \(n\)=unpaired electrons; reduces to \(\sqrt{n(n+2)}\).
derivation:
\(S=n/2\)
\(4S(S+1)=4\cdot\frac{n}{2}\left(\frac{n}{2}+1\right)=2n\cdot\frac{n+2}{2}=n(n+2)\)
So \(\mu_s=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\) BM.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mn3+ Disproportionation
description: Aqueous \(Mn^{3+}\) (\(E^\circ_{Mn^{3+}/Mn^{2+}}=+1.51\) V) is unstable and disproportionates to \(Mn^{2+}\) and \(MnO_2\). Explains rarity of +3 Mn in solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: E°(M³⁺/M²⁺) Irregular Trend
description: Reduction potential anomaly across 3d series explaining ion stability. \(E^\circ\)=standard reduction potential (volts); higher \(E^\circ\) means the \(M^{2+}\) (or \(M^{3+}\)) ion is more easily formed/more stable. High \(E^\circ(Mn^{3+}/Mn^{2+})\) reflects extra stability of \(d^5\) \(Mn^{2+}\); low \(E^\circ(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+})\) reflects stability of \(d^5\) \(Fe^{3+}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: E°(M²⁺/M) Trend & Cu Anomaly
description: Most \(E^\circ(M^{2+}/M)\) are negative (metals displace H₂), but Cu is positive. \(E^\circ\)=standard reduction potential. Positive value for Cu arises because its high \((\Delta_aH + \Delta_{ie}H)\) is not balanced by its low hydration enthalpy, so Cu does not liberate H₂ from acids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidising Power: Order of MnO4⁻ > Cr2O7²⁻
description: Compares oxidising strength of the two key oxidants. \(E^\circ\)=standard reduction potential; higher value means stronger oxidising agent, so \(KMnO_4\) is a stronger oxidiser than \(K_2Cr_2O_7\) in acidic medium.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acidified Dichromate + H2S
description: Standard oxidation reaction of \(K_2Cr_2O_7\) used to show oxidising action (sulphide \(\to\) sulphur). Confirms \(Cr_2O_7^{2-}\) oxidises \(H_2S\) to S; useful counterpart to its \(Fe^{2+}\)/\(I^-\) reactions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lanthanoid Common Oxidation State
description: Characteristic oxidation states of f-block (lanthanoids). \(+3\) is most common; \(+4\) (Ce) and \(+2\) (Eu) appear when they give stable empty \(f^0\), half-filled \(f^7\) or filled \(f^{14}\) configurations. \(Ce^{4+}\) is a strong oxidant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Unpaired e⁻ vs Colour/Paramagnetism
description: Ions with empty or fully-filled d-subshell have no d-d transition and no unpaired electrons. Hence \(Sc^{3+}\) and \(Zn^{2+}\) are colourless and diamagnetic, unlike partially filled \(d^{1-9}\) ions which are coloured and paramagnetic.

subject: Chemistry
title: Stability: K2Cr2O7 vs K2CrO4 (pH)
description: Inter-conversion governs which species dominates with pH. Acidic/neutral → orange \(Cr_2O_7^{2-}\) favoured; alkaline → yellow \(CrO_4^{2-}\). Cr stays \(+6\) throughout (no redox, only condensation).

subject: Chemistry
title: Inductive Effect (+I)
description: Electron Releasing Groups (ERG). Stabilize carbocations, destabilize carbanions.
derivation:
Mechanism: Partial shifting of sigma electrons.
Alkyl groups are electron releasing.
Reason: Higher electron density on Hydrogen/Carbon relative to the substituted center (or Hyperconjugation overlap).
More branching = More carbons pushing electrons = Stronger +I effect.
Application: Tertiary alcohols are less acidic than primary because +I destabilizes the alkoxide ion.

related_concepts.name: Permanent Effect
related_concepts.definition: Inductive effect operates permanently in the ground state of the molecule.

subject: Chemistry
title: Inductive Effect Order (-I)
visual_data: NF_3^+ > NO_2 > CN > F > Cl > Br > I
description: Electron Withdrawing Groups (EWG). Increases acidity of carboxylic acids by stabilizing the carboxylate ion.
derivation:
Mechanism: Sigma bond electron displacement towards more electronegative atom.
1. Cationic poles (\(N^+\)) are the strongest withdrawers due to electrostatic attraction.
2. \(NO_2\) and \(CN\) have strong electronegativity and sp/sp2 character.
3. Halogens follow electronegativity order (F > Cl > Br > I).
Effect decays rapidly with distance (negligible after 3 carbons).

related_concepts.name: Acid Strength
related_concepts.definition: Directly proportional to -I effect strength of substituents.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mesomeric Effect (+M)
visual_data: O^- > NH_2 > OH > OR > NHCOR > Ph
description: Electron Donating Groups via Resonance. Activates benzene ring towards electrophilic attack.
derivation:
Groups with Lone Pairs can donate electrons into a conjugated system.
1. \(O^-\): Full negative charge, strongest donor.
2. \(NH_2\) vs \(OH\): N is less electronegative than O, so it holds lone pairs loosely and donates better.
3. \(NHCOR\): The lone pair on N is cross-conjugated with the carbonyl group, reducing donation to the ring.

related_concepts.name: Ortho-Para Director
related_concepts.definition: Groups that increase electron density specifically at ortho and para positions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hyperconjugation
description: No-bond resonance. Stabilizes carbocations and alkenes.
derivation:
Orbital Overlap:
Interaction between the filled \(\sigma\)-orbital of the \(C_\alpha-H\) bond and the empty p-orbital of the carbocation (or \(\pi^*\) of alkene).
Electrons delocalize from the bond into the empty orbital.
More \(\alpha\)-hydrogens \(\rightarrow\) More contributing structures \(\rightarrow\) Higher Stability.
Order: \((CH_3)_3C^+ > (CH_3)_2CH^+ > CH_3CH_2^+ > CH_3^+\).

related_concepts.name: Baker-Nathan Effect
related_concepts.definition: Another name for Hyperconjugation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Heat of Hydrogenation
description: Energy released when 1 mole of alkene is hydrogenated. Measure of stability.
derivation:
Hydrogenation is Exothermic.
\(\text{Alkene} + H_2 \rightarrow \text{Alkane} + \text{Heat}\)
Since the product (Alkane) energy is fixed for isomers:
A more stable alkene has lower potential energy to start with.
Therefore, the difference (Heat Released) is smaller.
Trans-2-butene is more stable than Cis-2-butene \(\rightarrow\) Trans has lower HOH.

related_concepts.name: Steric Hindrance
related_concepts.definition: Repulsion between groups in cis-alkenes raises energy, increasing HOH.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aromaticity (Huckel's Rule)
description: Criteria for aromatic stability. System must be Cyclic, Planar, and Fully Conjugated.
derivation:
Molecular Orbital Theory:
In cyclic conjugated systems, stability arises when all bonding MOs are filled and anti-bonding are empty.
This configuration occurs with \(4n+2\) pi electrons (2, 6, 10, 14...).
Example: Benzene (6 pi e-, n=1) is aromatic.
Cyclobutadiene (4 pi e-) is Anti-aromatic.

related_concepts.name: Resonance Energy
related_concepts.definition: The difference in energy between the real hybrid structure and the most stable hypothetical contributor.

subject: Chemistry
title: Ortho Effect
description: Ortho-substituted benzoic acids are strongest acids, regardless of group nature.
derivation:
Steric Inhibition of Resonance (SIR):
1. Bulky group at ortho position forces the -COOH group out of the plane of the ring.
2. Resonance between benzene ring and -COOH is lost.
3. The electron-withdrawing benzene ring destabilizes the acid less (or the carboxylate is not destabilized by donation).
4. Main Factor: The carboxylate ion is stabilized by solvation, which is easier when twisted out of plane.

related_concepts.name: Benzoic Acid
related_concepts.definition: Simplest aromatic carboxylic acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lassaigne's Test (Nitrogen)
description: Detection of Nitrogen. Formation of Ferric Ferrocyanide.
derivation:
1. Sodium Fusion: \(Na + C + N \rightarrow NaCN\).
2. Add Ferrous Sulfate: \(FeSO_4 + 2NaCN \rightarrow Fe(CN)_2 + Na_2SO_4\).
   \(Fe(CN)_2 + 4NaCN \rightarrow Na_4[Fe(CN)_6]\) (Sodium Ferrocyanide).
3. Acidification/Oxidation: Some \(Fe^{2+}\) oxidizes to \(Fe^{3+}\).
4. Complex Formation: \(4Fe^{3+} + 3[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-} \rightarrow Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3\).

related_concepts.name: Sodium Fusion Extract
related_concepts.definition: Ionic solution prepared by fusing organic compound with Na metal to convert covalent elements (N, S, X) to ions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Kjeldahl's Method
description: Quantitative estimation of Nitrogen via Ammonia conversion.
derivation:
1. Digestion: Compound + Conc \(H_2SO_4 \rightarrow (NH_4)_2SO_4\).
2. Distillation: Add Alkali (NaOH) \(\rightarrow\) Releases \(NH_3\) gas.
3. Titration: Absorb \(NH_3\) in known excess standard acid.
   Moles of N = Moles of \(NH_3\) = Moles of Acid Neutralized.
   Formula derived from equivalents: \(N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2\).

related_concepts.name: Dumas Method
related_concepts.definition: Alternative N estimation where N is converted directly to N2 gas.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fehling's Test
description: Test for Aliphatic Aldehydes. Forms Red precipitate of Copper(I) Oxide.
derivation:
Reagents:
Fehling A: Aqueous \(CuSO_4\) (Blue).
Fehling B: Alkaline Sodium Potassium Tartrate (Rochelle Salt).
Reaction:
Aldehyde acts as reducing agent.
\(Cu^{2+} (Blue) \xrightarrow{reduction} Cu^+ (Red ppt)\).
Note: Aromatic aldehydes (Benzaldehyde) do NOT respond because the C=O bond is stabilized by resonance.

related_concepts.name: Reducing Sugar
related_concepts.definition: Sugars with free aldehyde/ketone groups that give positive Fehling's test.

subject: Chemistry
title: Iodoform Test
description: Specific test for Methyl Ketones (-COCH3) or Methyl Carbinols (-CH(OH)CH3).
derivation:
1. Oxidation (if alcohol): \(CH_3-CH(OH)-R \rightarrow CH_3-CO-R\).
2. Halogenation: Base catalyzed alpha-halogenation replaces all H in \(CH_3\) with I.
   \(R-CO-CH_3 \rightarrow R-CO-CI_3\).
3. Hydrolysis: The electron-withdrawing \(CI_3\) group makes the carbonyl carbon susceptible to attack by \(OH^-\).
   C-C bond cleaves to form \(CHI_3\) (Yellow ppt) and Acid Salt.

related_concepts.name: Haloform Reaction
related_concepts.definition: General term for reaction with Cl2, Br2, or I2 to form CHX3.

subject: Chemistry
title: Specific Rotation
description: Measure of optical activity. $\alpha$: observed angle, $l$: length (dm), $c$: conc (g/mL).
derivation:
Optical rotation depends on the number of chiral molecules encountered by light.
$\alpha_{obs} \propto l$ (path length).
$\alpha_{obs} \propto c$ (concentration).
Proportionality constant is Specific Rotation $[\alpha]$.
Standard state: $l=1$ dm, $c=1$ g/mL.

related_concepts.name: Racemic Mixture
related_concepts.definition: Equimolar mixture of enantiomers. Net rotation is zero.

subject: Chemistry
title: Enantiomeric Excess (ee)
description: Purity of a chiral sample. Also equal to $\frac{\alpha_{obs}}{\alpha_{pure}} \times 100$.
derivation:
If a mixture contains 70% R and 30% S:
The 30% S cancels the rotation of 30% R (Racemic part).
The remaining 40% R contributes to rotation.
$ee = 70 - 30 = 40\%$.

related_concepts.name: Optical Purity
related_concepts.definition: Synonymous with enantiomeric excess.

subject: Chemistry
title: Iodometric Titration
description: Indirect estimation of oxidizing agents (Cu2+, KMnO4, K2Cr2O7).
derivation:
Step 1: Oxidizing Agent liberates Iodine from Iodide ($KI$).
   $2Cu^{2+} + 4I^- \rightarrow Cu_2I_2 + I_2$.
Step 2: Liberated $I_2$ is titrated against standard Sodium Thiosulfate (Hypo).
   $I_2 + 2Na_2S_2O_3 \rightarrow 2NaI + Na_2S_4O_6$ (Sodium Tetrathionate).
Indicator: Starch (Blue $\to$ Colorless at endpoint).

related_concepts.name: Iodimetry
related_concepts.definition: Direct titration using standard Iodine solution against reducing agents.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hardness of Water (EDTA)
description: Complexometric titration to estimate $Ca^{2+}$ and $Mg^{2+}$.
derivation:
1. Buffer: pH 10 ($NH_4OH/NH_4Cl$).
2. Indicator: Eriochrome Black T (EBT). Forms unstable Wine Red complex with metal.
3. Titration: EDTA (stronger ligand) displaces EBT from the metal.
   $M-EBT + EDTA \rightarrow M-EDTA (Stable) + EBT (Free)$.
4. Endpoint: Color changes from Wine Red to Blue (color of free EBT at pH 10).

related_concepts.name: Chelation
related_concepts.definition: EDTA is a hexadentate ligand forming stable ring complexes.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Stereoisomers
description: Formulas for calculating optical isomers. $n$: number of chiral centers.
derivation:
1. Unsymmetrical Molecule: No plane of symmetry. Total = $2^n$.
2. Symmetrical (Even n): Total = Active ($2^{n-1}$) + Meso ($2^{n/2-1}$).
3. Symmetrical (Odd n): Total = $2^{n-1}$. (Meso = $2^{(n-1)/2}$).

related_concepts.name: Meso Compound
related_concepts.definition: A molecule with chiral centers that is superimposable on its mirror image (optically inactive).

subject: Chemistry
title: Degree of Unsaturation (DBE)
description: Counts rings + pi-bonds in a molecule from its formula. \(C\)=carbon atoms, \(H\)=hydrogen, \(N\)=nitrogen, \(X\)=halogen atoms (oxygen and divalent S are ignored).
derivation:
Saturated acyclic \(C_nH_{2n+2}\) has zero unsaturation.
Each ring or pi-bond removes 2 H atoms.
Each monovalent X behaves like an H; each trivalent N adds one H.
Count missing H-pairs relative to saturation: \(DBE = \frac{(2C+2+N-X)-H}{2}\).

related_concepts.name: Index of Hydrogen Deficiency
related_concepts.definition: Alternate name for DBE; one ring = one pi-bond = 1 unit. Benzene = 4 (3 pi + 1 ring).

related_concepts.name: Use in structure elucidation
related_concepts.definition: DBE narrows possible structures: \(DBE \geq 4\) hints at an aromatic ring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molecular vs Empirical Formula
description: Relates empirical and molecular formula. \(M\)=molecular mass, \(E\)=empirical formula mass, \(n\)=integer multiple.
derivation:
Empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number atom ratio from \(\frac{\%\text{ mass}}{\text{atomic mass}}\).
Molecular formula is a whole multiple of it.
So \(n = \frac{\text{molecular mass}}{\text{empirical formula mass}}\), then multiply each subscript by \(n\).

related_concepts.name: Empirical formula
related_concepts.definition: Simplest integer ratio of atoms, e.g. CH for benzene.

related_concepts.name: Molecular formula
related_concepts.definition: Actual atom count, e.g. C6H6 for benzene (n = 6).

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbocation Stability Order
description: Order of carbocation (electron-deficient C+) stability for SN1/E1 and rearrangements. Stabilised by +I, hyperconjugation and resonance.

related_concepts.name: Reasons for stability
related_concepts.definition: More alkyl groups donate electron density (+I) and give more hyperconjugating C-H bonds; resonance (allyl/benzyl) delocalises the charge.

related_concepts.name: Rearrangement
related_concepts.definition: Less stable carbocations rearrange by 1,2-hydride or 1,2-methyl shift to a more stable one.

subject: Chemistry
title: Free Radical Stability Order
description: Order of free-radical (odd-electron C) stability governing halogenation selectivity.

related_concepts.name: Stabilising factors
related_concepts.definition: Same as carbocations: hyperconjugation and +I from alkyls, resonance for allyl/benzyl, since the radical is electron-deficient.

related_concepts.name: Bond dissociation energy
related_concepts.definition: More stable radical forms from the C-H bond with lower BDE (3 deg C-H < 2 deg < 1 deg).

subject: Chemistry
title: Acidic Strength Order (Functional Groups)
visual_data: RCOOH > H_2CO_3 > ArOH > H_2O > ROH > HC\equiv CH > NH_3 > RH
description: Relative acidity of common organic species; lower \(pK_a\) = stronger acid (more stable conjugate base).

related_concepts.name: Conjugate base stability
related_concepts.definition: Carboxylate is resonance-stabilised over two equivalent O; phenoxide over the ring; alkoxide is least stabilised, so ROH is weakest among O-H acids.

related_concepts.name: s-character & acidity
related_concepts.definition: Terminal alkyne (sp, 50% s) is far more acidic than alkene/alkane because the carbanion lone pair is held tightly.

subject: Chemistry
title: Basic Strength of Amines (Aqueous)
description: Order of basicity of aliphatic amines in water (net of +I, solvation, steric). In gas phase pure +I gives \(3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ\).

related_concepts.name: Why 3 deg drops in water
related_concepts.definition: Bulky alkyls hinder solvation/H-bonding of the conjugate ammonium ion, lowering the observed basicity despite the strongest +I.

related_concepts.name: Aniline vs ammonia
related_concepts.definition: Aniline is far weaker (\(pK_b \approx 9.4\)) because the N lone pair delocalises into the ring; alkylamines (\(pK_b \approx 3-4\)) are stronger than ammonia (4.75).

subject: Chemistry
title: Estimation of C and H (Liebig)
description: Combustion analysis of an organic compound. \(m\)=mass of compound burnt, \(m(CO_2)\) and \(m(H_2O)\)=masses of products absorbed.

related_concepts.name: Principle
related_concepts.definition: Compound burnt in excess O2/CuO; CO2 absorbed in KOH, H2O in anhydrous CaCl2; masses give C and H.

related_concepts.name: Mass factors
related_concepts.definition: 12/44 = C mass fraction in CO2; 2/18 = H2 mass fraction in H2O.

subject: Chemistry
title: Estimation of Nitrogen (Duma's)
description: Nitrogen by volume of N2 gas liberated. \(V_{N_2}\)=volume of N2 at STP (mL), \(m\)=mass of compound; 22400 mL = molar volume at STP.

related_concepts.name: Principle
related_concepts.definition: Compound heated with CuO in CO2 stream; N converted to N2, collected over KOH, volume measured.

related_concepts.name: vs Kjeldahl
related_concepts.definition: Duma's works for all N compounds; Kjeldahl fails for ring-N (pyridine), nitro and azo compounds.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carius Method (Halogen)
description: Halogen estimation as silver halide. \(m(AgX)\)=mass of AgCl/AgBr/AgI precipitate, \(m\)=mass of compound.

related_concepts.name: Principle
related_concepts.definition: Compound heated with fuming HNO3 and AgNO3 in a Carius tube; halogen precipitates as AgX, which is weighed.

related_concepts.name: Mass factors
related_concepts.definition: AgCl=143.5, AgBr=188, AgI=235; use atomic mass of the halogen over the AgX molar mass.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carius Method (Sulphur)
description: Sulphur estimation as barium sulphate. \(m(BaSO_4)\)=mass of precipitate (molar mass 233), \(m\)=mass of compound.

related_concepts.name: Principle
related_concepts.definition: S oxidised by fuming HNO3 to sulphate, precipitated as BaSO4 with BaCl2, then weighed.

related_concepts.name: Phosphorus analogue
related_concepts.definition: P estimated as Mg2P2O7 (mol.mass 222): \(\%P = \frac{62}{222} \times \frac{m(Mg_2P_2O_7)}{m} \times 100\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Estimation of Oxygen
description: Oxygen found by difference (no direct routine method). Sum all other element percentages and subtract from 100.

related_concepts.name: Direct method
related_concepts.definition: Pyrolysis over hot coke gives CO, then \(\%O = \frac{32}{88}\times\frac{m(CO_2)}{m}\times100\) after CO -> CO2.

related_concepts.name: Caution
related_concepts.definition: By-difference value carries the accumulated error of all other estimations.

subject: Chemistry
title: Rf Value (Chromatography)
visual_data: R_f = \frac{\text{distance moved by component}}{\text{distance moved by solvent front}}
description: Characterises a spot in paper/thin-layer chromatography. Dimensionless, \(0 < R_f < 1\); characteristic of a compound in a given solvent.

related_concepts.name: Adsorption chromatography
related_concepts.definition: Separation on a stationary phase (silica/alumina); more strongly adsorbed component has smaller \(R_f\).

related_concepts.name: Use
related_concepts.definition: Identity check and purity test; compare \(R_f\) with a known standard under identical conditions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bond Fission (Homolytic vs Heterolytic)
visual_data: A : B \rightarrow A^\bullet + B^\bullet \quad (\text{Homolysis}); \quad A : B \rightarrow A^+ + B^- \quad (\text{Heterolysis})
description: Two modes of covalent bond cleavage. Homolysis gives free radicals (one electron each); heterolysis gives ions (both electrons to one atom).
derivation:
Homolytic: symmetrical breaking, each atom keeps one electron \(\rightarrow\) free radicals.
Favoured by: nonpolar bonds, UV light, heat, gas phase, peroxides.
Heterolytic: unsymmetrical breaking, more electronegative atom takes both electrons \(\rightarrow\) carbocation/carbanion.
Favoured by: polar bonds, polar solvents.
For \(C-Z\): if C keeps the pair \(\rightarrow\) carbanion; if C loses the pair \(\rightarrow\) carbocation.

related_concepts.name: Reaction Intermediates
related_concepts.definition: Homolysis yields free radicals; heterolysis yields carbocations and carbanions.

related_concepts.name: Curved Arrows
related_concepts.definition: Half-headed (fish-hook) arrow shows single-electron (homolytic) movement; full-headed arrow shows electron-pair (heterolytic) movement.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 0 (Zero Group)
description: Detection of Ammonium ion. Ammonia gas turns Red Litmus Blue and gives white fumes with HCl.
derivation:
Principle: Ammonium salts are weak acid salts.
Reaction with a strong base (NaOH) liberates the weak base (Ammonia).
Confirmatory Test (Nessler's Reagent):
\(2K_2[HgI_4] + NH_3 + 3KOH \rightarrow H_2N-Hg-O-Hg-I\) (Brown ppt, Iodide of Millon's base).

related_concepts.name: Nessler's Reagent
related_concepts.definition: Alkaline solution of Potassium Tetraiodomercurate(II).

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 2 (Acidic Radicals)
visual_data: K_{sp} \text{ Principle: Low } K_{sp} \text{ sulfides precipitate in acid.}
description: Reagent: H2S in Dilute HCl. Precipitates Cu, Pb, Hg, Cd, As, Sb, Sn.
derivation:
Common Ion Effect:
HCl provides high concentration of \(H^+\).
\(H_2S \rightleftharpoons 2H^+ + S^{2-}\).
High \([H^+]\) shifts equilibrium backward, suppressing \([S^{2-}]\).
Only sulfides with very low Solubility Product (\(K_{sp}\)) precipitate at this low sulfide concentration.
Group 4 sulfides (Zn, Mn, Ni) have higher \(K_{sp}\) and need basic medium to precipitate.

related_concepts.name: Solubility Product
related_concepts.definition: The equilibrium constant for a solid substance dissolving in an aqueous solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 3 Analysis
description: Precipitation as Hydroxides. Reagent: NH4OH in presence of NH4Cl.
derivation:
Buffer Action:
We need a controlled concentration of \(OH^-\).
If \(OH^-\)- is too high, Group 4 and 5 might coprecipitate.
\(NH_4Cl\) (Strong Electrolyte) suppresses ionization of \(NH_4OH\) (Weak Base) via Common Ion Effect.
This ensures \([OH^-]\) is just enough to exceed \(K_{sp}\) of trivalent metals (Fe, Al, Cr) but not divalent ones.

related_concepts.name: Buffer Solution
related_concepts.definition: A solution that resists change in pH. Here, NH4OH + NH4Cl acts as a basic buffer.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 4 Analysis
description: Precipitation as Sulfides in Basic Medium. Reagent: H2S + NH4OH.
derivation:
Reverse of Group 2.
Base (\(NH_4OH\)) consumes \(H^+\) produced by \(H_2S\).
Equilibrium \(H_2S \rightleftharpoons 2H^+ + S^{2-}\) shifts forward.
\([S^{2-}]\) increases significantly.
High sulfide concentration exceeds the higher \(K_{sp}\) values of Zn, Mn, Ni, Co sulfides.

related_concepts.name: Kipp's Apparatus
related_concepts.definition: Laboratory apparatus used for preparing small volumes of gases like H2S.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 5 Analysis
description: Precipitation as Carbonates. Reagent: (NH4)2CO3 + NH4OH.
derivation:
Role of \(NH_4OH\):
Prevents the precipitation of Magnesium Carbonate.
\(MgCO_3\) has a high solubility product.
Ammonium salts lower the \([CO_3^{2-}]\) slightly and form soluble complex with Mg, keeping it in solution for Group 6.

related_concepts.name: Flame Test
related_concepts.definition: Ba (Apple Green), Sr (Crimson Red), Ca (Brick Red).

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 6 Analysis (Mg)
description: Detection of Magnesium. Formation of white crystalline precipitate.
derivation:
Reagent: Disodium Hydrogen Phosphate (\(Na_2HPO_4\)) in ammoniacal solution.
Reaction:
1. \(Mg^{2+}\) does not precipitate in previous groups.
2. In the presence of \(NH_4OH\) and \(NH_4Cl\), phosphate ions precipitate Mg.
3. Product: Magnesium Ammonium Phosphate (White ppt).
Note: Solution must be cooled and scratched against the glass wall to induce crystallization.

related_concepts.name: Microcosmic Salt Bead
related_concepts.definition: Another test for Mg, forming a colorless bead.

subject: Chemistry
title: Brown Ring Test
description: Confirmatory test for Nitrate (\(NO_3^-\)). Formation of Nitroso Ferrous Sulphate complex.
derivation:
1. Reduction: Ferrous sulfate (\(Fe^{2+}\)) reduces Nitrate to Nitric Oxide (NO).
   \(NO_3^- + 3Fe^{2+} + 4H^+ \rightarrow NO + 3Fe^{3+} + 2H_2O\)
2. Complexation: The NO molecule coordinates with remaining \(Fe^{2+}\) ions.
   \([Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+} + NO \rightarrow [Fe(H_2O)_5(NO)]^{2+} + H_2O\)
3. Observation: A brown ring forms at the junction of the solution and concentrated \(H_2SO_4\).

related_concepts.name: Charge Transfer
related_concepts.definition: The brown color arises from charge transfer between Fe and NO (Fe is +1, NO is +1 in complex).

subject: Chemistry
title: Nessler's Reagent Test
description: Detection of Ammonium (\(NH_4^+\)). Formation of Iodide of Millon's Base (Brown ppt).
derivation:
Reagent: \(K_2[HgI_4]\) (Potassium Tetraiodomercurate) + KOH (Alkaline).
Reaction:
1. \(2K_2[HgI_4] + NH_3 + 3KOH \rightarrow H_2N \cdot HgO \cdot HgI + 7KI + 2H_2O\)
   Structure is often written as \(NH_2-Hg-O-Hg-I\).
2. Sensitivity: Can detect trace amounts of ammonia (ppm level).

related_concepts.name: Zero Group
related_concepts.definition: Ammonium is analyzed separately before Group 1 because reagents for other groups introduce ammonium salts.

subject: Chemistry
title: Prussian Blue
description: Test for Ferric (\(Fe^{3+}\)) ions using Ferrocyanide.
derivation:
Reaction between \(Fe^{3+}\) and Potassium Ferrocyanide (\(K_4[Fe(CN)_6]\)).
Ion Exchange:
\(4Fe^{3+} + 3[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-} \rightarrow Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3\)
Appearance: Deep blue precipitate.
Note: Often called 'Ferric Ferrocyanide'.

related_concepts.name: Mixed Valence Complex
related_concepts.definition: Compounds containing the same element in two different oxidation states.

subject: Chemistry
title: Turnbull's Blue
description: Test for Ferrous (\(Fe^{2+}\)) ions using Ferricyanide.
derivation:
Reaction between \(Fe^{2+}\) and Potassium Ferricyanide (\(K_3[Fe(CN)_6]\)).
Ion Exchange:
\(3Fe^{2+} + 2[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-} \rightarrow Fe_3[Fe(CN)_6]_2\)
Appearance: Deep blue precipitate.
Note: While historically distinct, X-ray diffraction suggests Prussian and Turnbull's blue have the same lattice structure.

related_concepts.name: Redox Stability
related_concepts.definition: Fe2+ with Ferrocyanide gives white ppt; Fe3+ with Ferricyanide gives brown solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Scarlet Red Precipitate
description: Confirmatory test for Mercuric ion (\(Hg^{2+}\)). Dissolves in excess reagent.
derivation:
1. Addition of KI: Reacts with \(Hg^{2+}\).
   \(Hg^{2+} + 2I^- \rightarrow HgI_2 \downarrow\) (Scarlet Red ppt).
2. Excess KI: Complex formation.
   \(HgI_2 + 2I^- \rightarrow [HgI_4]^{2-}\) (Soluble, Colorless).
   This complex is the precursor to Nessler's reagent.

related_concepts.name: Complexation
related_concepts.definition: The process of forming a coordination complex, often increasing solubility.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dimethyl Glyoxime (DMG) Test
description: Confirmatory for Nickel. Rosy Red precipitate. Stabilized by Hydrogen Bonding.
derivation:
1. Reagent: Dimethyl Glyoxime in ammoniacal (basic) medium.
2. Chelation: Two DMG molecules coordinate with one \(Ni^{2+}\).
3. Structure: Square Planar complex.
   Key Feature: Formation of Strong Intramolecular Hydrogen Bonds between the Oxygen atoms of the oxime groups, providing extra stability.

related_concepts.name: Chelate Effect
related_concepts.definition: Enhanced stability of complexes containing multidentate ligands.

subject: Chemistry
title: Borax Bead Test
description: Dry test for transition metals. Forms colored metaborates in oxidizing flame.
derivation:
1. Bead Formation: Heating Borax (\(Na_2B_4O_7 \cdot 10H_2O\)).
   Loses water \(\rightarrow\) Swells \(\rightarrow\) Transparent glassy bead (\(NaBO_2 + B_2O_3\)).
2. Color Formation: Boric Anhydride (\(B_2O_3\)) reacts with Metal Oxide.
   \(CuO + B_2O_3 \rightarrow Cu(BO_2)_2\) (Blue Bead).
   \(CoO + B_2O_3 \rightarrow Co(BO_2)_2\) (Deep Blue Bead).

related_concepts.name: Oxidizing/Reducing Flame
related_concepts.definition: Colors may differ based on flame zone (e.g., Cu is Red in reducing flame due to Cu2O formation).

subject: Chemistry
title: Flame Test (Sodium)
description: Excitation of valence electrons emits characteristic yellow light.
derivation:
Principle: Thermal Excitation.
1. Heat from Bunsen burner volatilizes the chloride salt.
2. Valence electron (3s) absorbs energy and jumps to higher levels (3p).
3. Relaxation: Electron falls back to 3s, emitting photon.
   Energy gap corresponds to wavelength of yellow light (~589 nm).

related_concepts.name: Emission Spectrum
related_concepts.definition: The spectrum of frequencies of electromagnetic radiation emitted due to an atom or molecule making a transition from a high energy state to a lower energy state.

subject: Chemistry
title: Flame Test (Barium)
description: Characteristic flame color for Barium salts.
derivation:
Electronic transition specific to Barium cation.
Usually performed with Platinum wire dipped in Conc HCl (to form volatile chlorides).
Caution: Copper salts (if Cu is not removed) can sometimes mimic green flames (bluish-green), so Group 2 removal is essential.

related_concepts.name: Calcium Flame
related_concepts.definition: Brick Red.

related_concepts.name: Strontium Flame
related_concepts.definition: Crimson Red.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbonate Test
description: Detection of \(CO_3^{2-}\). Lime water turns milky.
derivation:
1. Action of Acid: Dilute HCl/H2SO4 on carbonate releases \(CO_2\).
   \(CO_3^{2-} + 2H^+ \rightarrow H_2O + CO_2 \uparrow\)
2. Lime Water Test: Gas passed through \(Ca(OH)_2\).
   Forms insoluble Calcium Carbonate (Milky).
3. Excess Gas: Milkiness disappears due to formation of soluble Bicarbonate.
   \(CaCO_3 + CO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(HCO_3)_2\).

related_concepts.name: Bicarbonate Test
related_concepts.definition: Bicarbonates also give CO2 but do not precipitate with MgSO4 in cold.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sulphite Test
description: Detection of \(SO_3^{2-}\). Gas turns dichromate paper Green.
derivation:
1. Action of Acid: Releases \(SO_2\) (suffocating smell of burning sulfur).
2. Redox Reaction: \(SO_2\) is a reducing agent.
   It reduces Orange Dichromate (\(Cr^{+6}\)) to Green Chromium (\(Cr^{+3}\)).
   This distinguishes \(SO_2\) from \(CO_2\).

related_concepts.name: KMnO4 Test
related_concepts.definition: SO2 also decolorizes Pink KMnO4 solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sulphide Test
description: Detection of Sulphide ion (\(S^{2-}\)). Lead Acetate paper turns black.
derivation:
1. Acidification: Dilute \(H_2SO_4\) releases \(H_2S\) gas (Rotten egg smell).
2. Confirmatory Test: The gas is passed over filter paper dipped in Lead Acetate.
3. Reaction: \(H_2S + Pb^{2+} \rightarrow PbS\) (Lead Sulphide).
4. Observation: The paper turns shiny black due to formation of PbS.

related_concepts.name: Sodium Nitroprusside Test
related_concepts.definition: Another test for sulphide giving a violet color: \([Fe(CN)_5NOS]^{4-}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitrite Test
description: Detection of Nitrite (\(NO_2^-\)). Evolves brown fumes with dilute acid.
derivation:
1. Action of Dilute Acid: Nitrites are unstable in acid.
   \(2HNO_2 \rightarrow H_2O + NO + NO_2\)
2. Oxidation: Nitric Oxide (NO) reacts with oxygen in air to form Nitrogen Dioxide (\(NO_2\)).
   \(2NO + O_2 \rightarrow 2NO_2\) (Brown Fumes).
3. Starch-Iodide Test: The fumes turn starch-iodide paper blue (oxidizes \(I^-\to I_2\)).

related_concepts.name: Diazotization
related_concepts.definition: Nitrites react with aromatic primary amines at low temp to form diazonium salts.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitrate Test (Ring Test)
description: Confirmatory for Nitrate (\(NO_3^-\)). Brown ring forms at interface.
derivation:
1. Reduction: Ferrous sulfate (\(Fe^{2+}\)) reduces Nitrate to NO in presence of conc \(H_2SO_4\).
   \(NO_3^- + 3Fe^{2+} + 4H^+ \rightarrow NO + 3Fe^{3+} + 2H_2O\)
2. Complexation: NO binds to excess \(Fe^{2+}\).
   \([Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+} + NO \rightarrow [Fe(H_2O)_5NO]^{2+} + H_2O\)
   The complex (Nitroso ferrous sulphate) forms a brown ring at the junction of acid and solution.

related_concepts.name: Brown Ring Complex
related_concepts.definition: In this complex, Fe is in +1 oxidation state and NO is +1.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chromyl Chloride Test
description: Specific test for Chloride ions using K2Cr2O7 and Conc H2SO4.
derivation:
1. Formation: Chloride salt + \(K_2Cr_2O_7\) + Conc \(H_2SO_4\) \(\rightarrow\) Heating.
   \(K_2Cr_2O_7 + 4NaCl + 6H_2SO_4 \rightarrow 2CrO_2Cl_2 + 4NaHSO_4 + 2KHSO_4 + 3H_2O\)
2. Confirmation: Pass red vapors into NaOH \(\rightarrow\) Yellow solution (\(Na_2CrO_4\)).
3. Precipitation: Add Lead Acetate \(\rightarrow\) Yellow ppt (\(PbCrO_4\)).
Note: Chlorides of Ag, Pb, Hg, and Sn do not give this test.

related_concepts.name: Dry Test
related_concepts.definition: A test performed on the solid salt rather than a solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Layer Test (Br/I)
description: Redox test using Chlorine water and \(CHCl_3\) (Chloroform) or \(CS_2\).
derivation:
Principle: Chlorine is a stronger oxidizing agent than Bromine or Iodine.
1. Displacement: \(Cl_2\) displaces \(Br^-\)/\(I^-\).
   \(2Br^- + Cl_2 \rightarrow Br_2 + 2Cl^-\)
   \(2I^- + Cl_2 \rightarrow I_2 + 2Cl^-\)
2. Extraction: The free halogen dissolves in the organic layer (Chloroform).
3. Color: Bromine \(\rightarrow\) Orange/Brown layer. Iodine \(\rightarrow\) Violet layer.

related_concepts.name: Solvent Extraction
related_concepts.definition: Separation of compounds based on their relative solubilities in two immiscible liquids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Phosphate Test
description: Canary Yellow precipitate of Ammonium Phosphomolybdate.
derivation:
1. Reagent: Ammonium Molybdate \((NH_4)_2MoO_4\) in presence of Conc \(HNO_3\).
2. Reaction: Phosphate reacts with Molybdate.
   \(PO_4^{3-} + 12MoO_4^{2-} + 24H^+ + 3NH_4^+ \rightarrow (NH_4)_3[PMo_{12}O_{40}] + 12H_2O\)
3. Condition: Solution must be acidic and heated gently.
Arsenic gives a similar yellow ppt, so interfere must be removed.

related_concepts.name: Heteropoly Acid
related_concepts.definition: Complex acids composed of hydrogen, oxygen, a heteroatom (P), and addenda atoms (Mo).

subject: Chemistry
title: Flame Photometry Colors
description: Qualitative detection of Alkali metals.
derivation:
Principle: Thermal Excitation.
1. Heat atomizes the salt.
2. Valence electron is excited to higher energy level.
3. Electron relaxes to ground state, emitting photon.
4. Energy gap corresponds to specific wavelength in visible region.
$Mg$ and $Be$ do not give flame test (High Ionization Energy, electron not excited by Bunsen flame).

related_concepts.name: Cobalt Glass
related_concepts.definition: Used to view Potassium flame (filters out yellow Na light).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mohr's Salt (Formula)
description: Ferrous Ammonium Sulfate. A Double Salt.
derivation:
Structure:
Contains $Fe^{2+}$, $NH_4^+$, and $SO_4^{2-}$ ions in equimolar ratio.
Stability: More stable towards aerial oxidation than pure Ferrous Sulfate.
Use: Primary standard in Redox titrations (titrated against $KMnO_4$).
Note: It is a double salt (dissociates fully), not a coordination complex.

related_concepts.name: Double Salt
related_concepts.definition: Addition compound stable in solid state but loses identity in solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Potash Alum (Formula)
description: Double salt of Potassium and Aluminium. General formula $M_2SO_4 \cdot M'_2(SO_4)_3 \cdot 24H_2O$.
derivation:
Geometry:
Both cations ($K^+$ and $Al^{3+}$) are surrounded by 6 water molecules (Octahedral).
Applications:
1. Coagulant in water purification (neutralizes negative charge on colloidal clay).
2. Antiseptic (Aftershave).
3. Mordant in dyeing.

related_concepts.name: Pseudo Alum
related_concepts.definition: Alums containing divalent ions instead of monovalent ones are not true alums.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cobalt Nitrate Test
description: Charcoal cavity test for Zinc, Magnesium, Aluminum.
derivation:
1. Salt + $Na_2CO_3$ heated on charcoal $\rightarrow$ Oxide ($ZnO$).
2. Add Cobalt Nitrate ($Co(NO_3)_2$) and heat.
3. Formation of Mixed Oxides (Spinels).
   $ZnO + CoO \rightarrow CoZnO_2$ (Rinmann's Green).
   $Al_2O_3 + CoO \rightarrow CoAl_2O_4$ (Thenard's Blue).
   $MgO + CoO \rightarrow CoMgO_2$ (Pink).

related_concepts.name: Dry Test
related_concepts.definition: Preliminary test performed before dissolving salt in water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Test for Fluoride
description: Etching of glass test or Water Drop test.
derivation:
1. Mix salt with Sand ($SiO_2$) and Conc $H_2SO_4$.
2. Heating releases $SiF_4$ gas.
   $CaF_2 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CaSO_4 + 2HF$
   $4HF + SiO_2 \rightarrow SiF_4 + 2H_2O$
3. Hold a drop of water in a loop over the gas.
   $3SiF_4 + 2H_2O \rightarrow SiO_2 \downarrow + 2H_2SiF_6$.
   Turbidity ($SiO_2$) appears in the water drop.

related_concepts.name: Etching
related_concepts.definition: Corrosive action of HF on glass (silicates).

subject: Chemistry
title: Beilstein Test
description: Detection of Halogens (Cl, Br, I) in organic compounds.
derivation:
Procedure: Heat Copper wire with compound in Bunsen flame.
Reaction: Halogen reacts with Copper to form volatile Copper Halide ($CuX_2$).
Observation: Copper halides impart a characteristic Green or Blue-Green color to the flame.
Limit: Does not distinguish between Cl, Br, I. Urea/Thiourea also give positive test (due to C-N).

related_concepts.name: Lassaigne's Test
related_concepts.definition: More reliable wet test for halogens involving Silver Nitrate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 1 (Group I) Cations
description: Dilute HCl precipitates Group I chlorides (white). \(M^{n+}\)=cation, \(Cl^-\)=group reagent (dil. HCl).

subject: Chemistry
title: Group I Group Reagent
visual_data: \text{Group I (dil. HCl): } PbCl_2, AgCl, Hg_2Cl_2 \text{ (all white } \downarrow)
description: Group reagent and precipitates of analytical Group I (insoluble chlorides). Identifies \(Pb^{2+}, Ag^+, Hg_2^{2+}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: PbS / CuS / CdS Colors
description: Characteristic colors of Group II sulfide precipitates for identification. Color distinguishes cations within Group II.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group II Subdivision (IIA/IIB)
visual_data: IIB: \; As_2S_3, Sb_2S_3, SnS_2 + S^{2-} \rightarrow \text{soluble thio-salts}
description: Group IIB sulfides dissolve in yellow ammonium sulfide (amphoteric) separating from IIA. Basis of IIA/IIB split.

subject: Chemistry
title: Common Ion Effect (H2S Control)
description: Controls sulfide ion concentration to selectively precipitate Group II vs IV. \(K_{a1},K_{a2}\)=dissociation constants of H2S, \([H^+]\)=acidity.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility Product Condition
description: Precipitation occurs when ionic product exceeds solubility product. \(Q_{sp}\)=ionic product, \(K_{sp}\)=solubility product.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group IV Sulfide Colors
description: Colors of Group IV sulfide precipitates used to distinguish the cations. Aids confirmation within Group IV.

subject: Chemistry
title: Role of NH4Cl in Group III/IV
visual_data: NH_4Cl \rightarrow NH_4^+ + Cl^-; \quad NH_4^+ \text{ suppresses } OH^-/S^{2-}
description: Common ion suppresses NH4OH/H2S ionization so only Group III hydroxides (or IV sulfides) precipitate, not higher groups. \(NH_4^+\)=common ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group III Hydroxide Colors
description: Colors of Group III hydroxide precipitates for cation identification. Distinguishes Fe(III), Al, Cr.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group V (Carbonate) Reagent
description: Ammonium carbonate in NH4OH/NH4Cl precipitates Group V carbonates (white). \(M^{2+}\)=alkaline earth cation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Flame Test (Calcium)
description: Confirmatory flame color for calcium (Group V). Distinguishes Ca from Ba/Sr.

subject: Chemistry
title: Flame Test (Strontium)
description: Confirmatory flame color for strontium (Group V). Distinguishes Sr from Ba (green) and Ca (brick red).

subject: Chemistry
title: Flame Test (Potassium / Copper)
description: Confirmatory flame colors: K violet (lilac), Cu bluish-green. K seen through blue cobalt glass.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Ba (Chromate)
description: Yellow chromate precipitate confirms barium in Group V. \(CrO_4^{2-}\)=chromate reagent (K2CrO4).

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Ca (Oxalate)
description: White calcium oxalate precipitate (insoluble in acetic acid) confirms calcium. \(C_2O_4^{2-}\)=oxalate reagent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Cu (Blue/KI)
description: Cu(II) oxidizes iodide giving white Cu2I2 plus brown I2; also deep blue with NH4OH. Confirms copper (Group II).

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Cu (Ammonia)
description: Deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) confirms copper. \([Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}\)=ammine complex.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Fe(III) (Thiocyanate)
description: Blood-red ferric thiocyanate confirms Fe(III). \(SCN^-\)=thiocyanate reagent (KSCN).

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Al (Lake Test)
description: Al(OH)3 adsorbs blue litmus/alizarin dye forming a colored lake, confirming aluminium (Group III). Distinguishes Al from Cr/Fe.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Cr (Oxidation)
description: Cr(III) oxidized by alkaline H2O2 to yellow chromate; acidify to orange dichromate / blue CrO5. Confirms chromium.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chromium Peroxide (Blue)
description: Blue chromium pentoxide \(CrO_5\) in ether/amyl alcohol confirms chromium/chromate. \(CrO_5\)=peroxide (peroxo) of Cr(VI).

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Mn (Pink/MnO4)
description: Sodium bismuthate oxidizes Mn(II) to purple permanganate, confirming manganese (Group IV). \(MnO_4^-\)=permanganate (purple).

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Zn (Cobalt/Ferro)
description: Bluish-white potassium zinc ferrocyanide confirms zinc (Group IV). \([Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}\)=ferrocyanide reagent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Pb (Yellow PbI2)
description: Yellow PbI2 (golden spangles on heating) and yellow PbCrO4 confirm lead. \(Pb^{2+}\)=lead(II) cation.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Ag (AgCl Solubility)
description: White AgCl dissolves in ammonia (diammine complex) and re-precipitates on acidification, confirming silver (Group I). \([Ag(NH_3)_2]^+\)=diamminesilver(I).

subject: Chemistry
title: PbCl2 Hot-Water Solubility
description: PbCl2 dissolves in hot water (unlike AgCl, Hg2Cl2) separating Pb from Group I. \(PbCl_2\)=lead chloride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hg2Cl2 with Ammonia (Black)
description: Mercurous chloride turns black/grey with ammonia (Hg + white aminochloride) confirming \(Hg_2^{2+}\) (Group I).

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Bi (Hydrolysis)
description: Bismuth(III) hydrolyzes on dilution giving white bismuth oxychloride, confirming Bi (Group II). \(BiOCl\)=bismuthyl chloride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Co (Thiocyanate)
description: Blue tetrathiocyanatocobaltate confirms cobalt (Group IV); Vogel's test. \([Co(SCN)_4]^{2-}\)=cobalt thiocyanate complex.

subject: Chemistry
title: Preliminary Test: Dry Heating
description: Heating dry salt evolves characteristic gases/vapors hinting at acid radical. Used in preliminary qualitative analysis.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbonate vs Bicarbonate (MgSO4)
description: Magnesium sulphate gives white ppt with carbonate (cold) but not bicarbonate, distinguishing the two anions. \(CO_3^{2-}/HCO_3^-\)=carbonate/bicarbonate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sulphate Test (BaCl2)
description: White barium sulphate insoluble in dil. HCl confirms sulphate. \(SO_4^{2-}\)=sulphate, \(BaSO_4\)=barium sulphate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chloride Test (AgNO3)
description: White AgCl soluble in ammonia confirms chloride. \(Cl^-\)=chloride, \(AgCl\)=silver chloride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bromide / Iodide with AgNO3
description: Silver bromide (pale yellow, partly NH3-soluble) and silver iodide (yellow, NH3-insoluble) confirm Br⁻/I⁻. \(AgX\)=silver halide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acetate Test (Ester / FeCl3)
description: Neutral FeCl3 gives blood-red ferric acetate (turns brown ppt on boiling) confirming acetate. \(CH_3COO^-\)=acetate ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acetate (Ester Smell)
description: Warming acetate with ethanol + conc. H2SO4 gives fruity-smelling ethyl acetate, confirming acetate radical. \(CH_3COOC_2H_5\)=ethyl acetate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbonate Evolution (Dil. Acid)
description: Brisk effervescence of CO2 with dil. acid indicates carbonate (Group I acid radical). \(CO_3^{2-}\)=carbonate, gas turns lime water milky.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sulphide Evolution (Dil. Acid)
description: Rotten-egg H2S with dil. acid (blackens lead acetate paper) indicates sulphide. \(S^{2-}\)=sulphide ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitrate (Conc. H2SO4 + Cu)
description: Heating nitrate with conc. H2SO4 and Cu turnings evolves brown NO2 fumes, confirming nitrate. \(NO_2\)=nitrogen dioxide (brown).

subject: Chemistry
title: Halide with Conc. H2SO4
visual_data: Cl^- \rightarrow HCl\uparrow; \; Br^- \rightarrow Br_2\uparrow; \; I^- \rightarrow I_2\uparrow
description: Conc. H2SO4 evolves HCl (colorless), Br2 (reddish-brown), I2 (violet) vapors distinguishing halides by reducing power. \(X^-\)=halide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxalate Test (KMnO4)
description: Warm oxalate decolorizes acidified KMnO4 (CO2 evolved) confirming oxalate. \(C_2O_4^{2-}\)=oxalate, \(MnO_4^-\)=permanganate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Phosphate (Ammonium Molybdate)
description: Canary-yellow ammonium phosphomolybdate confirms phosphate with conc. HNO3. \(PO_4^{3-}\)=phosphate, yellow ppt = phosphomolybdate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sodium Carbonate Extract
description: Boiling insoluble salt with Na2CO3 converts interfering cations to carbonates, leaving soluble sodium salts of anions for testing. \(X^{n-}\)=acid radical.

subject: Chemistry
title: Microcosmic Salt Bead
visual_data: NaNH_4HPO_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} NaPO_3 + NH_3 \uparrow + H_2O; \; NaPO_3 + MO \rightarrow NaMPO_4
description: Microcosmic salt bead test: metaphosphate dissolves metal oxides giving colored metaphosphates (like borax bead). \(MO\)=metal oxide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of NO3 vs NO2 (Ring)
visual_data: NO_3^- \rightarrow \text{ring with conc. } H_2SO_4; \; NO_2^- \rightarrow \text{ring with dil. acid}
description: Nitrate gives brown ring only with concentrated H2SO4; nitrite gives ring even with dilute acetic acid, distinguishing them. \(NO_3^-/NO_2^-\)=nitrate/nitrite.

subject: Chemistry
title: Halide Discrimination (Chlorine Water / Layer Test)
visual_data: 2Br^- + Cl_2 \rightarrow Br_2 \text{ (orange layer)}; \quad 2I^- + Cl_2 \rightarrow I_2 \text{ (violet layer)}
description: Comparative test to distinguish Cl-, Br-, I- using chlorine water and an organic layer (CS2/CCl4). Cl- gives no colour, Br- gives orange/brown layer, I- gives violet/pink layer; excess Cl2 bleaches I2 to colourless. \(Cl_2\)=chlorine water; coloured layer = liberated free halogen dissolved in organic solvent.
derivation:
Oxidising power: \(Cl_2 > Br_2 > I_2\)
Cl_2 displaces both Br^- and I^- (not vice versa)
2Br^- + Cl_2 \rightarrow Br_2 + 2Cl^- \;(orange)
2I^- + Cl_2 \rightarrow I_2 + 2Cl^- \;(violet)
Excess Cl_2: I_2 + 5Cl_2 + 6H_2O \rightarrow 2IO_3^- + 12H^+ + 10Cl^- \;(colourless)

subject: Chemistry
title: Confirmation of Cd (Yellow CdS)
description: Cd2+ separated from Cu in Group IIA: ammonia gives colourless tetrammine (unlike deep-blue Cu), then H2S reprecipitates bright yellow CdS. \(Cd^{2+}\)=cadmium(II); yellow CdS is the confirmatory precipitate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Magnesium Confirmation (Titan Yellow)
description: Confirmatory dye test for Group VI Mg2+: Mg(OH)2 adsorbs titan yellow dye giving a bright red lake/precipitate in alkaline medium. \(Mg^{2+}\)=magnesium ion; \(OH^-\)=alkaline (NaOH) medium.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nitrate Confirmation (Devarda's Alloy)
description: Devarda's alloy (Cu-Al-Zn) in NaOH reduces NO3- (and NO2-) to ammonia, detected by smell/Nessler. \(NO_3^-\)=nitrate; Al=reducing alloy; NH3 gas turns litmus blue.

subject: Chemistry
title: Borate Test (Green-Edged Flame)
description: Confirmatory test for borate: heating borate with ethanol and conc. H2SO4 forms volatile triethyl borate that burns with a characteristic green-edged flame. \(H_3BO_3\)=boric acid; \(B(OC_2H_5)_3\)=triethyl borate ester.

subject: Chemistry
title: Interfering Radical: Phosphate Removal
visual_data: PO_4^{3-} + FeCl_3 \rightarrow FePO_4 \downarrow \text{ (removed before Group V)}
description: Phosphate, borate, oxalate, fluoride are interfering anions removed before Group V/VI; phosphate is precipitated as FePO4 in acetic acid medium so it cannot precipitate Ca/Ba/Mg prematurely. \(PO_4^{3-}\)=phosphate; \(Fe^{3+}\)=ferric ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Why H2S in Group II vs Group IV
visual_data: \text{Gp II (acidic): low } [S^{2-}] \Rightarrow \text{only low-} K_{sp} \text{ sulphides}; \quad \text{Gp IV (basic): high } [S^{2-}]
description: Selective sulphide precipitation: in acidic (HCl) medium [S2-] is low so only very low-Ksp sulphides (Group II) precipitate; in basic (NH4OH) medium [S2-] is high so higher-Ksp sulphides (Group IV) also precipitate. \([S^{2-}]\) controlled via common-ion effect of \(H^+\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Manganese Bead / Sulphide Dissolution
description: Buff/pink MnS (Group IV) readily dissolves in dilute acid (high Ksp), distinguishing it from black NiS/CoS; borax bead is violet/amethyst in oxidising flame. \(MnS\)=manganese sulphide; \(Mn^{2+}\)=manganous ion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Free Chlorine Test (Starch-Iodide)
description: Detection of oxidising anions/free halogen (e.g. hypochlorite, chlorine water) using starch-iodide paper which turns blue from liberated iodine. \(Cl_2\)=oxidant; blue colour from iodine-starch complex.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acid Rain
description: Precipitation with pH < 5.6 due to dissolved oxides of Sulfur and Nitrogen.
derivation:
Natural rain is slightly acidic (pH ~5.6) due to \(H_2CO_3\).
