Mechanism of Acid Rain:
1. Emission: \(SO_2\) (burning fossil fuels) and \(NO_2\) (vehicles).
2. Oxidation: Catalyzed by particulate matter or ozone.
   \(4NO_2 + 2H_2O + O_2 \rightarrow 4HNO_3\)
3. Deposition: Acids fall with rain, damaging marble (\(CaCO_3\)) and aquatic life.

related_concepts.name: Stone Leprosy
related_concepts.definition: Corrosion of historical monuments (Taj Mahal) by acid rain: \(CaCO_3 + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow CaSO_4 + H_2O + CO_2\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Photochemical Smog
description: Oxidizing Smog (Los Angeles Smog). Contains Ozone, PAN, and NO2.
derivation:
Condition: Warm, dry, sunny climate + Vehicular exhaust.
Chain Reaction:
1. Photolysis: \(NO_2\) absorbs sunlight \(\rightarrow NO + O (atomic)\).
2. Ozone Formation: \(O + O_2 \rightarrow O_3\).
3. PAN Formation: Hydrocarbons + \(O_3/NO_2 \rightarrow\) Peroxyacetyl Nitrate (PAN).
PAN is a powerful eye irritant.

related_concepts.name: Secondary Pollutants
related_concepts.definition: Pollutants formed in the atmosphere (Ozone, PAN) rather than emitted directly.

subject: Chemistry
title: Classical Smog
description: Reducing Smog (London Smog). Occurs in cool, humid climates.
derivation:
Composition:
1. Smoke (Carbon particulates/soot).
2. Fog (Condensed water vapor).
3. Sulfur Dioxide (\(SO_2\)).
Nature: Reducing (due to Carbon and SO2).
Mechanism: \(SO_2\) is adsorbed on particulates and inhaled, forming \(H_2SO_4\) in lungs.

related_concepts.name: Particulate Matter (PM)
related_concepts.definition: Microscopic solid or liquid matter suspended in the atmosphere (PM2.5, PM10).

subject: Chemistry
title: Ozone Depletion Mechanism
description: Catalytic destruction of ozone by CFCs (Freons).
derivation:
1. Photolysis: UV breaks C-Cl bond in CFCs.
   \(CF_2Cl_2 \xrightarrow{h\nu} \cdot CF_2Cl + Cl^\bullet\)
2. Propagation (Ozone destruction):
   \(Cl^\bullet + O_3 \rightarrow ClO^\bullet + O_2\)
3. Regeneration of Catalyst:
   \(ClO^\bullet + O^\bullet \rightarrow Cl^\bullet + O_2\)
Result: One Chlorine radical can destroy thousands of Ozone molecules.

related_concepts.name: Ozone Hole
related_concepts.definition: Thinning of ozone layer, particularly over Antarctica during spring.

subject: Chemistry
title: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD)
description: Measure of dissolved oxygen consumed by microorganisms to decompose organic matter over 5 days at 20°C.
derivation:
Water pollution indicator:
High Organic Waste \(\rightarrow\) High Bacterial Activity \(\rightarrow\) High Oxygen Consumption \(\rightarrow\) High BOD.
Clean Water: BOD < 5 ppm.
Highly Polluted Water: BOD > 17 ppm.

related_concepts.name: Eutrophication
related_concepts.definition: Nutrient enrichment leading to algal blooms and oxygen depletion.

subject: Chemistry
title: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD)
description: Oxygen required to oxidize ALL organic matter (biodegradable + non-biodegradable) using a strong oxidizer.
derivation:
1. Reagent: Acidified Potassium Dichromate (\(K_2Cr_2O_7\)).
2. Process: Oxidizes all organic carbon to \(CO_2\).
3. Comparison: Since it degrades chemicals that bacteria cannot, COD is always higher than BOD for the same sample.

related_concepts.name: TOC
related_concepts.definition: Total Organic Carbon, another measure of water quality.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hardness of Water (Types)
description: Caused by Ca and Mg salts. Temporary (Boiling removes), Permanent (Chemicals needed).
derivation:
1. Temporary Hardness: Bicarbonates.
   Removal: Boiling. $Ca(HCO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaCO_3 \downarrow + H_2O + CO_2$.
2. Permanent Hardness: Chlorides/Sulfates.
   Removal: Washing Soda ($Na_2CO_3$) or Ion Exchange (Zeolite/Resin).
   $Ca^{2+} + Na_2Z \rightarrow CaZ + 2Na^+$ (Z = Zeolite).

related_concepts.name: Calgon's Method
related_concepts.definition: Use of Sodium Hexametaphosphate to sequester calcium ions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Green Chemistry (Atom Economy)
visual_data: \% \text{Atom Economy} = \frac{\text{Mass of Desired Product}}{\text{Total Mass of Reactants}} \times 100
description: Measure of reaction efficiency in terms of waste reduction.
derivation:
Contrast with % Yield.
Yield calculates actual vs theoretical.
Atom Economy calculates how many atoms from reactants end up in the final useful product vs waste byproducts.
Addition reactions (e.g., Hydrogenation) have 100% atom economy.
Substitution/Elimination reactions have lower economy due to byproducts.

related_concepts.name: E-Factor
related_concepts.definition: Ratio of mass of waste to mass of product (Environment Factor).

subject: Chemistry
title: Calgon's Method
description: Water softening agent. Sequesters $Ca^{2+}$ ions.
derivation:
Dissociation: $Na_2[Na_4(PO_3)_6] \rightleftharpoons 2Na^+ + [Na_4P_6O_{18}]^{2-}$.
Action: Calcium ions from hard water displace Sodium ions in the complex anion.
$M^{2+} + [Na_4P_6O_{18}]^{2-} \rightarrow [Na_2MP_6O_{18}]^{2-} + 2Na^+$.
Calcium stays trapped in the complex and doesn't precipitate with soap.

related_concepts.name: Sequestration
related_concepts.definition: Process of forming a soluble complex with metal ions to prevent them from reacting.

subject: Chemistry
title: Tropospheric Pollutant: CO Formation
description: Incomplete combustion of carbon/fossil fuel gives carbon monoxide, the most abundant air pollutant. \(CO\)=carbon monoxide. CO binds haemoglobin ~300x stronger than \(O_2\) forming carboxyhaemoglobin.

subject: Chemistry
title: Acid Rain (Nitric Acid Route)
description: Nitrogen oxides contribute to acid rain alongside sulphur oxides. Acid rain has \(pH < 5.6\); \(H_2SO_4\) and \(HNO_3\) are the main acids lowering rainwater pH.

subject: Chemistry
title: PAN (Peroxyacetyl Nitrate)
description: Major secondary pollutant of photochemical smog; powerful eye irritant. Formed from hydrocarbons + \(NO_2\) under sunlight; smog is oxidising in nature (contains \(O_3\), PAN, \(NO_2\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Ozone Layer Trigger (CFC Photolysis)
description: UV photolysis of CFCs (freons) releases chlorine free radicals that catalytically destroy ozone. \(Cl^\bullet\)=chlorine radical; one radical can destroy ~100000 ozone molecules.

subject: Chemistry
title: ClO Radical Regeneration
description: Regeneration step that makes ozone depletion catalytic, returning the \(Cl^\bullet\) radical. Net effect: chlorine is a catalyst, consumed in step 1 and regenerated here.

subject: Chemistry
title: Stratospheric Ozone Formation
description: Natural ozone formation in the stratosphere that shields Earth from UV radiation. The ozone layer maintains a dynamic equilibrium between formation and decomposition.

subject: Chemistry
title: BOD as Pollution Index
description: BOD value classifies water purity. \(BOD\)=biochemical oxygen demand (ppm); higher BOD means more biodegradable organic matter and dirtier water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Eutrophication
description: Nutrient enrichment (phosphates/nitrates from fertilizers, detergents) causes excessive algal growth, whose decay depletes dissolved oxygen and kills aquatic life.

subject: Chemistry
title: Drinking Water Nitrate Limit
description: WHO/BIS upper limit of nitrate in potable water. Excess \(NO_3^-\) causes methemoglobinemia (blue baby syndrome) in infants. Fluoride limit \(\approx 1\) ppm, lead \(\leq 0.05\) ppm.

subject: Chemistry
title: Particulate Matter (Smoke/SPM)
description: Solid/liquid particles suspended in air; classified as viable (bacteria, fungi) and non-viable (smoke, dust, mist, fumes). Smaller particles are more harmful to lungs.

subject: Chemistry
title: Greenhouse Gas Contribution Order
description: Relative contribution of greenhouse gases to global warming (highest first). \(CO_2\) is the single largest contributor (\(\sim 50\text{-}60\%\)), followed by methane, CFCs/freons, and nitrous oxide; water vapour also contributes. Common recall: 'which gas contributes most' and 'arrange in order'.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dissolved Oxygen (DO) Levels
description: Threshold DO value distinguishing clean from polluted water (measures actual oxygen present, not demand). \(DO\)=dissolved oxygen in ppm (mg/L); clean water holds \(\sim 6\text{-}8\) ppm, and \(DO\) below \(\sim 6\) ppm is harmful/lethal to aquatic life. O\(_2\) is more soluble in cold water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Drinking Water: Fluoride & Lead Limits
description: Permissible (WHO/NCERT) limits of fluoride and lead in drinking water. \(F^-\) max \(\sim 1\) ppm: excess (>2 ppm) causes brown mottling/fluorosis of teeth and harms bones; \(Pb\) max \(\sim 50\) ppb damages kidney/liver/brain. Concentrations above these are toxic.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dobson Unit & Ozone Hole Chemistry
visual_data: ClONO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow HOCl + HNO_3; \quad ClONO_2 + HCl \rightarrow Cl_2 + HNO_3
description: Polar ozone-hole chemistry; ozone thickness measured in Dobson Units (DU). Over Antarctic polar stratospheric clouds in spring, reservoir species chlorine nitrate \(ClONO_2\) and \(HCl\) react on ice to release \(Cl_2\) and \(HOCl\), which photolyse to \(Cl^\bullet\) radicals that destroy O\(_3\), forming the ozone hole.

subject: Chemistry
title: Methane: Greenhouse & Marsh Gas
description: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas (also 'marsh gas'/biogas main component) from paddy fields, cattle, and wetlands. Per molecule its global-warming potential far exceeds \(CO_2\), though its atmospheric concentration is lower; it oxidises to \(CO_2\) and water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Aspirin (Non-Narcotic)
description: Analgesic (pain), Antipyretic (fever), Anti-inflammatory.
derivation:
Mechanism of Action:
1. Pain/Inflammation is caused by Prostaglandins.
2. Aspirin acetylates the enzyme Cyclooxygenase (COX).
3. This irreversibly inhibits COX, stopping Prostaglandin synthesis.
Note: Also acts as an anti-coagulant (prevents heart attacks).

related_concepts.name: Salol
related_concepts.definition: Phenyl salicylate, used as an intestinal antiseptic.

subject: Chemistry
title: Antiseptics vs Disinfectants
description: Same chemical acts differently based on concentration.
derivation:
Principle: Toxicity to tissues.
1. 0.2% Phenol: Low toxicity, safe for living tissues \(\rightarrow\) Antiseptic.
2. 1.0% Phenol: High toxicity, damages tissues, kills germs on floors/drains \(\rightarrow\) Disinfectant.
Other examples: Chlorine (0.2-0.4 ppm in water is antiseptic, higher is bleach).

related_concepts.name: Dettol
related_concepts.definition: Mixture of Chloroxylenol and Terpineol.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cationic Detergents
description: Quaternary ammonium salts (e.g., Cetyltrimethylammonium bromide).
derivation:
Structure:
1. Hydrophobic Tail: Long hydrocarbon chain (Cetyl = C16).
2. Hydrophilic Head: Positively charged Ammonium ion.
Properties:
- The cation is the active cleansing agent.
- Possesses germicidal properties.
- Used in hair conditioners (neutralizes static negative charge on hair).

related_concepts.name: Anionic Detergent
related_concepts.definition: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (Head is negative). Used in toothpaste and laundry.

subject: Chemistry
title: Tranquilizers (Mechanism)
description: Drugs for stress/anxiety. Example: Equanil, Barbiturates.
derivation:
Biochemical Basis:
Depression is often linked to low levels of Noradrenaline (neurotransmitter).
Antidepressants inhibit the enzymes that degrade noradrenaline.
Sedatives (Barbiturates like Luminal) act as GABA potentiators, depressing the CNS.

related_concepts.name: Psychotherapeutic Drugs
related_concepts.definition: Chemicals used for treatment of mental diseases.

subject: Chemistry
title: Vitamins (Fat Soluble)
description: Stored in liver/adipose tissue. Excess can be toxic (Hypervitaminosis).
derivation:
Functions/Deficiency:
- **A (Retinol):** Vision. Def: Night Blindness, Xerophthalmia.
- **D (Calciferol):** Calcium absorption. Def: Rickets (kids), Osteomalacia (adults).
- **E (Tocopherol):** Antioxidant. Def: Muscular weakness, sterility.
- **K (Phylloquinone):** Blood clotting. Def: Hemorrhage.

related_concepts.name: Water Soluble
related_concepts.definition: Vitamins B and C. Excreted in urine, must be supplied regularly.

subject: Chemistry
title: Antibiotics (Action)
description: Classification based on mode of action.
derivation:
1. Bactericidal (Kills): Penicillin, Ofloxacin, Aminoglycosides.
   - Targets cell wall synthesis or irreversible binding.
2. Bacteriostatic (Inhibits growth): Erythromycin, Tetracycline, Chloramphenicol.
   - Inhibits protein synthesis or metabolism, allowing immune system to clear infection.

related_concepts.name: Broad Spectrum
related_concepts.definition: Antibiotics effective against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria (e.g., Chloramphenicol).

subject: Chemistry
title: Antifertility Drugs
description: Oral contraceptives that suppress ovulation by mimicking natural hormones. Norethindrone is a synthetic progesterone derivative; Ethynylestradiol (Novestrol) is the estrogen component.

subject: Chemistry
title: Antibiotic Spectrum
description: Classification by range of microbes attacked. Broad-spectrum (e.g. Chloramphenicol, Tetracycline, Ampicillin) act on many bacteria; narrow-spectrum (Penicillin G) act on few; limited-spectrum act against a single organism.

related_concepts.name: Salvarsan
related_concepts.definition: Arsenic-based, first effective antibiotic (Paul Ehrlich) used against syphilis.

related_concepts.name: Bactericidal vs bacteriostatic
related_concepts.definition: Penicillin/Aminoglycosides kill (cidal); Erythromycin/Tetracycline/Chloramphenicol inhibit growth (static).

subject: Chemistry
title: Sulpha Drugs
description: Antibacterials (e.g. Sulphapyridine, Sulphadiazine) structurally similar to PABA; competitively block folic acid synthesis in bacteria. Used as substitute when antibiotics unsuitable.

subject: Chemistry
title: Analgesics (Narcotic)
description: Opioid pain relievers that bind CNS receptors, relieve pain and induce sleep in moderate doses. Habit-forming; used in cancer/post-op care. Non-narcotic (e.g. Aspirin) do not cause addiction.

subject: Chemistry
title: Biodegradability of Detergents
description: Detergents with straight (unbranched) hydrocarbon chains are degraded by microorganisms; highly branched chains (e.g. with quaternary carbon) resist degradation and pollute water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Food Preservatives
description: Prevent spoilage by microbial growth. Common: sodium benzoate (metabolized, safe), salts of sorbic/propanoic acid, table salt, sugar, vegetable oils, and sodium metabisulphite.

subject: Chemistry
title: Antioxidants (Food)
description: Added to fats/oils to retard oxidation (rancidity); they are more readily oxidized than food, sacrificing themselves. BHA = butylated hydroxyanisole, BHT = butylated hydroxytoluene.

subject: Chemistry
title: Drug-Enzyme Interaction
description: Drugs can inhibit enzymes. Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate and compete for the active site; non-competitive (allosteric) inhibitors bind a different site, altering active-site shape.

subject: Chemistry
title: Receptors as Drug Targets
description: Drugs act on receptor proteins. Agonists mimic the natural messenger and activate the receptor; antagonists bind and block the receptor, preventing the natural messenger's action.

subject: Chemistry
title: Antacids (Acidity)
description: Drugs that remove excess stomach acid. \(\text{Mg(OH)}_2/\text{Al(OH)}_3\)=mild bases neutralizing HCl; \(\text{NaHCO}_3\)=baking soda antacid.

related_concepts.name: H2-receptor antagonist
related_concepts.definition: Cimetidine / Ranitidine block histamine at H2 receptors of stomach wall, reducing HCl secretion at the source (more effective than simple neutralizers).

related_concepts.name: Omeprazole
related_concepts.definition: Newer antacid that controls acidity by inhibiting the proton pump that releases H+, preventing acid formation.

related_concepts.name: Limitation of simple antacids
related_concepts.definition: Metal hydroxides/NaHCO3 only neutralize existing acid; cannot stop over-production, and excess base can make stomach alkaline triggering more acid.

subject: Chemistry
title: Antihistamines (Antiallergic)
description: Drugs that interfere with histamine's allergic action by competing at receptors. \(\text{H}_1\)=histamine receptors mediating allergy/inflammation.

related_concepts.name: Synthetic examples
related_concepts.definition: Brompheniramine (Dimetapp) and Terfenadine (Seldane) are common synthetic antihistamines.

related_concepts.name: Why they do NOT reduce acid
related_concepts.definition: Antihistamines act on H1 receptors (allergy); they do not affect H2 receptors that control HCl secretion, so they cannot reduce stomach acidity. Cimetidine/Ranitidine target H2 instead.

related_concepts.name: Mechanism
related_concepts.definition: They compete with histamine for binding at receptor sites, preventing histamine's effect rather than reducing its amount.

subject: Chemistry
title: Classification of Drugs
visual_data: \text{(1) Pharmacological effect} \quad \text{(2) Drug action} \\ \text{(3) Chemical structure} \quad \text{(4) Molecular targets}
description: Four bases for classifying drugs in medicinal chemistry. Each basis serves a different user (doctor vs chemist).

related_concepts.name: On pharmacological effect
related_concepts.definition: Groups by the biological effect (e.g. all analgesics relieve pain); useful for DOCTORS as it gives a full range of drugs for an ailment.

related_concepts.name: On drug action
related_concepts.definition: Based on the action on a particular biochemical process, e.g. antihistamines inhibit the action of histamine.

related_concepts.name: On chemical structure
related_concepts.definition: Groups drugs with common structural features, often having similar pharmacological activity (e.g. sulphonamides).

related_concepts.name: On molecular targets
related_concepts.definition: Groups by the biomolecule (enzyme/receptor) targeted; most useful for medicinal CHEMISTS designing drugs.

subject: Chemistry
title: Soaps (Saponification)
description: Soaps = Na/K salts of long-chain fatty acids made by alkaline hydrolysis of fats. \(\text{RCOONa}\)=soap; reaction is called saponification.

related_concepts.name: Hard vs soft soap
related_concepts.definition: Sodium salts = hard soaps (toilet soaps); potassium salts = soft soaps used in shaving creams and liquid soaps.

related_concepts.name: Types of soap
related_concepts.definition: Toilet soaps (excess alkali removed, colour/perfume added), transparent soaps (dissolved in ethanol, evaporated), medicated soaps (with antiseptics), shaving soaps (with glycerol + rosin as gum), laundry soaps.

related_concepts.name: Soaps fail in hard water
related_concepts.definition: Ca2+/Mg2+ ions in hard water react with soap forming insoluble calcium/magnesium stearate (scum/curdy precipitate), wasting soap and reducing cleansing.

subject: Chemistry
title: Cleansing Action (Micelle)
description: How soap/detergent removes oily dirt. Tail (non-polar) dissolves in grease; ionic head stays in water; aggregates into micelles emulsifying grease.

related_concepts.name: Micelle
related_concepts.definition: Spherical aggregate (formed above critical micelle concentration) with non-polar hydrocarbon tails pointing inward toward grease and polar/ionic heads facing the surrounding water.

related_concepts.name: Emulsification
related_concepts.definition: Grease is trapped at the centre of the micelle and pulled into the water as a stable oil-in-water emulsion, then rinsed away with agitation.

related_concepts.name: Stabilization
related_concepts.definition: Negatively charged heads on the micelle surface repel one another, so micelles do not coalesce and the grease stays suspended.

subject: Chemistry
title: Anionic & Non-ionic Detergents
description: Two of three detergent classes. Anionic = active part is the anion; Non-ionic = no ionic group, cleans via H-bonding.

related_concepts.name: Anionic detergents
related_concepts.definition: Sodium salts of sulphonated long-chain alcohols/hydrocarbons: sodium alkylbenzenesulphonates (SABS) and sodium lauryl sulphate (CH3(CH2)10CH2OSO3-Na+). The cleansing anion bears the negative charge. Used in toothpastes and laundry.

related_concepts.name: Non-ionic detergents
related_concepts.definition: No ionic group; e.g. esters of polyethylene glycol (PEG) with stearic acid (a fatty acid). Remove grease by micelle formation like other detergents; used in liquid dishwashing detergents.

related_concepts.name: Cationic detergents
related_concepts.definition: Quaternary ammonium salts (active part = cation), e.g. cetyltrimethylammonium bromide; used in hair conditioners, also germicidal.

subject: Chemistry
title: Artificial Sweeteners
description: Sugar-substitute food additives (no calories). Sweetness given relative to sucrose; key exam point is heat stability.

related_concepts.name: Saccharin
related_concepts.definition: First popular artificial sweetener, ~550x sweeter than sucrose; calorie-free, excreted unchanged; safe for diabetics.

related_concepts.name: Aspartame
related_concepts.definition: ~100x sweeter than sucrose; UNSTABLE at cooking temperature, so its use is limited to cold foods and soft drinks only.

related_concepts.name: Sucralose
related_concepts.definition: Trichloro derivative of sucrose, ~600x sweeter; looks/tastes like sugar and is STABLE at cooking temperature, so it can be used in baked/cooked foods.

related_concepts.name: Alitame
related_concepts.definition: ~2000x sweeter than sucrose (high-potency); control of sweetness in food is difficult.

subject: Chemistry
title: Bactericidal vs Bacteriostatic
description: Two modes of antibiotic action, frequent match-the-column item. Distinguishes whether the antibiotic kills or only halts multiplication.

related_concepts.name: Bactericidal
related_concepts.definition: Kill bacteria outright: Penicillin, Aminoglycosides (e.g. streptomycin), Ofloxacin.

related_concepts.name: Bacteriostatic
related_concepts.definition: Arrest growth/multiplication of bacteria without killing them: Erythromycin, Tetracycline, Chloramphenicol.

related_concepts.name: Spectrum vs mode
related_concepts.definition: Spectrum (broad/narrow) describes the RANGE of bacteria affected; cidal/static describes the EFFECT on those bacteria - independent classifications.

subject: Chemistry
title: n-factor (Oxidizing/Reducing Agent)
description: Valency factor used to calculate Equivalent Weight ($E = M/n$).
derivation:
Example: Dichromate ($Cr_2O_7^{2-} \rightarrow Cr^{3+}$)
1. O.S. of Cr in reactant: $+6$
2. O.S. of Cr in product: $+3$
3. Change per atom: $|3 - 6| = 3$
4. Number of Cr atoms in molecule: 2
$n = 3 \times 2 = 6$

related_concepts.name: Normality
related_concepts.definition: Concentration term defined as $N = n \times Molarity$.

subject: Chemistry
title: n-factor (Disproportionation)
description: Equivalent weight for species undergoing both oxidation and reduction.
derivation:
Consider $2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2$
1. Oxidation half: $H_2O_2 \rightarrow O_2$ ($O^{-1} \to O^0$). Change = 1 per O. $n_{ox} = 2$.
2. Reduction half: $H_2O_2 \rightarrow H_2O$ ($O^{-1} \to O^{-2}$). Change = 1 per O. $n_{red} = 2$.
Total Equivalent Weight $E = E_{ox} + E_{red} = M/n_{ox} + M/n_{red} = M(1/n_{ox} + 1/n_{red})$.

related_concepts.name: Disproportionation
related_concepts.definition: A redox reaction where the same element is simultaneously oxidized and reduced.

subject: Chemistry
title: Equivalent Weight
description: Mass of substance combining with/displacing one mole of electrons in redox. \(E\)=equivalent weight, \(M\)=molar mass, \(n\)=n-factor (electrons gained/lost).

subject: Chemistry
title: Normality from Molarity
description: Relates normality to molarity via n-factor. \(N\)=normality (eq/L), \(n\)=n-factor, \(M\)=molarity (mol/L).

subject: Chemistry
title: Gram Equivalents
description: Number of gram-equivalents of a redox species. \(w\)=mass (g), \(E\)=equivalent weight, \(n\)=n-factor, \(M\)=molar mass, \(N\)=normality, \(V\)=volume in litres.

subject: Chemistry
title: Equivalents Balance (Redox)
description: Mole-ratio form of equivalence: electrons lost = electrons gained. \(n_{ox}\),\(n_{red}\)=n-factors of oxidant and reductant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Standard Cell EMF
description: EMF of a galvanic (redox) cell from standard electrode potentials. \(E^{\circ}_{cell}\)=standard cell potential; cathode=reduction, anode=oxidation half-cell.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nernst Equation
description: Cell potential under non-standard conditions at 298 K. \(E_{cell}\)=emf, \(E^{\circ}_{cell}\)=standard emf, \(n\)=electrons transferred, \(Q\)=reaction quotient.
derivation:
Start from \(E = E^{\circ} - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln Q\).
At \(T=298\,K\), substitute \(R=8.314\), \(F=96500\) and convert \(\ln\) to \(\log\): \(\frac{2.303RT}{F}=0.0591\).
Thus \(E_{cell}=E^{\circ}_{cell}-\frac{0.0591}{n}\log Q\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Gibbs Energy and EMF
description: Links spontaneity of a redox cell to its EMF. \(\Delta G^{\circ}\)=standard Gibbs energy, \(n\)=electrons, \(F\)=96500 C/mol, \(E^{\circ}_{cell}\)=standard emf.

subject: Chemistry
title: EMF and Equilibrium Constant
description: Relates standard cell EMF to the equilibrium constant of the redox reaction at 298 K. \(K\)=equilibrium constant, \(n\)=electrons, \(E^{\circ}_{cell}\)=standard emf.
derivation:
At equilibrium \(E_{cell}=0\) and \(Q=K\).
From Nernst: \(0=E^{\circ}_{cell}-\frac{0.0591}{n}\log K\).
Rearrange: \(\log K=\frac{nE^{\circ}_{cell}}{0.0591}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Faraday's First Law
visual_data: w = \frac{E \times I \times t}{F} = Z I t
description: Mass deposited/liberated in electrolysis (a redox process at electrodes). \(w\)=mass, \(E\)=equivalent weight, \(I\)=current (A), \(t\)=time (s), \(F\)=96500 C, \(Z\)=electrochemical equivalent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Equivalents from Charge
description: Number of gram-equivalents deposited by charge \(Q\) in electrolysis. \(Q\)=charge (C), \(I\)=current (A), \(t\)=time (s), \(F\)=Faraday constant.

subject: Chemistry
title: Faraday's Second Law
description: Same charge through different cells deposits masses in ratio of equivalent weights. \(w\)=mass deposited, \(E\)=equivalent weight; subscripts denote the two substances.

subject: Chemistry
title: Percentage Purity (Titration)
description: Purity of a redox sample from titration data. \(N\)=normality of titrant, \(V\)=volume used (L), \(E\)=equivalent weight of analyte, \(w_{sample}\)=mass of impure sample.

subject: Chemistry
title: n-factor of KMnO4 (Acidic)
description: Half-reaction and n-factor of permanganate in acidic medium (purple to colourless). \(n=5\) so \(E = M/5 = 158/5 = 31.6\).

subject: Chemistry
title: n-factor of KMnO4 (Neutral/Basic)
description: Permanganate reduction in neutral/weakly basic medium (purple to brown \(MnO_2\)). \(n=3\), so \(E = 158/3\). Strongly basic: \(n=1\) (to \(MnO_4^{2-}\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: n-factor of K2Cr2O7 (Acidic)
description: Dichromate reduction in acidic medium (orange to green \(Cr^{3+}\)). \(n=6\), so \(E = 294/6 = 49\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxidation State Balance Rule
description: Computes oxidation number of an unknown atom in a molecule/ion. Sum of oxidation states of all atoms equals net charge (zero for neutral molecule).

subject: Chemistry
title: Rules for Assigning O.N.
description: Standard rules to assign oxidation number to each atom (the basis of all redox/n-factor work). Defaults: \(H=+1\), \(O=-2\), \(F=-1\), alkali metals \(=+1\), alkaline earth \(=+2\); monatomic ion O.N. = its charge.

related_concepts.name: O in peroxides
related_concepts.definition: Oxygen is \(-1\) in peroxides like \(H_2O_2\), \(Na_2O_2\), \(BaO_2\).

related_concepts.name: O in superoxides
related_concepts.definition: Oxygen is \(-\frac{1}{2}\) in superoxides like \(KO_2\), \(RbO_2\).

related_concepts.name: O in OF2
related_concepts.definition: Oxygen is \(+2\) in \(OF_2\) (and \(+1\) in \(O_2F_2\)) since F is more electronegative.

related_concepts.name: H in metal hydrides
related_concepts.definition: Hydrogen is \(-1\) in ionic/metal hydrides like \(NaH\), \(CaH_2\), \(LiAlH_4\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Average Oxidation Number
description: Computes the mean (often fractional) O.N. of one element in a species. Numerator = species charge minus contribution of all other atoms; denominator = count of the atoms whose O.N. is sought.

related_concepts.name: Fe in Fe3O4
related_concepts.definition: \(Fe_3O_4\) gives average \(Fe = +\frac{8}{3}\) (mix of \(Fe^{2+}\) and \(2\,Fe^{3+}\)).

related_concepts.name: S in Na2S2O3
related_concepts.definition: Sodium thiosulphate: average \(S = +2\) (one \(+5\), one \(-1\) on structural analysis).

related_concepts.name: C in C3O2
related_concepts.definition: Carbon suboxide: average \(C = +\frac{4}{3}\); sucrose \(C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}\) gives \(C=0\).

related_concepts.name: N in NH4NO3
related_concepts.definition: Average \(N = 0\), but distinct values \(-3\) (in \(NH_4^+\)) and \(+5\) (in \(NO_3^-\)).

related_concepts.name: S in Caro's/Marshall's acid
related_concepts.definition: S is \(+6\) in both \(H_2SO_5\) (Caro's) and \(H_2S_2O_8\) (Marshall's) due to peroxide \(O\!-\!O\) linkage.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mole Ratio at Equivalence
description: Bridges molarity-based and equivalent-based titration math at the end point. \(m_1,m_2\)=moles of the two species, \(n_1,n_2\)=their n-factors; equivalents of oxidant equal equivalents of reductant.

related_concepts.name: Equivalence point
related_concepts.definition: Stage where stoichiometrically equal equivalents of oxidant and reductant have reacted.

related_concepts.name: Link to molarity titration
related_concepts.definition: Equivalent form \(N_1V_1=N_2V_2\) reduces to mole form \(m_1n_1=m_2n_2\) since \(N=nM\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Strength (g/L)
description: Converts a titre concentration to mass per litre of solution. \(N\)=normality, \(E\)=equivalent weight, \(M\)=molarity, \(M_{molar}\)=molar mass.

related_concepts.name: Strength to mass
related_concepts.definition: Mass of solute \(w = \text{Strength} \times V_{(L)}\) of solution.

related_concepts.name: Normality-molarity link
related_concepts.definition: Since \(N = nM\) and \(E = M_{molar}/n\), both expressions for strength give the same value.

subject: Chemistry
title: Decay Constant Relation
description: Radioactive decay follows first order kinetics. $\lambda$: decay constant.
derivation:
Rate of decay is proportional to number of nuclei present.
$-dN/dt = \lambda N$.
Integrate from $N_0$ to $N_t$:
$\ln(N_t/N_0) = -\lambda t$.
$N_t = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$.

related_concepts.name: Activity
related_concepts.definition: The rate of decay ($A = \lambda N$). Unit: Becquerel (Bq) or Curie (Ci).

subject: Chemistry
title: Average Life
description: The average time a radioactive nucleus survives.
derivation:
Definition: Sum of lifetimes of all atoms / Total atoms.
$\tau = \frac{\int_0^\infty t (\lambda N_0 e^{-\lambda t}) dt}{N_0}$.
Solving the integral yields $\tau = 1/\lambda$.
Since $t_{1/2} = 0.693/\lambda$, then $\tau = t_{1/2} / 0.693 = 1.44 t_{1/2}$.

related_concepts.name: Nuclear Stability
related_concepts.definition: Determined by n/p ratio. Unstable nuclei decay to adjust this ratio.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nuclear Binding Energy
description: Energy released when nucleons form a nucleus. $\Delta m$: Mass defect.
derivation:
Mass of nucleus is always less than sum of masses of individual protons and neutrons.
$\Delta m = [Z m_p + (A-Z) m_n] - M_{nucleus}$
This 'lost' mass is converted to energy holding the nucleus together.
1 amu $\approx$ 931.5 MeV.

related_concepts.name: Binding Energy per Nucleon
related_concepts.definition: Measure of stability. Higher BE/A (e.g., Fe-56) means higher stability.

subject: Chemistry
title: Q-Value of Reaction
description: Energy released ($Q>0$, Exo) or absorbed ($Q<0$, Endo) in a nuclear reaction.
derivation:
Based on Mass-Energy Equivalence.
Total Mass-Energy is conserved.
If product mass is lower, mass was converted to kinetic energy (Q).
$Q = [\sum m_{parent} - \sum m_{daughter}] \times 931.5 \text{ MeV}$.

related_concepts.name: Alpha Decay
related_concepts.definition: Emission of Helium nucleus ($^4_2He$). Usually has positive Q-value for heavy nuclei.

subject: Chemistry
title: Half-Life
description: Time for half of a radioactive sample to decay (first-order). \(t_{1/2}\)=half-life, \(\lambda\)=decay constant.
derivation:
First order: \(N_t = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}\).
At half-life \(N_t = N_0/2\):
\(\frac{1}{2} = e^{-\lambda t_{1/2}}\).
Take \(\ln\): \(\ln 2 = \lambda t_{1/2}\).
\(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{\lambda}\), independent of \(N_0\).

related_concepts.name: Independence from amount
related_concepts.definition: Half-life of a first-order (radioactive) process is constant and does not depend on initial quantity.

subject: Chemistry
title: Fraction Remaining (n Half-Lives)
description: Fraction of nuclei left after \(n\) half-lives. \(N_t\)=nuclei left, \(N_0\)=initial, \(n\)=number of half-lives, \(t\)=elapsed time.
derivation:
Each half-life halves the amount.
After 1: \(N_0/2\); after 2: \(N_0/4\).
After \(n\): \(N_0 (1/2)^n\).
With \(n = t/t_{1/2}\) this matches \(N_0 e^{-\lambda t}\).

related_concepts.name: Amount left
related_concepts.definition: Mass/moles left \(= W_0 (1/2)^n\); amount decayed \(= W_0[1-(1/2)^n]\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Activity
description: Rate of disintegration of a sample. \(A\)=activity, \(\lambda\)=decay constant, \(N\)=number of nuclei, \(A_0\)=initial activity.
derivation:
Activity \(A = -dN/dt = \lambda N\).
Since \(N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}\):
\(A = \lambda N_0 e^{-\lambda t} = A_0 e^{-\lambda t}\).
Activity decays with the same half-life as the nuclei.

related_concepts.name: Units of activity
related_concepts.definition: 1 Becquerel (Bq) = 1 disintegration/s; 1 Curie (Ci) = \(3.7\times10^{10}\) Bq.

subject: Chemistry
title: Age / Time of Decay
description: Time elapsed for a radioactive sample to fall from \(N_0\) to \(N_t\). \(t\)=time, \(\lambda\)=decay constant.
derivation:
From \(N_t = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}\):
\(\lambda t = \ln(N_0/N_t)\).
Convert to base-10:
\(t = \frac{2.303}{\lambda}\log(N_0/N_t)\).
May use \(N\), activity \(A\), or mass interchangeably.

related_concepts.name: Form flexibility
related_concepts.definition: Ratio \(N_0/N_t\) may be replaced by \(A_0/A_t\), \(W_0/W_t\), or mole ratio — all proportional.

subject: Chemistry
title: Carbon Dating
description: Estimates age of carbon-bearing material from \(^{14}C\) activity. \(A_0\)=activity in living matter, \(A_t\)=present activity, \(t_{1/2}\approx 5730\) yr.

related_concepts.name: Principle
related_concepts.definition: \(^{14}C\) is replenished in living organisms; after death it only decays, so activity ratio gives age.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass Defect
description: Difference between mass of free nucleons and the nucleus. \(Z\)=protons, \(A\)=mass number, \(m_p\)=proton mass, \(m_n\)=neutron mass, \(M_{nucleus}\)=actual nuclear mass.

related_concepts.name: Packing fraction
related_concepts.definition: \(f = (M_{atomic} - A)/A\); negative \(f\) implies a more stable nucleus.

subject: Chemistry
title: Binding Energy per Nucleon
description: Stability index of a nucleus. \(BE\)=binding energy, \(A\)=mass number, \(\Delta m\)=mass defect in amu.
derivation:
\(BE = \Delta m \times c^2\); using \(1\,\text{amu}=931.5\,\text{MeV}\):
\(BE = \Delta m \times 931.5\,\text{MeV}\).
Divide by nucleon count \(A\) to compare nuclei of different sizes.

related_concepts.name: Peak stability
related_concepts.definition: \(BE/A\) is maximum (\(\approx 8.8\) MeV) near \(^{56}Fe\); fusion of light and fission of heavy nuclei both release energy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass-Energy Equivalence (amu)
description: Energy equivalent of a mass change in nuclear reactions. \(\Delta m\)=mass change in amu; \(1\,\text{amu}=931.5\,\text{MeV}=1.49\times10^{-10}\,\text{J}\).

related_concepts.name: Conversion
related_concepts.definition: \(1\,\text{MeV}=1.602\times10^{-13}\,\text{J}\); used to express nuclear energies.

subject: Chemistry
title: Alpha Emission (Group Displacement)
description: Alpha decay reduces \(A\) by 4 and \(Z\) by 2. \(X\)=parent, \(Y\)=daughter, \(^{4}_{2}He\)=alpha particle.

related_concepts.name: Soddy-Fajans rule
related_concepts.definition: Alpha emission shifts the daughter two places left in the periodic table.

subject: Chemistry
title: Beta-minus Emission
description: Beta-minus decay keeps \(A\) constant and raises \(Z\) by 1. A neutron converts to a proton; \(\bar{\nu}\)=antineutrino.
derivation:
In the nucleus: \(^{1}_{0}n \rightarrow {}^{1}_{1}p + {}^{0}_{-1}e + \bar{\nu}\).
Proton number rises by 1, mass number unchanged.
Occurs in neutron-rich nuclei (high n/p ratio).

related_concepts.name: Group displacement
related_concepts.definition: Beta-minus emission shifts daughter one place right in the periodic table.

subject: Chemistry
title: Positron Emission & K-Capture
description: Routes that lower \(Z\) by 1 with \(A\) constant in proton-rich nuclei. \(^{0}_{+1}e\)=positron, \(\nu\)=neutrino.
derivation:
Positron emission: \(^{1}_{1}p \rightarrow {}^{1}_{0}n + {}^{0}_{+1}e + \nu\).
K-electron capture: \(^{1}_{1}p + {}^{0}_{-1}e \rightarrow {}^{1}_{0}n + \nu\).
Both decrease \(Z\) by 1, leave \(A\) unchanged; favoured at low n/p ratio.

related_concepts.name: When each occurs
related_concepts.definition: Positron emission needs energy gap \(>1.02\) MeV; K-capture dominates for heavy nuclei where this gap is small.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Alpha & Beta Particles
description: Particles emitted in a full decay series. \(A_p,Z_p\)=parent mass/atomic no., \(A_d,Z_d\)=daughter mass/atomic no.
derivation:
Mass change only via alpha (each removes 4): \(\alpha = (A_p-A_d)/4\).
Charge balance: \(Z_p = Z_d + 2\alpha - \beta\).
Rearrange: \(\beta = 2\alpha - (Z_p - Z_d)\) (counts beta-minus particles).

related_concepts.name: Decay series
related_concepts.definition: Natural series: 4n (Thorium), 4n+2 (Uranium), 4n+3 (Actinium); 4n+1 (Neptunium) is artificial.

subject: Chemistry
title: Parallel Decay (Branching)
description: A nuclide decaying by two simultaneous paths. \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\)=individual decay constants, \(\lambda\)=effective constant.
derivation:
Two parallel first-order paths:
\(-dN/dt = \lambda_1 N + \lambda_2 N = (\lambda_1+\lambda_2)N\).
Effective \(\lambda = \lambda_1+\lambda_2\).
Fraction via path 1 \(= \lambda_1/(\lambda_1+\lambda_2)\).

related_concepts.name: Branching ratio
related_concepts.definition: Fraction decaying by a given mode equals that mode's \(\lambda\) divided by total \(\lambda\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Radioactive Equilibrium (Secular)
description: Steady state in a decay chain where parent (1) is much longer-lived than daughter (2). \(N\)=nuclei, \(\lambda\)=decay constant.
derivation:
At equilibrium, daughter forms as fast as it decays:
rate of formation = rate of decay.
\(\lambda_1 N_1 = \lambda_2 N_2\) (activities equal).
Since \(\lambda \propto 1/t_{1/2}\): \(N_1/N_2 = t_{1/2}(1)/t_{1/2}(2)\).

related_concepts.name: Secular vs transient
related_concepts.definition: Secular: \(t_{1/2}\) of parent \(\gg\) daughter (equal activities); transient: parent only moderately longer-lived.

subject: Chemistry
title: Energy from Mass Loss (Joules)
description: Energy released per kg of mass converted in fission/fusion. \(\Delta m\)=mass lost (kg), \(c=3\times10^8\,\text{m/s}\).
derivation:
Einstein: \(E=mc^2\).
For \(\Delta m = 1\,\text{kg}\):
\(E = 1 \times (3\times10^8)^2 = 9\times10^{16}\,\text{J}\).
Scales linearly with mass destroyed.

related_concepts.name: Fission vs fusion
related_concepts.definition: Fission splits heavy nuclei (e.g. \(^{235}U\)); fusion joins light nuclei (e.g. H to He) — both move toward higher \(BE/A\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Law of Radioactive Decay (Log Form)
description: Integrated first-order rate law for radioactive decay; parent result for half-life and dating. \(N_0\)=initial nuclei, \(N\)=nuclei left after time \(t\), \(\lambda\)=decay constant.
derivation:
Rate \(-\frac{dN}{dt} = \lambda N\)
Separate: \(\frac{dN}{N} = -\lambda \, dt\)
Integrate \(N_0 \to N\): \(\ln \frac{N}{N_0} = -\lambda t\)
Rearrange: \(\ln \frac{N_0}{N} = \lambda t\)

subject: Chemistry
title: Units of Activity (Bq, Ci, Rd)
description: Standard units of radioactivity (disintegrations per second) and their conversions. \(\text{Bq}\)=becquerel (1 dps), \(\text{Ci}\)=curie, \(\text{Rd}\)=rutherford; SI unit is the becquerel.

subject: Chemistry
title: Specific Activity
description: Activity per unit mass of radioactive sample (used in dating & medical isotopes). \(A\)=activity (\(\lambda N\)), \(m\)=mass of sample, \(\lambda\)=decay constant, \(N\)=number of radioactive nuclei.

subject: Chemistry
title: n/p Ratio & Belt of Stability
description: Neutron-to-proton ratio predicts nuclear stability and decay mode. \(n\)=neutrons, \(p\)=protons; high \(n/p\) emits \(\beta^{-}\) (n\(\to\)p), low \(n/p\) undergoes positron emission or K-capture (p\(\to\)n); \(Z>83\) all unstable.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Half-Lives & Time
description: Direct exponential form linking nuclei remaining to elapsed time in half-life units. \(N\)=nuclei left, \(N_0\)=initial nuclei, \(t_{1/2}\)=half-life, \(n\)=number of half-lives elapsed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Nuclear Radius & Density
description: Empirical nuclear size and (nearly constant) nuclear density. \(R\)=nuclear radius, \(A\)=mass number, \(R_0\approx1.2\ \text{fm}\); volume \(\propto A\) so density is independent of \(A\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Volume Strength of H2O2
description: Relates molarity to the volume of O2 gas released at STP.
derivation:
Decomposition: $2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2$
2 moles of $H_2O_2$ produce 1 mole of $O_2$ (22.4 L at STP).
Thus, 1 Molar solution ($1$ mol/L) produces $11.2$ L of $O_2$.
Formula: $V = 11.2 \times M = 5.6 \times N$.

related_concepts.name: Perhydrol
related_concepts.definition: Commercial name for 30% H2O2 solution (approx 100 volume strength).

subject: Chemistry
title: Mole - Number of Particles
description: Four equivalent ways to count moles of a substance. \(n\)=moles, \(N\)=number of particles, \(N_A=6.022\times10^{23}\), \(w\)=given mass (g), \(M\)=molar mass (g/mol), \(V\)=volume of gas at STP (mL).
derivation:
1 mole = \(N_A\) particles \(\implies n = N/N_A\).
1 mole weighs \(M\) grams \(\implies n = w/M\).
1 mole of any gas at STP occupies \(22.4\) L \(= 22400\) mL \(\implies n = V/22400\).

related_concepts.name: Avogadro's Number
related_concepts.definition: Number of particles in one mole = \(6.022\times10^{23}\).

related_concepts.name: Molar Volume
related_concepts.definition: Volume of 1 mole of an ideal gas: 22.4 L at STP (0°C, 1 bar ≈ 22.7 L by new NCERT).

subject: Chemistry
title: Molarity (M)
description: Moles of solute per litre of solution; temperature-dependent. \(n\)=moles of solute, \(V\)=volume of solution, \(w\)=mass of solute (g), \(M_{solute}\)=molar mass.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mole Fraction
description: Fraction of total moles contributed by a component; dimensionless. \(n_A,n_B\)=moles of components; sum of all mole fractions = 1.

subject: Chemistry
title: Normality (N)
description: Gram equivalents of solute per litre of solution. \(w\)=mass of solute (g), \(E\)=equivalent mass, \(V\)=volume of solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Normality - Molarity Link
description: Converts molarity to normality via the n-factor. \(N\)=normality, \(M\)=molarity, \(n_f\)=n-factor (basicity/acidity/electrons transferred). Equivalently \(E = M_{molar}/n_f\).
derivation:
Equivalent mass \(E = M_{molar}/n_f\).
\(N = \frac{w\times1000}{E\times V} = \frac{w\times1000}{(M_{molar}/n_f)\times V} = n_f\cdot\frac{w\times1000}{M_{molar}\times V} = n_f \times M\).

related_concepts.name: n-factor
related_concepts.definition: For acids = basicity (replaceable H+); for bases = acidity (replaceable OH-); for salts = total +ve charge; in redox = electrons gained/lost per formula unit.

subject: Chemistry
title: Equivalent Mass (n-factor)
description: Mass that combines with/replaces 1 mole of H or 1 mole of electrons. \(E\)=equivalent mass, \(M_{molar}\)=molar mass, \(n_f\)=n-factor.

related_concepts.name: Equivalent mass of acid
related_concepts.definition: Molar mass ÷ basicity, e.g. H2SO4 = 98/2 = 49.

related_concepts.name: Equivalent mass of oxidant
related_concepts.definition: Molar mass ÷ electrons gained per formula unit, e.g. KMnO4 (acidic) = 158/5 = 31.6.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dilution Formula
description: On dilution moles of solute stay constant. \(M_1,V_1\)=initial molarity & volume, \(M_2,V_2\)=final molarity & volume. Same form holds for normality (\(N_1V_1=N_2V_2\)).

subject: Chemistry
title: Law of Equivalents (Titration)
description: At the equivalence point, gram equivalents of the two reacting species are equal. \(N\)=normality, \(V\)=volume of each solution; valid for acid-base and redox titrations.

related_concepts.name: Equivalence point
related_concepts.definition: Stage at which equivalents of titrant exactly equal equivalents of analyte.

related_concepts.name: Back titration
related_concepts.definition: Excess reagent reacted then estimated; equivalents balanced overall.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mixing Solutions (Resultant Molarity)
description: Molarity after mixing two solutions of the same solute (no reaction). \(M_R\)=resultant molarity, \(M_1,M_2\)=molarities, \(V_1,V_2\)=volumes mixed.

subject: Chemistry
title: Molarity from %w/w & Density
description: Converts a commercial solution's strength to molarity. \(d\)=density (g/mL), \(\%w/w\)=mass percent of solute, \(M_{solute}\)=molar mass.
derivation:
Take 100 g solution: solute \(=\%w/w\) g, volume \(=100/d\) mL.
\(M = \dfrac{(\%w/w)/M_{solute}}{(100/d)/1000} = \dfrac{10\,d\,(\%w/w)}{M_{solute}}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Molarity - Molality Relation
description: Interconverts molarity and molality using solution density. \(M\)=molarity, \(m\)=molality, \(d\)=density (g/mL), \(M_{solute}\)=molar mass of solute.
derivation:
1 L solution has mass \(1000\,d\) g and contains \(M\) mol solute of mass \(M\cdot M_{solute}\) g.
Mass of solvent \(= 1000d - M\,M_{solute}\) g.
\(m = \dfrac{M}{(1000d - M\,M_{solute})/1000} = \dfrac{1000M}{1000d - M\,M_{solute}}\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Parts Per Million (ppm)
description: Concentration of very dilute solutions (e.g. trace impurities, hardness of water). Numerator and denominator in same mass units.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass Percent (%w/w)
description: Mass of solute per 100 g of solution. \(w_{solute}\)=mass of solute, \(w_{solvent}\)=mass of solvent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Empirical & Molecular Formula
description: Links molecular formula to empirical formula. EFM=empirical formula mass, \(M_{molar}\)=molecular (molar) mass, \(n\)=whole-number multiple. Molecular formula \(=(\text{empirical formula})_n\).

related_concepts.name: Empirical formula
related_concepts.definition: Simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element, found from %composition ÷ atomic mass, then normalising.

subject: Chemistry
title: Percentage Composition by Mass
description: Mass percent of an element in a compound. Numerator = total mass of that element per formula unit, \(M_{molar}\)=molar mass of compound.

subject: Chemistry
title: Average Atomic Mass
description: Mean atomic mass from isotopic abundances. \(a_i\)=isotopic mass, \(x_i\)=% abundance of each isotope.

subject: Chemistry
title: Moles of a Gas (Ideal Gas)
description: Counts moles of gas from measurable state variables. \(P\)=pressure, \(V\)=volume, \(R\)=0.0821 L·atm·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹, \(T\)=absolute temperature (K).

subject: Chemistry
title: Molar Mass from Gas Density
description: Molar mass of a gas from its density. \(d\)=density (g/L), \(R\)=gas constant, \(T\)=temperature (K), \(P\)=pressure.
derivation:
From \(PV=nRT\) with \(n=w/M_{molar}\): \(PV=\frac{w}{M_{molar}}RT\).
Rearrange: \(M_{molar}=\frac{w}{V}\cdot\frac{RT}{P}=\frac{dRT}{P}\) since \(d=w/V\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Percentage Yield
description: Efficiency of a reaction. Actual yield=mass/moles obtained experimentally; theoretical yield=amount predicted from stoichiometry of the limiting reagent.

related_concepts.name: Limiting reagent
related_concepts.definition: Reactant fully consumed first; it decides the maximum (theoretical) amount of product. Found by comparing mole ÷ stoichiometric coefficient for each reactant - smallest value limits.

subject: Chemistry
title: POAC (Conservation of Atoms)
description: Principle of Atom Conservation: total atoms of an element are conserved, so balancing the full equation can be skipped. Useful for multi-step/sequential reaction problems.

subject: Chemistry
title: Limiting Reagent Method
description: Identifies the reactant that runs out first and fixes the maximum product in any mass-mass numerical. \(\text{moles}\)=moles of each reactant taken, \(\text{stoich. coeff.}\)=its balanced-equation coefficient; the reactant giving the SMALLEST ratio is the limiting reagent and all product amounts are calculated from it.
derivation:
For \(aA + bB \rightarrow \text{products}\):
Compute \(\frac{n_A}{a}\) and \(\frac{n_B}{b}\).
The smaller value is the limiting reagent (consumed completely).
Product moles \(= (\text{coeff. of product}) \times (\text{smallest ratio})\).
Leftover of excess reagent \(= n_{excess} - (\text{coeff.}_{excess}) \times (\text{smallest ratio})\).

related_concepts.name: Excess Reagent
related_concepts.definition: The reactant left over after the reaction stops; present in more than the stoichiometric requirement.

related_concepts.name: Stoichiometric Ratio
related_concepts.definition: Mole ratio of reactants exactly equal to the coefficient ratio, where neither is in excess.

subject: Chemistry
title: Vapour Density & Molar Mass
description: Molar mass of a gas equals twice its vapour density (density relative to H2). \(M\)=molar mass (g/mol), \(\text{V.D.}\)=vapour density = mass of a gas volume / mass of same volume of \(H_2\) at same \(T, P\).
derivation:
\(\text{V.D.} = \frac{\text{mass of } n \text{ molecules of gas}}{\text{mass of } n \text{ molecules of } H_2} = \frac{M_{gas}}{M_{H_2}}\).
Since \(M_{H_2} = 2\): \(\text{V.D.} = \frac{M}{2}\).
Therefore \(M = 2 \times \text{V.D.}\)

related_concepts.name: Degree of Dissociation
related_concepts.definition: \(\alpha = \frac{D - d}{(n-1)d}\), where D = normal V.D., d = observed V.D., n = no. of product moles per reactant mole.

related_concepts.name: Abnormal Vapour Density
related_concepts.definition: Observed V.D. differs from theoretical due to dissociation (lower) or association (higher) in gas phase.

subject: Chemistry
title: Mass-Mass Stoichiometry
description: Mass of product/other reactant from a given mass of one reactant via the balanced equation. \(w_A\)=given mass of A, \(M_A, M_B\)=molar masses, \(a, b\)=balanced coefficients of A and B.
derivation:
Moles of A \(= \frac{w_A}{M_A}\).
Mole ratio from balanced equation: \(\frac{n_B}{n_A} = \frac{b}{a}\).
Moles of B \(= \frac{w_A}{M_A} \times \frac{b}{a}\).
Mass of B \(= \text{moles} \times M_B\).

related_concepts.name: Gravimetric Analysis
related_concepts.definition: Quantitative determination of an analyte by measuring the mass of a product from a known reaction.

subject: Chemistry
title: Number of Equivalents
description: Counts reacting capacity, basis of the law of equivalents in redox/acid-base titrations. \(w\)=mass, \(E\)=equivalent mass, \(n\)=moles, \(n_f\)=n-factor (valency / electrons transferred / H+ or OH- exchanged).

related_concepts.name: n-factor (Acid/Base)
related_concepts.definition: Number of replaceable H+ for an acid or OH- for a base; e.g. n=2 for \(H_2SO_4\), n=1 for HCl.

related_concepts.name: n-factor (Redox)
related_concepts.definition: Total number of electrons gained or lost per formula unit in the redox change.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solvay Process (Ammonia-Soda)
visual_data: NaCl + NH_3 + CO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow NaHCO_3 \downarrow + NH_4Cl
description: Industrial preparation of Sodium Carbonate (Washing Soda). Principle: Low solubility of sodium bicarbonate.
derivation:
1. Carbonation: Ammoniated brine reacts with $CO_2$.
   $2NH_3 + H_2O + CO_2 \rightarrow (NH_4)_2CO_3$.
   $(NH_4)_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2 \rightarrow 2NH_4HCO_3$.
2. Precipitation: Ammonium bicarbonate reacts with NaCl.
   $NH_4HCO_3 + NaCl \rightarrow NaHCO_3 \downarrow + NH_4Cl$.
3. Calcination: Heating gives Soda Ash.
   $2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} Na_2CO_3 + CO_2 + H_2O$.
4. Recovery: Ammonia regenerated using $Ca(OH)_2$.

related_concepts.name: Potassium Carbonate
related_concepts.definition: Cannot be made by Solvay process because $KHCO_3$ is too soluble to precipitate.

subject: Chemistry
title: Heating of Nitrates (Trends)
description: Thermal decomposition depends on polarization power of cation.
derivation:
1. Alkali Metals ($Na, K, Rb, Cs$): Stable nitrates. Decompose to Nitrite.
   $2NaNO_3 \rightarrow 2NaNO_2 + O_2$.
2. Lithium & Alkaline Earth ($Li, Mg, Ca...$): High polarizing power ($Li^+$ is small).
   Distorts electron cloud of $NO_3^-$, weakening N-O bonds.
   Decomposes to Oxide + Brown $NO_2$ gas.
   $4LiNO_3 \rightarrow 2Li_2O + 4NO_2 + O_2$.

related_concepts.name: Diagonal Relationship
related_concepts.definition: Similarity between Li and Mg due to similar ionic potential (Charge/Size ratio).

subject: Chemistry
title: Structure of BeCl2
description: Beryllium Chloride exists as a polymer in solid state and dimer/monomer in vapor.
derivation:
1. Solid State: Polymeric chain via Chloro-bridges.
   Be is $sp^3$ hybridized (tetrahedral env). Coordination Number = 4.
2. Vapor Phase (< 1200K): Chloro-bridged Dimer ($Be_2Cl_4$).
   Be is $sp^2$ hybridized.
3. Vapor Phase (> 1200K): Linear Monomer ($Cl-Be-Cl$).
   Be is $sp$ hybridized (electron deficient, 4 valence e-).

related_concepts.name: Banana Bond
related_concepts.definition: 3-center-2-electron bond, though BeCl2 bridging is considered coordinate covalent (3c-4e in simple terms).

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility of Group 2 Sulfates
description: Solubility decreases down the group. $BeSO_4$ is soluble, $BaSO_4$ is insoluble.
derivation:
Solubility depends on $\Delta H_{sol} = \Delta H_{hyd} - U$.
Down the group, Lattice Energy ($U$) remains roughly constant (dominated by large Sulfate ion).
However, Hydration Energy ($\Delta H_{hyd}$) decreases significantly as cation size increases.
Result: $\Delta H_{sol}$ becomes less negative (less favorable) down the group.

related_concepts.name: Hydration Energy
related_concepts.definition: Energy released when ions are surrounded by water molecules ($HE \propto 1/r^+$).

subject: Chemistry
title: Diagonal Relationship
visual_data: Li \sim Mg, \quad Be \sim Al, \quad B \sim Si
description: Similarity of an element with the one diagonally placed in the next group/period (similar charge/radius ratio). \(Li\)~\(Mg\), \(Be\)~\(Al\) are the s-block cases.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lithium Combustion (Nitride)
description: Only Li (among alkali metals) directly combines with N2 to form a nitride (diagonal similarity with Mg). \(Li_3N\)=lithium nitride.

subject: Chemistry
title: Alkali Metal + Water
description: Alkali metals react vigorously with water giving hydroxide + H2; reactivity Li<Na<K<Rb<Cs. \(M\)=alkali metal, \(MOH\)=strong base.

subject: Chemistry
title: Alkali Metals in Liquid Ammonia
description: Dissolving alkali metals in liquid NH3 gives blue (ammoniated electron), paramagnetic, conducting solutions; bronze and diamagnetic when concentrated. The colour is due to the solvated free electron.

subject: Chemistry
title: Thermal Stability of Carbonates
description: Group 2 carbonates decompose on heating; stability increases down the group (BeCO3<MgCO3<...<BaCO3) as cation polarising power falls. \(M\)=alkaline earth metal.

subject: Chemistry
title: Li2CO3 Anomaly
description: Unlike other alkali metal carbonates (stable to heat), Li2CO3 decomposes on heating due to small Li+ polarising power (diagonal similarity with Mg).

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility: Group 2 Hydroxides
description: Solubility of alkaline earth metal hydroxides increases down the group (lattice energy falls faster than hydration energy). Be(OH)2 is amphoteric.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lattice/Hydration Energy Solubility Rule
description: Net dissolution enthalpy decides solubility trends of s-block salts. \(\Delta H_{hyd}\)=hydration enthalpy (released), \(\Delta H_{lattice}\)=lattice enthalpy; salt dissolves readily when \(|\Delta H_{hyd}|>|\Delta H_{lattice}|\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Flame Colours (s-Block)
visual_data: Li{:}\text{crimson}, \; Na{:}\text{yellow}, \; K{:}\text{lilac}, \; Ca{:}\text{brick-red}, \; Sr{:}\text{crimson}, \; Ba{:}\text{apple-green}
description: Characteristic flame test colours from electron de-excitation; Be and Mg show no colour (electrons too tightly bound, high excitation energy).

subject: Chemistry
title: Castner-Kellner Process
visual_data: \text{At Hg cathode: } Na^+ + e^- \rightarrow Na (\text{amalgam}); \quad 2Na/Hg + 2H_2O \rightarrow 2NaOH + H_2 + Hg
description: Manufacture of NaOH by electrolysis of brine using a mercury cathode; Cl2 liberated at anode. Gives high-purity NaOH.

subject: Chemistry
title: Washing Soda from Baking Soda
description: Heating sodium bicarbonate (in Solvay process) gives soda ash Na2CO3. Washing soda crystallises as \(Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Lime: Quicklime & Slaked Lime
visual_data: CaCO_3 \xrightarrow{\Delta} CaO + CO_2; \quad CaO + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2
description: Calcination of limestone gives quicklime (CaO); slaking with water gives slaked lime Ca(OH)2 (an exothermic reaction).

subject: Chemistry
title: Limewater Test for CO2
visual_data: Ca(OH)_2 + CO_2 \rightarrow CaCO_3 \downarrow + H_2O; \quad CaCO_3 + CO_2 + H_2O \rightarrow Ca(HCO_3)_2
description: Limewater turns milky with CO2 (CaCO3 ppt); excess CO2 redissolves it as soluble calcium bicarbonate. Classic CO2 identification test.

subject: Chemistry
title: Plaster of Paris
description: Heating gypsum at ~393 K (120 C) gives Plaster of Paris (hemihydrate); setting reverses this by re-adding water. POP = \(CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Bleaching Powder
description: Action of Cl2 on slaked lime gives bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride). Formula often written \(CaOCl_2\); acts as oxidising/bleaching agent.

subject: Chemistry
title: Be Amphoterism
description: Beryllium (unlike other group 2 metals) dissolves in alkali giving beryllate + H2, showing amphoteric character (diagonal similarity with Al).

subject: Chemistry
title: Atomic Radius & IE Trend
visual_data: r_{atomic} \uparrow \text{ down group}, \quad IE_1 \downarrow \text{ down group}
description: Down a group atomic/ionic radius increases and ionisation enthalpy decreases; Group 1 has lowest IE in its period. \(IE_1\)=first ionisation enthalpy.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lithium Hydrogencarbonate (No Solid)
visual_data: LiHCO_3 \text{ exists only in solution (no solid)}
description: Unlike Na/K, solid LiHCO3 cannot be isolated (Li anomaly); only NaHCO3 and heavier exist as solids. Diagonal similarity with Mg (no solid MgHCO3).

subject: Chemistry
title: Reducing Power Anomaly (E° )
description: Li is the strongest reducing agent in aqueous solution despite high IE, due to its very high hydration enthalpy. \(E^{\circ}\)=standard reduction potential.

subject: Chemistry
title: Peroxide / Superoxide with Water
description: Peroxides and superoxides hydrolyse to give O2 (and H2O2 from superoxide); KO2 is used in breathing masks/submarines to release O2.

subject: Chemistry
title: Dead Burnt Plaster
description: On strong heating (>200 C) gypsum/POP loses all water to give anhydrous CaSO4 (dead burnt plaster), which no longer sets with water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Washing Soda Hydrate & Efflorescence
description: Hydrate forms of sodium carbonate and its efflorescence (loss of water in air). \(Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O\)=washing soda (decahydrate), \(Na_2CO_3 \cdot H_2O\)=monohydrate; on strong heating monohydrate gives anhydrous soda ash \(Na_2CO_3\).

subject: Chemistry
title: Saline Hydrides + Water
visual_data: NaH + H_2O \rightarrow NaOH + H_2 \uparrow \quad ; \quad CaH_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow Ca(OH)_2 + 2H_2 \uparrow
description: Hydrolysis of ionic (saline) s-block hydrides; H is present as hydridic \(H^-\) (strong reducing agent). \(NaH\)=sodium hydride, \(CaH_2\)=hydrolith; both liberate \(H_2\) violently with water.

subject: Chemistry
title: Oxide Formation Trend (Excess O2)
visual_data: 4Li + O_2 \rightarrow 2Li_2O \;;\; 2Na + O_2 \rightarrow Na_2O_2 \;;\; K + O_2 \rightarrow KO_2
description: Product type in excess \(O_2\) down Group 1: Li gives monoxide \(Li_2O\), Na gives peroxide \(Na_2O_2\), and K/Rb/Cs give superoxides \(MO_2\). Larger cations stabilise the larger \(O_2^-/O_2^{2-}\) anions.

subject: Chemistry
title: Alkali Bicarbonate Decomposition
description: All alkali metal bicarbonates decompose to carbonate on heating; the resulting \(Na_2CO_3\) is thermally stable (does NOT decompose), unlike \(Li_2CO_3\). \(NaHCO_3\)=baking soda, \(Na_2CO_3\)=soda ash.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 2 Carbonate Decomposition Trend
description: Thermal stability (and decomposition temperature) of alkaline-earth carbonates increases down the group. Smaller, more polarising \(Mg^{2+}\) distorts \(CO_3^{2-}\) more, so \(MgCO_3\) decomposes at the lowest temperature; \(BaCO_3\) the highest.

subject: Chemistry
title: Sodium Peroxide with CO2
description: Reaction of sodium peroxide with carbon dioxide; basis of its use in submarines/confined spaces to absorb \(CO_2\) and regenerate \(O_2\). \(Na_2O_2\)=sodium peroxide.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydration Enthalpy Trend (Group 1 & 2)
visual_data: \Delta H_{hyd}: \; Li^+ > Na^+ > K^+ > Rb^+ > Cs^+
description: Hydration enthalpy decreases down the group as ionic size increases (smaller ion = denser charge = stronger hydration). Explains why \(Li^+\) is the most hydrated/largest hydrated ion and least mobile in solution.

subject: Chemistry
title: Hydrated Ionic Radius / Mobility
visual_data: r_{hydrated}: \; Li^+ > Na^+ > K^+ > Rb^+ > Cs^+ \;;\; \text{conductance: } Li^+ < Cs^+
description: Smaller bare ion has larger hydration sphere, so \(Li^+\) is the largest hydrated ion and moves slowest; ionic mobility/molar conductance increases down the group (\(Cs^+\) fastest).

subject: Chemistry
title: Lattice Energy / Basic Strength of Hydroxides
visual_data: \text{Basic strength: } LiOH < NaOH < KOH < RbOH < CsOH
description: Basic (and thermal) stability of alkali hydroxides increases down the group; ionic character rises and lattice energy falls, so \(CsOH\) is the strongest base. \(LiOH\) is the weakest and decomposes on heating.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility of Group 1 Bicarbonates/Carbonates
visual_data: Li_2CO_3 \ll Na_2CO_3 < K_2CO_3 \;;\; Li_2CO_3 \text{ sparingly soluble}
description: Alkali metal carbonates are water-soluble except \(Li_2CO_3\), which is sparingly soluble (anomaly, diagonal link to \(MgCO_3\)). Solubility of \(M_2CO_3\) increases down the group.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lithium Anomaly: LiCl Hygroscopic / Covalent
description: Owing to high polarising power of small \(Li^+\) (Fajans' rule), \(LiCl\) is appreciably covalent, deliquescent and crystallises as the hydrate \(LiCl\cdot 2H_2O\); other alkali chlorides are anhydrous ionic solids.

subject: Chemistry
title: Solubility Trend: Group 2 Hydroxides vs Sulfates
visual_data: OH^-: Be(OH)_2 \to Ba(OH)_2 \uparrow \;;\; SO_4^{2-}: BeSO_4 \to BaSO_4 \downarrow
description: Down Group 2, hydroxide solubility increases but sulfate/carbonate solubility decreases. Large anion (\(SO_4^{2-}\)): lattice energy ~constant, hydration enthalpy falls down group, so solubility falls; small anion (\(OH^-\)): lattice energy dominates and falls faster, so solubility rises.

subject: Chemistry
title: Group 2 Carbide + Water (Acetylene)
description: Calcium carbide (an ionic acetylide) hydrolyses to give acetylene (ethyne). \(CaC_2\)=calcium carbide; \(C_2H_2\)=acetylene, used in oxy-acetylene welding.

subject: Chemistry
title: Lithium Anomaly: Li Combustion Oxide
description: Lithium is the only alkali metal that forms only the normal monoxide \(Li_2O\) in air/excess oxygen (no stable peroxide or superoxide), unlike Na (peroxide) and K/Rb/Cs (superoxide). A key lithium anomaly.

subject: Chemistry
title: Stability of Peroxide/Superoxide Down Group
description: Larger alkali cations stabilise larger anions: stability of superoxides \(MO_2\) and peroxides \(M_2O_2\) increases down the group (lattice-energy/size-matching argument). \(r_{M^+}\)=cation radius.
